specifying loan origination, treating it as an ordinary missing value silently introduces a
different intervention.


11.3.1      A missingness law that no imputer can learn from these records

Suppose P (R = 1) = 1/2 and observed binary outcomes are evenly split. One full model has
P (Y = 1 | R = 0) = 0 and mean 1/4; another has P (Y = 1 | R = 0) = 1 and mean 3/4. They
have exactly the same recorded law (R, RY ). The general bounded-outcome identified interval
is

      P (R = 1)E[Y | R = 1] ≤ E[Y ] ≤ P (R = 1)E[Y | R = 1] + P (R = 0),         0 ≤ Y ≤ 1.

Every value between the endpoints can be attained by a suitable unobserved outcome dis-
tribution. Filling the gaps with the observed mean selects 1/2 through an assumption;
11.4. Measurement error is another inverse problem                                             113


prediction validation on observed cases cannot distinguish these models. A sensitivity parame-
ter δ(x) = E[Y | X = x, R = 0] − E[Y | X = x, R = 1] instead yields the explicit correction
E[(1 − π(X))δ(X)] to the MAR mean. Its admissible range can be connected to bounded
outcomes or external follow-up data.
   Missingness also changes graph discovery. Test-wise complete cases for different triples
need not come from one common observational law; conditioning on observation can open
collider paths. Tu et al. (2019, Section 3, Assumptions 1–4) studies this problem under
causal sufficiency, faithfulness/observability restrictions and specific constraints on missingness
indicators, including no self-masking. Its correction procedure is not a general MNAR solution.
If customers with the greatest unrecorded distress avoid reporting their distress, the no-self-
masking premise is precisely the questionable restriction.


11.4     Measurement error is another inverse problem
Consider binary true receipt A and recorded receipt W . Under a known nondifferential error
model, P (W = w | A = a, Y, X) = Kwa (X). For each outcome value and covariate stratum,
the observed joint probabilities obey
                                          !                              !
                        p(W = 0, Y | X)              p(A = 0, Y | X)
                                              = K(X)                 .                      (11.3)
                        p(W = 1, Y | X)              p(A = 1, Y | X)
                                                                              
                                                                          g
If false-positive and false-negative probabilities are f, g, then K = 1−f
                                                                       f 1−g has determinant
1 − f − g. Known invertible K identifies the true joint law algebraically; a nearly singular K
amplifies error. Unknown K is an additional identification problem requiring validation data,
repeated measurements or other restrictions. Correcting recorded receipt does not by itself
remove confounding of true receipt.
   For an exact example, let true receipt be randomized with probability 1/2, and let P (Y =
1 | A = 0) = 1/5 and P (Y = 1 | A = 1) = 4/5. Its causal contrast is 3/5. With symmetric
misclassification f = g = 1/5, the recorded conditional means are 8/25 and 17/25, so the
naive contrast is 9/25. Applying the known matrix inverse recovers 3/5. If f = g = 1/2, W
contains no information about A and the inverse does not exist. This is a finite version of the
operator/rank distinction in Chapter 4; more rows cannot restore lost rank.
   High-dimensional denoising can use additional structure. Agarwal and Singh (2022, Sections
3.2–3.3 and 4) studies corrupted covariates under approximate low-rank/repeated-measurement
structure, with a specified corruption model and inference that accounts for cleaning. The main
model uses covariates plus additive noise and masking; it does not cover arbitrary deterministic
rounding or arbitrary informative missingness. The scientific contribution is a joint restriction
on cleaning, target estimation and error rates. Applying PCA to any bank table and then
using an ordinary standard error is not that procedure.


11.5     Entity uncertainty and the unit of intervention
A household may own several customer identifiers, an SME may merge, and a branch portfolio
may transfer to another legal entity. The unit for assignment can therefore differ from the
unit for reporting and the unit over which interference occurs. A household-level promotion
analyzed as independent accounts can both misstate treatment versions and exaggerate sample
information. A stable identifier is not evidence of a stable economic unit across a merger.
114                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Let L denote a candidate linkage and θL the effect estimate or parameter under it. If a
justified joint probabilistic model supplies linkage weights, its posterior uncertainty satisfies

                   Var(θ | O) = E[Var(θ | O, L) | O] + Var(E[θ | O, L] | O).                (11.4)

The second term disappears when a most-likely linkage is treated as certain. This is the law of
total variance, not a guarantee that an arbitrary matcher’s confidence scores are calibrated
posterior weights. For example, two equally weighted linkage models with effect means 0 and 2
and conditional variance 1/4 give total variance 5/4. Reporting 1/4 misses the between-linkage
component.
   An alternative is sensitivity across a defensible set of linkages, returning a union of their
identified/estimated effect sets. This does not require invented posterior probabilities but
can be wide. Averaging linked rows first generally differs from averaging the resulting causal
functional because propensity scores, conditional laws and target weights are nonlinear. The
entity service should preserve uncertain links, historical validity and their effect on the target
population.


11.6      Which transformations preserve the scientific question?
A one-to-one covariate transformation preserves its sigma-field: σ(f (X)) = σ(X) when the
inverse is measurable. Conditional exchangeability and conditional expectations can then be
translated without losing information. A coarsening generally cannot. A special exception
is a balancing score under the assumptions derived in Section 3.6; arbitrary low-dimensional
embeddings do not enjoy that property.
   Outcome transformations also change the target. An effect on E[log Y ] is not the log of an
effect on E[Y ]. Portfolio sums, account averages and balance-weighted averages assign different
units and weights. In finance, a useful reward must reconcile interest margin, fees, credit losses,
funding cost, servicing cost and capital charges over the same intervention horizon. Internal
transfers can be a gain to one branch and no gain to the banking group. Accounting identities
should be retained as constraints, not supplied as independent variables to a faithfulness-based
discovery procedure.
   For example, if ending deposits equal starting deposits plus net flows, then the three variables
are deterministically related. Their covariance is singular and their independences need not
behave like a generic noisy DAG model. Choose primitive quantities or an explicit constrained
measurement model. Likewise, mechanically constructing an interest income variable as balance
times rate does not establish either economic causal direction from a discovered association.
   At large scale, an immutable analysis recipe can specify event/availability filters, revision
policy, entity map, action history, eligibility, outcome windows, units and observation indicators.
A generated query should be checked for future information, join multiplicity, unsupported
follow-up, unexpected missingness and reconciliation to source totals. Partitioning by enti-
ty/date and streaming score reductions can preserve this recipe; downsampling, aggressive
screening and global imputation can change the scientific information. Their consequences
must be tested separately from query execution time.


11.7      A finite candidate search with explicit abstention
An initial automatic organization operation can be specified without claiming to infer arbitrary
economic meaning. Let a candidate observation plan be c = (k, e, a, r, g, u): record key k,
11.7. A finite candidate search with explicit abstention                                       115


event and availability clocks e, a, revision relation r, aggregation g, and entity map/unit u.
The input includes a finite grammar C, raw versioned records, decision identifiers and times,
declared units, and constraints with their provenance. The grammar is itself part of the
scientific input. A method cannot recover an interpretation that the grammar excludes.
   The implemented reference grammar has two timestamp assignments, two record-key
hypotheses (source/record or source/entity/record), latest-version versus append semantics,
stock versus flow aggregation, and account versus a supplied candidate household map.
This gives 32 initial candidates. The engine tests key uniqueness, finite values, currency
compatibility, declared column roles, and any supplied chronology, revision-publication or
accounting constraints. For example, e ≤ a can distinguish two timestamp assignments only
if the analyst has declared that this feed records realized events before their publication.
Scheduled future events do not obey that restriction. An external closing-minus-opening
ledger identity can distinguish flow summation from a last stock only if that identity and its
independent measurement are actually supplied.
   For each surviving candidate and each requested decision time t, first keep versions with
a < t. Within its record identity, select the largest eligible version; then restrict its economic
date to the requested half-open interval [b, t). A correction moving an event outside the interval
must not resurrect the older version. Distinct decision identifiers and distinct events remain
distinct even when their amounts match. A flow is the sum of distinct eligible increments. A
stock is its latest eligible economic observation; component accounts at that instant can be
summed only under the supplied additive household interpretation. Missing support returns
a missing value, not a fabricated zero. The output retains the source/entity/record/version
identifiers of every selected term.
  Let Vc be this materialized view including units and lineage. Hard constraints define C0 ⊆ C.
A transparent inspection score is
                           X
                  s(c) =       1{candidate field j agrees with supplied hint j}.
                           j

Hints order inspection; they cannot eliminate a surviving material alternative. Partition the
survivors by equality of requested values, lineage, aggregation meaning and economic unit.
Return incompatible if none survive, accept the current requested view if one class remains, and
abstain from a unique view otherwise. Even accepted equality for the current decisions does
not identify a rule for unseen data. Changing the request can separate previously equivalent
plans.
   This construction has a simple conditional correctness statement. If the true plan belongs to
the grammar and every hard constraint is valid for it, that plan survives. If all surviving plans
agree on the required view, the accepted view equals its oracle counterpart. No probabilistic
calibration is needed for this implication. Incorrect metadata or an incomplete grammar
invalidates its premise. A large hint score cannot estimate the probability that those premises
are true. Under ambiguity, fit the scientific functional separately in each view and retain the
resulting sensitivity set; do not average the tables or treat hint scores as linkage probabilities.


11.7.1     An evaluation that reaches the effect estimate

The synthetic experiment fixes the oracle before constructing candidates. For 240 customers
draw independent standard-normal X, W , assign an offer with probability expit(.7X), and
generate Y = 20A + 30X + ϵ, ϵ ∼ N (0, 25). The predecision record contains X; a later revision
contains X + 2A and is unavailable at the decision. OLS on (1, A, X) estimates the constant
effect of 20 in this specified law. Using the eventual revision instead gives the population
116                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


equation Y = −40A + 30(X + 2A) + ϵ: the nominal cleaning choice changes the adjustment
variable into a treatment descendant.
   Across 300 repetitions, labeled revisions and the valid chronology case accept the oracle
view in every run, with effect RMSE about 0.68–0.69. Retrospective revision adjustment has
RMSE about 60. In the unlabeled aggregation case an earlier independent record W leaves
last-stock X and flow-sum X + W as materially different possibilities. In the linkage case
pairing two accounts changes the available confounder to their sum. Both cases abstain in
every run and retain the oracle. Forcing the top hint-ranked candidate gives RMSE 10.19 and
10.59, while the mean spread between alternative estimates is 9.77 and 10.13. Those spreads
are observation sensitivity, not confidence intervals.
   An accounting case has increments W and X −W , with an independently declared reconciled
total X. The constraint selects the flow plan in every run, with RMSE 0.70. The additional
total provides the distinguishing information; the algorithm did not discover it from column
names. Zero wrong acceptances among these fixtures is conditional evidence for this grammar
and generator. It does not establish population error rates for previously unseen bank feeds.
With zero errors in 300 trials, the two-sided 95% Wilson upper bound is about 1.27% for the
particular repeated experiment, not zero.
   The bounded search costs O(|C|RD) in a direct implementation with R records and D
decisions. Indexing by entity and availability time, caching common candidate projections
and expressing eligible-version selection in a columnar engine reduce repeated scans without
changing the semantics. Probabilistic record linkage is a separate extension requiring a
calibrated joint linkage/outcome model or an explicitly conservative linkage set. The practical
stopping point is a reproducible observation plan or a short list of decision-relevant alternatives
that an analyst can resolve with additional metadata or measurement.


11.8      Automation with a defensible stopping point
The data layer can propose schemas, map candidate variables, construct as-of joins, expose
revisions and generate reproducible views. It can identify an ambiguous action timestamp
or a proxy measured after the decision and explain which analysis is affected. It cannot
establish exclusion, exchangeability, missing-at-random or a unique household definition solely
from column names. Those inputs belong to the scientific model and may remain alternative
hypotheses.
   The output is consequently more than a clean matrix: it is a defined population and
observation law, an analysis view with provenance, and explicit unresolved measurement or
linkage alternatives. Passing that object to discovery, longitudinal estimation or state-space
fitting preserves the connection between the bank’s intervention and the numbers ultimately
reported.


11.9      Generating observation hypotheses and asking useful ques-
          tions
The preceding finite grammar supplies an exact conditional reconstruction operation. A
reusable product must also explain where candidates come from. The new profiler extracts
datetime columns as possible clocks, string columns as possible identifiers, small nonnegative
integer fields as possible versions, and finite floating fields as possible values. Candidate entity
fields must contain the supplied decision-unit identifiers. The search forms record keys of up to
11.10. Linkage as a measurement model with audit uncertainty                                       117


two additional fields, pairs event and availability clocks, and combines version, append/latest
and stock/flow alternatives. These are type and membership hypotheses; economic meaning is
not inferred from the arbitrary column names.
   For decision cutoff c, a latest-version plan first restricts records to availability strictly before
c, then selects the last eligible revision within its record identity, then applies the event-time
window. This order matters when a correction changes the event timestamp. A stock plan
selects the latest event instant and rejects multiple conflicting stock values; a flow plan sums
its eligible records. Chronology tevent ≤ tavailable is imposed only for a feed explicitly declared
to contain realized events. A scheduled future contract can validly be known earlier, so the
same inequality is not a universal cleaning rule. Unique revision identity, supplied semantic
facts and supported search bounds determine rejection. Empty survivors mean incompatibility
within this candidate language; they do not certify that no correct interpretation exists.
  Let C be surviving plans and θc the downstream diagnostic effect computed under plan c.
A semantic question q partitions candidates by possible answer a. The implemented choice
minimizes
                                 max{ max θc − min θc },
                                       a   c∈Cq,a      c∈Cq,a

then the worst remaining number of material views. With no justified probability over
interpretations this is a minimax ambiguity criterion, not expected information gain. A trusted
answer filters the candidates; the algorithm never supplies its own answer from the ranking.
Using outcomes to prioritize questions is exploratory. If the resulting choice changes the final
statistical analysis, inference must account for that selection or use independent metadata/pilot
information. Small effect spread today does not prove semantic equivalence under future
decisions or populations.


11.9.1     Conditional correctness and missing interpretations

Suppose a correct plan c⋆ is generated, all hard constraints and analyst answers are true
of it, and accepted plans agree on the requested material observation. Then c⋆ survives
every filtering step and the accepted observation equals its projection. This induction proves
the conditional correctness claim. It does not prove candidate inclusion, answer truth or
population-level semantic recovery. Consequently the workflow records proposed hypotheses,
supplied facts, rejected reasons and unresolved views independently. A contradiction triggers
a new candidate/search request; it must not silently promote the highest-ranked survivor.
   The test fixtures rename and reorder every field, include future revisions, and vary stock/flow
interpretation and alternative value roles. Across 80 repetitions in each supported case, the
oracle observation survives and is resolved without wrong acceptance. One oracle-supplied
answer resolves stock and flow cases; two resolve the value-role ambiguity. An intentionally
unrepresented three-field record key yields incompatibility in every run, with no false acceptance.
These are synthetic heterogeneous schemas with trusted fixture answers, not measured analyst
accuracy or burden in a bank. The downstream adjusted-effect spread determines question
priority, while the answer’s provenance remains the actual source of semantic resolution.


11.10       Linkage as a measurement model with audit uncertainty
A resolved table schema does not guarantee the correct customer is linked. For a transparent
randomized example let A ∼ Bernoulli(1/2), Y = τ A + ϵ, and let Ye = (1 − M )Y + M Y ′ with
M ∼ Bernoulli(α) independent of (A, Y, Y ′ ). The replacement Y ′ is independent of the current
treatment and has the same marginal outcome distribution. The known-randomization score
118                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


is Z = 2(2A − 1)Ye . Then

                              E[Z] = (1 − α)τ,      τ̂ = Z̄/(1 − α̂).

The replacement contribution is zero because E[2(2A − 1)Y ′ ] = 0. With an independent
truthful audit of Mv links, the first-order expansion is

                           Z̄ − (1 − α)τ    τ
                τ̂ − τ =                 +     (α̂ − α) + op (N −1/2 + Mv−1/2 ),
                               1−α         1−α
and its variance is
                                     Var(Z)     τ 2 α(1 − α)
                                              +              .                                (11.5)
                                    N (1 − α)2 Mv (1 − α)2
Plugging Z̄ into the second term gives the implemented Z̄ 2 α̂(1 − α̂)/{Mv (1 − α̂)4 }. An
overlapping audit would add cross covariance. Near α = 1, the denominator is weak and
a normal ratio interval is inappropriate. This special attenuation calculation is a project
construction; the broader linked-data causal analysis requires conditional mismatch and
independent truthful-audit restrictions (Slawski, 2025, Assumptions A1–A5). A generic fuzzy-
match confidence score is not an estimate of this α.
   With N = 3, 000, Mv = 80, α = .2 and true effect eight, 400 repetitions give naive bias
−1.5923 and zero nominal 95% coverage. Joint audit correction gives bias .0337 and .955
coverage. Treating the estimated audit rate as fixed gives .615 coverage. A biased audit drawn
from links with mismatch rate .05 gives bias −1.2519 and .015 coverage despite retaining its
sampling variance. Propagating uncertainty is necessary; a biased measurement model remains
biased after propagation.
  For richer entity resolution, preserve a distribution or set of plausible link assignments
together with its calibration source. Averaging causal estimates over match weights is justified
only by a coherent joint linkage and outcome/assignment model; conditioning on a match
chosen using outcome information can introduce selection. The product should offer either
a qualified audited correction, sensitivity over linkage laws, or separate candidate analyses
with unresolved status. The synthetic audit calculation shows why exporting a single hard
customer ID and discarding the matching evidence is not an adequate scientific interface.


11.11      Conflicting source meaning and calibrated candidate
           histories
Consider a deposit feed with business date, warehouse arrival date and revision number, plus
a separate account/customer ownership table. A row for business day 10 may arrive on day
20, after the day-15 decision. A business-date filter then exposes a revision unavailable to the
decision maker. Joint ownership creates another ambiguity: copying an account balance to
both owners changes the economic unit and can double exposure. These are observation-model
questions before any causal estimator is called.
   Five source-owner fixtures are specified separately from the interpretation code. A current
trusted arrival-clock statement excludes the late revision and gives balance 90. Conflicting
trusted arrival/business-clock statements retain balances 90 and 110; missing clock documenta-
tion does the same. A customer request with two joint owners and no allocation rule abstains.
Finally, a plausible but incorrect accepted migration specification yields the unique wrong
balance 110. The algorithm reports conditional acceptance in that case, and the external
fixture evaluation records wrong acceptance. The result is not hidden by defining every supplied
answer as correct.
11.11. Conflicting source meaning and calibrated candidate histories                          119


   Verified provenance means that the stated owner supplied the assertion, not that the
assertion’s economic meaning is true. Schema profiles can generate candidate clocks and entity
relations; they cannot establish first availability or ownership allocation by themselves. An
analyst question must therefore request the missing semantic fact and identify its source. If
pilot outcomes rank useful questions, the ranking and answers are frozen before final evaluation.
The executed final linkage experiment below uses predeclared strata and independent audit
information, with no final-outcome question selection.


11.11.1     Whole candidate maps and a recoverable mixture

A scalar replacement rate is inadequate when plausible candidate entities have different
responses. Use two candidate portfolio histories at each origin, with the entire response
vector assigned consistently under each map. In linkage stratum s, the two histories are
correctly ordered with probability ps and swapped otherwise. This is a one-to-one pair
assignment, not independent per-column linking. The match event is independent of the
complete potential histories conditional on the declared stratum and matching information.
That strong noninformative-linkage restriction is part of identification; a name-match score
is not evidence for it. The executed map is redrawn by origin, while retaining all horizons
within that origin together. It models an independently reconstructed candidate window,
not a persistent customer alias across the entire calendar. A fixed erroneous crosswalk or
time-dependent matching mechanism would need its own joint map law and covariance; the
following evidence does not qualify them.
  Let θsA , θsB be the true response vectors of the two portfolios to the same price innovation.
The two observable candidate response vectors satisfy
                      !                       !     !
                ηs1             ps   1 − ps       θsA             ps ηs1 − (1 − ps )ηs2
                          =                           ,   θsA =                         .   (11.6)
                ηs2           1 − ps   ps         θsB                    2ps − 1

This corrects two different candidate responses rather than assuming every wrong entity has
zero effect. An independently audited set of pair matches estimates each ps . At ps = 1/2 the
matrix has rank one: these mean equations identify only the sum of the two responses. In
the symmetric pair-swap observation law, exchanging portfolio labels preserves the observed
law; more unlabelled histories cannot resolve that named-portfolio ambiguity. Higher mixture
moments under additional restrictions could still identify more than these mean equations do.
If probabilities are not calibrated, plausible maps produce a set of targets, not a probability-
weighted point estimate justified by convenience.
  The funding experiment fits candidate conditional means separately by stratum using
an independent pilot and the prespecified driver basis. The potentially misassigned lagged
balance is excluded from this basis. Under the stationary Gaussian driver law, conditional
means of every past driver and its centered square given the current driver are linear and
quadratic, respectively. Summing the stable balance recursion therefore keeps the candidate
outcome means in the driver basis after that lagged balance is marginalized. This justification
depends on the stated law; it does not license dropping a confounding history in a new
bank dataset. Treatment residuals, candidate outcomes and stratum indicators produce the
candidate response moments. The conditional mean of treatment does not depend on stratum,
but allowing stratum interactions in its learner preserves the common nuisance interface.
Estimating candidate outcomes with one pooled stratum mean could destroy the orthogonality
needed for stratum-specific inference; the executed design retains those interactions.

The calibration term is a matrix outer product: a single map probability affects the entire
response curve. Both T and Ms must grow in the regular joint-sample approximation; a fixed
small audit is not washed out by arbitrarily many production records. Bias in the audit changes
the inverse map itself. Covariance correction cannot remove that bias. If the Wilson audit
interval contains 1/2, the regular reference withholds the regular inverse-map interval. This
is an explicit availability rule, not a claim of uniform post-selection coverage. Section 11.12
supplies a separate projection procedure that retains unbounded and disconnected financial
confidence sets near rank failure. It does not extend this delta approximation by changing its
label.
   In the registered experiment p0 = .95, p1 = .8, the true second-portfolio price coefficient
is .5 rather than the focal portfolio’s 2, and both histories share common shocks. With 720

financial coverage is .9625; at 400 audits it is .950. Treating calibration as fixed gives .960 and

modest relative to the calendar noise in this design. The naive first-candidate analysis has bias
about −68,000 and −80,000 currency units in the two runs, with coverage .900 and .9075. The
correctly mapped financial target is about 375,149 under the fixed accounting inputs. These
wide intervals are evidence about a difficult dynamic observation problem, not a promised
precise business case.
   This construction is a bounded project derivation. Audit-based mismatch correction provides
one related approach (Slawski, 2025); joint probabilistic linkage and causal modeling offers a
different route (Guha et al., 2022) when a well-specified joint likelihood and linking covariates
are defensible. Such a joint model may let outcomes inform linkage. Its posterior target and
feedback assumptions differ from this independent-audit frequentist experiment; posterior
match draws cannot simply be treated as additional independent customers. The product
records the selected mapping law, audit population, covariance and unresolved semantic
alternatives together.
   The publisher version of Guha et al. (2022, Section 2.3, equation (2.4)) models a constrained
one-to-one map z, agreement fields and outcome regressions jointly. The linked-record likelihood
includes f1 (yi | xj , aj ); unlinked outcomes have f2 (yi ). Thus the posterior odds of a map
contain the outcome likelihood ratio as well as field agreement. Section 2.1 requires strong
treatment ignorability and positivity; the model cannot repair hidden action confounding by
better linkage. The journal version explicitly separates linking variables from causal covariates
and discusses conditioning/altering the likelihood when they overlap. Its linked-population
treatment effect and within-file no-duplicates assumption differ from a repeated banking history
with joint ownership. These differences are why a production adapter must represent the map
law and target population, rather than passing arbitrary posterior links into an otherwise
unchanged temporal estimator.

11.12       Weak linkage identification is a financial inverse problem
The inability to distinguish two candidate histories is structurally related to a weak instrument.
In Equation (11.6), the eigenvalues of the assignment matrix are 1 and rs = 2ps − 1. The
portfolio sum survives even when the difference is unidentified. A Wilson interval containing 1/2
usefully stops the regular inverse, but that screening rule does not construct an identification-
robust confidence set. Nor does a large number of production dates create audit information.
The relevant analogy with Section 2.4 is to build uncertainty for observable quantities before
dividing by an uncertain identification coefficient (Staiger and Stock, 1994, Section 2D, Theorem
3).
  Use the fixed financial coefficient vector k from Equation (9.14), including the cost of paying
the higher first-month rate on induced balances. Within stratum s, define
                                                         ms1 + ms2               ms1 − ms2
              ms1 = k ′ ηs1 ,   ms2 = k ′ ηs2 ,   Ss =             ,    Ds =               .
                                                             2                       2
Let vsA = k ′ θsA and vsB = k ′ θsB . Adding and subtracting the two mixing equations gives
                            vsA + vsB                    vsA − vsB
                     Ss =             ,       Ds = rs              = rs (vsA − Ss ).           (11.8)
                                2                            2
Thus vsA = Ss + Ds /rs for rs ̸= 0. At rs = 0, the observable restriction in these mean
equations is Ds = 0 and vsA is unrestricted by them because vsB can compensate. The final
funding value is V = s ws vsA − C, with fixed ws = 1/2 and C = N crB0 . These are monetary
                     P

contrasts before the common fixed price cost is subtracted; no balance stock is reinterpreted
as a flow.
   This is an inverse problem for response moments. It is not a claim that every value is
compatible with every feature of the full observed mixture distribution. At p = 1/2, conditional
on an action/history, that distribution has the symmetric form {P (YA , YB ) + P (YB , YA )}/2.
Exchanging the two named portfolio laws preserves it, so focal identity can remain ambiguous.
Additional distributional restrictions may nevertheless identify unordered components or their
separation and produce a smaller set than the mean equations permit. The procedure below
constructs a conservative outer confidence set without using those restrictions; it does not
compute the sharp identified set of a fully specified mixture. Its independent audit supplies
correctness counts only. Audited action/outcome histories could directly inform portfolio
responses and would define a richer experiment.

11.12.2     Projection, coverage and the shape of the result

Let R be the Cartesian product of the four observable bands and the two audit intervals. For
each stratum construct

                  Vs = {v : ∃S ∈ ISs , D ∈ IDs , p ∈ Ps , D = (2p − 1)(v − S)},
                                  !
                         X
                  V=          ws Vs − C.                                                       (11.11)
                          s

The sum denotes all sums of one element from each set, not the sum of arbitrarily selected
endpoints. On the event that all primitive quantities lie in R, the true vsA satisfy the displayed
equations, including at ps = 1/2. Hence the true V lies in V on that same event. The union
bound gives
                                 P {V ∈ V} ≥ 1 − α + o(1).
This is a project coverage argument, not a new theorem attributed to the linkage paper or a
direct application of the Gaussian Anderson–Rubin test. The audit region is finite-sample valid;
the response region remains asymptotic. Projection itself needs no lower bound on |2ps − 1|. A
uniform claim over a sequence of linkage probabilities additionally requires uniform validity of
the primitive response bands along that sequence. Pointwise CLTs cannot establish that claim
by renaming the result. The distinction between a finite normal experiment and an asymptotic
approximation is also explicit in Rambachan and Roth (2023, Section 2.5, equations (9)–(11)).
   There is a complete scalar algorithm without a bounded effect grid. Write IS = [a, b],
ID = [c, d] and R = [2L − 1, 2U − 1]. On each positive or negative part of R, the extrema
of D/r are its four rectangle corners, with signed infinite limits at zero. Add [a, b], retain
both sign components, and merge only overlapping closed intervals. If 0 ∈ R and 0 ∈ ID ,
11.12. Weak linkage identification is a financial inverse problem                              123


the rank-one equation permits every real v, so return R. If R = {0} and 0 ∈ / ID , return the
empty set: that primitive region is incompatible with the model. Weighted interval sums
then produce Equation (11.11). This finite interval arithmetic preserves unbounded rays and
disconnected components.
  For example, S = 1.5, D = .5 and p ∈ [.4, .6] give

                                     Vs = (−∞, −1] ∪ [4, ∞).

Neither a finite interval joining plotted points nor a selected positive branch describes this
information. As an independent check on the algorithm, fix a candidate v and ask whether the
rectangle image {r(v − S) : r ∈ R, S ∈ [a, b]} intersects [c, d]. Its endpoints are four products,
so this test uses no ratio. The executed 16,800 comparisons agree, including exactly singular
regions, and a finite enumeration over all binomial counts for sizes 1–25 and 201 probability
values gives minimum audit coverage .95096 for nominal .95. These checks validate finite
identities; they are not a proof of the calendar CLT.


11.12.3     Precision, alternatives and the bank’s next decision

A second valid projection uses separate bands for (ms1 , ms2 ) and the original inverse map. It
ignores much of their correlation when forming a rectangle. The sum/difference construction
uses that covariance before forming bands: a common monetary shock cancels from the
difference, while uncertainty in the sum need not be amplified by 1/|2p−1|. Neither rectangular
construction is uniformly shorter for every covariance law. The registered comparison therefore
evaluates both on the same draws, alongside the regular delta interval and its availability rule.
   A joint ellipsoidal response region could exploit further covariance but requires reliable
constrained projection, including unbounded directions. Alternatively, for proposed (v, p) one
can test D b − (2p − 1)(v − S)
                             b using its candidate-specific covariance and combine the audit
evidence before eliminating p. Its variance includes VDD + (2p − 1)2 VSS + 2(2p − 1)VSD ; using
a fixed variance at a fitted inverse would recreate the weak-normalization error. A justified
joint test could improve power, but its critical value, nuisance elimination and degenerate cases
require a separate derivation. The selected rectangle projection buys transparent coverage and
exact topology at the cost of conservatism. A joint Bayesian linkage/outcome model (Guha
et al., 2022) instead uses a different likelihood, feedback and prior restriction; its posterior is
not this confidence set.
   The five-regime funding comparison uses 720 evaluation dates, an independent 2,880-date
nuisance pilot and 200 independent audits per stratum, with 400 repetitions in each regime.
Its true financial value is about 375,149 currency units. The response law, target and error
allocation remain fixed while the mapping probabilities change.

   Projection covers the retained truth in all 400 draws in every regime; a 95% binomial Monte

two, only one covering truth. Those conditional denominators cannot justify promoting the
screened interval to inference robust to weak linkage.

justified lower bound on mapping accuracy excludes 1/2, it changes the admissible model and
may recover a bounded result. More representative correctness-count audits can resolve a
genuinely nonzero rs , but cannot invert these mean equations when ps is exactly 1/2. In that
case stronger identifiers, an additional measurement, or a changed economic target such as
the portfolio sum is required. Mislabelled audits, selected audits and a persistent crosswalk
outside the declared per-origin map law require different observation models. High coverage
obtained by returning R is honest lack of information, not a useful investment case or evidence
of universal causal inference.


11.13      Persistent customer identities and the price of new in-
           formation
A correctness count is not the same observation as an audited customer history. Suppose a
deposit team sees two candidate balance histories for each customer pair. A fixed alias can
swap these histories for every month. Adding months then adds outcome information but
no independent evidence about which customer is which. If the probability of the correct
map is one half, the preceding mean equations identify the pair’s total response and leave its
allocation unrestricted. Neither an inverse regularization nor a larger sample of correctness
counts changes that algebra.
  Consider instead a declared population of independent pairs, indexed by i = 1, . . . , n,
with a fixed follow-up length H. The focal customer has randomized actions Ait ∈ {−1, 1},

Suppose an audited label Li flips Mi with a known independent symmetric probability e < 1/2.

The error rate must be identified by a separate gold-standard design. Two uncertain assertions

11.13.2     A reproducible deposit decision

The synthetic experiment has 800 independent pairs, eight dates, focal population response 1.2
and companion response −0.4. A pair’s focal slope also depends on a balanced binary feature
and a random slope; its map is fixed and has correctness probability one half. Audit inclusion
is qi = q(1 + 0.5Xi ) for Xi ∈ {−1, 1}. The nominal q values are 0.1, 0.3, 0.6. A unit response is
worth 1,000 currency units in the declared fixed account, so the synthetic focal truth is 1,200.
It is not a measured deposit return for any bank.
   Across 2,000 independent repetitions in each design, the augmented intervals cover in 1,895,
1,895 and 1,894 draws respectively. Their mean monetary widths are 413.27, 247.81 and 184.36.
The corresponding 95% Monte Carlo interval for the first coverage frequency is [.9368, .9569].
With 15% symmetric label errors and the correct externally supplied error rate, coverage is
126                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


1905/2000 = .9525 and mean width is 344.21. Falsely supplying the original inclusion law
when actual inclusion also depends on the feature reduces coverage to 82/2000 = .041. This is
evidence against ignoring audit selection, not a limitation repaired by increasing the number
of dates.
  The richer audit design therefore supplies useful information in a case where correctness
counts and mean mixing alone do not. It does so by observing the missing map and outcomes,
not by extracting an identified contrast from the old singular equations. Many-to-many
ownership still needs an allocation target, and an unknown selected audit still needs a sampling
model. A source owner’s false semantic assertion can remain observationally undetectable. The
operation preserves that boundary and rejects a proposed combination with common-calendar
funding uncertainty until a joint sampling argument has been supplied.


11.14       Using covariance without hiding singular identification
The rectangular confidence construction is transparent but discards response covariance when
forming the financial set. A joint region can exploit that covariance while retaining the same
identification restrictions. Write the four monetary response coordinates as x = (s0 , d0 , s1 , d1 )′ ,
with candidate average sj and half-difference dj in stratum j. Let m estimate x and let V
estimate its covariance. Assume a fixed full-rank four-dimensional response limit and consistent
V . Allocate half of error probability α to the ellipsoid

                     E = {x : (x − m)′ V −1 (x − m) ≤ k},          k = χ24,1−α/2 ,

and error α/4 to each of the two exact binomial audit intervals. Finite-sample exactness of the
audit region does not turn a fitted calendar response ellipsoid into an exact finite-sample pivot.
   At fixed nonzero ranks rj = 2pj − 1, the focal financial contribution is c(r)′ x − K, where K
is the fixed direct cost and

11.14.1     A global calculation over audit uncertainty

If neither audit interval contains one half, each reciprocal rank 1/rj ranges over a compact
interval. Their product is a rectangle. The upper support function U is convex in these
reciprocal coordinates because it is the sum of a linear function and a norm; L is concave. Every
point in a rectangle is a convex combination of its vertices. Convexity gives U (u) ≤ maxv U (v)
and concavity gives L(u) ≥ minv L(v). Consequently the four corners give the global enclosing
interval. No local optimizer or finite effect grid can silently remove a tail.
   When an audit interval touches one half, the implementation conservatively retains the
whole line. Some such cases admit a sharper disconnected result; the original rectangle routine
retains those rays and remains a challenger. The ellipsoid implementation does not claim
sharpness in this case. A singular empirical response covariance also receives a declared
11.14. Using covariance without hiding singular identification                                127


conservative fallback, rather than a pseudoinverse labelled as a four-dimensional confidence
pivot. Special-function inversions and endpoint rounding use ordinary floating-point arithmetic.
The global geometric argument is exact; a certified bound on floating-point error has not been
supplied.
   If the true response is in E and both true audit probabilities are in their intervals, the
true financial contribution belongs to the projected set. The union bound therefore gives
asymptotic coverage at least 1 − α under the stated response approximation, without a lower
bound on linkage rank. The set can be valid and financially uninformative.


11.14.2     What the comparisons diagnose

The preserved 400-draw strong-calendar design permits a retrospective comparison because
each draw retains all four means and their covariance. The median bounded width falls from
1,498,486.81 for the rectangle to 1,202,977.31 for the ellipsoid; coverage is 400/400 and 399/400.
Moderate and reversed designs also have smaller median bounded widths in this comparison.
Every retained weak and singular ellipsoid remains the whole line. These observations do not
establish uniform dominance or confirmatory calibration on newly selected calendar data.
   The regular strong-design interval covers 370/400 = .925. Supplying the true audit probabil-
ities gives 372/400 = .930, and using the oracle first-order linearization gives 371/400 = .9275.
Thus estimated audit probabilities alone do not explain the failure; the response approximation
and its finite sample behavior remain important. These arms identify contributors, not a
unique causal diagnosis of the coverage error. With freshly simulated Gaussian primitive
responses of known covariance, strong-design regular coverage is 1920/2000 = .960, while both
conservative projection constructions cover all 2,000 draws. That primitive experiment isolates
geometry from the original calendar covariance estimation; it cannot retrospectively validate
the latter.
   The practical alternatives are consequently clear. Use the original rectangle when preserving
disconnected topology matters; use the registered ellipsoid when covariance is well qualified
and its outer interval is suitable; retain the regular calculation as a disclosed research route;
or purchase the outcome-linked information in Section 11.13. None may be selected after
observing which produces the narrowest favorable answer.
Chapter 12

Continuous time, observation events
and structural dynamics

A credit line can change on a decision date, a payment can arrive at any instant, and a financial
statement can be entered weeks after the period it describes. Putting all three on a monthly
grid is a modeling choice. The event clock in Chapter 5 must extend to continuous time
without confusing a changing customer state, the times at which the bank observes it, and the
times at which the bank acts.


12.1      A process equation acquires causality through modular
          interventions
On a finite horizon [0, T ], consider the structural diffusion

                     dXt = b(Xt , At , t) dt + Σ(Xt , At , t) dWt ,   X0 ∼ P0 .            (12.1)

Here Xt is the scientific state, At a predictable action, and Wt an exogenous Brownian motion
independent of the initial state. A specified joint noise law, nonanticipating coefficients,
and existence and uniqueness under the proposed actions are part of the model. Global
Lipschitz and linear-growth conditions supply a familiar sufficient well-posedness route. The
causal assertion is that replacing the mechanism for A leaves the other structural mechanisms
and exogenous law invariant. A fitted conditional drift without that assertion describes
observational dynamics.
   A deterministic intervention can specify the whole action path a(t). A feedback intervention
specifies a predictable rule using information available immediately before t. A jump in an
account limit, a continuing rate incentive, and a continuously clamped balance are different
interventions even if their observed values agree at one instant. Intervening on an accounting
total may require an operational action that changes several underlying flows. The mathematical
substitution must have a feasible banking interpretation.
   A dynamic SCM treats each coordinate’s entire path as a random element. This allows
feedback between processes while excluding dependence on their future realizations. Boeken
and Mooij (2024, Definitions 4–7 and Sections 4–5) develops this path-space connection and
defines time splitting and subsampling. The later Boeken and Mooij (2026, Definitions 3–5
and Theorems 3, 5–6) distinguishes essential unique solvability for every subsystem, preserving
it under marginalization. These conditions give well-defined causal laws; they are not inferred
from a low prediction error.

                                                  128
12.2. Exact sampling and an observational alias                                                      129


   The distinction between a graphical Markov property and intervention calculus matters
here. The 2026 source proves a σ-separation Markov property under its general solvability
conditions and a stronger d-separation property for its specified additive-noise class. Its
Theorem 12 establishes the σ-separation do-calculus, with absolute-continuity conditions for
the relevant conditional laws. It explicitly does not deduce the cyclic d-separation do-calculus
from the stronger Markov property; that extension is conjectural in the archived text. An
implementation may therefore not replace every path-space separation test by an ordinary
DAG routine. On acyclic graphs the two separations coincide.

12.3      Equilibrium and an intervention on a feedback rule
The steady balance response to a bank’s pricing rule differs from its response to a clamped
offered rate. For a small illustrative model, let x denote scaled deposits and r a rate deviation:
                  ẋ = −x + br + u,         ṙ = −κ(r − r0 + cx),           b, c, κ > 0.
The customer disturbance u is constant for a trajectory. The bank lowers its incentive as
deposits increase; r0 is the intercept of that rule. The system matrix has negative trace −(1+κ)
and positive determinant κ(1 + bc), so it converges to its unique equilibrium:
                                       br0 + u
                                x∗ =           ,      r∗ = r0 − cx∗ .
                                        1 + bc
Changing the rule intercept has derivative ∂x∗ /∂r0 = b/(1 + bc). Fixing r(t) = r̄ removes
its feedback equation and instead yields x∗ = br̄ + u, with derivative b. If only u varies
across observed equilibria while r0 is fixed, the observational slope of x∗ on r∗ is −1/c. A
negative fitted rate–balance relation is compatible with a positive structural rate response in
this specified model.
   This calculation requires convergence under the relevant intervention. Setting derivatives
to zero gives candidate equilibrium equations; it does not establish that actual paths reach
them. Bongers et al. (2022, Definition 4.9, Theorems 4.11 and 4.18) formalizes equilibration
and its commutation with steady interventions under the stated convergence conditions.
Nonconverging paths, multiple solutions, and selection of only equilibrated units need separate
analysis. A stationary diffusion generally fluctuates forever: an invariant distribution is not a
pathwise equilibrium obtained by setting Brownian forcing to zero.
   A bank action can also change competitors’ responses and market clearing. The example
exposes the feedback distinction but is not a model of an entire banking market. A portfolio
calculation holding competitor rates fixed and a market equilibrium counterfactual must be
different product requests, with different maintained mechanisms.

these adherence weights reduce to products of inverse action probabilities.
   This does not make an arbitrary deterministic event path supported by a continuous clock.
The source distinguishes its regime-specific g-formula distributions from the larger class of
measures obtained by changing compensators while preserving other local laws (Ryalen et al.,
2026, Definition 5, Remark 2 and Theorem 2). The routes encode different intervention
classes and premises. A product must state which one justifies a request, rather than attach
continuous-time g-formula to any hazard model.

that contract. Their numerical success must remain separate from evidence for its structural
assumptions.
Chapter 13

Learning decisions and designing
their evidence

An estimated causal response is an input to a decision problem. The bank must specify which
decisions it can change, which resources they consume and whose value is averaged. Selecting
a policy also changes the statistical problem: the selected rule is random, and its empirical
value benefits from the same noise that made it win.

controls, the regret has the familiar VC(Π)/n scale, with the score-variance and logarithmic
factors in the theorem. The source permits approximate maximization with its objective gap
o(n−1/2 ). These conditions cannot be replaced by ordinary ATE consistency. In particular,
weak-IV weights violate its bounded representer requirement, and arbitrary dependent panel
rows do not satisfy its sampling model.


13.2      Evaluation after policy selection
One defensible design uses separate samples for nuisance learning, policy selection and final
evaluation. Conditional on the first two, the selected rule is fixed for the last sample; its
fixed-policy gradient can be used subject to that sample’s nuisance-rate and dependence
conditions. Cross-fitting can improve data use, but every observation’s roles must remain
explicit. Training a policy on all customers and then cross-fitting only the outcome regressions
does not make the policy independent of their outcomes.
   For a prespecified finite class, simultaneous value intervals offer another route. If P (∀π ∈
Π : G(π) ∈ Iπ ) ≥ 1 − α, the interval indexed by any data-selected member covers on that same
event. A valid joint multiplier or a conservative allocation of error probabilities can construct
such intervals under their respective sampling assumptions. Repeatedly choosing subgroups,
outcomes and horizons enlarges the family beyond the final policy names. A lower confidence
bound on improvement is a possible deployment criterion; it is a decision rule with a specified
loss of power, not an unbiased estimate of the selected maximum.
   The same distinction applies to POMDP planning. Maximizing value over an estimated
transition model adds an optimization layer to parameter and identification uncertainty. A
small Bellman residual certifies numerical accuracy inside that model; it does not certify the
out-of-sample value of its selected policy.

validity after selecting any outcome, subgroup or policy. For delayed defaults, revealing only

13.4      Clusters and interference are part of the design
A branch rollout or household pricing action can affect several accounts. Let independent
clusters be indexed by c, with account outcomes Yci (ac ). Partial interference means another
cluster’s assignment does not affect this outcome. An exposure mapping further assumes
Yci (ac ) = Yci (aci , sci (ac,−i )), where s might be the fraction of neighbors offered the product.
This mapping is a restriction on spillovers, not a fact inferred from account identifiers. Defining
the intervention unit and interference is a prerequisite to consistency (Hernán and Robins,
2020, Fine Point 1.1).
  For a finite population of N accounts and a known randomization design, let pci (a, s) > 0
be each account’s exposure probability. Then the design-based estimator

                                          1 X 1{Aci = a, Sci = s}Yci
                              µ
                              b(a, s) =
                                          N c,i     pci (a, s)

is unbiased for N −1 c,i Yci (a, s): for each account, the indicator’s expectation cancels its
                       P

exposure probability. This project derivation says exactly which mean is recovered. Its
variance depends on joint exposure probabilities; accounts sharing a branch are not independent
replicates. Equal branch weights instead target an average branch, which differs from the
account mean when branch size and effects covary.
  If the entire branch is assigned together, exposures (1, 1) and (0, 0) may occur while (1, 0)
and (0, 1) never do. The rollout identifies their bundled contrast but cannot separately identify
individual and spillover effects. More accounts within the same branches do not create the
missing variation. A two-stage design that randomizes branch saturation and then accounts
can supply additional exposures at an explicit operational cost.
   An exact randomization test also requires a stated null. Under the sharp null Yci (ac ) is
identical for every assignment, all missing potential outcomes can be filled with observed values.
Recomputing a statistic over the known randomization distribution then gives a valid tail
probability by that distribution itself. A zero average-effect null does not impute all potential
outcomes; the same exact-null proof does not apply to it. Spillovers across branches or through
shared market prices further invalidate the partial-interference design and require a broader
network or equilibrium model.
  The resulting evidence contract must distinguish a fixed-policy interval, a uniform class
bound, a time-uniform sequence, and a randomization test. Their probability statements
quantify over different objects. A generic field named “confidence” cannot preserve the
guarantee needed by a decision maker.
Chapter 14

Transport, invariance and sensitivity
across bank environments

A shared library can reproduce an estimator in another repository without making its original
causal answer valid in another market. Product eligibility, customer composition, competitive
responses and measurement systems can all change. The relevant question is which parts of a
causal model remain invariant, and which target-domain information can replace the parts
that do not.


14.1     Selection diagrams encode changes of mechanism
Let P describe a source environment and P ∗ a target environment. A selection diagram adds
a node Sj → Vj wherever the mechanism or exogenous distribution generating Vj may differ.
These nodes mark permitted differences; they are not necessarily record-inclusion indicators
or measured causes in a pooled dataset. The absence of Sj → Vj is a substantive invariance
assertion. Transportability asks whether the target causal law is uniquely determined by the
available source observational/experimental laws, the target observational law and this shared
model class (Pearl and Bareinboim, 2014, Definitions 4–5).
   Suppose the only population difference is in a pretreatment covariate X, and X separates
Y from the selection nodes in the graph with incoming arrows to A removed. The conditional
intervention response is then invariant by the first rule of do-calculus. Averaging it over the
target population gives
                                              Z
                           p∗ (y | do(a)) =       p(y | do(a), x) dP ∗ (x).               (14.1)

This is the pretreatment S-admissibility result in Pearl and Bareinboim (2014, Theorem 2
and Corollary 1). The right side needs a source experiment or a justified source identification
route, and source support at target covariates. The intervention and outcome must also have
the same meaning in both places.
   For a project calculation in currency units, let the causal offer effect be τ (x) = 10 + 20x
for binary X. If P (X = 1) = .2 in the pilot and P ∗ (X = 1) = .8 in the intended rollout, the
average effects are 14 and 26. Reusing the pilot average confuses composition with causal
response. The transport formula recovers 26 by using the invariant conditional effects and the
new composition.
   Reweighting every variable with a different distribution is not justified. Suppose instead U
is a stable fair binary effect modifier with τ (U ) = 10 + 20U , and the observed proxy Z equals

                                                  138
14.2. A transported mean has two sources of statistical error                                   139


U at the source. In the target, let P ∗ (Z = 1 | U = 1) = 1 and P ∗ (Z = 1 | U = 0) = .6. The
population effect remains 20 because P ∗ (U ) = P (U ). Yet weighting source proxy-specific effects
(10, 30) by the target proxy prevalence .8 gives 26. The relevant diagram has S → Z ← U → Y ;
conditioning on Z connects the environment to the outcome mechanism through the latent
modifier. This finite example reconstructs the distinction between a population shift and a
proxy-measurement shift in Pearl and Bareinboim (2014, Section 3, Examples 1–2).
   If the changing variable is a mediator, its target distribution must generally be taken under
the intervention, p∗ (m | do(a)), not its observed margin p∗ (m). If the response mechanism
itself changes, no reweighting of source covariates alone removes that change. General transport
may combine several source experiments and target kernels. The source’s do-calculus reduction
explains how such a formula can be justified; the simple admissibility criterion is not a complete
transport algorithm for every diagram.


14.2      A transported mean has two sources of statistical error
For a concrete sampling model, observe independent draws from a pooled population. Let
S = 1 denote a source trial and S = 0 a target cohort whose X is observed. Outcomes and
treatments are available in the source. Set q = P (S = 0) > 0, s(x) = P (S = 1 | X = x),

randomized or conditionally exchangeable source treatment, consistency, conditional mean

Then
                           θa = E[Y (a) | S = 0] = E[ma (X) | S = 0].

   Independent target and source samples with fixed sizes are usually more natural operationally.

14.3      Invariant prediction can constrain causal structure
Transport starts from specified invariant mechanisms. Invariant causal prediction uses observed
environments to test candidate restrictions on one such mechanism. Its linear model assumes
140                                                                      Causal analysis for a universal bank


that some set S ∗ and coefficient vector β ∗ satisfy, in every environment e,

                         Y e = µ + (XSe ∗ )′ β ∗ + εe ,   εe ⊥ XSe ∗ ,     εe ∼ Fε .

The coefficient, intercept and noise law are shared. In a suitable acyclic structural model, inter-
ventions on predictors that leave the outcome assignment and its relevant noise independence
intact make its parent set one valid S ∗ (Peters et al., 2016, Assumption 1 and Proposition 1).
An arbitrary split of calendar time into “environments” does not establish these conditions; a
recession may change the outcome mechanism and measurement as well as the predictors.
  For each candidate subset S, test the null that one such common linear mechanism exists.
Let Sb be the subsets not rejected by valid level-α tests and define Sb = S∈Sb S, taking an
                                                                             T

empty result if none is accepted. If the candidate family contains S ∗ , then

                                          P (Sb ⊆ S ∗ ) ≥ 1 − α.                                      (14.3)

Indeed, whenever the true subset is not rejected, the intersection is contained in that subset.
A false positive thus requires rejecting its one true null, an event of probability at most α. No
union bound over all tested subsets is needed for this particular intersection guarantee. This
reproduces the proof of Peters et al. (2016, Theorem 1).
   The direction of inclusion is essential: this is control of false causal inclusions, not a promise
to find every parent. Weakly differing environments may leave the answer empty. Nor is
it a probability distribution over graphs or proof that every accepted regression is causal.
Testing all subsets is exponential in the candidate dimension; screening that removes the true
set can invalidate the guarantee. Dependence, latent confounding, nonlinear responses and
interventions on Y require the corresponding extended model and a valid test, rather than
reusing the linear theorem unchanged. In a banking application, environments should have
documented intervention or mechanism-change meanings and temporally appropriate testing
units.


14.4      Sensitivity quantifies a specified failure of transport
Define the departure from mean transportability by

                              ba (x) = E[Y (a) | X = x, S = 0] − ma (x).

Then the true target effect equals the transported effect plus E[b1 (X) − b0 (X) | S = 0]. If
substantive analysis specifies |b1 (x) − b0 (x)| ≤ Γ(x), the identification uncertainty is at most
E[Γ(X) | S = 0] in either direction. The bound has financial units and can be calibrated against
observed effect variation across comparable markets. It is an assumption-indexed sensitivity
interval, not a confidence interval for an empirically identified parameter. Sampling error can
be added using a jointly valid procedure conditional on the chosen sensitivity restriction.
   Support failure is another, separate uncertainty. For a bounded potential outcome Y (a) ∈
[ymin , ymax ], let O be target covariates covered by the source, with unsupported target mass ω.
If the transported conditional mean is valid on O, then
                        Z                                Z                              
                 θa ∈        ma (x)dP ∗ (x) + ωymin ,          ma (x)dP ∗ (x) + ωymax .
                         O                                 O

Flexible extrapolation chooses one completion inside or even outside these unrestricted bounds;
it does not remove the missing support. Domain balancing that discards uncovered customers
changes the population being answered and should report its mass and composition.
14.4. Sensitivity quantifies a specified failure of transport                               141


   Finally, transport to a future market combines causal invariance with uncertainty about the
future environment. A forecast of future covariate distributions is not an observed target law.
Large-scale adoption may itself change competitor prices, customer choices and funding costs,
so that the environment depends on the policy. Such equilibrium effects need a structural
market model or a design with variation at the relevant market scale. Historical invariance
tests and account-level causal estimates can inform that model but cannot identify the resulting
equilibrium merely by being pooled together.
Chapter 15

Sensitivity when the identifying
assumptions are uncertain

The preceding estimators are conditional conclusions: given the stated graph, moment restric-
tions, support and observation process, they estimate a specified causal functional. A bank
rarely knows those premises with certainty. Sensitivity analysis should therefore describe an
explicit larger model class and propagate its ambiguity to the financial target. Replacing one
flexible regression by another mostly probes estimation choices; it does not probe the omitted
mechanisms those regressions share.

Assume the displayed denominators are positive. The observable scale S multiplies two

not be at most one. These are the nonlinear functional quantities in Chernozhukov et al.

The covariance’s correlation can tighten the bound if a restriction on its sign or magnitude is

   For a finite sign and magnitude check, use the hidden-confounding model from Section 1.6:
U is fair, P (A = 1 | U ) = .2 + .6U , and P (Y = 1 | A, U ) = .2 + .6U . The true ATE is
zero and the observed short contrast is .36. Direct enumeration of the projection product
gives −.36, in agreement with θ − θs . The squared upper bound is .1296, attained in this
construction. The example checks the signed identity and a sharp special case; it does
not prove that every imposed sensitivity pair is compatible with every observed law. The
source’s sharpness statement is conditional on admissible function choices without additional
observed-law constraints.
   Measured-covariate deletion can supply a benchmark: compare the estimated regression
and representer changes when removing an observed variable of known operational importance.
Assuming an unmeasured variable is no stronger than that benchmark is still a substantive
judgment. Better prediction of recorded outcomes does not demonstrate small CY or CA .
Statistical intervals for the learnable scale and short effect also need to account for their joint
estimation; merely appending the point estimate of a bias bound to an ordinary interval is not
generally a calibrated procedure.


15.2       Trend restrictions produce an identified set
Let β be a vector of population event-study contrasts, all relative to a reference date normalized
to zero. With no anticipation, write

                                 βpre = δpre ,       βpost = τpost + δpost .

Here δ describes counterfactual differences between groups in the absence of treatment and τ
is the causal path effect. The target is θ = l′ τpost for declared weights l. Rather than impose
exact parallel trends, choose a restriction set ∆ for δ. Algebra alone gives

                          Θ(β, ∆) = {l′ βpost − l′ δpost : δ ∈ ∆, δpre = βpre }.                        (15.3)

For closed convex restrictions with finite attained extrema, the endpoints are obtained by
maximizing and minimizing l′ δpost under those constraints. Unbounded sets produce infinite
   1
    The first signed equation in Theorem 2 of the archived 2022 working paper reverses the left-hand difference
