21.19.5     Choosing a route and preserving omissions

The useful proposal choice is method-specific. FixedEffectModels.jl is a conditional Julia
worker candidate after numerical, covariance and failure-contract qualification. RegressionDis-
continuity.jl remains a research reference whose naive and optimized/noise-based paths need
separate treatment. The old InstrumentalVariables.jl remains historical reference material; its
runtime and local hazards argue against current native adoption. The distinct RDRobust.jl
port is a comparator requiring provenance, rank and matched-output trials. The inspected Rust
trading implementation is rejected as the current scientific engine because its ratio uncertainty
and unavailable-density fallbacks would require substantive repair. All five retained license
texts declare MIT terms, but the actual numerical, optimization and runtime dependencies
still need distribution-specific review. (FixedEffects/FixedEffectModels.jl contributors, 2026;
nignatiadis/RegressionDiscontinuity.jl contributors, 2024; gragusa/InstrumentalVariables.jl con-
tributors, 2016; xiangao/RDRobust.jl contributors, 2026; suenot/127-regression-discontinuity
contributors, 2026)
   An integration trial should compare the complete intervention request under declared
assumptions, not just regression coefficients. Retain sample exclusions, score support, timing,
first-stage strength, complete covariance, numerical convergence, diagnostics and failures. Use
the independent ratio, probability, rank and mutation witnesses as initial oracles, followed by
predeclared public or synthetic calibration and cost trials in an authorized installed environment.
The scientific owner approves the estimand and inference; the maintainer owns exact versions
and regression cases; the operator owns custody and complete cost accounting. A new port
needs a demonstrated benefit before duplicating these obligations. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026bx)
  Eight additional Julia repositories returned by the bounded discovery queries remain
uninspected, including alternative IV, shift-share, system-projection and model-averaging
routes. Other languages and registries are also unresolved. A zero-result Rust IV query is a
coverage limit, not proof that no implementation exists. These omissions prevent a claim of
comprehensive coverage while allowing the concrete source findings and proposed comparisons
above to guide the next prototype decision.


21.20      R effect estimation: preserve the target before choosing
           the learner
A servicing team may ask which customers should receive an intervention, what the intervention
achieves on average, or how much additional credit should be offered. These questions require
different statistical objects. Let X denote information available before the decision, A ∈ {0, 1}
a recorded intervention, and Y (a) its potential monetary outcome. The conditional effect
τ (x) = E{Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x}, its population average, and its average among customers
actually treated are not interchangeable. For a continuous amount W , the dose-response
21.20. R effect estimation: preserve the target before choosing the learner                   249


curve µ(w) = E{Y (w)} introduces another target. Identification still requires the relevant
consistency, exchangeability and support assumptions; orthogonal nuisance estimation does
not supply them. Forest and double-machine- learning results impose their own sampling and
regularity conditions. (Chernozhukov et al., 2018; Athey et al., 2018)
   The R routes examined here have distinct strengths. The selected grf interface exposes
conditional forests and several average-effect targets; tmle addresses observed binary point
treatments and outcome missingness; R DoubleML exposes explicit orthogonal-score models.
CausalGPS and causaldrf supply different paths to continuous-exposure analysis. The pro-
posed product should wrap their qualified statistical contracts before considering a native port.
Matching an algorithm name or programming language does not establish matching targets or
uncertainty. (GRF contributors, 2026c; cran/tmle contributors, 2026; DoubleML/doubleml-
for-r contributors, 2026; cran/CausalGPS contributors, 2026; cran/causaldrf contributors,
2026)


21.20.1     An R score is a specification, not a Python alias

The inspected R DoubleML revision is dated 1 September 2026 and declares development
version 1.0.1.9000. Its R6 and mlr3 implementation must be assessed separately from the
Python installation considered earlier. The selected interactive-regression class requires one
binary treatment. Write m(x) = P (A = 1 | X = x) and ga (x) = E(Y | A = a, X = x). Its
ATE score uses
                              A{Y − g1 (X)} (1 − A){Y − g0 (X)}
     ψb = g1 (X) − g0 (X) +                −                    ,             ψa = −1,    (21.29)
                                 m(X)            1 − m(X)

and solves the empirical equation ψa θ + ψb = 0. For ATTE, the selected code instead uses the
control outcome nuisance, a treated fraction calculated within each test fold, and ψa = −A/pb.
It fits the treated-outcome nuisance for ATE and custom scores, but does not require that fit for
its built-in ATTE path. These choices must survive the wrapper: changing the target cannot be
implemented merely by changing a returned field name. The propensity truncation option clips
predictions; it does not itself define a new trimmed population. (DoubleML/doubleml-for-r
contributors, 2026; Chernozhukov et al., 2018)
  The nuisance helper supplies explicit training and test indices to custom mlr3 resampling.
Treatment-specific outcome fits restrict training indices while retaining the requested prediction
rows. This is distinct from cross-validation used to tune a learner: the inspected tuning method
defaults to global tuning and has an explicit option for tuning separately within folds. A
proposed validation protocol must record both sets of folds and any use of outcomes during
tuning. Neither a default option nor the existence of custom scores proves that an arbitrary
nuisance learner or new score satisfies a theorem. (DoubleML/doubleml-for-r contributors,
2026; Chernozhukov et al., 2018)
   For continuous W , the partialling-out score solves a different moment. Let e(X) = E(W | X),
ℓ(X) = E(Y | X) and v = W − e(X). Its population target, when the denominator is positive,
is
                                             E[v{Y − ℓ(X)}]
                                    θPLR =                      .                       (21.30)
                                                   E(v 2 )
Under the stipulated conditional model Y = a(X) + β(X)W + ϵ, with E(ϵ | W, X) = 0,
conditioning shows E(vY | X) = β(X) Var(W | X). Hence

                                           E{Var(W | X)β(X)}
                                  θPLR =                     ,                            (21.31)
                                             E{Var(W | X)}
250                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


rather than generally E{β(X)}. Two equally probable risk groups with slopes 1 and 3 and
treatment variances 1 and 4 give respectively 13/5 and 2. The difference is a population-target
difference even with perfect nuisances. These are exact authored laws, not measurements of
package error. (DoubleML/doubleml-for-r contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project,
2026av)


21.20.2     Forests, clustering and the information needed for uncertainty

In the selected grf R path, all-sample AIPW averaging uses scores and sums weighted
centered scores within declared clusters for its variance. The continuous-treatment score learns
conditional treatment variance with an additional forest and divides a treatment residual by
that variance. Positivity of this denominator and stable estimation are substantive conditions.
A returned local slope cannot be relabelled as an arbitrary finite-dose effect. The overlap
target uses a separate residual-regression path; the documented method choice does not
bypass earlier guards. In particular, the inspected average-effect function rejects TMLE with
clusters or sample weights. Honesty in forest construction, treatment residualization and
independent-cluster inference solve different problems. (GRF contributors, 2026c; Athey et al.,
2018)
   The selected R DoubleML base class draws partitions over cluster identifiers and has separate
one- and two-way cluster variance calculations. This does not establish validity for arbitrary
serial dependence or few calendar periods. Moreover, its multiplier-bootstrap method explicitly
stops for clustered data. Its joint-interval method requires bootstrap output, whereas the
ordinary interval method uses a normal critical value with the reported standard error. A
wrapper must preserve this unsupported combination; silently substituting row multipliers
would change the sampling law. A cluster-aware pointwise standard error and a jointly valid
set of comparisons are different deliverables. (DoubleML/doubleml-for-r contributors, 2026)
   For servicing data, the request must therefore name the independent sampling units, repeated-
customer identifiers, common calendar shocks, and how entire units are kept out of nuisance-
training folds. The public prototype can compare supported regimes with known generated
truth before an expensive bank trial. It must retain failed folds, absent treatment arms,
unsupported uncertainty requests and denominator failures. These are proposed admission
requirements; the source inspection does not execute either R engine.


21.20.3     Missing outcomes do not make missing treatment labels observed

The pinned tmle 2.1.1 help text describes outcome missingness, but its Delta argument also
mentions missing treatment assignment. The selected function body provides a narrower
operational contract: its argument verifier requires no missing values in A or W , and the public
entrypoint stops when verification fails. Earlier preprocessing can also fail on an incompletely
observed treatment vector. Passing A=NULL, or an all-zero vector, selects a constant-treatment
path by replacing A with ones. The documentation describes the no-variation case as mean-
outcome estimation. This is not treatment imputation, and the missingness regression still
conditions on recorded A. The proposal should reject arbitrary missing-A admission for
this inspected path and retain the conflicting wording for clarification and native fixtures.
(cran/tmle contributors, 2026)
   There is a scientific reason to keep those fields separate. Consider an authored law in which
observation group R and randomized treatment A are independent fair coins. When R = 1,
both worlds have Y (a) = a and the treatment is recorded. When R = 0, the treatment label
is erased: world I has Y (a) = a, while world II has Y (a) = 1 − a. The observed tuple consists
21.20. R effect estimation: preserve the target before choosing the learner                   251


of R, the treatment label when present, and Y . Both worlds give the same distribution of that
tuple: each observed group has a fair binary outcome. Nevertheless,

                       E{Y (1) − Y (0)}I = 1,        E{Y (1) − Y (0)}II = 0.              (21.32)

This witness deliberately lacks treatment-observation positivity in group R = 0 and grants
no restriction transporting effects from R = 1. It does not claim impossibility under every
missingness model. At a stipulated USD 100 outcome scale, the two effects are USD 100
and USD 0 despite the identical observations. More rows with the same missing information
cannot distinguish them; verified labels or justified additional restrictions can. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026av)


21.20.4     Dose curves require units, support and complete transformations

A conditional regression slope also differs from a dose curve in one homogeneous group.
Suppose incremental credit W is measured in thousands of dollars, is uniform on [0, 2], and
the stipulated margin curve is Y (w) = 20w2 − 5w dollars. Direct polynomial integration gives
                      Cov(W, Y )
                                 = 35,     Y ′ (0) = −5,   Y (1) − Y (0) = 15.            (21.33)
                       Var(W )
Using the projection slope to value a USD 1,000 increase from zero would report USD 35 in
this law, whereas the stipulated contrast is USD 15. Expressing credit in dollars changes the
slope to 35/1000; it does not change the finite monetary contrast. This example illustrates
target and unit errors, not bank profitability. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026av)
   The inspected CausalGPS kernel path standardizes an exposure residual and stores an
estimated residual density. Its weighting helper divides an estimated marginal exposure density
by that stored quantity. Under a location-scale model W = e(X) + s(X)U , with s(X) > 0,
the change of variables is
                                              1        w − e(x)
                                                                    
                             fW |X (w | x) =     f              x .                       (21.34)
                                             s(x) U |X   s(x)
The inspected kernel branch does not divide by s(x) before returning its GPS. With different
conditional scales, replacing the original-unit density with residual density changes relative
weights. An exact two-row illustration with scales 1 and 2, the same residual density and
marginal numerator, gives weights 1 and 2 rather than 1 and 1. Applied to stipulated
outcomes USD 0 and USD 100, their weighted means are USD 200/3 and USD 50. This is
algebraic motivation for a conformance fixture, not a measured error for every package output.
(cran/CausalGPS contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026av)
   Under a constant positive change of exposure units, both a correctly expressed marginal
density and conditional density acquire the same reciprocal unit factor, so their ratio is
invariant. A covariate-dependent omitted scale is a different issue. A public test should vary
units and conditional scales separately, then trace the resulting weighting and response fits.
The selected response routine supplies parametric, semiparametric and nonparametric routes;
it rejects negative weights but changes an all-zero weight vector to equal weights. The product
should refuse an all-zero causal weighting request before that fallback changes its meaning.
Balance statistics and effective sample size are useful diagnostics, not proof of exchangeability
or calibrated uncertainty. Trimming and complete-case filtering must also be reflected in the
target population and reported support. (cran/CausalGPS contributors, 2026)
  The selected causaldrf hi_est path follows a different design. It fits a treatment model, fits
an outcome regression on treatment and the estimated score, then recalculates the score at each
252                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


requested dose for every row before averaging predicted outcomes. This counterfactual-score
step must be preserved. Its log and square-root branches evaluate densities on transformed
scales without applying the corresponding original-scale Jacobian in that function. At a fixed
positive dose those Jacobian factors are constant across covariates, so their omission does not
by itself prove a failure of a balancing argument at that dose. It does change the density
interpretation and the representation supplied to a restricted response regression across doses.
Positive support, transformation rules and the whole fitted response surface therefore need
explicit comparison before adoption. (cran/causaldrf contributors, 2026)
   The accompanying get_ci helper receives a matrix of bootstrap coefficients, forms linear or
quadratic predictions, and sorts each dose column. It neither generates the resamples nor refits
the treatment model. Its separate column order statistics are pointwise constructions, not a
simultaneous curve band. The selected lower index is ⌊0.025B⌋, which is zero when B < 40;
native edge cases need inspection rather than a claim that increasing B solves statistical
validity. A proposed curve experiment must specify which sampling units are resampled, which
stages are refitted, and whether it evaluates pointwise coverage, joint coverage, or a selected
optimal-dose decision. (cran/causaldrf contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project,
2026av)


21.20.5     A bounded reuse proposal and the remaining comparison

For a first public prototype, the proposal is to wrap R DoubleML’s supported IRM/PLR score
paths, grf’s target-specific forest paths, and tmle’s observed point-treatment paths. Requests
should carry target, units, treatment-label status, support, weighting, folds and sampling units.
Responses should preserve unsupported modes and diagnostic failures. Native ports remain
conditional on demonstrated semantic and numerical parity; translating a wrapper does not
reproduce a learner’s statistical contract. CausalGPS remains a conditional candidate pending
scale and downstream weight checks, while causaldrf is a useful proposed parametric baseline
subject to transformation and full-pipeline uncertainty qualification.
   The selected originals establish these specific contrasts, not a complete R market census.
BART-based alternatives such as bartCause, causalweight, further continuous-exposure
methods, and their aliases still require matched primary-source review. Package license
declarations and copyright notices do not settle all distribution or learner-dependency rights.
No R package has been executed in this source comparison. Public and generated experiments
can decide which wrappers merit a prototype; bank truth, deployment acceptance and observed
returns remain subsequent questions. The immediate comparison must preserve the question
being estimated before ranking a learner.


21.21      Commercial staggered DID: compare the target before
           the coefficient
A staggered branch rollout poses a different question from the cross-sectional graphical query.
Branches can adopt a policy at different dates, the policy’s effect can change with exposure,
and calendar shocks can move all outcomes. A commercial panel command should therefore
be compared on the treatment history, cohort-time target, admissible controls and uncertainty
procedure. A numerical coefficient without these meanings is insufficient for a banking decision.
The inspected Stata manuals distinguish scalar linear DID and heterogeneous cohort-time
effects; the EViews introduction supplies a more limited panel-DID capability statement.
(StataCorp, 2026k,l,n; EViews, 2025b)
21.21. Commercial staggered DID: compare the target before the coefficient                               253


  The scalar Stata pair is didregress for repeated cross-sections and xtdidregress for panels.
The first fits time and group fixed effects; the second fits time and panel fixed effects. Their
heterogeneous counterparts are hdidregress and xthdidregress, respectively. The latter
manuals describe regression adjustment, inverse-probability weighting, augmented weighting
and an extended two-way fixed-effects approach. Listing these alternatives does not make their
assumptions or output interchangeable. The selected heterogeneous panel formulas assume
that treatment remains on after adoption. A history (0, 1, 0) therefore requires refusal under
that profile or a separately justified switching-treatment design. (StataCorp, 2026k,l,n)
   Let Gi denote branch i’s first adoption date, with infinity for a never-treated branch. Write
Yit (g) for its outcome if adoption begins at g, and Yit (∞) for its untreated outcome. A
cohort-time target and one possible aggregation are
                                                     X                                      X
  θ(g, t) = E{Yit (g) − Yit (∞) | Gi = g},    Θω =           ωgt θ(g, t),    ωgt ≥ 0,              ωgt = 1.
                                                     g,t≥g                                 g,t≥g
                                                                                          (21.35)
This notation is our explicit target convention. Its identification needs the selected comparison
assumptions, including consistency, an appropriate no-anticipation condition, overlap and
untreated parallel trends for the declared comparison population. The inspected manuals
allow never-treated or not-yet-treated controls and document base-time choices for preperiod
effects. Those choices alter which contrasts and support are available. Not-yet-treated units
cease to be eligible untreated comparisons after adoption. The request must therefore retain
the control rule, anticipation window, base period and the branch/time population before
aggregation. (StataCorp, 2026l,n)


21.21.1     An exact positive-effect rollout can have a negative projection

Consider five equally weighted hypothetical branches, E1 , E2 , L1 , L2 , N , observed at dates
0, 1, 2. Number them i = 0, . . . , 4 in that order. Their untreated outcomes, in thousands of
stipulated USD per branch-period, are Yit (∞) = 10i + 2t. The early cohort adopts at date 1,
the late cohort at date 2, and N never adopts. There is no anticipation, spillover, attrition or
missing period. Treatment adds 1 at the early cohort’s first treated date, 100 at its second,
and 1 at the late cohort’s treated date. These are deliberately extreme finite values that make
a target error visible, rather than forecasts of a bank rollout. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026v)

              Cohort and date Branches Effect ATT weight TWFE weight
              Early, date 1          2      1        1/3         5/8
              Early, date 2          2   100         1/3       −1/8
              Late, date 2           2      1        1/3         1/2

Here ATT means the average over the six treated branch-periods, so it is (2 + 200 + 2)/6 = 34
thousand USD. Never-treated DID contrasts recover the three effects exactly: compare each
early date with date 0 and the late treated date with date 1, subtracting the corresponding
change in N . These are finite arithmetic equalities under the stipulated untreated law. They
carry no sampling confidence statement. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026v)
  Now fit the scalar least-squares projection Yit = αi + λt + βDit + eit to the same 15 rows,
where Dit = 1{t ≥ Gi }. In this balanced panel, let bars denote branch, date and grand means.

   If the cost is stipulated to be USD 10,000 per treated period, the true retrospective mean net
increment under this law is USD 24,000. Mistaking the projection for that ATT would instead
produce minus USD 21,375. The latter is an explicitly invalid value calculation. Neither
quantity evaluates a new rollout policy, estimates bank prices or measures ROI. An investment
comparison still needs the applicable population, treatment costs, feasible alternative and
uncertainty about its transported outcomes. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026v)


21.21.2     Aggregation, trends and uncertainty belong to the request

The heterogeneous postestimation manual distinguishes aggregation by cohort, calendar
time, exposure time, and cohort/time, and distinguishes weights(timecohort) from
weights(cohort). The former builds weights using the subsets used for the individual ATETs;
the latter uses cohort sizes. A branch closure or a changing observed sample can therefore
matter to the interpretation of an aggregate. The adapter should return the supported
cohort-time cells and their denominators first, then the chosen normalized weights and the
resulting estimand. Replacing those weights by a convenient average can change the banking
population. (StataCorp, 2026m)
   Preperiod diagnostics are useful checks, but cannot validate the unobserved postperiod
counterfactual. For an exact counterexample, let two groups have identical paths at dates
−2, −1. At adoption, suppose the treated group’s true treatment effect is 2, and an otherwise
unobserved group-specific untreated-outcome shock is 3. The observed postperiod DID is 5.
A world with effect 5 and no differential shock has the same observed contrast. Thus even
exact preperiod equality cannot distinguish those worlds without an additional restriction
on the untreated postperiod path. A nonrejected pretrend test is weaker still. Sensitivity to
differential trends and anticipation must remain part of the business interpretation. (Causal
banking proposal project, 2026v)
   Inference is likewise command-specific. The inspected xthdidregress manual equates
vce(robust) with clustering at the declared treatment group. That is not a generic promise of
independent branch-level rows or a universal interpretation of every command’s robust option.
The postestimation manual disallows its multiplier simultaneous intervals after TWFE and
disallows estat aggregation after bootstrap or jackknife estimation. A requested interval
may target one cell, one fixed aggregate or simultaneous coverage of many cells; those events
differ. A wrapper must check the selected estimator, clustering, interval target and option
compatibility before returning uncertainty. The five-branch arithmetic example supplies
no cluster asymptotics, multiplier qualification or confidence coverage. A future generated
multi-cluster trial must declare its sampling law and coverage target separately. (StataCorp,
2026n,m; Causal banking proposal project, 2026v)
21.22. Choosing a fixed-effect engine without changing the bank’s question                  255


21.21.3     What the commercial evidence supports and what to build first

The acquired Stata originals contain July/August 2026 creation metadata and StataNow
feature flags. They were acquired on 18 October 2026; neither their metadata nor a displayed
copyright authenticates the precise bytes or entitlements available at the 7 October cutoff.
An edition-specific comparison needs the release and options actually under consideration.
The EViews page, displaying a March 2025 update, states that built-in DID is provided for
panel workfiles and introduces a TWFE and diagnostics chapter. That introductory page is
insufficient evidence of every referenced algorithm, complete covariance implementation or
licensed product edition. These source limits qualify the historical comparison; they do not
imply that an uninspected vendor lacks a feature. (StataCorp, 2026k,l,n,m; EViews, 2025b)
   Our bounded candidate search also retains SAS, IBM SPSS, MATLAB and commercial
frontends to open-source tools as unresolved families. DID-specific primary originals and exact
editions are missing for those comparisons. Generic panel regression is not sufficient evidence
of a causal DID workflow. The immediate comparison is consequently a documented Stata
baseline and a limited EViews lead, with explicit omissions rather than a claim of a saturated
commercial market. Embedding rights, prices, support and executable compatibility remain
separate selection questions.
   The current common dispatcher returns an unsupported disposition for the dependent-panel
DID request used in the saved local probe. This is an observed interface limitation, not
evidence that every panel research module in the repository is absent. A proposed extension
should admit a fully declared cohort-time target, preserve the treatment and information
history, report cells and weights, and reject unsupported reversals or inference options. A
licensed vendor comparison can then reproduce the 15-row reference, add unbalanced support
and alternative controls, and examine an independently designed uncertainty trial. Completing
this bounded path would provide a meaningful prototype comparison; it would not by itself
establish general trend validity or bank qualification. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026t,v)


21.22      Choosing a fixed-effect engine without changing the
           bank’s question
A bank comparing outreach across branches and months needs more than a fast regression.
It must know which account-periods remain in the calculation, whether the treatment varies
after the fixed effects are removed, what variation supports uncertainty, and which customers
an aggregated event-study effect describes. These requirements motivate conditional reuse of
the original fixest engine through a typed R worker. The scope initially proposed here is
linear fixed-effect estimation; an IV formula, a nonlinear family or an event-study expansion
needs its own scientific and numerical qualification.
   The inspected revision is commit 789f888416e9 of 26 June 2026, whose DESCRIPTION
declares version 0.14.2. This identifies the selected source, without establishing the latest
or a distributed release. Its R dependency is at least 3.5.0, with Rcpp linking and imports
including numDeriv, nlme, sandwich, dreamerr and stringmagic. The declaration is GPL-3;
the associated standard license text is available separately. A root LICENSE file is absent from
the inspected tree. That absence does not erase the declaration or establish complete rights
for an assembled distribution. A separate process is an engineering choice and does not settle
distribution obligations. The selected change log records covariance-class, IV-collinearity and
degrees-of-freedom fixes; a workflow specifies checks on three operating systems. These are
maintenance evidence, not observed passing checks or a support commitment.(Laurent Berge
256                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


and fixest contributors, 2026)


21.22.1     Projection, causal meaning and the retained population

Let Y be the vector of contribution margins before the incremental outreach cost, D the binary
outreach indicator and Z the full-rank matrix of branch indicators. With equal observation
weights, write

                   MZ = I − Z(Z T Z)−1 Z T ,        βb = (DT MZ D)−1 DT MZ Y.                  (21.38)

The expression requires DT MZ D > 0. It is the coefficient obtained by ordinary least squares
on the explicit dummy matrix [Z, D]: minimizing over branch intercepts first gives the residual
objective ∥MZ (Y − Dβ)∥2 , whose scalar normal equation yields (21.38). For strictly positive
weights W , the corresponding argument applies to W 1/2 Y , W 1/2 D and W 1/2 Z. Consequently
a conversion that changes weights changes the projection being requested.
   This algebra alone identifies no intervention effect. For example, a constant-effect panel
interpretation additionally needs a credible restriction such as E[εit | Di1 , . . . , DiT , Z] = 0 in
the specified model, as well as consistent treatment, an appropriate interference assumption
and the required sampling conditions. Outreach triggered by an unobserved deterioration in
customer finances can violate that restriction. An IV extension substitutes instrument relevance
and substantive exclusion and exogeneity assumptions; the formula syntax cannot supply
them. Likewise, adding time effects changes Z and may remove the variation that previously
identified the projection. These are scientific choices that the proposed business-to-model
interface must state before submitting a regression.
  Consider the following exact authored example, with two periods per branch. The outcomes
are hypothetical USD contributions per account-period.

                                     Branch D1 D2        Y1   Y2
                                       A    0 1          10   12
                                       B    1 0          20   16
                                       C    0 1          30   36

Within-branch residualization gives DT MZ D = 3/2 and βb = 4. Solving the explicit dummy
normal equations gives the same result, with intercepts (9, 16, 31). Reversing input row order
leaves the coefficient and group scores unchanged when row identifiers travel with their data.
If instead treatment is one for every observation in B and zero elsewhere, D lies in the span of
Z and MZ D = 0. The coefficient is unavailable; reporting zero would invent an answer to an
unidentified regression target. These are rational-arithmetic reference cases, not results from
running R.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026am)
   The inspected feols documentation describes recursive removal of singletons and perfect-fit
observations under its default setting. Its stated slope invariance in the relevant removal
setting does not imply invariant inference or population reporting. The source also tracks
collinear variables and observation selections. For finite weights it rejects negative values and
removes zero weights; missing or infinite weights enter sample-selection handling. Our initial
adapter should prevalidate all weights and require an explicit policy for exclusions, rather
than rely on a message printed after estimation. Every retained and removed row needs its
original identifier and reason. A factor level disappearing after exclusions can change rank,
and a dropped treatment must remain a typed unavailable result.(Laurent Berge and fixest
contributors, 2026)
21.22. Choosing a fixed-effect engine without changing the bank’s question                        257


21.22.2     A covariance request is part of the estimand service

The selected startup code sets the default covariance family to iid. Later calls can read session
options. Thus a formula containing branch fixed effects does not by itself request branch-
clustered errors. A reproducible worker must set the covariance family, cluster identifiers,
small-sample correction and reference degrees of freedom explicitly. The source’s ssc interface
separates K adjustment, fixed-effect counting, cluster adjustment and the degrees of freedom
used for the Student reference distribution. The default fixed-effect count is nonnested; none,
full and optional exact counting express different conventions. Its upstream tests describe
an irregular two-way example with counts 6, 1, 8 and 7 under these choices. Those tests are
useful future conformance specifications and have not been executed here.(Laurent Berge and
fixest contributors, 2026)

An explicitly chosen correction VbK = Vb0 {(n − 1)/(n − K)}{G/(G − 1)} gives 4/3 for n =

uncertainty procedure.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026am)
   Numerical covariance repair adds another distinction. In the inspected code, vcov_fix
defaults to true. A nonpositive eigenvalue triggers a candidate repair; assignment of the
repaired covariance occurs inside if(vcov_fix). An adjacent comment says repair always
occurs even when the flag is false, but the executable branch has the narrower behavior. The
warning decision uses a maximum change greater than 10−8 , so an absence of a warning is
not proof that nothing was changed. A proposed adapter must preserve the requested policy
and the original and repaired matrices, or refuse to certify a repair state it cannot observe.
Positive definiteness is a numerical property; it does not validate a causal model, cluster law
or interval coverage.(Laurent Berge and fixest contributors, 2026)


21.22.3     Event-time support and the meaning of an aggregate

Suppose branches adopt a servicing policy in different calendar months. The cohort is the
adoption month and relative time is the observed month minus that cohort. The inspected
sunab documentation warns that, when relative time is inferred from calendar values, a cohort
absent from the supplied period support is treated as never treated. Its example uses cohort
1994 and observed years 1995–2005: an already-treated cohort can be misclassified as never
treated. The proposed conversion must therefore construct treatment status from the business
history before invoking the helper. It must distinguish never treated, treated before observation
and not yet treated, and preserve reference periods, binning and unsupported cells. A valid
design further needs the substantive comparison assumptions, including appropriate parallel
trends and no anticipation; a matrix expansion does not verify them.(Laurent Berge and fixest
contributors, 2026)
  The selected aggregation routine constructs shares from the signs of design columns, using
observation weights when requested, normalizes those shares and averages the corresponding
258                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


coefficients. It calculates uncertainty from the full coefficient covariance. For a fixed vector of
shares a and coefficient vector bb, the target and conditional variance are

                                  θb = aTbb,    d θ)
                                                Var( b = aT Vb a.                          (21.40)

The second identity follows by expanding the covariance of a linear combination. If shares
themselves are estimated for a different population target, their uncertainty needs an additional
argument; treating the observed shares as fixed does not settle that question.(Laurent Berge
and fixest contributors, 2026)
   For an authored contrast take bb = (2, 8)T , a = (3/4, 1/4)T and Vb = ( 41 19 ). Then θb = 7/2
and the variance is 51/16. Dropping the covariance
                                               √       cross term gives 45/16; averaging the
two standard errors gives 9/4, which is not 51/4. Equal coefficient shares would instead
give an effect of 5. At a stipulated incremental cost of USD 4 per account, these two
different targets imply net margins of USD −0.50 and USD 1. Neither is an observed bank
return; the contrast shows why silently changing aggregation weights can reverse a proposal’s
recommendation.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026am)


21.22.4     A conditional reuse choice and a public qualification path

The original R engine is the preferred proposal route because its sample, design and covariance
behavior can be kept together behind one typed boundary. feols, feglm and femlm are
distinct model surfaces within that package; qualifying one linear profile does not qualify all of
them. pyfixest remains a separately assessed implementation. An explicit-dummy reference
is attractive for small transparent examples, while a direct port of numerical routines would
also have to reproduce formula coding, row selection, fixed-effect rank, covariance defaults,
aggregation and failures. No measured cost or target-platform requirement currently justifies
that duplication.(Laurent Berge and fixest contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project,
2026am)
   The proposed request carries the immutable data snapshot, units, row keys, calendar,
design, target population and uncertainty choices. The response carries coefficient identities,
covariance, retained sample, exclusions, rank and convergence diagnostics, aggregation shares
and any repair status. Library, CLI and MCP surfaces must preserve those meanings. A
missing target, invalid request, unsupported model, numerical failure and cancelled job remain
different outcomes. An agent may propose a reviewed design, but an initial tool should accept
bounded formula structures rather than arbitrary generated R expressions. These are proposed
contracts; no such fixest worker has been admitted by this source review.
   Public and generated panels can test the merit of that design before a bank experiment. Start
with exact dummy/within agreement and an absorbed treatment, then test row permutations,
zero/missing weights, singleton cascades, near-collinearity, covariance defaults and correction
choices. Event-time cases must include adoption outside the observed calendar and aggregation
with nonzero covariance. Native runs should compare outputs, masks and typed failures against
the authored references and independently inspected upstream specifications. A complete
pinned distribution, compiler/runtime environment and dependency rights review precede
executable admission. Subsequent public data studies may assess numerical stability and
workflow value; they cannot establish a private bank’s assignment mechanism or actual return.
  The scientific owner must own identifying assumptions and dependence; the data owner
must own calendars, weights and exclusions; the adapter maintainer must own conversions
and upgrade conformance. Operational costs to measure include worker startup, serialization,
memory, rank and covariance computation, dependency maintenance and diagnostics. This
conditional proposal selection can be completed now while native qualification and deployment
21.23. Panel software as a contract for timing, weighting and uncertainty                      259


remain open. It converts a broad intention to reuse panel software into a testable design
without treating an available coefficient as a validated causal conclusion.


21.23       Panel software as a contract for timing, weighting and
            uncertainty
A bank comparing staggered branch interventions with a simultaneous regional launch faces two
different designs. A Python fixed-effect regression and an R synthetic difference-in-differences
fit can both return a scalar measured in dollars, but that coincidence does not establish
that they estimate the same policy value. The reusable object must describe the population,
adoption clock, control eligibility, outcome horizon, weighting and uncertainty. This section
examines concrete interfaces in PyFixest and the original R synthdid package, building on the
separate R fixest discussion. Source inspection establishes what the selected code says and
how a proposed adapter must represent it; it does not establish that an installed package has
passed our trials. (PyFixest contributors, 2026; synthdid contributors, 2024)
   The PyFixest snapshot is commit 45d52b6e368cefc7321239921f2547b4e08c8f20, dated
6 October 2026. Its Python version is dynamic through Maturin; the Rust core declares 0.60.0.
The original synthdid snapshot is commit 70c1ce3eac58e28c30b67435ca377bb48baa9b8a,
dated 15 January 2024, and declares version 0.0.9. The different dates matter for maintenance
planning: the latter README describes a beta interface, while the former has changing
Python and native numerical boundaries. A cutoff-selected commit and a package version are
identities, not promises of future support. Neither Python syntax similarity to R fixest nor
the use of the name SDID by other implementations transfers a qualified capability. (PyFixest
contributors, 2026; synthdid contributors, 2024)

the projection’s meaning, not a successful causal design. With a stipulated cost of 2 dollars
per treated cell, the target net is 2 dollars but treating the projection as that target would

follow different fitting and aggregation paths. The product therefore needs an explicit estimator
profile and a displayed estimand, rather than an event-study label that conceals the formula
actually fitted. (PyFixest contributors, 2026)


21.23.2     Calendar conversion, first-stage support and aggregation

PyFixest’s common DID base accepts numeric time and cohort fields but constructs relative
time by subtraction. A calendar code is not necessarily a period index: 202601 − 202512 = 89,
whereas the elapsed month count is one. The proposed adapter should retain real calendar
dates and an explicit consecutive index, including a policy for missing observations. The
base constructs absorbing treatment from the declared cohort and uses zero for never treated.
Its event origin is the first observed treated period. If declared adoption is period two and
the first observed post-treatment record is period three, the declared event time is one while
recentering on the observed record makes it zero. Both dates must survive conversion so that
an observation gap cannot silently change the scientific question. (PyFixest contributors, 2026;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026bz)
   The DID2S helper verifies two unique numeric treatment values and then casts them to
Boolean. Codes two and three both map to true; the adapter must validate the actual
binary convention before that conversion. Its first stage fits untreated observations. Missing
fixed-effect levels in that sample lead to missing predictions and an explicit error. This is
meaningful support information: a bank should retain which branches or calendars could
not be represented, instead of deleting the error from the request denominator. The GMM
covariance uses residuals from both stages. The wrapper retains the second-stage inference
degrees of freedom and disables specified post-estimation capabilities; availability of a generic
fitted-object method does not establish that it is valid for this two-stage result. (PyFixest
contributors, 2026)
   The saturated branch also needs a narrower contract than its common public surface might
suggest. The inspected dispatcher does not pass the covariate formula to its saturated helper.
The actual aggregation implementation accepts period and shares choices, despite broader
options in its docstring; its period-weight code includes relative period zero despite contrary
prose. Its linear-combination interval uses the normal multiplier 1.96. This is not automatically
a few-cluster correction or a simultaneous event-time band. Those source discrepancies are
reasons to test and constrain the chosen profile, not empirical claims that a newly executed
native request failed. (PyFixest contributors, 2026)
  Aggregation is itself part of the estimand. For effects θb = (10, −2)′ , weights w = (1/4, 3/4)′
and the stated covariance
                                     !

                         V =        ,        w′ θb = 1,    w′ V w =      ,                 (21.43)
                                1 9                                   16

the equal-cohort effect would instead be 4. Omitting cross-covariance gives 85/16, a different
variance even with unchanged marginal standard errors. The example assumes fixed aggregation
weights. If the weights are estimated, their additional uncertainty must be justified for the
chosen procedure. The reporting schema should retain cohort sizes, eligible populations, full
covariance and coefficient order so an analyst can see why the summaries differ. (Causal
banking proposal project, 2026bz)
  PyFixest offers useful numerical machinery: its demeaning wrapper checks the success flag
21.23. Panel software as a contract for timing, weighting and uncertainty                      261


and raises on nonconvergence. But a profile must also retain singleton removal, analytic-weight
defaults, rank tolerance, solver choice, backend-specific preconditioner fallback and warnings.
Rust, within, optional Numba and Torch paths are not one interchangeable execution guarantee.
The earlier weighted-IV source discussion remains relevant to its IV branch; fixed-effect fitting
and first-stage diagnostics do not by themselves provide weak-instrument confidence-set
inversion. (PyFixest contributors, 2026)


21.23.3     The original synthetic difference-in-differences block

The original synthdid package addresses a different layout. There are N0 control units followed
by N1 treated units, and T0 pre-treatment periods followed by T1 post-treatment periods.
Its treatment indicator equals one only in the bottom-right block. This is the block design
identified in the original paper’s inspected discussion; broader extensions in the literature
are not evidence that this package supports staggered adoption. (Arkhangelsky et al., 2021;
synthdid contributors, 2024)
  Let Z = Y − Xβ denote outcomes after the selected covariate adjustment, and let ω and λ
be control-unit and pre-period weights. The code computes the bilinear contrast

                              τb = (−ω ′ , N1−1 1′N1 )Z(−λ′ , T1−1 1′T1 )′ ,                (21.44)

so treated units and post periods receive equal weights within that block. A branch-period
effect is not automatically a customer-weighted portfolio effect. If customer populations differ,
the proposal must either defend this target or derive and qualify an alternative instead of
changing weights after seeing the answer. The code’s scalar result alone cannot establish no
anticipation, no interference, or the counterfactual trend, factor and noise restrictions needed
for a causal interpretation. (synthdid contributors, 2024)
   The panel converter rejects missing values, nonbinary treatment and anything other than
one observation at every unit–time pair. It then checks simultaneous adoption. It converts
factor and date fields to character before sorting. ISO dates may preserve calendar order, but
arbitrary period labels need an explicit ordering map. The option that leaves treated units
unsorted does not change the estimator’s expectation that controls occupy the first N0 rows.
Nor does the converter retain other columns as a covariate array; that alignment remains an
adapter obligation. The direct matrix entrypoint has a different, narrower set of checks. The
proposed worker must enforce finite data, nonempty treatment/control and pre/post groups,
valid noise estimation support, and row identity on either entry route. (synthdid contributors,
2024)

changes the contrast by 25 dollars. The direct estimator checks supplied weight lengths but
does not enforce the simplex constraints for fixed weights. An SDID profile must check those

21.23.4     Optimization and inference are separate reproducibility obligations

The default unit penalty scales with estimated pre-treatment first-difference noise and (N1 T1 )1/4 ;
the time penalty uses a small multiplier. The no-covariate path uses Frank–Wolfe steps with
exact line search, followed by optional sparsification and another optimization. Its stopping
condition uses objective decrease and an iteration limit. The covariate path alternates weight
updates with a 1/t gradient step and tests absolute objective change. Neither returns a
separate certified error bound just because iteration stopped. A worker should retain objective
histories, limits, finite-value checks and an independent numerical comparison when feasible.
The upstream CVXR/ECOS reference provides an explicit simplex objective; the inspected test
compares one California example at tolerance 0.03. That source test is useful for planning, but
has not been run here and cannot establish general parity or calibrated uncertainty. (synthdid
contributors, 2024)
   Reproducibility also extends beyond the fitted point estimate. The attached options retain
penalties, intercepts, update flags, minimum decrease and the main iteration limit, but omit the
sparsification function and the pre-sparsification iteration limit. Resampling refits reconstruct
calls from these saved options. When a caller changed an omitted option, subsequent refits can
return to its default. The proposed adapter must record the full fit configuration independently
and replay it deliberately; preserving the scalar and its attached setup alone is insufficient.
This is a static call-path observation requiring native regression tests. (synthdid contributors,
2024)
   The package offers bootstrap, jackknife and placebo variance estimators with different
support requirements. Bootstrap and jackknife return missing uncertainty for one treated
unit. The default fixed-weight jackknife also returns missing uncertainty when only one
control has nonzero weight; it fixes the unit and time weights rather than reoptimizing them.
Placebo requires more controls than treated units and constructs artificial treated groups from
controls. That construction needs its own scientific comparability argument. The package
vignette explicitly cautions about the single-treated placebo illustration. A default refusal
must not become a zero standard error, and a placebo standard deviation is not by itself a
randomization-test p-value. (synthdid contributors, 2024)
   The bootstrap retries until it has the requested count of nonmissing estimates, with no
attempt limit in the inspected loop. For two controls and two treated units, independent
sampling of four rows with replacement draws only controls or only treated units with
probability 2(1/2)4 = 1/8. Even if every mixed draw computes successfully, the expected
attempt count per acceptable composition is 8/7. Further numerical missing values can
increase work or prevent termination; exceptions have a distinct failure path. This calculation
quantifies composition rejection only. It is not a native timing result or a claim that every
problematic numerical fit returns missing rather than throwing an error. Record attempts,
exclusions, accepted draws and deadlines separately. (synthdid contributors, 2024; Causal
banking proposal project, 2026cf)
  Finally, a display method can change the inference presented to a reader. The default
summary calls bootstrap, a fast summary calls jackknife, and the formatter uses the fast
21.24. EconML reuse: preserve the target, history and sampling experiment                      263


summary with a 1.96 multiplier. A service that requests placebo variance and later parses
the formatted object could thus report a different uncertainty convention. The output should
carry the selected variance method, seed, successful and failed draws, weights and interval
convention as explicit fields. Native output, statistical validity and user-interface presentation
need separate checks. (synthdid contributors, 2024)


21.23.5     A proposed reuse decision with accountable costs

For this proposal, both packages are retained as reference implementations with conditional
routes to a Python or R worker. PyFixest is attractive for its formula interface and native
numerical backends; synthdid exposes a compact original block estimator and a separate
optimization reference. Direct adoption of either package as an unrestricted causal service
is deferred. Porting now would duplicate numerical, inferential and maintenance obligations
before a measured bottleneck establishes the benefit. A cohort-time DID estimator may be
preferable for staggered adoption, while SC, ordinary DID and SDID must be compared under
matched estimands and appropriate assumptions rather than a shared scalar output. (PyFixest
contributors, 2026; synthdid contributors, 2024)
   PyFixest declares MIT licensing; synthdid declares GPL version two or later or the supplied
three-clause BSD alternative. These source declarations and the retained notice texts do
not clear every distributed dependency or deployment artifact. The scientific owner must
approve the target, timing, support and uncertainty; the adapter maintainer must own identity
conversion, exact options, native oracles and upgrade regressions; the operator must account
for budgets, failure recovery and distribution requirements. (PyFixest contributors, 2026;
synthdid contributors, 2024)
   The first useful public or synthetic trial should therefore compare the complete request: eligi-
ble sample construction, estimation, uncertainty, failed requests, explanation and reproducible
cost accounting. Measure preparation time, model fitting, covariance or resampling, rejected
draws, worker recovery and maintenance separately. The exact examples here are input/output
oracles for such a trial, not evidence that it has already succeeded. A successful source-based
reuse decision can justify the prototype experiment while leaving native qualification, external
review and actual bank economics explicitly unresolved. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026bz,cf)


21.24      EconML reuse: preserve the target, history and sampling
           experiment
A bank choosing which customers should receive a servicing offer needs an effect for a specified
population and decision time. A flexible treatment-effect package can supply useful estimation
machinery, but the meaning of the output depends on the effect model, the variables used
for adjustment and the population over which predictions are averaged. A repeated-contact
application adds a second obligation: the computational history must preserve the customer’s
actual sequence of decisions. These obligations motivate a selective EconML reference profile,
with a separate contract for a future executable adapter.
   The primary comparison uses the Python repository py-why/EconML at commit
d625dd696ea28c62e6e4d8baea6e4154b98c30b4, dated 1 October 2026. The source declares
version 0.17.0, and its README records that version’s 31 July 2026 release. Seventeen selected
original files cover package notices, dependency declarations, static DML, DynamicDML,
common inference machinery and selected upstream tests. The immutable source revision is
264                                                                     Causal analysis for a universal bank


the identity used here; it does not authenticate every wheel or installation labelled 0.17.0.
The selected files support source-level conclusions, while an actual native fit and complete
estimator-family qualification remain separate work. (PyWhy contributors, 2026d)

21.24.1     A residual projection can answer a different banking question

Write A for an offer indicator, Y for its monetary outcome, X for pre-action characteristics used
to describe effect heterogeneity, and W for additional adjustment variables. In the selected DML
formulation, the nuisance functions are m(X, W ) = E[A | X, W ] and q(X, W ) = E[Y | X, W ].
Residuals Ae = A − m(X, W ) and Ye = Y − q(X, W ) enter the objective
                                                     n
                                                  1X

The selected documentation states a structural residual relationship and orthogonality condi-
tions; the R-learner implementation forms the corresponding residuals and final regression. A
causal reading additionally needs the stated identifying information and an appropriate effect-
function class Θ. An accurate nuisance model alone cannot correct a deliberately inadequate
effect model. Variables admitted to W also need causal justification: automatic adjustment
for a post-offer variable can change the question. (PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
  For a binary offer under a sufficient observed adjustment variable S, let e(S) = P (A = 1 | S)
and τ (S) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | S]. With exact nuisances and a constant final effect, differentiating
the population squared loss gives

The second equality uses the identified binary-treatment conditional mean relationship and a
positive residual variance. Thus the constant projection weights strata by treatment variation.
The population average effect instead uses the target population’s stratum probabilities. They
agree under a correct constant-effect model, or particular balancing conditions, but need not
agree when effect heterogeneity has been omitted. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ae)
   Consider a fully specified example with S ∼ Bernoulli(1/2), e(0) = 1/2, e(1) = 1/10, and
potential outcomes Y (a) = 100Sa in USD. The offer is assigned using only observed S, so
there is no hidden confounding in this construction. The two strata have effects USD 0 and

At an assumed offer cost of USD 35, offering to the whole target population has expected net
value USD 15 per customer. Labelling the constant projection as that population effect would
instead report net value 450/17 − 35 = −145/17, about USD −8.53. This is a consequence of
the specified misspecification and target mismatch, not a demonstrated EconML error under
