   The base ate method averages predicted contrasts over the supplied X rows. It cannot
recover missing heterogeneity merely by averaging the same fitted constant repeatedly. A
proposed adapter must therefore record the contrast, treatment scale and reference category,
effect-function class, prediction population and aggregation weights. A marginal effect per
unit of a continuous dose also needs conversion before being interpreted as the effect of a
finite banking action. These fields are part of the scientific request, not incidental serialization
metadata.(PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
21.24. EconML reuse: preserve the target, history and sampling experiment                          265


21.24.2     Cross-fitting, numerical conventions and uncertainty have different
            roles

The inspected final wrapper offers a feature–treatment-residual linear path and an alternative
weighted path. The latter divides the outcome residual by a signed treatment residual whose
magnitude is clipped below at 10−5 , and uses the original squared treatment residual as
a weight. That convention needs to be preserved in a numerical comparison; it does not
supply missing treatment support. The wrapper should report the convention and diagnostics
without presenting a finite result as evidence that every requested contrast has adequate
overlap.(PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
   The common learner uses group-aware folds when groups are supplied and a compatible
splitter is used; setting cv=1 explicitly disables cross-fitting. The selected static linear covariance
implementation offers HC0, HC1 and nonrobust choices. It uses a pseudoinverse in the variance
calculation and warns that inference is invalid when the design is rank deficient. Keeping
a borrower’s rows in one nuisance fold is useful for preventing a particular form of training
leakage. It does not itself change the covariance formula into a cluster or calendar estimator.
Rank and sampling warnings must therefore survive the proposed CLI or MCP boundary,
including when the backend returns numerical arrays. (PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
   A small construction makes the sampling issue explicit. Suppose four customer score
contributions all equal a shared fair shock Z ∈ {−1, 1}. Each has mean zero and variance one,
but their average equals Z and hence has variance one. A working calculation that treats the
four contributions as independent gives 1/4. Group labels in a fitting call cannot remove the
off-diagonal covariance terms. This example concerns a declared common-shock law; it is not
a measured coverage result for EconML. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ae)


21.24.3     A dynamic panel requires an explicit clock and complete histories

The DynamicDML guide considers treatments assigned over time with all relevant dynamic
confounders observed. Its displayed structural family combines a state transition linear in
previous treatment and state, a potentially nonlinear assignment policy, and an outcome
equation with baseline effect heterogeneity. The selected implementation targets the final-
period outcome, fits treatment effects backwards through the periods, and uses the first period’s
X for heterogeneity. Later X enters as time-varying controls. These are meaningful design
choices for a specified sequential problem; they do not establish an unrestricted hidden-state
servicing or optimal-policy value guarantee.(PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
   The code assigns a group’s period from its occurrence count in the input. Its prefit check
requires each group to have the same number of rows, but equal counts do not verify timestamps.
For example, the ordered rows (a, 0), (b, 1), (a, 1), (b, 0) contain two dates for each customer.
Occurrence counting nevertheless assigns customer b’s date 1 to period 0 and date 0 to period
1. A future adapter must require unique unit–time keys and canonical chronological histories
before making the call. It should also verify identical unit alignment across period slices,
because period-specific arrays are subsequently combined positionally. (PyWhy contributors,
2026d; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ae)
   An unbalanced panel raises an error whose text suggests padding the data. Padding has
scientific consequences: an absent contact, an unobserved repayment and an observed zero
are different events. The proposal therefore requires a declared observation and censoring
treatment before any such conversion. The same principle applies to weights. Although the
selected fit signature accepts sample weights and sample variances, its code warns that these
are unsupported and passes neither into fitting. A requested weighted population answer must
266                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


be refused under this profile, rather than returned as an unweighted result with its warning
discarded. (PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
  The dynamic analytic covariance does include cross-period within-unit score products. It
constructs a block sensitivity matrix and a block score covariance, then divides the resulting
sandwich by the number of groups. This deserves recognition as more than a rowwise static
variance calculation. It still does not establish covariance qualification for shared calendar
shocks across customers. The proposed request must declare both the history model and the
between-unit sampling law.(PyWhy contributors, 2026d)


21.24.4    The inspected bootstrap composition can change a history

The source exposes an additional issue that should be resolved before dynamic bootstrap
admission. The common CATE inference mapping selects BootstrapInference; that object
calls BootstrapEstimator.fit. The latter asks the estimator for strata. DynamicDML
returns its group labels. The bootstrap then draws rows with replacement inside each distinct
stratum and concatenates the draws. Consequently, this composition holds the original units
fixed and resamples their time rows internally. It is not a draw of whole ordered histories from
a population of units. This conclusion follows from the inspected source call path; no installed
backend was run here. (PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
  For an authored two-period history (0, 1), two independent uniform draws from its rows give
                                                                               1
               (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1),   P (original ordered history) = .         (21.49)
                                                                               4
Only (0, 1) preserves that history; for two independent unit draws the probability that both
histories survive is 1/16. Since the selected dynamic code infers time from occurrence order,
duplicated or reversed rows can be treated as successive periods. This enumeration establishes
a contract risk, not a measured coverage shortfall or a general indictment of the package’s
other inference modes.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ae)
   The selected upstream dynamic tests exercise shapes and inference choices, including a
two-draw bootstrap configuration, and compare selected panel layouts under automatic analytic
inference. Those layouts preserve the intended chronological information. The selected common
bootstrap tests exercise interval shapes, options and treatment-stratified examples. These
tests were inspected rather than executed. They do not supply the proposed whole-history
conformance evidence. The next prototype should instrument the pinned resampler with unit,
row and time identifiers, preserve the observed draws, and compare the actual path against an
independently specified panel sampling experiment. A whole-unit bootstrap would itself need
an appropriate independent-unit law; common calendar dependence cannot be repaired by
that substitution without a separate argument.(PyWhy contributors, 2026d)


21.24.5    Selective reference now, a testable adapter proposal next

EconML is a useful reference for flexible effect-function estimation and for comparison with
separately qualified DoubleML profiles. The proposed route is a narrow Python boundary
that preserves targets, histories, warnings and inference choices. Direct adoption of every
estimator and a wholesale port would enlarge the verification obligation without resolving the
scientific questions above. A transparent finite residual-moment implementation provides a
cheap numerical reference; an estimator with a different longitudinal contract may be preferable
when the selected dynamic structural family is inappropriate. Refusal remains necessary when
identification is unsupported.
21.25. Python effect estimators: population, clipping and the last covariance step            267


   The package’s root notice contains MIT terms and explicit BSD 3-Clause notices for specified
scikit-learn-derived tree and generalized-random-forest code. The pinned metadata declares
Python at least 3.9, eleven direct dependency bounds and optional integrations. Its native
build requirements include Cython at least 3.0.11 and below 3.3. These declarations inform
feasibility and maintenance costs; they are not a resolved environment, a complete transitive
notice inventory or proof that a future installation reproduces the selected source. A prototype
needs exact artifacts and applicable notices, with optional services enabled only when that
profile requires them. (PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
   The first public or synthetic prototype should keep one identified static target, an explicit
effect-function class and a fixed prediction population. It should reproduce the exact nuisance
oracle, test keyed reordering and treatment-scale conversions, and retain the misspecified
constant comparison. A subsequent dynamic prototype should add complete-history and
weight refusals, trace resampling, and compare declared independent-unit and common-shock
designs. Coverage, interval availability, width and total failed-run cost should be specified
before final evaluation. Such work can establish whether a narrow implementation merits an
expensive bank trial. The assumed USD amounts above motivate the decision; observed bank
prices, assignment truth and institutional acceptance remain later evidence. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026ae)


21.25       Python effect estimators: population, clipping and the
            last covariance step
A bank evaluating retention offers must first decide whether it wants the effect for all eligible
customers, for customers historically offered the intervention, or for a risk-defined population
facing a future decision. The same Python method name can hide different averaging, nuisance-
fitting and uncertainty choices. A reusable service must retain these choices in its request
and result. This section compares the already inspected EconML, DoubleML, CausalML,
Delicatessen and statsmodels paths, then develops two conversion hazards: propensity clipping
and the final covariance calculation. These selected paths do not exhaust Python’s effect-
estimation ecosystem or qualify continuous-dose, longitudinal or survival families by association.


21.25.1     Five routes with different scientific responsibilities

The selected EconML DML path residualizes outcome and treatment and fits an effect model.
Averaging predictions through an ATE interface retains that model’s restrictions; a misspecified
constant projection does not become the population effect merely because its output is called
an average. Its grouping for nuisance splits must also be distinguished from the sampling law
used for covariance. The earlier dynamic discussion shows why unit histories, encounter order
and bootstrap behavior need separate inspection.(PyWhy contributors, 2026d)
   The inspected Python DoubleML IRM route makes the score, external nuisance predic-
tions, folds and repetitions central objects. Its ATE and ATTE choices are distinct; the R
implementation and other model families retain their own contracts. Earlier matching of seven
configurations with fixed identical nuisance predictions and folds is useful bounded runtime
evidence, but does not qualify new learners, unrestricted dependence or a complete package
distribution. In particular, nuisance vectors must be joined by stable row keys when another
repository prepares them.(doubleml contributors, 2026)
   The selected CausalML T-learner instead fits arm-specific outcomes and reports contrasts
in a defined treatment-label order. An average over prediction rows depends on the chosen
268                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


prediction population. Its row bootstrap is not a borrower-history or common-date bootstrap,
and prediction percentiles and the default ATE interval formula are different objects. An
initial binary treatment profile avoids silently extending that limited review to every multiarm
variance calculation.(uber/causalml, 2026)
   Delicatessen is attractive when the proposal needs transparent stacked estimating equations
and joint nuisance/target inference. The inspected implementation differentiates the supplied
equations and builds a sandwich from their contribution columns. Those columns encode
the sampling units; the routine does not reconstruct household or calendar dependence from
labels supplied elsewhere. Its allowed pseudoinverse can make a calculation available without
establishing that the target is locally identified. Analytic small-model derivatives, rank checks
and a defensible sampling law are therefore part of the proposed use.(delicatessen project,
2026b,a)
   The selected statsmodels TreatmentEffect path supplies five point-treatment procedures:
inverse probability weighting (IPW), regression adjustment (RA), augmented IPW (AIPW),
AIPW with weighted outcome fits, and IPW regression adjustment. Its documented outcome
model is linear OLS. It combines target, outcome and selection moments for inference where
applicable. This is a useful parametric comparison route, with a different nuisance-fitting
architecture from a cross-fitted flexible learner. The inspected revision is 8278e2d218cc of
6 October 2026; the following claims concern its selected source, not an unverified later
release.(statsmodels project, 2026b; statsmodels contributors, 2026)
   For a proposal, the choice is consequently conditional. Use a declared DML or IRM profile
when its score and effect model match the question; retain arm-specific fits for a separately
qualified CATE comparison; use explicit stacked equations or the parametric statsmodels
paths as interpretable baselines. Reimplementing all five would duplicate model, variance and
failure semantics before a measured need exists. Original engines behind typed boundaries are
the preferred candidates, with executable admission limited to profiles that later pass their
source, environment and behavior checks. DoWhy, zEpid, causallib and CausalPy remain
complementary leads for target-specific inspection; naming them here grants no capability
finding.


21.25.2     All customers, treated customers and untreated customers

Let A ∈ {0, 1} denote the historical offer, X baseline information, Y (a) a contribution outcome
under intervention a, and τ (X) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X]. Under consistency, conditional
exchangeability and positivity in the chosen eligible population, τ (X) is identified by the
corresponding conditional outcome contrast. Three averages still differ:

                                      E[p(X)τ (X)]                    E[(1 − p(X))τ (X)]
      θall = E[τ (X)],   θtreated =                ,   θuntreated =                      ,    (21.50)
                                        E[p(X)]                          E[1 − p(X)]

where p(X) = Pr(A = 1 | X). The latter two expressions follow by conditioning on X and
using the historical assignment probabilities. They refer to historical populations; an effect for
a future targeting rule requires that rule’s population and information set.
   For an exact authored example, suppose low- and high-risk customers are equally common.
Their offer probabilities are 1/4 and 3/4, and their conditional effects are USD 20 and USD
80. Then θall = 50, θtreated = 65 and θuntreated = 35. At a stipulated incremental cost of
USD 55, the corresponding net averages are USD −5, USD 10 and USD −20. Selecting the
treated-population answer for an all-customer proposal could therefore reverse the investment
story. These are imposed-law calculations, not observed benefits or a reason to use historical
treatment as a future policy.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026au)
21.25. Python effect estimators: population, clipping and the last covariance step              269


   The inspected statsmodels methods expose these target distinctions through effect_group.
RA averages fitted potential outcomes over the selected rows. IPW-RA changes both arm-
fitting weights and prediction rows: for the treated target, for example, treated-arm weights
are one and control-arm weights are propensity odds. AIPW and AIPW-WLS share target-
specific potential-outcome terms. Their joint moments reorder selection scores to match the
grouped outcome rows. An adapter must preserve these masks and row identities through
every nuisance component, rather than rely on position after independent sorting. Arbitrary
user-weight arrays are outside the initial proposed profile until their point and inference paths
are separately traced.(statsmodels contributors, 2026)


21.25.3     Clipping an estimated probability changes the score

Consider the ordinary all-population AIPW score with proposed outcome functions ma (X)
and a working propensity q(X):

                                         A{Y − m1 (X)} (1 − A){Y − m0 (X)}
              ϕq = m1 (X) − m0 (X) +                  −                    .                 (21.51)
                                             q(X)            1 − q(X)

Write µa (X) = E[Y | A = a, X], and suppose 0 < q(X) < 1. Taking the expectation
conditional on X gives the exact identity
                                                       µ1 − m1 µ0 − m0
                                                                                    
               E[ϕq | X] − {µ1 (X) − µ0 (X)} = (p − q)        +                          .   (21.52)
                                                          q     1−q
The right side vanishes if q = p, or if both outcome functions equal their conditional means.
Replacing a correct p by a clipped q generally removes the first route to a zero bias. This is a
score identity; estimation error, sample splitting and asymptotic remainder control need their
own argument.
   At the inspected source revision, ps_bounds defaults to (0.001, 0.999) and probabilities
are clipped in both point calculations and selected joint-GMM moment paths. AIPW-WLS
also uses probability-derived outcome weights; the final target calculation still uses the same
population-specific augmented terms. Clipping can reduce numerical extremes, but it neither
establishes positivity in the source population nor manufactures the rare untreated observations
that inference needs. (statsmodels contributors, 2026)
   To isolate the consequence, take a constant true propensity p = 1999/2000, a clipped value
q = 999/1000, conditional means µ0 = 20, µ1 = 80, and deliberately incorrect working outcome
functions m0 = m1 = 0. The unclipped expected score is 60. The clipped expectation is
69970/999, approximately 70.04, with bias 10030/999. At a stipulated USD 65 cost, the true
mean margin is USD −5, whereas the clipped-score margin is 5035/999, approximately USD
5.04. Correct outcome functions would restore the expected score to 60 even with this clipping.
No native package was run, and no claim is made that a fitted OLS model in this example
would select the imposed zero functions. The example shows what a blanket statement about
robustness after clipping would have to rule out.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026au)
   A proposed service should therefore return the original probability range, clipping bounds
and counts, target weights and overlap diagnostics. If it trims observations or changes to
an overlap-weighted target, that is another population contract. A sensitivity display across
clipping choices is useful only when the underlying score and target are named; a visually
stable coefficient is not a proof of identification or calibrated uncertainty.
270                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


21.25.4    Follow inference through to the final moment covariance

The statsmodels class explicitly states that its preliminary outcome covariance option does
not control the final GMM result. The selected five wrappers call joint GMM without an
alternative weights_method; the default is cov. The final covariance code reads stored fit
options and recomputes moment covariance. HAC is a separate path requiring a lag choice
and kernel; the selected wrapper signatures do not expose that choice merely by accepting a
preliminary robust covariance label. Thus an HC1 label on an intermediate weighted regression
cannot establish household clustering or common-date uncertainty for the final causal effect.
(statsmodels contributors, 2026; statsmodels project, 2026a)
   Joint nuisance moments can account for estimation of the specified parametric nuisance
model under their sampling and regularity conditions. They do not justify silently substituting
arbitrary machine-learned predictions, a dependent panel law or a different target score. Record
the full moment vector, derivative matrix, numerical residuals and rank. An optimizer returning
a result establishes a numerical event, not the required orthogonality, model correctness or
sampling approximation.
  One small source detail illustrates why that numerical record matters. The selected
covariance routine centers a moment matrix by moms.mean(), a scalar mean over all entries.
Let each row mi ∈ Rk be one observation’s moments, let m̄ = n−1 i mi , and set c = k −1 1T m̄.
                                                                    P

Denote the second-moment matrices after column and scalar centering by Ccol and Cscalar .
Expansion gives
                             Cscalar − Ccol = (m̄ − c1)(m̄ − c1)T .                  (21.53)
Cross terms vanish because the column-centered rows sum to zero. If all moment means are
exactly zero, the two constructions agree. At nonzero residual means they can differ, especially
when moment scaling and an ill-conditioned derivative amplify a numerical discrepancy. This
identity is a qualification question, not a measured software defect or an allegation of invalid
intervals in every fit. (statsmodels contributors, 2026)
  For the authored moment rows (1, 0) and (3, 0), m̄ = (2, 0) and c = 1. The two matrices are
                                       !                           !
                                   1 0                      2 −1
                          Ccol =       ,       Cscalar =         .                       (21.54)
                                   0 0                     −1 1

The difference is the outer product of (1, −1) with itself. These rows deliberately do not solve
zero-mean moment equations. A conformance test should therefore include both an exact root
and controlled nonzero residuals, recording the derivative and covariance response rather than
concluding from this example that a particular native estimate is wrong. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026au)


21.25.5    A public prototype that tests meaning before scale

The first comparison should freeze one binary intervention, units, an eligible population and
independent sampling units. Use the exact target and clipping laws above, followed by generated
heterogeneous outcomes with known assignment, intentional nuisance misspecification and
weak overlap. Fix row keys, folds, repetitions, predictions and treatment-level order. For each
engine, compare the target expression and retained population before comparing numbers.
Evaluate uncertainty only under its declared law; then add separately justified clustered or
temporal regimes.
   The same contract should travel through library, CLI and MCP requests: target population,
treatment contrast, nuisance identities, weighting and uncertainty settings enter together. The
21.26. Java effect engines: uplift, graph-compatible slopes and decision value                271


response preserves point estimate, uncertainty, diagnostics and unavailable states separately.
Under an incorrect model or unsupported dependence law, a successful tool call must not
become a qualified causal claim. Package upgrades reopen the relevant conversion checks,
including row sorting, clipping defaults, target labels, covariance construction and error
handling.
  The proposed comparison can measure whether this semantic discipline helps analysts
detect consequential mistakes before an expensive bank experiment. Setup and dependency
maintenance, nuisance training, memory, conversions, diagnostics and repeated inference are
cost categories to measure, not current prices or savings. Complete distribution provenance
and rights, target-specific native fixtures and broader original-source coverage remain open.
Five reviewed implementations supply concrete choices and tests; they do not establish a
completed ecosystem survey or universal inference.


21.26       Java effect engines: uplift, graph-compatible slopes and
            decision value
A servicing team may wish to rank customers by the incremental benefit of an offer, while
a treasury analyst may wish to rank possible causes of a funding response. Both tasks can
return a number called an effect, but the corresponding software contracts differ. H2O-3
supplies a Java implementation of uplift forests with separate treated and control predictions.
Tetrad supplies graph-compatible regression effects and a stability-ranking construction. The
proposed common library should preserve these useful distinctions rather than turn every
numeric output into a causal confidence interval. The selected H2O source declares version
3.47.0 and a bleeding-edge profile at the pinned 20 September 2026 revision. Tetrad is
inspected at its pinned 22 September 2026 revision. These identities specify the primary text
being compared; they do not certify a released binary or a completed integration. (H2O.ai
contributors, 2026; Tetrad contributors, 2026c)


21.26.1     The target precedes the ranking algorithm

Let A ∈ {0, 1} denote a servicing action, Y (a) a binary desirable response by a declared
horizon, and X the information available before the action. The conditional effect of interest is

                                 τ (x) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x].                        (21.55)

For the proposed public comparison, assume consistency, no interference, conditional exchange-
ability of the two potential responses and A given X, and positive probability of both actions
in the relevant covariate region. Then E[Y (a) | X = x] = E[Y | A = a, X = x], so the
difference of the two conditional response means identifies (21.55). This follows by replacing
the conditioning on A under exchangeability and then using consistency; a treatment-column
name alone supplies neither step. The argument is conditional on these imposed assumptions,
not an assertion that a bank’s historical assignments satisfy them. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026aq)
  An exact example makes the cost of omitting assignment information visible. Suppose half
the customers are in each of two pre-action risk groups. Their action probabilities are 1/5 and
4/5, and their response probabilities are also 1/5 and 4/5. Within each group impose identical
potential responses, Y (1) = Y (0), so the causal effect is zero. If the group is omitted,
                   17                        8                                        9
 E[Y | A = 1] =       ,     E[Y | A = 0] =      ,     E[Y | A = 1] − E[Y | A = 0] =      . (21.56)
                   25                        25                                       25
272                                                                 Causal analysis for a universal bank


For example, the first conditional mean is [ 12 ( 15 )2 + 12 ( 45 )2 ]/( 12 ) = 17/25. With an assumed USD
100 value per incremental response and USD 20 action cost, the unadjusted contrast suggests
USD 16, while the stipulated causal margin is USD −20. This construction does not show that
an uplift forest fails when the confounder is supplied and the model is adequate. It shows why
assignment, covariates, eligibility and target population must accompany a proposed engine.
(Causal banking proposal project, 2026aq)

21.26.2      H2O’s Java training and scoring contract

The selected H2O builder accepts binomial response modeling and requires a categorical
treatment column with two levels, no missing treatment values and internal extrema zero
and one. These checks do not by themselves bind a business label such as “contacted” to
the intended treatment code. The wrapper must save the category domain and the desirable
response event. The selected training path explicitly rejects weights, offsets, a fold column
and a positive built-in cross-validation fold count. A proposed weighted observational analysis
therefore cannot silently pass its weights through this interface. External held-out evaluation
is a separate possible design, subject to its own sampling and training separation. (H2O.ai
contributors, 2026)
  The uplift tree uses a common split structure for both arms and retains two leaf predictions.
For an ordinary leaf with n1 , n0 treated and control observations and s1 , s0 positive responses,
the documented smoothing is
                                  s1 + 1              s0 + 1
                          pb1 =          ,    pb0 =          ,    b = pb1 − pb0 .
                                                                  u                              (21.57)
                                  n1 + 2              n0 + 2
The inspected ordinary split code constructs these smoothed rates; the forest and the selected
MOJO scorer average the two probability sums over trees and return their difference. The three
prediction entries are the uplift score, the treated positive-response prediction and its control
counterpart. A probability difference is not the probability that this particular customer
benefits: that individual statement additionally depends on the joint law of the two potential
responses. (H2O.ai contributors, 2026)
   For ten observations in each arm with eight versus two positive responses, the raw contrast
is 3/5, but (21.57) gives 3/4 − 1/4 = 1/2. At an assumed USD 100 response value and USD
40 cost, these two point calculations give USD 20 and USD 10. The difference is an explicit
consequence of smoothing, not empirical evidence of which estimate is better. If the control
arm has no observations, the same formula supplies 1/2 for its probability. That numerical
value does not identify an unobserved control response. The result contract should report
the missing support alongside any regularized prediction. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026aq)
   Missing-feature routing and a tree that never splits require additional qualification. In
the selected nonsplitting-root branch, the two leaf values are taken from the two entries of
priorClassDist. The route and meaning of that inherited object must be traced before
treating this branch as an arm-specific estimate. The selected upstream depth-zero test checks
that a model exists; it does not resolve that semantic question. Other inspected tests do assert
prediction-column names and Java/MOJO scoring comparisons, which are useful acceptance
designs but have not been executed in this work. (H2O.ai contributors, 2026)

21.26.3      A split criterion needs an executable mathematical identity

H2O documents KL, squared Euclidean and chi-squared divergences for uplift splits. The
selected default resolves AUTO to KL, and the histogram constructor selects the corresponding
21.26. Java effect engines: uplift, graph-compatible slopes and decision value                      273


divergence object. The inspected KL method contains the expression
      p * log2(p / q == 0 ?       epsilon :     q).

Here p and q abbreviate its two probability arguments. The division and comparison determine
the conditional branch passed to the logarithm; the expression is not the documented p log(p/q).
For p = q = 1/2, each selected literal contribution is −1/2, so the two-class node sum is −1.
The documented KL sum is zero. The discrepancy persists regardless of the logarithm base
used for the documented zero. (H2O.ai contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project,
2026aq)
   This is a bounded source-and-arithmetic finding. It is not a report of an executed Java
failure, a statement about all H2O versions, or a measurement of the resulting fitted forest.
The next public prototype should evaluate the selected method, normalization and actual split
choices on equal probabilities, zero-support boundaries and asymmetric arm counts. A literal
port would carry the discrepancy; replacing the formula without preserving the original would
create a new algorithm that needs separate review. An alternative divergence is a candidate to
compare, not an already-qualified repair. (H2O.ai contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal
project, 2026aq)

21.26.4     Average predictions and AUUC answer different questions

The selected metric builder accumulates predicted uplift values and reports their averages
over all retained rows, treated rows and control rows as ATE, ATT and ATC. It skips rows
with a missing outcome. Thus both the prediction function and the retained-row population
matter; the labels do not by themselves establish an independently identified or unbiased
causal estimate. For fixed scores (0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4) with the first two rows treated, the three
averages are 1/4, 3/20, 7/20. Excluding the fourth row because its outcome is missing changes
the all-row and control averages to 1/5 and 3/10, while the treated average remains 3/20. A
production result must explain such changes in its population rather than merely label them
ATE. (H2O.ai contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026aq)
   For a prefix of customers ordered by a score, let N1 , N0 be arm counts and S1 , S0 positive-
response counts. The selected AUUC implementation uses
                        S1   S0                        N1
                   L=      −    ,        Q = S1 − S0      ,      G = (N1 + N0 )L,               (21.58)
                        N1 N0                          N0
for lift, qini and gain. These expressions require support in the relevant arms. Quantile
thresholds determine bins; its area convention is a sum of the cumulative curve value times the
bin frequency, divided by n + 1. This convention must be fixed in a cross-engine comparison.
The selected implementation replaces a sole NaN curve value with zero and otherwise calls an
interpolation helper for NaNs. Such display processing does not create the missing assignment
information. (H2O.ai contributors, 2026)
   Consider four ordered bins, each containing one treated and one control customer, with
observed response pairs (1, 0), (0, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1). Their cumulative qini values are 1, 1, 1, 0; the
stated rectangle convention gives 2(1 + 1 + 1 + 0)/9 = 2/3, and the endpoint random-reference
curve is zero. Scores (0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1) and their doubled values produce exactly the same order
and these same bins. Their average predictions are 1/4 and 1/2. Thus a matched ranking
curve does not establish probability-difference calibration. This fixed-label arithmetic does not
assert any potential-outcome law for the eight customers. A causal policy comparison needs
an independent design, assignment support, a suitable value estimator and uncertainty for its
sampling unit. Reusing a validation sample repeatedly to choose a threshold also needs to be
included in that evaluation design. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026aq)

21.26.5     Tetrad’s effects retain direction, graph ambiguity and failure

Tetrad’s selected IDA interface works with continuous data and legal partially directed acyclic
graphs. It enumerates admissible local parent choices and computes regression coefficients
using covariance submatrices, with indices matched by variable names. This preserves a
set of candidate linear slopes, not a general nonlinear heterogeneous response surface. The
unchanged IDA source also underlies the earlier identification discussion; its reuse here does
not add an independent algorithmic coverage result. A selected singular inverse catch returns
zero, while other candidate exceptions can be logged and omitted. These branches motivate a
typed distinction among a graph-implied zero, a numerical failure and an incomplete candidate
collection. (Tetrad contributors, 2026c)
   For example, if two regressors are identical, a covariance system can determine only βX +βZ =
1. The solutions (0, 1), (1, 0), (−1, 2) give the same fitted combination. Returning zero for the
first coefficient does not show that its causal effect is identified as zero. This exact algebra is a
proposed numerical qualification case; it has not been run through Tetrad. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026aq)
   CStaR extends the comparison from a graph effect set to a magnitude ranking across
subsamples. Its selected code takes the minimum of the absolute candidate effects. For
candidates {−2, −1/2}, this is 1/2, whereas taking the absolute value of the signed minimum
gives 2. The first is the inspected implementation’s intended magnitude summary, but neither
operation retains the sign. At a hypothetical USD 100 value per response unit and USD
20 action cost, the two signed candidates imply margins −220 and −70. Misreading the
minimum magnitude as a positive benefit gives USD 30. An integration should retain the
signed candidates and their units beside the ranking summary. (Tetrad contributors, 2026c;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026aq)
   The selected default uses thirty half-samples without replacement; its bootstrap option
also draws half the rows, with replacement. Neither route alone specifies branch-cluster or
shared-calendar resampling. The ranking uses an inclusive cutoff at the requested bracket
times the number of effect variables. With one effect, bracket one, and three equal positive
magnitudes, all three meet the cutoff. If this happens in every subsample, each has selection
frequency one. That frequency is a property of the construction; it is not automatically a
probability of causation or an interval’s coverage. The displayed PCER calculation uses the
displayed rank as its q argument. Its presence does not verify the theoretical assumptions
behind an error bound for the proposed data. The source also states that required and
forbidden edge knowledge is not respected by this class. A business constraint must therefore
be preserved through a verified route or explicitly refused. (Tetrad contributors, 2026c; Causal
banking proposal project, 2026aq)


21.26.6     A proposed adoption route and a public qualification experiment

H2O is a candidate for an original Java training worker with a separate MOJO scoring
service; Tetrad is a candidate for graph-effect and stability-ranking reference services. The two
should expose different result types through the library, CLI and MCP surfaces. A request
should bind row and variable identities, action and positive-event mappings, horizon, eligible
population, graph type, original units, sampling law, source revision and executable artifact
hash. A response should separate prediction, causal estimand, graph candidates, ranking
metric, numerical status and qualified uncertainty. None of these proposed Java services has
been implemented or admitted by this source review. (H2O.ai contributors, 2026; Tetrad
contributors, 2026c)
21.27. Native causal forests: preserve the target before accelerating it                       275


   Preserving the original engines is preferable as the first comparison because it makes a source-
to-output discrepancy observable before maintaining a port. H2O’s training and generated-
model modules have different dependencies; the generated-model build’s compatibility setting
is not a statement about every training deployment. Its selected MOJO subclasses both declare
format 1.40, but use different threshold-key strings in their writer and reader. Superclass and
default handling must be traced and a full archive roundtrip tested before concluding whether
this affects scoring or metadata. The root Apache 2.0 declaration and Tetrad’s GPLv3-or-later
source headers are relevant inputs to reuse review; neither a process boundary nor a source
notice resolves the complete distribution and dependency obligations. (H2O.ai contributors,
2026; Tetrad contributors, 2026c)
   The first public experiment should therefore use frozen synthetic mechanisms with known
action effects, followed by appropriately documented public data. The synthetic suite should
include the confounded zero-effect law, missing arm support, constant/root-only trees, missing
features, category and column permutations, the equal-probability split witness, signed graph
effects, singular covariance and ranking ties. Separate checks should match engine and MOJO
predictions and preserve keyed data through each transport. After that semantic comparison,
a fresh held-out study can evaluate calibration, ranking, policy value and repeated-fit costs
under declared independent or dependent sampling laws. No bank experiment is required to
establish whether these public prototype steps merit the next investment. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026aq)
   This review supplies two concrete Java profiles rather than an absence finding from an empty
search. Saved complementary repository leads and search remainder still need original-source
inspection. Foundational papers named in upstream comments need genuine local PDFs and
technical review before their theorems are attributed here. Those tasks can proceed alongside
the pinned public prototype design; their openness does not justify converting a score, a
frequency or a successful API call into an unsupported causal guarantee. (H2O.ai contributors,
2026; Tetrad contributors, 2026c)


21.27       Native causal forests: preserve the target before acceler-
            ating it
A servicing team considering different offers for different risk groups needs more than an
accurate forecast of repayment. It needs a contrast between actions, a declared population
over which to average that contrast, and uncertainty that corresponds to the decision. A C++
implementation can reduce computation while changing any of these meanings at a language
boundary. The useful comparison therefore starts with the statistical object and follows it
through wrappers, native learning, stored draws and portfolio aggregation. Four inspected
lineages provide complementary designs: generalized random forests, bcf, XBCF and flexBCF.
Their common use of trees does not make their targets, priors or intervals interchangeable.(grf
contributors, 2026a; bcf contributors, 2026; xbcf contributors, 2026; flexbcf contributors, 2026)
   The comparison binds grf 2.6.1 to its 30 April 2026 commit, bcf 2.0.2 to 26 September
2023, XBCF’s declared 0.1.2 source to 25 June 2024, and flexBCF 1.0.3 to 1 December 2025.
These are inspected versions preceding the literature cutoff, not assertions about the newest
release. The native grf boundary analysis developed elsewhere in this monograph remains
applicable: the initial proposal favors a qualified R process around its native core, rather
than a new direct embedding or port. This comparison extends the alternatives and semantic
contracts; it supplies no runtime qualification.(grf contributors, 2026a; bcf contributors, 2026;
xbcf contributors, 2026; flexbcf contributors, 2026)

21.27.1     A conditional effect and a dose slope answer different questions

For a binary action A, let Y (a) be the potential outcome under action a and X permitted
baseline information. Under consistency, no interference, conditional ignorability and overlap,
the conditional average effect is
                                τ (x) = E{Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x}.                             (21.59)
The inspected grf wrapper describes this binary target, estimates or accepts aligned outcome
and treatment nuisance predictions, and residualizes before forest fitting. Honesty separates
split selection from leaf estimation. The native trainer checks whether the sample and honesty
fractions leave observations in both parts; its tree trainer splits sampled clusters and repopulates
estimation leaves. Computational separation does not establish ignorability or validate a
treatment clock.(grf contributors, 2026a)
  For continuous treatment the wrapper documents a conditional covariance-to-variance slope,
                                            Cov(Y, A | X = x)
                                   s(x) =                     .                               (21.60)
                                             Var(A | X = x)
It cannot be substituted automatically for E{Y (a1 ) − Y (a0 ) | X = x}. In an authored example,
randomize A uniformly over {−1, 0, 1} and set Y (a) = a2 . The covariance numerator is zero
by symmetry, while the action contrast from zero to one is one. Neither confounding nor
a computational failure is needed for the discrepancy: the requested objects differ. A bank
seeking the response to a specific change in fee or service intensity must request that dose pair
or justify a response model under which the slope represents it. This is an exact semantic
witness, not a run of grf.(grf contributors, 2026a; Causal banking proposal project, 2026az)
   The native prediction strategy solves a weighted local moment ratio. Its instrumental im-
plementation divides an outcome–instrument covariance expression by a treatment–instrument
expression. A near-zero denominator is a scientific and numerical warning. The inspected vari-
ance code groups trees, skips groups with empty leaves and corrects between- and within-group
quantities. Its objective-Bayes correction avoids negative variance estimates; that label does
not make its output draws from a Bayesian causal forest. An adapter must retain effective
group counts, denominator diagnostics and unsupported variance status. Full upstream guard
behavior requires a qualified native trial.(grf contributors, 2026a)

21.27.2     Why regularizing prediction can distort a treatment contrast

The genuine inspected BCF original is the 33-page arXiv version 4 of 13 November 2019 by
Hahn, Murray and Carvalho; it is not asserted to be byte-identical to the later journal article.
Under its stated assumptions the conditional mean is modeled as
                          E(Y | X = x, A = a) = µ{x, π
                                                     b (x)} + aτ (x),                         (21.61)
with separate tree priors for the prognostic and treatment functions. The fitted propensity
π
b informs the response-surface prior. This addresses regularization-induced confounding:
shrinkage of the prognostic function can leave treatment to explain outcome variation associated
with selection. A propensity feature does not imply an orthogonal estimating equation or
double robustness. The paper explicitly disclaims double robustness for its natural Bayesian
estimates and discusses sensitivity to alternative propensity estimates.(Hahn et al., 2019)
   A project derivation isolates the mechanism. Let X be equally likely to be −1 or 1, with
treatment probabilities 1/4 and 3/4 respectively. Set Y (a) = 2X for both actions, so the true
causal effect is zero and overlap holds. Write Z = A − 1/2. Minimize
                           E{(Y − βX − tZ)2 } + λβ 2 ,        λ = 3/4.                        (21.62)
21.27. Native causal forests: preserve the target before accelerating it                     277


Only the prognostic coefficient is penalized. Here E(X 2 ) = 1, E(Z 2 ) = 1/4 and E(XZ) = 1/4.
The treatment normal equation gives t = 2 − β; the prognostic equation then gives
                                          2(3/4)
                                    β=           = 1,        t = 1.                      (21.63)
                                         3/4 + λ
The apparent treatment effect is produced by the stipulated shrinkage. The exact reference
verifies both normal equations. This motivates studying prior design, treatment selection and
nuisance learning jointly. It is not a theorem that every regularized learner fails or that BCF
necessarily repairs every selection mechanism.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026az; Hahn
et al., 2019)
   The bcf wrapper exposes separate prognostic and moderation matrices, supplied propensities
and their placement in either or both ensembles. Prior-scale choices and outcome standard-
ization belong to the fitted model. A port that copies trees but drops a scale prior changes
the procedure. flexBCF explicitly distinguishes its default model from bcf in scale priors,
treatment-recoding behavior and relative regularization of the two ensembles. A claim of speed
or flexibility therefore cannot establish identical inference. A prototype comparison must freeze
each configuration and compare a common target.(bcf contributors, 2026; flexbcf contributors,
2026)


21.27.3     Three meanings of weight must remain separate

The bcf argument w represents likelihood precision: the conditional variance is σ 2 /wi . The
native source uses these weights in tree updates and residual sums. They do not define the
population for a reported effect. For a declared cohort I and target weights qi , a draw-wise
average is

Likelihood precision, target weights and cohort selection require different fields. The target
can concern eligible customers, treated customers or a transported population; its meaning
cannot be recovered from an unlabeled vector.(bcf contributors, 2026; flexbcf contributors,

   For two equally represented groups with effects −2 and 6, the population effect is 2. Reusing
precisions 1 and 9 as target weights gives 26/5 = 5.2. If these effects are stipulated dollar
gains and the offer costs USD 3 per customer, the population margin is USD -1 while the
reweighted margin is USD 2.20. Better observation precision does not authorize replacing the
eligible customer mix.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026az)
   In grf, equalizing cluster weights changes training samples and average-effect weights. The
documented training rule draws equal numbers of units from sampled clusters, using the
smallest cluster size. This option is incompatible with supplying the ordinary sample-weight
vector in that interface. Balancing branches instead of customers changes both the target
and parts of learning; it cannot be implemented by relabeling a final average while leaving an
incompatible training run untouched.(grf contributors, 2026a)


21.27.4     Joint draws, scale restoration and persistence

A Bayesian portfolio interval averages customer effects within a common posterior draw
before summarizing portfolio draws. Averaging individual interval endpoints generally differs.
Consider two equally weighted customers with joint draws (−2, 6) and (6, −2). Each customer’s
marginal support is [−2, 6], but every portfolio draw is exactly 2. Averaging marginal endpoints
278                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


discards the perfect negative dependence. At the assumed USD 3 cost every portfolio margin
is USD -1. Two artificial draws illustrate algebra; they establish neither convergence nor
calibration.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026az)
   The inspected flexBCF native SATT routine evaluates each stored ensemble on supplied
rows, averages within the draw and then calculates quantiles. Its weighted companion divides
by the supplied weight sum. The routine name does not select treated rows: cohort selection
must already be reflected in its inputs. These selected functions do not settle how all public
callers validate empty cohorts, nonfinite weights, zero sums or category levels. The proposed
adapter must require explicit cohort and weight contracts; complete caller tracing remains
open.(flexbcf contributors, 2026)
  Scale parameters must remain aligned by draw. In inspected bcf prediction an ensemble
        (s)
output gi contributes
                                (s)       (s)  (s) (s)
                               τi = sY {b1 − b0 }gi ,                            (21.65)
where sY is the outcome scale. A treatment contrast receives no added outcome mean. XBCF
also restores a treatment draw using outcome scale and its treatment-scale difference. If raw
draws are 1, 2, sY = 10, and scale differences are 1/2, 2, restored draws are 5, 40 with mean
22.5. Omitting the contrast factor gives mean 15. At an assumed USD 20 action cost these
imply USD 2.50 and USD -5 margins. Multiplying mean raw output by mean scale also loses
their posterior dependence.(bcf contributors, 2026; xbcf contributors, 2026; Causal banking
proposal project, 2026az)
   bcf documents draws by units, whereas selected XBCF outputs use units by iterations.
Transport needs unit, chain and retained-draw identifiers rather than a guessed transpose.
bcf’s wrapper serializes tree samples for later prediction; suppressing file output prevents that
path. Its selected prediction wrapper requires both treatment labels, a restriction to reconcile
for a one-cohort request. The chain executor sets one core while retaining within-chain thread
controls. These are persistence and execution questions for an adapter, not measured speed or
scalability.(bcf contributors, 2026; xbcf contributors, 2026)


21.27.5     Static hazards define focused prototype tests

In pinned XBCF’s combined R predictor, the default propensity branch refers to z, which is not
a formal argument. The function assigns predictions to obj1 and obj2, then reads obj before
its local assignment at the end. The separate treatment-draw predictor uses its own local
object. These are particular source paths requiring isolated reconciliation, not failures observed
by executing the package. An enclosing environment, later release or different entrypoint must
not silently replace the inspected route.(xbcf contributors, 2026)
  In the selected Python wrapper, the zero-outcome-variance branch constructs ValueError
without raising it, and adjusted fitted draws are assigned inside the standardization branch.
Prediction has separate restoration logic. Tests should cover constant outcomes, both stan-
dardization settings, fit-versus-predict parity and return formats. The native loop alternates
prognostic and treatment updates and updates scales; stored output must be checked against
wrapper order. Source resemblance does not prove equivalent R and Python interfaces.(xbcf
contributors, 2026)
   The selected flexBCF trainer derives the control count from prognostic and treatment design
sizes and offsets treatment updates accordingly. Its wrapper transposes inputs and passes
the treatment indicator. Training order and treatment-specific rows therefore require tracing
through public callers and documentation. Assuming the same row layout across all four
libraries would hide a consequential boundary error.(flexbcf contributors, 2026)
21.27. Native causal forests: preserve the target before accelerating it                      279


21.27.6     Historical performance supports an experiment

The BCF paper offers evidence for its design and relevant limitations. Its targeted-selection
example improves bias and coverage over ordinary BART under that simulation; broader
experiments do not give uniformly nominal coverage. In the retrospective ACIC 2016 compari-
son, Table 4 reports nominal 95% interval coverage of 82% for BCF, 88% for propensity-score
BART, 81% for BART and 58% for the compared causal random forest. BCF’s mean interval
length is 0.026 versus 0.055 for that forest. Shorter intervals and lower estimation error coexist
with undercoverage. The paper discusses this limitation and supplies no general frequentist
coverage theorem for its credible intervals.(Hahn et al., 2019)
   These are historical reported results, not a project reproduction or ranking of today’s
implementations. They motivate public experiments reporting effect error, coverage, width,
failures and decision consequences together. Known counterfactual generators can vary
overlap, targeted selection, effect sparsity, response nonlinearity, propensity misspecification
and dependence. Public benchmarks provide complementary designs whose versions, targets
and access conditions must be fixed. Failed fits and invalid requests stay in the denominator.
Posterior uncertainty, Monte Carlo error and repeated-sampling coverage must remain separate:
more draws do not repair a wrong causal target or unmeasured confounding.(Hahn et al., 2019;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026az)


21.27.7     Integration choices and the remaining census

For the proposal, grf remains a candidate through its analyzed R/native boundary. bcf is a
candidate for a process-based Bayesian adapter with explicit priors and persisted trees. XBCF
warrants a performance comparison after selected wrapper paths are reconciled. flexBCF
is a distinct alternative needing prior, coding, training-order and cohort contracts. Porting
would transfer responsibility for random numbers, tree updates, priors, draw alignment and
persistence. The initial approach should preserve each native model behind a typed adapter
and qualify a narrow target before considering a port. These are reasoned proposal choices, not
completed reuse admissions.(grf contributors, 2026a; bcf contributors, 2026; xbcf contributors,
2026; flexbcf contributors, 2026)
   Inspected declarations are GPL-family terms for grf, bcf and flexBCF and Apache 2.0
for XBCF. They identify a rights review rather than completing one: dependencies, notices,
distribution and embedding remain to be examined. A separate process does not automatically
settle licensing obligations. Bounded repository discovery also found SparseBCF, time-series,
multivariate, survival and other candidates with CRAN mirrors. Names are leads; lineage,
cutoff availability, originals and capabilities remain uninspected. Mirrors do not count as
independent implementations.(grf contributors, 2026a; bcf contributors, 2026; xbcf contributors,
2026; flexbcf contributors, 2026)
   Library, CLI and MCP requests should carry action contrast or slope, cohort, clock, source
version, nuisance provenance, weight roles, uncertainty type and refusal reasons. An agent
can help formulate requests and inspect diagnostics, but cannot relabel posterior quantiles
as calibrated confidence limits. These exact witnesses justify inexpensive public prototype
tests before costly bank trials. Broader coverage, method originals, rights, native parity and
calibrated decision performance remain prerequisites for a stronger adoption claim.

21.28      Reusing the R forest package: nuisance provenance and
           population choice
A bank considering a retention offer needs an effect for the customers it intends to contact.
The R package grf is a useful reference candidate because its wrapper connects nuisance fitting,
forest prediction and average-effect estimation. That wrapper is part of the statistical method.
A proposed CLI or MCP interface must preserve its population and score construction when
exposing the underlying C++ engine. The R package and native core share one implementation
lineage; their different deployment routes do not supply independent corroboration. We select
the original R package as a bounded reference candidate, with an isolated worker considered for
a future prototype. The earlier native-boundary analysis explains the ownership and persistence
obligations; here the additional concern is the meaning of supplied nuisance predictions and
target options.(grf contributors, 2026b; GRF contributors, 2026a)
   The selected source declares version 2.6.1 at the 30 April 2026 commit. Its requirements
include R 3.5.0 or later, C++17, GNU make, Rcpp and RcppEigen, with imports including
DiceKriging, lmtest, Matrix and sandwich. A named maintainer and issue tracker establish
a maintenance contact route, not a service commitment. The DESCRIPTION declares
GPL-3; file-level terms and dependencies need to accompany any distribution decision. The
inspected license distinguishes running a program from conveying it. An isolated process is an
engineering boundary and does not by itself settle the licensing of a distributed system. These
observations justify retaining the original as a reference without claiming a qualified installed
environment.(grf contributors, 2026b)


21.28.1     What the nuisance inputs must mean

Let A ∈ {0, 1} denote the offer, X information available before assignment, and Y the
outcome over a fixed horizon. Define e(x) = P (A = 1 | X = x) and µa (x) = E[Y | A =
a, X = x]. Consistency, no interference, conditional exchangeability and positivity give
τ (x) = µ1 (x) − µ0 (x) the causal interpretation. These are substantive assumptions about
assignment and observation; fitting the forest does not verify them.
   The wrapper’s outcome nuisance is the marginal regression m(x) = E[Y | X = x] =
(1 − e(x))µ0 (x) + e(x)µ1 (x). Missing nuisance vectors are estimated by auxiliary regression
forests. Supplied scalar values are replicated, and supplied vectors are checked for length.
Such checks cannot establish that a prediction uses only permitted information or that it was
estimated without access to the evaluation outcome. The interface therefore needs the feature
clock, row identity and fitting provenance as well as the numbers. Initially, the proposed worker
retains the package’s ordinary nuisance path or an explicitly known randomized propensity;
externally fitted nuisance vectors require a separate qualification profile.(grf contributors,
2026b)
   Write m⋆ , e⋆ , t⋆ for fixed proposed nuisance functions, with 0 < e⋆ < 1. The binary score
reconstructed by the source is
                                       A − e⋆
                          Γ = t⋆ +                {Y − m⋆ − t⋆ (A − e⋆ )}.                   (21.66)
                                     e⋆ (1 − e⋆ )
Suppressing x, define u⋆0 = m⋆ − e⋆ t⋆ and u⋆1 = m⋆ + (1 − e⋆ )t⋆ . Substituting these definitions
yields Γ = u⋆1 − u⋆0 + A(Y − u⋆1 )/e⋆ − (1 − A)(Y − u⋆0 )/(1 − e⋆ ). For a fresh observation,
conditional on these fixed functions, direct expectation gives the project identity
                                                   ⋆
                                                   u1 − µ1    u⋆ − µ0
                                                                         
                                            ⋆
                        E[Γ | X] − τ = (e − e)               + 0             .               (21.67)
                                                       e⋆      1 − e⋆
21.28. Reusing the R forest package: nuisance provenance and population choice               281


Indeed, the two residual terms have conditional expectations e(µ1 − u⋆1 )/e⋆ and (1 − e)(µ0 −
u⋆0 )/(1 − e⋆ ), and collecting errors gives the identity. The conditional bias vanishes when the
propensity is correct or when both reconstructed treatment-specific regressions are correct.
Correctness of m⋆ alone is a different condition. Estimation rates, sample reuse and dependence
still govern whether a fitted procedure has valid uncertainty; this fixed-function calculation
supplies no finite-sample guarantee.(grf contributors, 2026b; Causal banking proposal project,
2026bb)
   Consider a deliberately simple law with no varying X: P (A = 1) = 1/4, Y (0) = 0 and
Y (1) = 2. The true marginal outcome mean is 1/2 and the effect is two. Supply the correct
values m⋆ = 1/2 and t⋆ = 2, but use e⋆ = 1/2. The reconstructed regressions become −1/2
and 3/2, although the true regressions are zero and two. Equation (21.66) gives scores one for
controls and three for treated observations, so their population mean is 3/2. Even a correct
marginal outcome regression and correct conditional-effect input do not restore the intended
mean in this example.
   For comparison, the correct propensity e⋆ = 1/4 with deliberately wrong m⋆ = 3 and t⋆ = 0
produces scores four and minus four, whose mean is two. Alternatively, keeping the wrong
propensity 1/2 but setting m⋆ = 1 and t⋆ = 2 reconstructs the correct outcome surfaces
and makes both scores two. Exact rational enumeration checks these cases and the bias
identity on 108 combinations. These are supplied-input witnesses, not claims that the fitted
grf algorithm generates these nuisance values. Their practical purpose is to prevent an adapter
from equating a correct outcome model with an unlabeled marginal prediction vector.(Causal
banking proposal project, 2026bb)


21.28.2     An overlap recommendation changes the target

The function average_treatment_effect exposes all, treated, control and overlap populations.
Under the preceding causal assumptions, their common representation is

                 E[q(X)τ (X)]
          θq =                ,     q(X) ∈ {1, e(X), 1 − e(X), e(X)(1 − e(X))}.          (21.68)
                   E[q(X)]

All denominators must be positive. The source warns when estimated propensities become
extreme and suggests alternative targets or filtering. A warning does not prove a failure of
identification, establish a universal threshold or authorize changing the requested population.
A business owner deciding about all eligible customers must explicitly reconsider the question
before receiving an effect for customers with greater assignment overlap.(grf contributors,
2026b)
   In a two-group hypothetical bank, let each group contain half the eligible population.
Treatment propensities are 1/2 and 1/10, and group effects are USD −4 and USD 12. The
all-customer effect is USD 4. The treated and control population effects are respectively USD
−4/3 and USD 44/7. Overlap weights are 1/4 and 9/100, giving

                                          (1/4)(−4) + (9/100)12  4

                                               1/4 + 9/100       17

With an assumed offer cost of USD 2 per recipient, the all-customer margin is USD 2, while
the overlap-population margin is USD −30/17, approximately USD −1.76. Both calculations
are correct for their stated populations. Applying the second margin to the original customer
population would be a change of decision target, not merely a more stable computation of the
same quantity. These dollar figures are reproducible assumptions and do not measure a bank’s
return.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bb)
282                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The implementation also makes the method label consequential. For the all-population
AIPW path, it aggregates scores and computes centered cluster sums for the standard error.
The overlap path instead regresses the outcome residual on the treatment residual, with an
intercept and observation weights, and uses a sandwich variance. Inside that branch the
AIPW/TMLE method choice is ignored, although the earlier TMLE guard rejects clustered or
sample-weighted inputs. A wrapper should report the actual residual-regression method and
preserve the combination restrictions. It should not label an overlap result as an all-population
augmented estimate merely because the request said AIPW.(grf contributors, 2026b)
   The population logic of that residual regression can be checked without executing the
package. With correct m and e, the treatment residual has conditional mean zero, and
E[(A − e)(Y − m) | X] = e(1 − e)τ (X) while E[(A − e)2 | X] = e(1 − e). The population
regression coefficient therefore equals the overlap effect in Equation (21.68), provided its
denominator is nonzero. This argument explains the target. It does not prove that estimated
residuals, a particular sandwich correction or a small sample deliver calibrated intervals.


21.28.3    Qualification follows the complete statistical request

The initial proposal profile is one binary action and complete independent customer rows, with
a fixed outcome horizon and all-population AIPW target. Clusters, sample weights, continuous
actions, instrumental variables, survival, multiarm comparisons and repeated policies need
separate profiles. The source exposes several of these methods, but their presence in a
dispatcher does not transfer their assumptions or uncertainty guarantees to the initial bank use.
A cohort chosen after observing treatment or outcome also changes the evaluation problem; the
documented subset warning recommends selection using baseline features. Adaptive selection
using fitted effects needs its own honest evaluation design.(grf contributors, 2026b)
   Prediction outputs need equally careful typing. With no newdata, the causal-forest wrapper
uses stored or recomputed out-of-bag predictions; explicitly supplying the training matrix as
new data follows a different prediction path. Those calls are not interchangeable evidence
of sample separation. The documented CATE variance, R-loss diagnostic and Monte Carlo
excess error answer different questions. Increasing tree count can address forest simulation
instability without creating exchangeability, recovering unsupported customers or resolving
dependence. Model serialization must also account for the stored original observations and
nuisance vectors.(grf contributors, 2026b)
   The future worker should retain target identity, actual estimator, customer keys, column
order, units, time horizon, warnings, source/dependency versions and nuisance provenance. It
must distinguish unavailable execution, an unsupported request, a refused profile, an audited
nonidentification finding and a failed computation. Failed or nonfinite output must not silently
publish a partial estimate. Qualification would compare the original package against exact
score and aggregation fixtures, test OOB and new-data routing, preserve warnings and refusal
behavior, and check persistence and process failures. Public generated laws can then assess
bias, interval coverage, widths and failed requests before an expensive bank trial. The small
examples above establish the logic of that experiment, not its outcome.
  Porting the wrapper or embedding its native core remains an unattractive initial route
because it transfers nuisance, targeting, uncertainty and lifetime responsibilities without
an observed benefit. Bayesian bcf, XBCF and flexBCF remain substantive comparators
with different priors, uncertainty and restoration contracts, as developed in the preceding
comparison. An original R worker is therefore the preferred prototype candidate, conditional
on its environment and rights review. The measured comparison must include validation,
auxiliary fits, training, scoring, serialization, human review and support costs for accepted
21.29. Julia effect estimators and the meaning of a reusable result                            283


outputs. No present evidence establishes a speed advantage, lower total cost or bank value
for any route.(grf contributors, 2026b; bcf contributors, 2026; xbcf contributors, 2026; flexbcf
contributors, 2026)


21.29       Julia effect estimators and the meaning of a reusable
            result
A servicing manager asks whether an additional contact is worth its cost for each risk group.
A numerical answer requires more than a treatment-effect method name. The population
average, the average among previously contacted customers, a conditional contrast and a
coefficient from residual regression can differ even when every conditional model is known.
Missing outcomes can change the averaging population again. A reusable interface must carry
this meaning from the business question through the numerical calculation.
   The selected Julia sources offer several distinct building blocks. CausalELM 0.8.0 sup-
plies g-computation and effect learners; CausalForest 0.1.5 implements tree-based contrasts;
TMLE 0.20.5 supplies targeted and one-step estimation; and CausalTables 1.3.4 represents
causal data and interventions in supplied structural models. Their selected source revisions
precede the 7 October 2026 cutoff. Their MIT notices permit substantial reuse subject to
retaining the specified notices, but do not establish dependency clearance or statistical validity.
The following comparison concerns inspected source paths, not native execution or a tested
combination of these packages. CausalELM.jl contributors (2026); CausalForest.jl contributors
(2026); TMLE.jl contributors (2026); CausalTables.jl contributors (2026)


21.29.1     An average effect is a population-specific quantity

Let W denote pre-contact risk information, A ∈ {0, 1} the contact action, and Y (a) the mone-
tary outcome under action a. Under consistency, conditional exchangeability and treatment
positivity, write e(w) = Pr(A = 1 | W = w) and τ (w) = E{Y (1) − Y (0) | W = w}. The popu-
lation average treatment effect is E{τ (W )}; the treated-population effect is E{τ (W ) | A = 1}.
A prediction vector containing estimated τ (Wi ) is useful, but does not by itself provide
uncertainty for a selected subgroup or a policy chosen using that vector.
   In the inspected CausalELM g-formula path, ATE, ITT and CATE labels use counter-
factual predictions at all supplied covariate rows; the other branch uses treated rows. The
g-computation wrapper averages the contrast, while the S-learner retains a contrast vector.
The T-learner fits each treatment arm and subtracts its predictions on the supplied covariates.
Thus an ITT label only has an assignment-effect interpretation when the supplied treatment
actually represents assignment; it cannot convert receipt of contact into randomized offer
assignment. Categorical coding, the action clock and the averaging population must be explicit
inputs.CausalELM.jl contributors (2026)
   The same source’s double-machine-learning path forms outcome and treatment residuals
and averages foldwise least-squares coefficients. Its fold constructor slices contiguous rows.
Neither the name nor contiguous slicing supplies a dependence argument for repeated customer
records. Even with oracle nuisance functions and independent observations, a partially
linear coefficient need not be the population average under heterogeneous effects. To see the
distinction, take Y = m0 (W ) + Aτ (W ) + ε with E(ε | A, W ) = 0. If m(W ) = E(Y | W ), then
Y − m(W ) = (A − e(W ))τ (W ) + ε. Consequently the population residual coefficient is

                         E[(A − e(W ))(Y − m(W ))]   E[e(W )(1 − e(W ))τ (W )]

21.29.2     Source-level uncertainty checks before adoption

The inspected CausalELM generic null routine samples treatment independently and uniformly
from its distinct observed values, or uniformly over its observed range for a continuous
treatment. This does not preserve the observed treatment count. It also does not reproduce a
nonuniform propensity law or a cluster-randomized design without additional construction.
For four customers assigned exactly one contact, independent fair binary draws retain that
design with probability 4/16 = 1/4 and create an empty treatment or control arm with
probability 2/16 = 1/8. This exact calculation identifies an assignment-law mismatch, rather
than estimating a package error rate. CausalELM.jl contributors (2026); Causal banking
proposal project (2026ba)
  There is also a direct dimensional problem in the selected source. For null statistics z1 , . . . , zB
and reported statistic t, its scalar stderr expression is
                                                 PB               2
                                                  b=1 (t − zb )
                                       scode =          √ .                                       (21.72)
                                                 (B − 1) B
If t and zb are monetary effects, this expression has squared monetary units. Multiplication
of all outcomes by a positive constant c multiplies it by c2 , whereas a standard error must
scale by c. With (z1 , z2 , z3 , z4 ) = (−1, −1, 1, 1) and t = 2, the expression is 10/3. Changing
dollars to cents multiplies it by 10,000 rather than 100. This is a source-level defect in the
expression at the selected revision. It does not require a Julia run to establish the algebra, and
it does not establish the finite-sample behavior of every other package function. CausalELM.jl
contributors (2026); Causal banking proposal project (2026ba)
   Taking a square root in one location would not settle the larger inference question. The
sampled null law, the centering, the effect being tested and the relationship between repeated
randomization draws and sampling uncertainty would still need justification. The inspected
interval routine searches a finite grid with tail comparisons against the same null draws;
that code alone is insufficient to claim a valid general confidence-interval inversion. The
proposed reuse decision is therefore to reject unqualified reuse of this uncertainty path, while
retaining the point-estimation family as a candidate for a separately justified implementation.
CausalELM.jl contributors (2026)
  CausalForest illustrates a different boundary. Its interface exposes bootstrap or subsampling
choices and separate split and leaf samples under the honest-tree option. However, its outcome-
centering forest is fitted before these per-tree splits. The inspected prediction paths form
21.29. Julia effect estimators and the meaning of a reusable result                         285


within-leaf treated and control weights and return centered-outcome contrasts. They return
point predictions, rather than a calibrated covariance object. Honesty of the tree split is
consequently not sufficient evidence that all nuisance fitting is independent of evaluation, nor
evidence of equivalence to the separately reviewed grf implementation. A native comparison
should examine the actual nuisance training rows, treatment coding, arm support in leaves,
