21.29.3     Targeted estimation, missingness and influence scales

TMLE exposes nuisance-model choices, outer resampling and propensity truncation. The
selected noncollaborative default uses no outer resampling; a requested cross-validation design
must be supplied and preserved. The implementation’s weighted constructor default is true
although adjacent prose says false, another reason to record actual resolved configuration.
Truncation prevents numerical division by a very small estimated probability but cannot create
absent treatment support. For an identified ATE in an independent sampling model, the
familiar influence expression clarifies what an adapter must carry:
                              Ai                       1 − Ai
                     Di =          {Yi − m1 (Wi )} −            {Yi − m0 (Wi )}
                            e(Wi )                   1 − e(Wi )                         (21.73)
                            + m1 (Wi ) − m0 (Wi ) − ψ.

The relevant source combines outcome-residual and counterfactual-mean components. It
stores the standard deviation of the estimated influence values together with their number,
and passes both to the testing interface. This scale is not already the standard error of the
effect. Conditional asymptotic inference additionally needs suitable nuisance remainder control,
positivity, moments and a sampling-law argument; the presence of an influence vector does
not prove those conditions. TMLE.jl contributors (2026)
   For example, influence values (−3, −1, 1, 3) have sample variance 20/3. Under the indepen-
dent mean calculation, the variance of the average is 5/3, since n = 4. Exporting the influence
                                                                       √
standard deviation as an effect standard error would miss the factor n. Conversely, dividing
                                                   √
a quantity that is already a standard error by n again would understate uncertainty. For
joint outputs, the source stacks influence vectors and computes their covariance. A bridge must
preserve the identity and order of contributing customers; equal vector length is insufficient
when different outcomes select different complete cases. Cluster or calendar dependence
requires an appropriate covariance construction, not a new field name on the independent
calculation.TMLE.jl contributors (2026); Causal banking proposal project (2026ba)
   The missingness documentation is explicit: rows missing variables needed for estimation are
dropped. Without cross-validation, propensity fitting may use additional records with observed
treatment and confounders even when outcomes are missing. The source’s final fluctuation
dataset nevertheless uses complete relevant records. This is useful data reuse, but is not a

   Let R indicate observation of the outcome. Consider independent customers with equally

and contact conditional on risk, so missing at random holds in this example and response

   Case-control sampling is also a distinct design. The inspected TMLE interface accepts

21.29.4     Supplied causal models are valuable public references

CausalTables supplies a useful route to inexpensive comparisons before bank experiments.
Its intervention functions modify treatment, recompute summaries and draw counterfactual
responses from a supplied structural causal model. Its cfmean and cfdiff functions ap-
proximate intervention means by Monte Carlo. Despite efficiency-bound wording in their
documentation, the inspected return tuples contain only the mean. A reference-generation
service must separately retain the generating equations, intervention, random seed, Monte
Carlo error and dependence structure. A simulated network summary does not establish a
variance formula for observations from a bank network.CausalTables.jl contributors (2026)
   The distinction between supplied truth and observational identification is not semantic. Let
U be a fair binary variable and consider two structural models. In both, A = U . In the first,
Y = A; in the second, Y = U . Both produce the same observed law, with probability 1/2 on
each of (A, Y ) = (0, 0) and (1, 1). Yet the intervention contrast is 1 in the first model and
0 in the second. A simulator can reproduce either contrast once its model is supplied. The
observed distribution alone does not choose between them. At an illustrative cost of 1/2, the
corresponding margins are 1/2 and −1/2.Causal banking proposal project (2026ba)
   TMLE’s CausalTables extension converts treatment columns to categorical arrays and
identifies an estimand using the causes recorded in the supplied table. This is an explicit
and promising connection, provided that level order, graph semantics and the provenance
of the causal declarations survive conversion. It does not verify that the declared graph is
true. The matching CausalInference revision supplies separately reviewed graphical interfaces;
that evidence should be reused for its established scope rather than treated as qualification of
heterogeneous-effect estimation. TMLE.jl contributors (2026); CausalInference.jl contributors
(2026)


21.29.5     A bounded adoption path and the wider language search

The proposed architecture is an isolated Julia worker with a pinned environment and an
explicit estimand/result schema. TMLE is a candidate for targeted mean estimation and
CausalTables for supplied-model reference generation. A first public comparison should use
exact finite distributions to verify scalar targets, treatment-level order, outcome-unit conversion,
complete-case selection and graph-to-estimand conversion. Subsequent native trials should
compare influence-vector scaling, fold membership, fitted nuisance behavior and refusal on
absent support. CausalELM’s selected uncertainty path needs a justified repair before inclusion;
21.29. Julia effect estimators and the meaning of a reusable result                           287


CausalForest’s point predictions need their own inference qualification. Porting either path
before understanding these contracts would copy its unresolved scientific meaning into a new
language.
   The library, CLI and MCP representations should carry the action/assignment distinc-
tion, target population, contributing unit IDs, missingness rule, fitted-model configuration,
uncertainty kind and all unavailable results. An agent can propose mappings and inspect
contradictory declarations, but must leave unsupported identification or uncertainty requests
unresolved. This gives the business user a meaningful answer when a requested population
effect cannot be supplied, and permits genuine comparison of methods that do answer the
same question.
   Rust coverage remains incomplete. Separate official repository and crate queries identify
leads including perpetual, causalkit, oxicuda-causal and propensity-score, alongside
graph and event-ordering projects. These are metadata leads; current descriptions are not
proof of functionality at the cutoff. The queries inspect only their first pages, and an exact
treatment-effect phrase query returning zero does not establish absence. Selected pre-cutoff
source revisions, licenses, estimators and inference paths must be inspected before any capability
or reuse conclusion. Wider language coverage and package-paper originals also remain to be
established.GitHub and crates.io (2026)
  These public comparisons can determine which Julia integrations merit a native prototype
and which assumptions a later banking experiment must test.
Chapter 22

Longitudinal and survival software
as a decision model

A bank comparing repeated servicing policies needs more than a curve with a confidence
ribbon. An account can default, repay early, cease to be observed, or receive a different action
after its financial condition changes. A policy that reduces default incidence can also shorten
the profitable relationship. A policy that improves every baseline risk stratum can have a
larger late hazard among its remaining accounts. Two programs can return numerically similar
objects named survival while counting different accounts. These differences affect both the
scientific question and the financial decision.
   The longitudinal identification and sequential-estimation results developed earlier supply
the foundation. Here the question is how to preserve that foundation when choosing and
combining software. The argument proceeds from the event clock and supported horizon
to survivor selection, competing-event simulation, the meaning of a modified action, and
uncertainty in the resulting monetary contrast. Its finite laws and monetary amounts are
stipulated, reproducible constructions. They provide exact comparison references and expose
otherwise hidden distinctions; they are not bank observations or new executions of the external
estimators.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ci)


22.1      The decision clock and the unsupported tail
Let j = 1, . . . , K index servicing periods. At the opening of a period the bank observes the
permitted history Hj , chooses an action Aj , and then observes transitions and exits during
that period. An intervention must specify what the bank would do using the history available
at that opening. A balance posted after the decision, a later repayment classification, and a
corrected record unavailable to the decision maker cannot enter that history merely because
all three eventually appear in a warehouse. The data schema must represent availability as
well as the time to which a value refers.
    Start with a single first-exit time T taking values in the positive integers, possibly with mass
beyond the horizon. Under a specified policy d, define S d (j) = P (T d > j) and S d (0) = 1. Thus
S d (j − 1) is the probability of an active account at the opening of period j. With payment for
each period entered, the expected restricted active time is
                                                           K−1
                                                           X
                             Rd (K) = E{min(T d , K)} =           S d (j).                   (22.1)
                                                            j=0
                                                                     PK−1
The identity follows account by account from min(T, K) =               j=0   1{T > j} before taking

                                                288
22.1. The decision clock and the unsupported tail                                              289


expectations. This convention earns a period’s margin even if exit occurs at its end. A different
payment clock needs its own reward function. In particular, the same numerical area must not
be priced as both opening-period activity and completed-period activity.
   Suppose the observation and identification assumptions support the policy survival proba-
bilities only through period m < K. This may be an administrative follow-up limit, rather
than random censoring that an observation model could remove. A fitted survival function
beyond m then supplies an extrapolation assumption. Increasing simulation draws does not
add observations at those times. Without a tail restriction, monotonicity of survival gives the
sharp discrete bounds
                   Rd (m) + S d (m) ≤ Rd (K) ≤ Rd (m) + (K − m)S d (m).                     (22.2)
To prove the lower bound, expand the remaining terms as S d (m) + S d (m + 1) + · · · + S d (K − 1)
and use nonnegativity. To prove the upper bound, bound every one of these K − m terms
by S d (m). The known term S d (m) cannot be discarded. The continuous-time argument that
allows all remaining activity to disappear immediately after an observed time would miss this
whole discrete period.
   Both endpoints are attainable. Keep the observed distribution through m unchanged. For
the lower endpoint, make all accounts still active at m exit at the end of period m + 1. For
the upper endpoint, keep them active through the entire requested horizon. Mixing these
two continuation laws preserves every observed survival probability and fills the interval. The
result is an identified set conditional on the supported earlier survival law, not a confidence
interval for a point target. Sampling uncertainty about that earlier law is a further problem.
   For an exact six-period example, take the observed policy survival sequence at times 0, 1, 2, 3
to be (1, 0.8, 0.65, 0.5) and the reference sequence to be (1, 0.9, 0.8, 0.6). Then
                        Rd (6) ∈ [2.95, 3.95],                R0 (6) ∈ [3.30, 4.50],
               Rd (6) − R0 (6) ∈ [−1.55, 0.65].                                             (22.3)
These contrast endpoints are sharp when there is no additional cross-policy restriction: select
the lower continuation for one policy and the upper for the other. Such potential event-time
marginals can coexist, for example by constructing each from a common uniform variable and
its inverse distribution function. A scientifically justified individual monotonicity restriction
would be additional information and could narrow the set.
   At USD 20 margin per period entered and USD 3 upfront policy cost, the incremental
retention-margin value is therefore in [−34, 10] USD per eligible account. This example prices
activity alone; it does not silently include a default loss or a repayment penalty. Those would
require the corresponding joint event probabilities. A decision to roll out the policy cannot be
justified by selecting the favorable end of this set. A bank with a more restrictive accepted tail
model could make a different, explicitly conditional decision.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ci)
  There are several substantive remedies. Shortening the requested horizon to the supported
period changes the business question but removes this tail ambiguity. Following a public or
generated cohort longer can demonstrate how a proposed analysis would use additional follow-
up, without supplying the bank’s missing future. An externally justified survival envelope or a
specified parametric tail gives conditional bounds or a point extrapolation. The report should
show how the monetary conclusion changes across those choices. An automatic default horizon
chosen from the largest event in the current sample answers a fourth question, whose end point
varies with the sample. That can be useful internally, but it does not establish comparability
between policies, software engines, or reporting vintages.
  The software interface consequently needs an explicit requested horizon, an observed-support
horizon, an event convention and a monetary payment clock. A response can legitimately
290                                                                  Causal analysis for a universal bank


contain a point estimate on the supported range and a set beyond it. It must distinguish
extrapolated uncertainty conditional on a tail model from uncertainty that includes the
choice of that model. Returning a finite number at every requested time does not settle the
identification question.


22.2      Why a late hazard can reverse a policy ranking
Consider two equally weighted baseline risk strata, high and low, and no competing exit or
censoring. Within each stratum an active account defaults with a constant probability per
period. Under the reference policy these probabilities are 0.8 and 0.1; under the intervention
they are 0.4 and 0.05. One can generate the potential histories using independent period
uniforms within each stratum. Randomized policy assignment, consistency and the stated
event clock then suffice for this illustrative policy comparison. Its reversal does not require an
unmeasured common cause of action and default.
 Write hdb for the hazard in baseline stratum b and πb = 1/2 for its baseline proportion.
Marginal survival and the opening-period risk composition are

                             S d (j) =       πb (1 − hdb )j ,

The two marginal hazards average over different survivor populations. By period three, the
reference high-risk share is 4/85, whereas the policy high-risk share is 144/505. Protecting the
high-risk accounts keeps more of them in the later policy risk set. Comparing those risk sets
as if they were the same baseline population confuses composition with a policy’s cumulative
consequence.
  The exact results make the reversal visible:

                    Quantity                     Reference     Policy
                    S(1)                              0.55      0.775
                    S(2)                             0.425   0.63125
                    S(3)                            0.3685 0.5366875
                    Period-three marginal hazard 113/850 1513/10100

The period-three hazards are approximately 0.13294 and 0.14980. Thus the policy has the
larger late marginal hazard, although every stratum has a smaller hazard under that policy
at every time and marginal survival is larger throughout. The marginal hazard ratio is a
valid description of its two selected risk sets. It is insufficient as a stand-alone ranking of the
baseline policy decision.
   For a portfolio entering together, suppose each period entered earns USD 20, default by
period three loses USD 1,000, and the policy costs USD 3 upfront. The incremental expected
value is

            20(2.40625 − 1.975) − 1000(0.4633125 − 0.6315) − 3 = 173.8125 USD.                    (22.5)
22.3. Competing exits and the order of a simulator                                                291


This ranking uses the same initial population and the cumulative event probabilities appropriate
to its financial objective. It remains conditional on the stipulated margins and losses. Changing
those amounts is a sensitivity analysis of the objective, while changing how histories are selected
is a change to the population or causal model.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ci)
  This example motivates a practical output hierarchy. Preserve stratum-specific and marginal
hazards as diagnostics, but also report the policy survival or cumulative incidence on a common
baseline population, the restricted active time and their joint uncertainty. If the bank wants
an effect among accounts that would survive under both policies, that is a principal-stratum
question requiring additional assumptions about joint potential histories. Neither conditioning
each fitted curve on its own observed survivors nor adjusting the plot legend identifies that
population.
   The same logic affects model assessment. A regression can accurately predict late defaults
among observed reference survivors and still be a poor model for the histories retained under
another policy. Checking calibration on the observed late risk set is informative about that
set. Transporting it to a policy-induced risk set requires overlap and stability of the relevant
conditional transition law. Flexible prediction and causal transport should therefore appear as
separate arguments in the proposal.


22.3      Competing exits and the order of a simulator
Now distinguish default D and early repayment P as mutually exclusive first events within
each period. Among accounts event-free at the opening, let λD,j and λP,j be their probabilities
conditional on the permitted history and intervention. They obey λD,j + λP,j ≤ 1. With
constant probabilities in a homogeneous example,

                              S(j) = (1 − λD − λP )j ,
                                      K
                                      X                                    K
                                                                           X
                           FD (K) =         S(j − 1)λD ,        FP (K) =         S(j − 1)λP ,
                                      j=1                                  j=1

        S(K) + FD (K) + FP (K) = 1.                                                             (22.6)

Here S means free of both first events. In contrast, 1 − FD = S + FP includes accounts that
have already repaid. It cannot be integrated as if those repaid accounts were still earning
the active-account margin. Treating prepayment as censoring would target another quantity
and needs a separate scientific interpretation; it does not automatically describe eliminating
prepayment while keeping every other mechanism fixed.
  Some simulators implement within-period draws sequentially. If prepayment is drawn first
with probability pP and default is then drawn among those without that prepayment with
probability pD , the induced unconditional first-event probabilities are

             λP = pP ,      λD = (1 − pP )pD ,       P (neither) = (1 − pP )(1 − pD ).          (22.7)

Consequently an adapter from mutually exclusive first-event probabilities must set pP = λP
and pD = λD /(1−λP ) when λP < 1. The constraint on the two first-event probabilities ensures
pD ≤ 1. If λP = 1, feasibility requires λD = 0 and the unused conditional default probability
does not determine any outcome. Reversing the order requires the converse factorization.
Multiplying two arbitrary competing hazards without defining their conditioning populations
supplies neither factorization.
   The conversion is elementary but consequential. Consider two periods. Set (λD , λP ) =
(0.1, 0.1) for reference and (0.12, 0.6) for policy. Although the policy’s default probability
292                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


among initially event-free accounts is larger each period, more of its accounts prepay before
a later default is possible. The resulting (FD , FP , S) vectors at period two are respectively
(0.18, 0.18, 0.64) and (0.1536, 0.768, 0.0784). The policy has the smaller default cumulative
incidence and the shorter active relationship.
   Price each entered period at USD 20, default at a USD 1,000 loss, prepayment at a USD 50
loss, and the intervention at USD 3 per initial account. The joint objective is

                      V d (K) = 20Rd (K) − 1000FDd (K) − 50FPd (K) − cd .                   (22.8)

Using c0 = 0 and cd = 3 gives reference value −153 USD and policy value −169.4 USD. The
incremental value is −16.4 USD despite a smaller default incidence. Default avoidance alone
does not establish a desirable servicing policy when relationship duration and competing exits
carry monetary value.
   For the ordered simulator the correct default probabilities after a non-prepayment draw are
1/9 for reference and 0.3 for policy. Suppose an adapter instead passes the policy’s unconditional
0.12 directly as pD , while setting pP = 0.6. The induced period default probability is then
0.4 × 0.12 = 0.048. At period two the wrong policy calculation returns

                 FDwrong = 0.064896,                   FPwrong = 0.8112,
                 Rwrong = 1.352,                       V wrong = −81.416 USD.               (22.9)

Compared with the correctly translated reference, the apparent gain becomes 71.584 USD. An
omitted conditional-probability conversion has reversed the decision. The example does not
identify a defect in an upstream package: the error is the deliberately incompatible meaning
supplied at its boundary. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ci)
   The inspected simulation path of pygformula draws a competing event before the target
event and marks the target event missing after that competing exit. Its aggregation multiplies
the target-event probability by the no-competing-event probability and the preceding survival
products. The stored object named survival is one minus accumulated target incidence; it
is therefore distinct from event-free survival when competing exits are present. These are
claims about the inspected original simulation and aggregation paths, not about newly fitted
models or all package releases. The model-fitting risk sets were not newly inspected for this
comparison, so the simulation order alone cannot establish how every fitted probability is
conditioned.(pygformula project, 2026b; Causal banking proposal, 2026ck)
   An integration should first check the complete tuple: opening risk set, within-period order,
event codes, probability conditioning, transition to an absorbing state, and the meaning of
every accumulated output. A generated two-period law is a useful exact semantic test before
statistical fitting. It can verify that a proposed wrapper conserves probability and obtains
Equation (22.8) under declared inputs. It does not establish that the observational data
identify those inputs, or that a fitted observational model is calibrated under intervention.


22.4      Modifying a natural action and redrawing an action
A dynamic servicing policy may modify the action that would naturally be chosen: shorten a
delay, reduce a proposed payment, or add support when the proposed contact intensity lies in
a specified range. This is more specific than drawing a new action from a distribution with the
same conditional marginal frequencies. At later times the natural action is evaluated under
the history produced by earlier interventions. Unobserved features of the action mechanism
can connect that later natural action to an earlier one, even when there is no unmeasured
confounding of the ordinary joint treatment regime and outcome.
22.4. Modifying a natural action and redrawing an action                                     293


   The longitudinal modified treatment policy analysis distinguishes a natural action policy
from its stochastic-intervention counterpart. Under its structural model, standard sequential
randomization separates a current treatment innovation from later covariate and outcome
innovations. The stronger condition also separates it from future treatment innovations.
Theorem 1 identifies the redrawn stochastic intervention under the standard condition and the
natural modified policy under the stronger condition, together with support. The two targets
must therefore be named before reusing the same observed-data recursion.(Díaz et al., 2023)
   An exact two-time construction shows why this distinction is necessary. Let U and V be
independent fair bits, with no measured covariates. In both worlds A1 = U and the structural
outcome is Y = A2 . The second natural action is generated by
                                  W0 : A2 = V,
                                            (
                                              V, A1 = U,                                 (22.10)
                                  W1 : A2 =
                                              1, A1 ̸= U.
In ordinary observations A1 = U , so the second branch of W1 is never used. In each world all
four (A1 , A2 ) cells have probability 1/4, and Y = A2 . Thus the complete observable law is
identical, with positive support for both actions at each observed history. This is equality of
the whole joint distribution, not merely equality of observed outcome means.
   Apply the policy d1 (a) = 1 − a, followed by d2 (a) = a: flip the first natural action and
leave the second natural action as generated under the changed history. In W0 , the second
                              ¯
action remains V and E(Y d ) = 1/2. In W1 , the first action becomes 1 − U ; the second action
mechanism then takes its other branch and sets A2 = 1. Its modified-policy mean is 1. The
natural-action effect is not identified by the common observed law under the weaker restrictions
of this construction.
   For the redrawn intervention, the observed conditional action law at both times is a fair
bit. Pushing those conditional laws through the flip and identity maps still gives fair bits;
drawing from them under the evolving history yields outcome mean 1/2 in both worlds. This
is a different intervention. It is identified by the common observed law under the stated
standard condition. Calling it a numerical approximation to the natural policy would obscure
a difference in counterfactual meaning.
   The construction satisfies the standard innovation condition used above: covariate and
outcome structural innovations can be constants, and the outcome under a joint assigned
sequence is simply the assigned second action. The second treatment innovation in W1 ,
however, contains the earlier U . Strong independence between the first and later treatment
innovations fails. In W0 independent U, V suffice. Support also holds in the example; the
failure does not arise from a missing observed action cell. These details explain why the witness
illustrates the theorem’s assumption distinction rather than contradicting its identification
result. (Díaz et al., 2023; Causal banking proposal, 2026ci)
   In banking terms, a latent servicing preference that influences several successive proposed
actions can matter to a policy that modifies those proposals. Observing all outcome confounders
for ordinary assigned regimes does not automatically reveal that proposal mechanism. This
interpretation is a possible mechanism, not an assertion about a bank’s data. A proposal should
ask whether the natural recommendation can be recorded, whether its history-dependent
generation can be justified, and whether a randomized redraw is operationally acceptable. If
the business instead intends a fresh randomized allocation at every time, the stochastic target
may be exactly the intended one.
   There are consequently several defensible responses to uncertain natural action dependence:
record and experimentally vary the recommendation mechanism; impose and defend the stronger
structural restriction; redesign the intervention as a redrawn policy; or retain an explicitly
294                                                                      Causal analysis for a universal bank


incomplete identification claim. An estimator’s robustness properties concern an identified
observed-data functional under its assumptions. They cannot choose among observationally
identical structural worlds with different natural-policy outcomes.

  Now compare the cap dc (a) = min(a + 1/4, 1). It maps the interval (3/4, 1] to the single

point probability zero, so the intervention law is not absolutely continuous with respect to the
observed law. A density-ratio estimator defined only with respect to the observed Lebesgue
density cannot represent this target by an ordinary Radon–Nikodym ratio. The endpoint
belongs to the topological support [0, 1]; the problem is the stronger absolute-continuity
requirement. A large finite ratio and a singular atom are different mathematical objects.

consistency and exchangeability identify the causal response mean almost everywhere on that

endpoint worlds and their intermediate values therefore attain the entire set while preserving
exchangeability and consistency.
  If the outcome is worth USD 100 at its unit value, the baseline is USD 50 and the intervention

endpoint would force u = 1 in this example. A structural model for the atom supplies a
different explicit restriction. Redesigning the intervention to avoid the atom changes the policy
instead. These remedies address distinct scientific questions; they must not be interchanged
by an automatic clipping rule. (Díaz et al., 2023; Causal banking proposal, 2026ci)
   Identification under continuity is also distinct from regular estimation. A value defined at
a single continuous treatment point can depend on local behavior that the nonparametric
observed-data model does not estimate at root-n rate. The LMTP paper’s threshold example
describes this non-pathwise-differentiability and restricts its efficiency theorem to piecewise
smoothly invertible maps. Continuity can resolve the choice of an endpoint version without
proving the square-integrable influence function required by that theorem. A parametric
model, quantitative smoothness restriction, mixed treatment law with a genuine endpoint
atom, or a smoothed policy would need its own estimation argument. The cap is operationally
meaningful; the unrestricted continuous-density theorem is simply not its automatic uncertainty
guarantee.(Díaz et al., 2023)


22.6      The derivative of a fixed modified-action map
For the supported fixed map in Equation (22.11), write g(a | W ) for the observed conditional

22.7     Translating software semantics before comparing esti-
         mates
The common package names in a longitudinal workflow conceal different data contracts. The
inspected ltmle documentation uses wide, time-ordered nodes; an absorbing event is encoded
as event one, censoring is a separate factor, and post-event or post-censor nodes are ignored.
22.7. Translating software semantics before comparing estimates                              297


Its documented bounds act on cumulative treatment probabilities. A continuous outcome
range can also be truncated or scaled. These choices determine the observed target before a
targeting step is run.(joshuaschwab contributors, 2026)
   The lmtp documentation uses chronological treatment, covariate and outcome nodes. A
supplied shifted data frame overrides the shift function; it is not an additional rule applied
after that function. The finite-memory parameter specifies how many previous time points
are used for estimation. That documented modeling choice does not establish that a bank’s
history can be truncated without changing its conditional law. Cluster identifiers, folds and
sampling weights affect the fitted calculation. Its returned density ratios are noncumulative.
Multiplying them to form the cumulative ratios required by a stated score is valid. Treating each
noncumulative ratio as an already cumulative quantity, or multiplying an already cumulative
output again, changes that score.(nt-williams contributors, 2026)
   For a two-step exact probability law with incremental denominators (1/2, 2/5), the incre-
mental ratios are (2, 5/2) and their cumulative products are (2, 5). If a floor of 1/4 is applied
to the cumulative denominator, the final weight is 4; if the floor is applied to each incremental
denominator before multiplying, the final weight is 5. Both procedures avoid an infinite value,
but they do not implement the same numerical calculation. The floor level and location
belong in the estimator specification. A fixed floor can leave bias for the original target,
while a vanishing floor needs rate and moment arguments. Clipping a denominator does not
automatically define a different normalized intervention law. If a deliberately changed target
is intended, that target needs its own definition and identification argument.(Causal banking
proposal, 2026ci)
   The stremr manual presents a long-data interface with subject and time fields and sep-
arates treatment, monitoring and censoring models. Its ‘fitTMLE‘ path wraps sequential
g-computation with targeting. The survtmle manual fixes a binary treatment, integer event
times and an event code for censoring; its default horizon is derived from the observed event
time. It documents mean and hazard methods, covariance and subject-level influence vectors,
and warns that finite-sample convergence is not guaranteed. The prose and argument material
                                                                                  √
also use different descriptions of a tolerance scaling: the displayed call uses 1/ n, while the
descriptive paragraph names 1/n. An adapter must inspect the selected executable path and
record the actual argument, rather than resolve that discrepancy by choosing whichever default
sounds preferable. Reaching the maximum iteration count and meeting the empirical-score
tolerance are different termination events. (stremr contributors, 2017; survtmle contributors,
2019)
  The survtmle horizon illustrates why defaults need scientific review. The saved API uses the
maximum failure time among noncensored event records, not the end of all recorded follow-up.
Two samples with identical requested six-period objectives can therefore have different implicit
output times. Passing an explicit common horizon removes that software difference, but does
not create positivity of observation or identify an unsupported tail. Likewise, its covariance
and subject influence vectors are useful for post-hoc contrasts only if the requested treatment,
event, horizon and subject indexing remain attached to their entries. The interface itself does
not establish successful targeting or valid nuisance rates.
   The gfoRmula API exposes risk and end-of-follow-up outcomes, censoring and competing-
event options, and custom intervention and history roles. Its names do not by themselves
establish whether an output is event-free survival, cumulative incidence, or a different comple-
ment. The pygformula simulation path draws competing events before target events, while
its bootstrap resamples whole histories for unique subjects, refits models, and uses common
seeds for intervention simulations. Those are useful building blocks for a prospective com-
parison. They do not prove that every model-fitting risk set or every release has the same
298                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


semantics.(CausalInference contributors, 2026; pygformula project, 2026b,a)
  These packages also answer different design questions. A fixed binary baseline-treatment
survival analysis can be compared with survtmle’s declared input. Repeated binary decisions
with censoring and an ordered wide history fit the selected ltmle contract; a long history
with a distinct monitoring process motivates examining stremr’s corresponding treatment,
monitoring and censoring components. Modified continuous action laws motivate the lmtp map,
support and ratio checks developed above. Parametric g-computation motivates gfoRmula or
pygformula when the goal includes simulating full intervention histories. An adapter can make
their results comparable only on an intersection of targets and observation assumptions. It
cannot turn a fixed baseline treatment into an evolving decision merely by repeating its value
down a long table.
   The distinction between ordinary and sequential double robustness also belongs in this
comparison. The inspected sequential-robustness paper distinguishes consistency when either
every outcome regression is correct or every treatment mechanism is consistently estimated
from consistency when, at each time, the appropriate outcome or treatment condition holds. Its
outcome conditions concern functional specification of the recursively defined regressions, and
its formal rate and inference conditions add further restrictions. A product should therefore
identify which algorithm, target and recursion support a robustness statement. The name
TMLE, an ensemble learner, or an empirical score near zero cannot by itself establish the
stronger per-time property. No rederivation of the earlier sequential remainder is needed to
make this software choice explicit. (Luedtke et al., 2018)
   An interoperable result should therefore carry at least: subject unit and cluster, clock and
horizon, event and censoring codes, absorbing-state rule, policy law and whether it is natural or
redrawn, treatment probability scale, ratio orientation and truncation, target type, influence-
vector convention, failed-replicate handling, software version and license. A result lacking one
of these fields can remain a useful exploratory number, but it cannot enter a common-target
comparison without an explicit refusal or translation proof. Package declarations currently
record gfoRmula 1.1.2 (GPL-3), ltmle 1.3-0 (GPL-2) and lmtp 1.5.4 (AGPL-3.0). The inspected
API bytes and package declarations are separate evidence; metadata alone does not prove
that those bytes belong to those exact releases. The selected pygformula source is pinned to
commit e66f787fcef2 dated 22 May 2026; the selected stremr and survtmle records identify
0.4 at 14d15651b247 and 1.1.1 at 295de8b4be18, respectively. These are scoped historical
identities, not a claim that all current releases were surveyed. Full dependency rights and
runtime qualification require separate inspection and trials. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ck)


22.8     Joint event uncertainty and the monetary objective
The financial objective in Equation (22.8) depends on three components of the same account
history. They should not be treated as independent measurements. Return to its two-period
policy law, with constant first-event probabilities d = 3/25 for default, p = 3/5 for prepayment,
and s = 1 − d − p = 7/25 for neither event. Write B for the indicator of no first-period
event, L = 1 + B for the number of periods entered, and ID , IP for indicators of default and
prepayment by period two. The complete subject vector is X = (L, ID , IP )⊤ . Its mean is

Dropping the off-diagonal terms overstates the variance by 11326.08 USD2 in this construction.
Independence is not necessarily an anticonservative approximation; its direction depends on
the objective’s signs and the joint law. Changing those signs or changing the event mechanism
can change the direction. An integration should preserve the covariance, rather than assume
that discarding it always gives a safer answer.
   For M = 1000 independent complete trajectories drawn from this fixed policy law, the
sample-average net reward has variance 119.20704 USD2 . This is an exact sampling or Monte
Carlo statement for those trajectories. It is not the variance of a causal estimator fitted
to 1000 observational subjects with estimated treatment and observation mechanisms. For
that estimator, a valid vector of subject influence contributions ϕi would instead supply
the covariance appropriate to its fitted target. Under its own asymptotic-linear and moment
conditions, the monetary influence is c⊤ ϕi ; a constant intervention cost contributes no influence,
while an estimated cost can contribute another component. Jointly estimated policy and
reference outputs also require their cross-policy covariance. The covariance identity remains
the same, but the random vector must be the correct one.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ch)
   This distinction guides a substantive adoption choice. When an engine exposes only marginal
standard errors, a monetary combination may be unidentified from its reported uncertainty even
when every point estimate is usable. Exposing subject-aligned influence vectors or a justified
joint bootstrap can repair that interface. If neither is available, one may derive a conservative
bound from additional covariance restrictions or return unavailable joint uncertainty. Summing
marginal variances asserts an independence restriction that competing first events visibly
violate here.

22.9      Sampling, simulation and model error are different quan-
          tities
Let Dn denote the full observed sample of independent subject histories, including the records
used for fitting and the empirical baseline population. Conditional on it, let U contain the
simulator’s baseline resampling and transition draws. For a value estimate using M simulated
trajectories, the law of total variance gives

                      Var(Vb ) = VarDn {E(Vb | Dn )} + EDn {Var(Vb | Dn )}.                 (22.25)

The first term is variation in the fitted baseline and observed sample; the second is simulation
noise conditional on that fitted object. If the simulator is conditionally unbiased for a fitted-
model functional V (Dn ), its first conditional mean is exactly V (Dn ). Model misspecification
can leave a bias E{V (Dn )} − Vtarget that is not removed by increasing M ; it can also affect the
two variance terms. Squared-error risk adds the square of that bias to the displayed variance.
A reported Monte Carlo standard error that omits the first term is not a confidence interval
for the full causal estimand.
   For a paired policy contrast, use one common uniform draw per simulated unit and set the
event indicator to 1{U < pd }. With p0 = 0.2 and p1 = 0.3, the single-draw difference has mean
0.1 and variance 0.09, because it is one when U ∈ (0.2, 0.3] and zero otherwise. Independent
draws have variance 0.2(0.8) + 0.3(0.7) = 0.37. At M = 10,000, the corresponding simulation
variances are 0.000009 and 0.000037. Common random numbers can improve a contrast by
coupling comparable paths, but resetting a seed alone does not guarantee that branching
histories remain aligned. The coupling rule must be declared.
   If each independent account contributes two identical rows, treating rows as iid understates
the variance of a subject-level mean by a factor of two. The bootstrap and influence calculation
must resample or retain the independent subject unit. The pygformula bootstrap’s whole-
history resampling is therefore semantically different from a row bootstrap. A future package
comparison must record this unit explicitly.(pygformula project, 2026a; Causal banking proposal,
2026ci)
   Coverage also needs a complete denominator. In an illustrative 200-request study, 160
requests are available, 152 are covered, so availability is 0.8, conditional coverage is 152/160 =
0.95, and request coverage is 152/200 = 0.76. Reporting only the conditional fraction would
hide the failed or unavailable requests. Pointwise intervals for several horizons or policies
are not simultaneous bands; retaining the joint subject influence vectors permits a declared
covariance calculation, while simultaneous control needs an explicit multiplier or resampling
rule. These are reporting choices with direct business meaning when a decision is based on the
worst horizon or the best policy.


22.10       A bounded transition-error envelope
An integration can state a conditional transition-error budget while retaining its scientific
premises. Suppose the reference and approximate processes have the same initial history law
on standard Borel spaces, use the same fixed policy and reward functions, and differ only in
transition kernels Pt (· | h) and Pet (· | h). Include any randomized policy draw in the common
transition description. Define total variation as supE |Pt (E | h) − Pet (E | h)|, and suppose it is
at most εt ∈ [0, 1] uniformly over histories reachable by either process. These are restrictions
on the compared laws, not conclusions from predictive fit on the observed histories.
  Couple the initial histories identically. While their full histories agree, use a measurable
22.10. A bounded transition-error envelope                                                        301


maximal coupling of the next kernels; its conditional probability of a first split is at most εt .
Once histories have split, regard the split flag as permanent, even if current states later agree.
If at denotes the actual probability of a split by step t, then at+1 ≤ at + (1 − at )εt . The map
on the right is increasing in at . Induction therefore bounds at by
                                                                           t−1
                                                                           Y
                  q0 = 0,      qt+1 = qt + (1 − qt )εt ,        qt = 1 −         (1 − εu ).   (22.26)
                                                                           u=0

The event of unequal histories is contained in the split event; this also bounds the total-variation
distance between their history laws. A simpler union bound, useful when an additive budget
is easier to report, gives
                              d0 = 0,      dt+1 ≤ min{1, dt + εt }.                          (22.27)
One may choose dt = min{1, u<t εu } as a conservative bound, with qt ≤ dt . For a common
                                P

running reward with range at most Bt on step-t histories, the absolute expected running-reward
bias is at most
                                      K−1
                                      X                K−1
                                                       X
                                             Bt qt ≤         Bt dt ,                          (22.28)
                                       t=0             t=0

and a common terminal loss with range at most L adds at most LqK , or conservatively LdK .
To see this, condition on the common history event and use equality of coupled rewards there;
on the split event the reward difference is bounded by its range. Summing those expected
absolute differences and applying the triangle inequality proves the stated envelope. If the
reward functions themselves are approximated, their uniform discrepancies add a separate
term; the displayed transition bound does not already include them.
   For K = 3, εt = 0.02, Bt = 20 USD and terminal loss range L = 1000 USD, the
recursion gives d = (0, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06), whereas the tighter coupling recursion gives q =
(0, 0.02, 0.0396, 0.058808). The additive running-margin and terminal bounds are USD 1.20
and USD 60, totaling USD 61.20. The tighter components are USD 1.192 and USD 58.808,
totaling USD 60. The difference is a proved consequence of counting the opportunity for a
first split only while the histories remain coupled.(Causal banking proposal, 2026ch)
    The tighter envelope is attainable under these restrictions. Let the reference stay in state zero.
Let the approximation, while in state zero, move to an absorbing state one with probability
εt ; otherwise it stays zero. At state one define both kernels to stay there. The two kernels
differ in total variation by exactly εt at state zero and agree at state one. The approximate
probability of state one at time t is qt , whereas the reference probability is zero. Choose the
common running reward Bt 1{state = 1} and terminal reward L1{state = 1}. Their expected
                      P
difference is exactly t Bt qt + LqK , attaining all components together. This abstract witness
establishes sharpness of the envelope over the declared kernel/reward class. It does not imply
that the stipulated budgets hold for a fitted bank model. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ch)
  A bank can replace these uniform budgets with validated conservative budgets only after
obtaining appropriate transition audits. A small average error on frequent histories does not
imply this uniform bound on rare but financially important histories. Likewise, a terminal
value range should include all competing event outcomes, not only defaults, if the policy
objective prices them jointly.
   The envelope offers a useful admission test for an implementation. The adapter must
expose the horizon, transition decomposition, reward range, stated TV or coupling budget, and
whether the bound includes model fitting, simulation, and observation error. More precisely,
the displayed envelope bounds the expected reward under two fixed laws; finite Monte Carlo
error and fitted-law sampling uncertainty need the separate arguments above. For a policy-
reference contrast, bounding each policy’s law separately and adding the two envelopes is valid;
302                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


a smaller paired envelope requires a justified common coupling. If any budget is unavailable,
the system can return a conditional point estimate with a declared numerical component, but
it should not label the resulting interval a full causal uncertainty interval. Refusal is a valid
output when the requested guarantee exceeds the declared budget.


22.11      A common-target public prototype and adoption routes
The practical next step is a public or generated comparison with a common target, not a claim
that six packages are interchangeable. Freeze a finite baseline cohort law, an integer event
clock, explicit default/repayment/censor codes, two policies, a supported horizon, monetary
rewards, and a complete seed and environment manifest. Admit an engine only after exact
two-period and single-shift references reproduce the probability, pushforward and reward checks
above. A candidate that cannot express an atom, competing first event, natural-versus-redrawn
choice, or subject-level resampling is not silently coerced into the target; it receives a typed
incompatibility record.
   For each admitted engine, register the input schema, version and license, training folds,
policy specification, simulation coupling, number of baseline and Monte Carlo draws, interval
or band method, failed-replicate rule and runtime. Compare the policy contrast, restricted
active time, each first-event incidence, joint covariance, availability, width, numerical error
and the resulting monetary decision. Keep model bias as a separate unknown. A generated
potential-outcome law establishes the truth of that construction only. Public data can exercise
the observation and clock pipeline, but cannot establish a bank’s unmeasured assignment truth
or accepted loss threshold.
   Adoption then has four defensible routes. Direct adoption is suitable when an engine’s
target, event semantics, license and runtime are accepted. A thin adapter is preferable when
the estimator is sound but its schema or result metadata differ. Porting is justified only when
the missing capability is material, the license permits it, and a reference implementation can
be reproduced. Rejection is appropriate for an unsupported target, unresolvable license or
dependency risk, missing uncertainty meaning, or an output that cannot preserve the bank’s
information clock. These are proposal decisions, not claims that the underlying packages are
defective.
   The shared library should expose a typed analysis manifest and a refusal object alongside
estimates. The CLI can validate the manifest, run exact semantic fixtures, and emit a versioned
result bundle. An MCP surface can request validation, explanation, and comparison while
preserving the same manifest and audit record; it should not infer a causal diagram or silently
choose a horizon from an unqualified natural-language request. LLM or agent assistance can
propose mappings and diagnostics, but a human or registered rule must approve the target,
assumptions, source clock and policy. The longitudinal engine should return an identified set or
an incompatibility when the tail, atom, event order or natural-policy condition is unsupported.
  A prospective public/generated pilot can test these translations before an expensive bank
experiment. Its adoption decision should distinguish an exact semantic match from statistical
qualification, complete dependency rights, accepted operating behavior and economic usefulness.
Authentic assignment and observation records, feasible policy versions, independent review
and accepted bank loss thresholds remain necessary for those later decisions. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026cg)

22.13      Which histories can validate the transition budget?
A useful error budget must refer to the histories reached under the requested policy. A held-out
prediction sample often has a different history mix. Even when its outcomes truthfully measure
22.13. Which histories can validate the transition budget?                                              305


the desired transition, averaging its errors under the wrong mix can hide financially important
failures. This distribution question remains after any causal identification argument has
supplied the relevant conditional transition law.
    At a fixed time, let ρt (x) be a validation input distribution and suppose µPt (x) > 0 implies
ρt (x) > 0. For the true signed continuation residual bt , write wt (x) = µPt (x)/ρt (x). Cauchy–
Schwarz gives
                X                      X

Thus a validated upper bound on the squared residual can be transported only with an

The transported bound correctly reflects the nearly complete movement of decision-relevant

as a policy-value guarantee. Such a residual can be generated by changing a transition to a
state whose continuation reward differs by USD 100; the numbers describe a possible finite
transition law, not merely an algebraic pair of incompatible scores.
   If validation never visits the second category, the density ratio there is undefined. No
finite value of Ct repairs that lack of support. With target occupancy 0.9 and an otherwise
unrestricted continuation range of USD 1000, the unseen category alone can contribute up to
USD 900 in absolute error. The missing information can be addressed by sampling that category,
changing the policy to avoid it, imposing and defending a transition restriction, or retaining
the resulting broad error set. The interface should expose this choice. Increasing draws from
the first category supplies none of the missing second-category transition information.(Causal
banking proposal, 2026cj)
   This support failure should be distinguished from two other problems. First, an observational
transition conditional on a chosen action need not equal the interventional transition needed
by the policy if hidden confounding remains. Reweighting the history mix cannot resolve
that scientific failure. Second, a measured account state can become available only after
the servicing action. Conditioning on its corrected warehouse value can define the wrong
information history even with complete statistical support. A validation design must establish
transition meaning and the availability clock before it establishes precision for a residual.
   These distinctions suggest concrete uses for public and generated data. A generated
finite process can reveal all transition rows and policy occupancies, so it can test both the
exact identity and deliberate support failures. A public longitudinal cohort can exercise
history construction, censoring, event order and reweighting diagnostics. If its assignment
or measurement process does not identify the requested causal rows, it can still test those
pipeline operations while leaving causal validation open. Public data do not become bank
306                                                                        Causal analysis for a universal bank


transition truth through a change of column names. Conversely, missing bank truth need not
delay a useful semantic prototype with a fully specified generated process.

   Known occupancy is a material premise, not a harmless convenience. In the three-period
example it follows from the scientifically imposed active probability 0.7 under both laws. The
validation class may allow the default/prepayment allocation to differ by time, while retaining
that known active probability. One can then validate each active row separately without
assuming that its default fraction is constant across times. When occupancy is estimated
instead, its error multiplies the row residual. A valid analysis needs a joint confidence region
or another justified bound for these weights; plugging estimated weights into Equation (22.38)
does not preserve its stated guarantee automatically.
   The independent draws can be obtained from a generated reference process, using distinct
trajectories or separate conditional-transition draws. Observational subject histories generally
do not provide arbitrary numbers of independent transitions at chosen histories. Repeated
rows from one account, adaptive stopping after a favorable residual, estimated causal weights
and random survivor counts require corresponding sampling arguments. They are not covered
by declaring nj to be the number of available rows. The public prototype can test the finite
result in its declared experiment before proposing the additional assumptions and costs of
authentic validation.

row confidence radii, each proportional to nj . It need not equal an allocation that minimizes
the variance of a different estimator. Zero-occupancy or zero-range rows require no observations
for this particular value bound, although other scientific and operating checks may still need
them. Minimum row counts, capacities and integer observations add constraints; the continuous
solution is then a planning reference.
   In the example, use three active rows, α = 0.05, w = (1, 0.7, 0.49) and full continuation
ranges (950, 950, 1000) USD. With equal row costs and budget 30000, equal allocation gives
10000 draws at each time and a simultaneous halfwidth of approximately USD 32.5680. The
continuous allocation is approximately (12337.92, 9726.89, 7935.18). The feasible integer choice
(12338, 9727, 7935) uses the same budget and has halfwidth USD 32.1752.
   For costs (1, 2, 4) and budget 60000 in the stipulated cost units, equal counts of 8571
spend 59997 and give halfwidth USD 35.1783. The continuous allocation is approximately
(19905.57, 9885.99, 5080.61). A feasible rounding and local leftover-allocation rule yields
(19908, 9886, 5080), spends 60000, and gives halfwidth USD 31.4016. This integer rule is
feasible; no claim of exact integer optimality follows from the continuous proof. The cost units
describe transition-validation effort. They do not establish staff prices, implementation costs
or bank return on investment.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cj)
   These are prospective radii from fixed counts, not intervals observed in a new validation
experiment. Even if the estimated center happened to equal the exact USD 20.805 discrepancy,
a USD 31.4016 halfwidth would not certify its sign. A useful design must therefore relate the
financial precision requirement to the sampling cost before commissioning expensive validation.
Better use of event-support restrictions or a justified homogeneous-row model may reduce that
cost, while introducing additional scientific premises. The calculation makes those tradeoffs
visible without pretending that a large nominal sample guarantees a useful decision.
   Finally, the interval addresses one fixed policy, a fixed continuation model and the specified
reference transition experiment. Two policy values require joint control over their rows and
their common or separate reference data. Choosing a policy or fitting Q using the same
validation observations changes the experiment. Numerical approximation of v Q , reward-model
error, unsupported tails, uncertain natural-action semantics and unmeasured assignment truth
also remain distinct. They can receive justified additional envelopes or explicit unavailable
components; none is already included in the row-sampling radius. An integration that
preserves these distinctions can explain exactly what a public prototype established and which
information an eventual bank experiment would still need.


22.15      Conclusion
Longitudinal causal software is comparable only after the decision clock, event law, intervention
meaning, support, uncertainty unit and monetary objective are aligned. The exact constructions
show where a plausible scalar can reverse a decision: an unsupported tail, survivor composition,
an ordered competing-event conversion, a natural action that is not a redraw, a singular cap,
a cumulative-weight translation, or a simulation error presented as a confidence interval. A
product proposal can close these semantic and design gaps with public/generated fixtures and
308                                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


bounded derivations now. It cannot claim that those fixtures establish bank truth, general
calibration, or final adoption.


22.16       Preserving longitudinal policies when reusing gfoRmula
A bank choosing repeated servicing actions must preserve the joint evolution of customer
condition, action and exit. A simulator can return a smooth risk curve while answering a
different intervention question from the one the bank intended. The gfoRmula source provides
a useful concrete reference because the simulation, intervention and bootstrap steps are in-
spectable. The selected November 2025 revision declares version 1.1.2, while its changelog
leaves that version’s release date as TBD. The comparison therefore concerns an immutable
source revision, not a claim about the latest released service. The inherited names gfor-
mula and gfoRmula refer here to the same project and do not count as two independent
implementations.(CausalInference gfoRmula contributors, 2025)


22.16.1     The target precedes the simulation settings

For a terminal outcome, let L0 denote the information available before a first action, A0
that action, L1 the next permitted measurement and A1 a second action. A deterministic
policy d = (d0 , d1 ) chooses A0 = d0 (L0 ) and A1 = d1 (L0 , A0 , L1 ). Write Y d for the resulting
terminal outcome and µ(d) = E(Y d ) for its population mean. With consistency, sequential
exchangeability, positivity for the requested actions and an appropriate observation process,
the earlier longitudinal argument gives
                                     X
                            µ(d) =            m{l0 , d0 (l0 ), l1 , d1 (l0 , d0 (l0 ), l1 )}
                                     l0 ,l1                                                                 (22.41)
                                              × p{l1 | l0 , d0 (l0 )}p(l0 ),

where m(l0 , a0 , l1 , a1 ) = E(Y | l0 , a0 , l1 , a1 ). For continuous variables the corresponding sums
become integrals. This is an identification statement under assumptions about the data-
generating experiment; fitting a conditional model does not supply those assumptions. In
particular, a financial condition affected by an earlier action can be a confounder for a later
action. Its distribution must evolve under the earlier policy rather than be held at its observed
marginal distribution.(Hernán and Robins, 2020)
   The inspected entry point distinguishes survival risks from continuous and binary end-of-
follow-up outcomes. These objects require different output types. The simulation takes baseline
covariates from the observed baseline rows; at later times it generates covariates in the supplied
covnames order, applies interventions, refreshes relevant histories and predicts outcomes. Thus
a model specification includes the within-period ordering and history definitions, not merely a
set of regression formulas. A treatment or balance field whose availability follows the outcome
decision is not made admissible by sorting the rows. Custom outcome prediction must return
the required probability or conditional mean; accepting a flexible prediction callback establishes
neither causal identification nor interval calibration.(CausalInference gfoRmula contributors,
2025)
   Three sample sizes should remain explicit. The number n of observed people governs the
information available for fitting. The nsimul value M governs the simulated population used in
numerical integration. The nsamples value B governs requested bootstrap replicates. Larger
M can reduce Monte Carlo error conditional on fitted models. Larger B can approximate a
chosen resampling distribution more closely. Neither change creates additional independent
22.16. Preserving longitudinal policies when reusing gfoRmula                                 309


observed histories or remedies unsupported policy actions. The adapter should report all three
quantities alongside the source population and time horizon.


22.16.2     An exact two-period policy comparison

Consider an authored binary law representing two opportunities for a helpful servicing action.
Let Y = 1 denote a beneficial terminal result. The variables and probabilities are stipulated,
not estimated from a bank:

                           P (L0 = 1) = 21 ,
                  P (L1 = 1 | L0 , A0 ) = 15 + 25 L0 + 15 A0 ,

Every displayed probability lies in [0, 1] on the binary support. Define never acting by
A0 = A1 = 0, always acting by A0 = A1 = 1, and a dynamic policy by A0 = 1 − L0 , A1 = L1 .
In the never arm, E(L1 ) = 2/5, so µnever = 1/20 + (1/5)(2/5) = 13/100. In the always arm,
E(L1 ) = 3/5, giving µalways = 3/5. For the dynamic arm, the two conditional probabilities of

   A tempting shortcut replaces L1 by its conditional mean p and applies the equivalent
binary-state rule A1 = 1{L1 ≥ 1/2} to that mean. At L0 = 0, this gives p = 2/5, A0 = 1
and A1 = 0, with predicted outcome probability 7/25. At L0 = 1, it gives p = 3/5, A0 = 0
and A1 = 1, with probability 9/20. Their average is 73/200, rather than 17/40. Integrating
over individual histories and intervening on a mean history are different operations. The
discrepancy follows from the thresholded action and the state–action interaction, without any
simulation noise.

preserving the outcome law. Neither figure is measured bank value.(Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ao)


22.16.3     Competing events define a different decision

Suppose default is the event of interest and an account’s early repayment prevents a later default
on that account. Early repayment also changes revenue and exposure, so treating it as ordinary
loss of observation may change both the causal question and the economic calculation. In the
inspected survival branch, the same-period main-event contribution is pY,t (1 − pD,t ), where
the competing event takes precedence. Previous main-event and competing-event survival
310                                                                     Causal analysis for a universal bank


multiply subsequent contributions. With constant probabilities pY = 1/5 and pD = 1/10 for
two periods, this convention gives
                                                         
                                        9
                        Rcompeting = 15 10 +       4 9
                                                   5 10
                                                              1 9    387
                                                              5 10 = 1250 = 0.3096.                 (22.45)
Suppressing the competing-event mechanism while keeping the stipulated main-event probabili-
ties gives Reliminate = 1/5 + (4/5)(1/5) = 9/25 = 0.36. The difference is 63/1250, or USD 50.40
at an assumed loss of USD 1,000 per main event. This is a difference between declared event
worlds, not a correction that should automatically be applied to either curve.(CausalInference
gfoRmula contributors, 2025; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ao)
   The inspected compevent_cens branch disables the competing hazard in intervention
simulation and retains separate handling for diagnostics. Its estimand therefore requires
explicit interpretation. An intervention that eliminates early repayment may be scientifically or
operationally implausible; identifying its consequences can require assumptions beyond those for
observed cumulative incidence. Censoring due to a missing report is yet another mechanism. A
library, CLI or MCP response must carry the target, event priority and observation convention
with the curve. A field named risk cannot safely conceal those distinctions.

22.16.4     Histories, thresholds and range clipping

The helper checks expect consecutive numeric time rows within each person. A monthly
history with an omitted month therefore needs an explicit measurement and missingness
model; silently closing the gap changes the decision clock. Without pre-baseline rows, lag
construction can use a baseline value or a zero/reference convention. A structural absence
of earlier treatment is different from a missing earlier measurement. For an absorbing status
such as permanent closure, neither choice should be inherited merely because it is a software
default.(CausalInference gfoRmula contributors, 2025)
   The static intervention function indexes its supplied vector at absolute time t + 1. Selected
intervention times therefore do not imply that the vector is indexed by the number of
interventions already performed. The newer intervention argument names identify both policy
number and variable. A conversion should preserve that association and reject an ambiguous
or too-short schedule before calling a worker. The threshold function directly clamps the
current value to its bounds. For natural values (−1, 2, −1), a lower bound of zero gives (0, 2, 0).
A different rule that retains the preceding positive level would give (0, 2, 2). The threshold
routine supplies no such direct absorbing state; feedback through simulated histories may still
affect later natural values. A bank asking for a persistent commitment needs to specify that
commitment explicitly.(CausalInference gfoRmula contributors, 2025; Causal banking proposal
project, 2026ao)
   The default sim_trunc=TRUE also matters. For selected continuous covariate types, the
inspected code clamps simulated draws to empirical observed ranges. Clamping maps a draw
outside a range to an endpoint; it is not rejection-resampling from a truncated distribution.
An authored discrete witness makes the distinction transparent. Let X take −2, 0, 2 with
probabilities 1/4, 1/2, 1/4. Then
                        E(X 2 ) = 2,      E{min(1, max(−1, X))2 } = 21 .                            (22.46)
At an assumed quadratic loss coefficient of USD 100, the expected losses differ by USD 150.
This witness is not a claim about the package’s fitted normal distribution or a measured
software defect. It demonstrates why a clipping option belongs in the scientific specification.
A prototype should compare declared bounds, clipped mass and decision values under justified
alternatives, and should not hide extrapolation problems by silently changing the simulated
law.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026ao)
22.16. Preserving longitudinal policies when reusing gfoRmula                                311


22.16.5     Bootstrap success is a scientific denominator

The inspected bootstrap resamples whole person identifiers and their associated histories, refits
models, and adjusts the simulated population. This preserves within-person records for each
sampled individual. It does not by itself represent common bank shocks, shared calendar
effects or errors in a common audit source. The appropriate independent unit depends on
the observation experiment. A larger person-level bootstrap cannot manufacture independent
calendars.(CausalInference gfoRmula contributors, 2025)
   The failure wrapper warns and returns missing results for failed replicates. The downstream
standard-deviation and quantile calculations remove missing values. This is an observable
source-level rule, not evidence that any particular native run has failed. Its implication for a
proposed interface is nevertheless concrete: report requested, completed and failed replicate
counts, failure reasons and the aggregation policy. An interval from the surviving replicates
must not be described as though every requested fit contributed.
   For a simple authored illustration, take four replicate estimates (0, 1, 2, 3). Their mean is
3/2 and their sample variance is 5/3. Retaining only (0, 1) changes the mean to 1/2 and the
sample variance to 1/2. Selective computational survival can therefore change the resampling
distribution. This example does not estimate actual failure probabilities or interval coverage
for gfoRmula. It motivates a qualification experiment that retains every request and tests
whether failure depends on difficult histories, sparse actions or unstable model fits.(Causal
banking proposal project, 2026ao)
   Monte Carlo error within each fit, sampling uncertainty across fits, model misspecification
and lack of causal identification remain distinct. A proposed study should vary M while
holding the observed data fixed to assess numerical integration, then repeat independent
observed datasets under a known mechanism to assess the complete estimation and interval
procedure. Natural-course agreement is a useful diagnostic for the fitted observed law, but
it cannot verify unobserved counterfactuals or exchangeability. The selected upstream tests
mainly check that example calls do not raise errors; they have not been run here and do not
replace an independent causal or numerical oracle.(CausalInference gfoRmula contributors,
2025)


22.16.6     A reference worker and a public qualification route

The proposal retains the pinned original R implementation as a reference candidate. A future
process-separated worker could preserve the existing intervention, history, visit and bootstrap
behavior more directly than a new port. Direct in-process adoption would add runtime and
dependency commitments; a port would duplicate scientifically material semantics and need
independent reconciliation. Neither has demonstrated an advantage here. Rejecting the entire
package would also be unjustified: the inspected methods are relevant to bounded longitudinal
questions even though unrestricted dependent-bank inference remains unsupported. The source
declares GPL-3 and R dependencies, but a complete distribution, dependency and rights review
is still required before packaging or porting it.(CausalInference gfoRmula contributors, 2025)
   The proposed request contract includes person identity, event and availability clocks, ordered
covariate models, intervention schedules, history conventions, observation and competing-
event targets, restrictions, n, M , B, seeds and range-clipping settings. Custom callbacks
need immutable, reviewed identities. The output should identify a terminal mean, terminal
probability or cumulative-risk curve; name its reference policy; preserve contrasts and numerical
warnings; and separate sampling from simulation uncertainty. Invalid clocks, unsupported
target coding, unqualified dependence and unacceptable replicate loss require explicit failure or
312                                                                    Causal analysis for a universal bank


unsupported status. The same typed object should survive library, CLI and MCP transport.
   The first qualification experiment can use generated public mechanisms with the exact
two-period values above, then extend to competing events, missing visits and alternative history
conventions. A second experiment should isolate threshold and schedule semantics, clipping
and person resampling, including intentionally failed fits. A third should test serialization,
deterministic seed handling where promised and sequential versus parallel reproducibility at
a frozen environment. Licensed public longitudinal data can then assess realistic support,
censoring, fit diagnostics and computational burden, while retaining that real-data causal truth
is usually unavailable. Simulation, refitting, conversion and analyst review costs should all be
measured on matched accepted outputs. These experiments justify a prototype comparison;
they do not confer native qualification, independent acceptance or bank adoption.

Sequential servicing software becomes useful only after the intervention is specified as a rule on

with no permission to infer that an adapter is implemented. The authenticated package
declaration and license are AGPL-3; the README’s GPL badge differs. In particular, a
separate process is not a sufficient argument about distribution or network-source obligations.
A concrete proposed arrangement and its dependency rights still require review. (Nicholas
Williams, Ivan Diaz and contributors, 2026)
  For a binary action with natural probability et (h) at history h, the inspected ipsi function
