22.17.1     Histories, folds, numerical safeguards and uncertainty are distinct
            contracts

In the inspected interface, supplied shifted data overrides a shift function; shifted censoring
becomes one, and each shift function reads the original data argument. A bridge must
preserve the declared sequence and the role of those inputs rather than silently reapply earlier
modifications. Restricting the history length k changes which information nuisance regressions
receive. That is a computational choice requiring a scientific sufficiency argument; it does not
establish sequential exchangeability. (Nicholas Williams, Ivan Diaz and contributors, 2026)
   Source inspection finds a further distinction between intended and realized cluster handling.
Data construction writes ..i..lmtp_id, while an outer-fold call reads ._lmtp_id. Inner
learner cross-validation checks and forwards its own IDs, and the final ife call receives
task$id. These are different paths. The naming mismatch needs a native reproduction before
any observed consequence is asserted. It cannot be repaired by pointing to the existence of
IDs elsewhere. The fold helper may lower the requested number of folds; at V = 1 it uses the
same training and validation set. The adapter should retain realized folds and clusters and
qualify the sampling law rather than report only a requested option.
   The documented prediction bound is 10−5 , but the control function’s default is 105 . Following
the estimator call sites changes the conclusion: the inspected TMLE predictions pass a hard-
coded 10−5 , while the SDR predictions pass a null bound. There is no basis here for claiming
an observed estimator output of 100,000. Density-ratio calculations cap a denominator at
0.999 and subsequently trim using a quantile over the supplied object. Warning suppression,
global trimming and cumulative ratio-weighted residuals can affect diagnostics. None of
these numerical devices proves support, nuisance convergence rates or calibrated uncertainty.
(Nicholas Williams, Ivan Diaz and contributors, 2026)
   The returned estimate is a policy value; its singular estimate field must not be mistaken
for an automatically formed contrast. A contrast between two estimated policies also needs
their covariance. Variance and contrast semantics delegated to ife, full survival handling,
learner internals and parallel random-number behavior remain unqualified. Public known-law
histories can test policy mapping, fold integrity and contrast preservation before expensive
bank experiments. This is a concrete route to evaluating a longitudinal reference while keeping
adoption and coverage as later claims.


22.18      Longitudinal regime contrasts: preserving the effective
           uncertainty method
A servicing proposal can compare a fixed contact schedule with a rule that responds to
hardship observed after an earlier contact. The distinction matters because the first contact
314                                                                  Causal analysis for a universal bank


may change both hardship and the second action. The selected ltmle source provides an R
reference for binary treatment regimes, longitudinal treatment and censoring histories, and
treatment-specific means. Its ltmle interface handles a single regime or a pair; its ltmleMSM
interface also supports a working marginal structural model. A general working model is a
projection under specified weights and covariates; it need not reproduce each separate regime
mean. A saturated two-regime parameterization is a special case. The number of policies
alone does not determine whether a working model is saturated.(Joshua Schwab and ltmle
contributors, 2023)
   The inspected revision declares version 1.3-0 and GPL-2. The main source, package decla-
ration and supporting files match the complete tree of commit 338c029dae9692ef20714125
773da7037688993b, dated 17 April 2023. A new default-branch query restricted to the client
cutoff returns this same commit. Repository metadata also records a June 2026 push; that
event alone does not establish a newer default-branch estimator or equality with a CRAN
artifact. The declared imports are Matrix and matrixStats; SuperLearner is suggested and
required by the inspected non-GLM path. The default SL.library="glm" uses generalized
linear models. It does not request an ensemble merely because an ensemble option exists.
(Joshua Schwab and ltmle contributors, 2023)

22.18.2     Why a named variance option is insufficient

The source defaults to variance.method="tmle", but CreateInputs switches to ic when the
additional variance method is unavailable. In the inspected revision, non-null id, nonbinary
outcomes, gcomp, stratification and a deterministic-Q function each make that additional
method unavailable. The fallback itself does not always warn: a separate warning path checks
selected positivity and rare-event indicators. The absence of that warning is therefore not
evidence that the caller’s requested method ran.(Joshua Schwab and ltmle contributors, 2023)
   For a single-regime TMLE summary, the code takes the larger of the available influence-curve
and additional variance estimates. For paired regimes, it applies each contrast gradient to
the covariance matrices and selects the larger available standard deviation for that reported
measure. It does not justify a new covariance matrix formed by taking every element’s
maximum. Risk and odds ratios are removed for nonbinary outcomes. Transformations back to
the outcome scale, including the distinction between mean and difference, must be preserved. A
larger variance estimate alone is not a proof of coverage.(Joshua Schwab and ltmle contributors,
2023)
  For clustered records, HouseholdIC sums record contributions within each identifier and
multiplies them by m/n, where m is the number of identifiers and n is the number of records.
Subsequent summary calculations use the number of influence rows. This keeps the record-
weighted target; it does not automatically change that target to an equally weighted mean of
households of different sizes. The choice of weights and scientific sampling unit must precede
the conversion.
  Consider a separate exact covariance fixture with four household influence pairs
(−3, −2), (−1, 0), (1, 0), (3, 2), each repeated twice as records. These are hypothetical influence
316                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


values, not fitted ltmle output. Aggregation and rescaling recover the four pairs. Dividing
their sample covariance by four gives the covariance of the two means as
                                 !
                        5/3 1            d θb1 − θb0 ) = 5/3 + 2/3 − 2 = 1/3.
                 Σ
                 b =           ,         Var(                                             (22.55)
                         1 2/3

Dropping the covariance instead gives 7/3. Treating the eight duplicated records as independent
gives variance 5/7 for the first mean, instead of 5/3. Their exact ratio is 7/3 because sample
variance uses different degrees of freedom. The often-quoted factor of two is the leading
population-variance comparison for two identical records per independent household. Neither
the four-household calculation nor a small-sample t critical value proves calibration. ltmle uses
a t critical value below 100 influence rows and a normal critical value otherwise; the sampling
law and nuisance remainder still need justification. (Joshua Schwab and ltmle contributors,
2023; Causal banking proposal authors, 2026)


22.18.3     A proposed R comparator and the alternatives

A candidate interface should declare the node order, policy information set, binary action
coding, event/censoring coding, outcome range, target weights and cluster identity. Dynamic
rules must not read future outcomes merely because the R function receives a complete row.
Numeric censoring inputs use zero for censored and one for uncensored; the named conversion
helper distinguishes that meaning from a censoring indicator. For absorbing events, the source
checks that later outcome nodes remain one before cleaning post-event records. The shorthand
that later data are “ignored” must not erase that validation requirement.(Joshua Schwab and
ltmle contributors, 2023)
   The cumulative-probability floor defaults to 0.01 after multiplying the incremental factors. It
is not a floor on each factor before multiplication. The source returns bounded and unbounded
cumulative probabilities, which support diagnostics; neither operation proves positivity. The
outcome-range code can truncate values before scaling and has a division by the range width,
motivating an explicit positive-width contract for a future adapter. No warning should be
interpreted as a complete fit audit: inspected helpers suppress some rank-deficient prediction
and extreme-probability warnings, and the targeting helper can suppress a nonconvergence
warning before its score-repair path. A failed matrix solve can return missing standard errors.
Unavailable uncertainty must remain an explicit result state. (Joshua Schwab and ltmle
contributors, 2023)
   The proposal retains this version as a technical reference and a candidate native R comparator.
Direct integration requires resolved dependencies, distribution rights, observed fit and warning
behavior, and matched tests against the declared policy and covariance targets. The GPL-2
declaration and license distinguish running software from distributing or modifying it; a
separate process is not, by itself, a legal compatibility determination. An integration design
must review the actual distribution and dependency chain. Porting to Python, Java or
C++ additionally requires parity for history/rule construction, censoring, outcome scaling,
cumulative bounds, learner behavior, clustering and covariance. No measured deployment
or performance need currently justifies that larger porting cost. (Joshua Schwab and ltmle
contributors, 2023)
   lmtp and gfoRmula remain substantive alternatives with their own modified treatment,
simulation and uncertainty contracts. Their names do not establish equivalent interventions
or interchangeable output. Selection should follow the requested regime and observation law,
then compare full fitting, diagnostics, uncertainty, failure handling and maintenance costs.
This source-level reference decision grants no native integration capability. The exact examples
22.18. Longitudinal regime contrasts: preserving the effective uncertainty method       317


specify what a proposed trial should preserve; package execution and empirical qualification
remain distinct evidence.
Chapter 23

Panel and time-series comparisons
for a banking rollout

A regional rollout of a deposit-servicing program creates several plausible comparisons. An
early region can be compared with a later region, with a weighted combination of unaffected
regions, or with its own forecast under the old operating rule. Each comparison uses a different
source of counterfactual information. They also answer different questions when treatment
effects vary over the life of a relationship, the donor regions face different funding shocks, or
the bank changes the rule that responds to those shocks.
   The earlier panel and time-series chapters establish the identification and estimation founda-
tions. The task here is to connect the resulting estimands to executable comparisons without
discarding heterogeneity, extrapolation risk or the calendar on which uncertainty arises. A
regression’s lead coefficient may contain post-treatment effects. Exact donor balance may
increase mean squared error. Positive persistence may reduce the variance of an adjacent
difference while leaving a much larger uncertainty for a comparison spanning several periods.
An impulse response under the existing feedback rule need not describe the response after that
rule changes.
  We develop these distinctions using exact stipulated laws. The amounts are illustrative
dollars per declared unit of exposure; none is an estimate from a bank. The constructions supply
reproducible mathematical references for a future public-data or generated-data prototype.
Literature claims retain their specific original versions, while the finite examples and the
extensions of their algebra are project derivations.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cn)


23.1      An event-study lead can be made from treatment effects
Let G denote the first treatment period, with G = ∞ for a never-treated group. Under an
absorbing rollout, the observed outcome in cohort g at time t has mean

                 ygt = µ0gt + 1{t ≥ g}τgt ,    τgt = E{Yt (g) − Yt (∞) | G = g}.            (23.1)

The superscript zero denotes the untreated mean. No anticipation says that the treated and
untreated potential outcomes agree before g. It places no restriction requiring the early and
late cohorts to have equal effects after their own adoption. Sun and Abraham show that
pooling relative-time indicators with unit and time effects can mix treatment effects from
other relative times into a reported coefficient, including a lead. The inspected original is their
September 2020 arXiv version, associated with the 2021 publication; its technical text is not
represented as the final journal version.(Sun and Abraham, 2021)

                                               318
23.1. An event-study lead can be made from treatment effects                                  319


   Consider an equally weighted, balanced population table with three groups, g = 2, 3, ∞,
and five periods, t = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. All untreated means are zero. All treatment effects are zero
except τ2,2 = 20. Thus the early region has a one-period implementation gain of USD 20,
and neither region has any anticipatory effect. These premises deliberately eliminate a true
pretrend. They isolate a projection problem that would otherwise be confused with a failure
of the rollout’s causal assumptions.
   For each of the 15 cells, put an intercept, two group indicators and four time indicators
in a nuisance matrix Z. Its seven columns are linearly independent. Put the five event-time
indicators
                   D(g,t),k = 1{g ̸= ∞, t − g = k},    k ∈ (−3, −2, 0, 1, 2)           (23.2)
in a matrix D. Every event indicator is zero for the never-treated group. The omitted relative
period is −1. The extreme lead −3 and lag 2 are included explicitly, rather than silently
pooled or dropped. The complete 15 by 12 design [Z, D] has exact rank 12. Consequently
the following coefficients are uniquely defined; no generalized inverse or accidental collinearity
supplies the result.
   Residualize against Z by MZ = I − Z(Z ′ Z)−1 Z ′ . The event coefficients in the population
least-squares projection are
                                b = (D′ MZ D)−1 D′ MZ y.                                (23.3)
For this example y consists entirely of the five possible post-treatment cell effects, ordered as
(τ2,2 , τ2,3 , τ2,4 , τ3,3 , τ3,4 )′ . The corresponding columns of the projection operator are

Rows follow the five event times in (23.2). These are projection weights for this declared table,
not universal software weights. For example, the first row subtracts the late cohort’s impact
and first-lag effects from positive weights on the early cohort’s corresponding effects. It is
not an average of pre-treatment outcomes or pre-treatment causal effects. The first two row
sums are zero, but their individual entries are nonzero. A zero row sum cannot protect a lead
against heterogeneous effects.
  Multiplication by (20, 0, 0, 0, 0)′ yields

Both leads are positive although every pre-treatment causal effect is zero. Even the lag-
two coefficient is negative although the only nonzero effect in the entire table is positive.
The example therefore concerns the meaning of the coefficients before any standard error is
computed.
   There are two useful checks on this calculation. Direct solution of the full normal equations
gives a residual orthogonal to all 12 columns. Alternatively, double demean every event
indicator and the outcome: subtract its group mean and time mean and add its overall mean.
Regressing the demeaned outcome on the five demeaned indicators gives exactly (23.5). The
two calculations use different representations of the nuisance adjustment. Both retain rational
arithmetic, so a small numerical tolerance cannot hide the false leads.(Causal banking proposal,
2026cn)
320                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The weights explain when cancellation would occur. If the two cohorts had the same impact
effect and the same first-lag effect, the positive and negative entries in the first two rows would
cancel pairwise. The witness violates that homogeneity while satisfying no anticipation and an
identical untreated law. It does not show that an observed bank pretrend is always spurious. An
actual lead can reflect genuine anticipation, a different untreated trend, changing composition,
or regression contamination. Distinguishing these possibilities requires a target-preserving
estimator and substantive knowledge of assignment and information.
   For a regional program, an apparent gain two periods before adoption should therefore
trigger examination of the comparison weights and rollout clock. It should not automatically
certify early customer response or disqualify the program. Adding more customers to the
same misinterpreted projection can make its standard error smaller while preserving the wrong
population quantity. In particular, a precise lead test cannot turn (23.3) into an estimate of a
different causal target.
   The operational alternative is to retain cohort-by-calendar-time contrasts, their admissible
untreated comparisons and their joint uncertainty, then aggregate to the declared exposure
target. The earlier cohort identification argument remains necessary: choosing a heterogeneous-
effect estimator does not establish parallel trends, support or absence of spillovers. The
inspected eventstudyinteract manual describes an interacted regression followed by cohort-
share weighting, and warns about its control cohort and balanced-panel validity conditions.
Its returned interacted coefficients and its weighted estimates are distinct objects. Those
restrictions should govern a proposed wrapper, including the choice of saved covariance; the
presence of a familiar event-study plot cannot serve as semantic admission.(EventStudyInteract
contributors, 2023)


23.2      The horizon determines the trend-sensitivity budget
Correcting the event-study projection does not settle the counterfactual trend. We now take
as input an admissible treated-minus-comparison mean series for a fixed population. This can
be one cohort or a fixed aggregation with a common, explicitly defined gap process. It cannot
be a sequence whose cohort composition changes and is then interpreted as the trend of one
unchanging population without further justification.
  Index the last untreated period by −1, and let dt be the untreated treated-minus-comparison
gap. Define the last observed untreated slope v = d−1 −d−2 . For future periods j = 0, . . . , J −1,
impose the specific curvature restriction

                             uj = dj − 2dj−1 + dj−2 ,        |uj | ≤ M.                       (23.6)

The constant M is measured in outcome units per squared calendar period. It is a maintained
sensitivity choice, not the largest observed residual relabelled as truth. Changing months to
quarters changes the restriction. Rambachan and Roth motivate smoothness and relative-
magnitude restrictions as distinct choices and develop inference that accounts for noisy pre-
treatment information. The construction below specializes a curvature restriction to one explicit
horizon target; it is not an implementation of their optimized inference procedures.(Rambachan
and Roth, 2023)
   The bias in a baseline-−1 contrast at horizon j is bj = dj − d−1 . Taking first differences in
(23.6) and summing twice gives

slopes counts the curvature uk exactly j − k + 1 times. A distant effect is exposed to an early
change of slope repeatedly. This triangular propagation is the reason a long rollout evaluation
can be much more sensitive than its first-period estimate, even with the same numerical M .

   For nonnegative aj , the radius simplifies to M j aj (j + 1)(j + 2)/2. Signed weights require

wide. For example, a = (1, −2, 0)′ has c = (−3, −2, 0)′ and radius 5M , whereas summing the

At M = 3 the effect set is [5, 25]. The endpoint paths can be constructed by setting all three
future curvatures to 3 or −3. Exhaustive evaluation of the eight vertices agrees with the
triangular formula. This is a population identification calculation, so its endpoints do not
carry a 95% coverage label.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cn)
   Suppose the recurring incremental operating cost is USD 10 in the same exposure-period
units. Subtracting this fixed cost gives the net-effect set [5 − (10/3)M, 5 + (10/3)M ]. A strictly
positive lower net value requires M < 1.5; at M = 1.5 it is exactly zero. At M = 3 the net
range is [−5, 15], which leaves the sign unresolved even with the population means known.
This threshold explains what substantive trend restriction an investment recommendation
would require. It does not establish that the restriction is credible or that the illustrative cost
is an actual price.
  An average exposure-period benefit must also be distinguished from a three-period total.
With the same three equal exposure counts, the total has target weights (1, 1, 1)′ , center 45
and curvature radius 10M . Three periods of the same recurring cost total 30, leaving net
center 15. The positivity threshold remains M < 1.5, because both benefit and cost were
322                                                                   Causal analysis for a universal bank


scaled consistently. Subtracting a single cost of 10 from that total would answer a different
economic question. Unequal exposure counts, discounting or an upfront fixed cost alter the
target weights or cost functional and require recalculation of the kernel.

23.2.1     Retaining the uncertainty in the extrapolated slope

The preceding center contains an estimated pre-period slope in a real study. Normalize
the gap at −1 to zero and let β−2 = d−2 − d−1 = −v. Assemble the estimate vector
ηb = (βb−2 , βb0 , . . . , βbJ−1 )′ with its full covariance matrix Σ. For fixed target weights, define
h = (L, a′ )′ . The trend-adjusted center and its sampling variance are
                                       b = h′ ηb,
                                       m               s2m = h′ Σh.                               (23.11)
The plus sign on the pre-period coefficient is necessary because the subtracted slope is v = −β−2 .
Even if the post-period contrasts were estimated independently of one another, the common
estimated baseline would generally induce covariance with the pre-period contrast. Removing
the normalized zero coefficient does not remove that sampling dependence.
   For a finite normal design with ηb − η ∼ N (0, Σ) and known Σ, a conservative 1 − α interval
for the fixed target under the fixed restriction M is
                       h                                                        i
                           b − z1−α/2 sm − M ∥c∥1 , m
                           m                        b + z1−α/2 sm + M ∥c∥1 .                      (23.12)
On the event |m−m|
              b      ≤ z1−α/2 sm , every target permitted by the curvature restriction lies in this
interval. That event has probability 1 − α under the stipulated Gaussian design. This proves
the stated conservative coverage without identifying the unknown curvature from a pretest.
With an estimated covariance and an asymptotic normal approximation, a corresponding
conclusion needs the approximation and covariance consistency; finite exact coverage does not
follow merely from inserting a standard error.
  For the three-period average, stipulate the diagonal covariance Σ = diag(1, 4, 4, 4) in squared
dollars. This is a separate hypothetical sampling law, not a covariance inferred from the 15-cell
event-study table. Then
                                h = (2, 1/3, 1/3, 1/3)′ ,     s2m = 16/3.                         (23.13)
Ignoring the noisy slope would retain only variance 4/3, one quarter of the correct variance
under this particular law. At a 95% normal critical value of about 1.96, the sampling radius
is about USD 4.53. For an observed
                               p     center of 15 and recurring cost 10, a positive lower net
endpoint would require 5 − 1.96 16/3 − (10/3)M > 0, approximately M < 0.142. Population
robustness up to M = 1.5 thus need not imply useful statistical robustness with this sample
precision.
   The simple interval is deliberately conservative and uses only the last pre-period slope.
Additional pre-period information, joint restrictions and better optimized inference can improve
efficiency. The comparison with HonestDiD should retain this distinction. Its documented
smoothness and relative-magnitude procedures use different restriction families; the original
paper discusses why fixed-length, conditional and hybrid approaches have different domains.
A result from one cannot be labelled as another because their output endpoints happen to
resemble each other.(Rambachan and Roth, 2023; asheshrambachan contributors, 2026)
  There is a further selection issue. The proof fixes M , the target a and the method before
examining favorable post-period estimates. Searching over horizons or restrictions and reporting
the first positive endpoint is a different random procedure. It requires a joint selection or
simultaneous inference argument. A sensitivity curve can be reported as a collection of
conditional conclusions without claiming that the most favorable point on the curve has its
nominal coverage after selection.
23.3. Donor balance is a bias–noise decision                                                 323


23.3      Donor balance is a bias–noise decision
An unaffected donor pool can supply a different counterfactual. Perfect pre-period fit is
attractive, but the future value of extrapolating beyond that pool depends on noise and
contamination as well as balance. To isolate the tradeoff, take a single post-period untreated
outcome law
                   YT (0) = 2f + εT ,     Y0 (0) = ε0 ,    Y1 (0) = f + ε1 .           (23.14)
Here the treated region has known loading 2, the two donors have known loadings 0 and 1,
and the common factor satisfies |f | ≤ B. The centered errors are independent with donor
variances σ 2 and treated variance σT2 . The loadings and bound are conditional premises of the
example, not quantities learned exactly from a short panel.
   Use donor weights (1 − a, a), which sum to one. Their sum removes a common additive
level, if present, but their weighted loading is a. The untreated counterfactual residual is

       R(a) = YT (0) − (1 − a)Y0 (0) − aY1 (0) = (2 − a)f + εT − (1 − a)ε0 − aε1 .       (23.15)

The same residual is the error in a treatment-effect estimate obtained by subtracting this donor
counterfactual from the treated observation. Conditional on f , its expectation is (2 − a)f , and
its variance is σT2 + σ 2 {(1 − a)2 + a2 }. Taking the worst mean squared error over the declared
factor interval gives

                         R(a) = σT2 + σ 2 {(1 − a)2 + a2 } + B 2 (2 − a)2 .              (23.16)

The derivative is 2σ 2 (2a − 1) + 2B 2 (a − 2), so the unique unrestricted minimizer, when
2σ 2 + B 2 > 0, is
                                             σ 2 + 2B 2
                                        a∗ = 2          .                              (23.17)
                                             2σ + B 2
It lies between 1/2 and 2. As B approaches zero with positive noise, the two donors are
averaged to reduce variance. As the factor bound dominates the noise, the weight approaches
2 and exactly matches the treated loading, at the cost of a negative first-donor weight.
  With B = 2 and σ 2 = σT2 = 1, the complete risk is
                                                       9
                           R(a) = 6a2 − 18a + 18 =       + 6(a − 3/2)2 .                 (23.18)
                                                       2
Nonnegative weights restrict a to [0, 1]; the best value on that interval is a = 1 with risk 6.
Exact loading balance uses a = 2 and also has risk 6. The intermediate weights (−1/2, 3/2)
have risk 9/2. Their squared bias at the worst factor endpoint is 1, while their noise variance
is 7/2. The exact fit eliminates this bias but raises the noise variance to 6. In this law, exact
fit spends too much variance to remove the remaining imbalance.
  This calculation is a conditional minimax comparison over a known factor bound and fixed
weights. It is not a general risk guarantee for ridge augmentation, and a∗ is not claimed to
be the output of a particular package. Ben-Michael, Feller and Rothstein develop augmented
synthetic control, including a ridge representation that adjusts balance and can produce
negative weights. Their inspected July 2020 manuscript explains how a penalty controls
departures from the original synthetic-control weights. That mechanism motivates comparison
with the tradeoff above; it does not identify the bank’s B or noise law.(Ben-Michael et al.,
2021)
  Diagnostics should therefore report more than a pre-fit score. The estimated loading or
outcome imbalance, the norm of the weights, and the validation distribution under which a
penalty is selected all matter. Selecting a penalty on post-treatment outcomes can absorb the
324                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


effect being estimated. Selecting it on held-out pre-periods avoids that specific leakage but
still requires an argument that the pre-period prediction task is informative about the relevant
untreated post-period task. A factor that becomes economically important only after rollout
can defeat that transfer.


23.3.1    Signed weights also amplify donor contamination

Suppose the donor observations instead contain unknown mean shifts c0 , c1 with |ci | ≤ C.
Such shifts may represent spillovers from the program or an unrecorded intervention in the
comparison region. Keeping (23.14) otherwise fixed, the worst absolute mean error is

                                   B|2 − a| + C{|1 − a| + |a|}.                              (23.19)

The bound is sharp over the rectangular uncertainty set: choose the sign of f and each donor
shift to align the terms in the residual. If scientific knowledge links the shifts or restricts their
signs, that uncertainty set should be changed instead of asserting this rectangle is inevitable.
   The weight sums are all one, but their absolute sums are 1, 2 and 3 at a = 1, 3/2, 2. At a
contamination bound C = 3, the donor component alone can therefore contribute USD 3, 6 or
9 of bias. Exact loading fit does not protect against this distinct source of error. In a regional
deposit rollout, transfers of customers or marketing exposure across region boundaries can be
more consequential for a signed counterfactual than for a nonnegative one, even though both
use the same named donors.
  If the desired criterion is worst mean squared error with both sources of bounded bias, the
correct objective is

              RC (a) = σT2 + σ 2 {(1 − a)2 + a2 } + [B|2 − a| + C{|1 − a| + |a|}]2 .         (23.20)

The two bias budgets add before squaring because an adverse law can align them. Adding
their squared radii would discard the possible cross term. This distinction is consequential
even when every error variance is known.
   For B = 2, C = 1 and both variances equal to one, the bias radius is 5 − 4a for a ≤ 0, 5 − 2a
for 0 ≤ a ≤ 1, 3 for 1 ≤ a ≤ 2, and 4a − 5 for a ≥ 2. The corresponding risks are
                                      
                                      

                                       18a2 − 42a + 27,

                                      
                                      6a2 − 22a + 27,
                                      
                                                       0 ≤ a ≤ 1,
                            R1 (a) =     2

                                     
                                     
                                      2a − 2a + 11,   1 ≤ a ≤ 2,
                                     
                                     18a2 − 42a + 27, a ≥ 2.
                                     


The risk decreases up to the kink at a = 1 and increases after it. More explicitly, the stationary
points of the four pieces lie outside their respective intervals, and checking the three finite
kinks gives risks 27, 11, 15. The global minimizer is now the nonnegative choice a = 1. The
previously optimal a = 3/2 has risk 25/2, while exact fit has risk 15.
   This reversal is not a demonstration that signed weights should always be rejected. It
demonstrates that a conclusion about regularization depends on the uncertainty class. A
comparison claiming robustness to spillovers must price that class explicitly. The numerical
reference also checks the three candidate risks by enumerating every endpoint of the factor
and contamination rectangle and every combination of independent centered unit-variance
two-point errors. That direct expectation calculation agrees with (23.20).(Causal banking
proposal, 2026cn)
23.4. Synthetic DiD needs both axes of balance                                                                    325


23.4     Synthetic DiD needs both axes of balance
The preceding donor example isolates the unit axis. A block rollout also permits weighting
the pre-treatment calendar. To see what this adds, suppose the untreated mean satisfies

                                          E{Yit (0)} = αi + γt + ℓ′i ft ,                                      (23.22)

where ℓi and ft are vectors of the same dimension. This is a conditional factor representation,
with additive unit and calendar effects written separately. We do not infer its rank or predictive
validity from a small pre-fit residual. Let ui be normalized nonnegative weights on treated
units, wi normalized donor weights, vt normalized nonnegative weights on post periods, and
λt normalized pre-period weights. Each of the four vectors sums to one over its own support.
Donor and pre-period weights may be signed in the algebra below; allowing such weights is a
comparison exercise, not a description of the default constraints in an upstream estimator.
  Form the fixed-weight double difference
                                                         !                                               !
                   X          X                X                X            X                X
         τbw,λ =         ui         vt Yit −         λt Yit −         wi           vt Yit −         λt Yit .   (23.23)
                   i∈T        t∈P              t∈B              i∈C          t∈P              t∈B

Here T, C are the treated and control sets, while P, B are post and pre calendars. In a block
design, only cells in T by P receive the treatment. The target causal effect is the treated-post
                        P
weighted mean τu,v = i∈T,t∈P ui vt τit . This explicit target allows heterogeneous effects; it
should not be silently exchanged for a simple unweighted ATT when the exposure weights
differ.
  Normalization cancels the unit effects because the post-minus-pre weights sum to zero for
each unit. It cancels the time effects because the treated-minus-donor weights sum to zero at
each time. The remaining factor contribution is exactly

                                     E(τbw,λ ) − τu,v = ∆′ℓ ∆f ,                                               (23.24)
                                                             X               X
                                                      ∆ℓ =         ui ℓi −         wi ℓi ,
                                                             i∈T             i∈C
                                                             X               X
                                                      ∆f =         vt ft −         λt ft .
                                                             t∈P             t∈B

The proof expands the four rectangles of the factor mean. Every term is bilinear, so they
collect into the product of the two imbalances. This gives a precise reason to combine unit and
time weighting. Eliminating either imbalance eliminates factor bias under this law. Reducing
both can make their product small without making either exactly zero.
  A Euclidean bound is |∆′ℓ ∆f | ≤ ∥∆ℓ ∥2 ∥∆f ∥2 . But the separate Euclidean norms depend on
how factors are scaled. Replacing ℓi by Aℓi and ft by A−T ft for an invertible A leaves every
outcome mean and the product unchanged. It need not preserve the two Euclidean norms.
Consequently numerical certificates for separate loading and factor bounds must declare their
normalization; the observed outcome fit alone does not provide a unique latent scale.
   For fixed weights and independent cell errors with common variance σ 2 , the noise variance
of the contrast is
                         Var(τbw,λ ) = σ 2 (∥u∥22 + ∥w∥22 )(∥v∥22 + ∥λ∥22 ).           (23.25)
Each cell’s coefficient is the product of its signed unit and time coefficient. Squaring and
summing these products separates into the two squared norms. This proof requires independent
cells and weights fixed relative to the errors. Serial correlation, shared calendar shocks or
weights fitted to those errors change the variance problem.
326                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   For an exact comparison, take one treated unit with loading 2, two donors with loadings 0
and 1, pre-period factors 0 and 1, and one post-period factor 3/2. Begin with donor weights
(0, 1) and pre-period weights (1/4, 3/4). The loading imbalance is 1 and the factor imbalance
is 3/4, giving bias 3/4 and noise variance (13/4)σ 2 . Changing only the time weights to
(−1/2, 3/2) matches the post factor exactly and eliminates the factor bias. It raises the noise
variance to 7σ 2 . Changing only the donor weights to (−1, 2) also eliminates factor bias, but
gives variance (39/4)σ 2 . All three calculations can be recovered by multiplying the actual 3 by
3 factor-mean table by its signed unit and time coefficients.
  Under these independent-cell premises, their mean squared errors are

               R+ = 9/16 + (13/4)σ 2 ,       Rtime = 7σ 2 ,     Runit = (39/4)σ 2 .        (23.26)

The signed time extrapolation improves on the nonnegative comparison only when σ 2 < 3/20.
The signed unit comparison has a still higher variance than the signed time comparison in this
particular table. At σ 2 = 1, leaving the small factor bias costs less in mean squared error than
either exact fit. At σ 2 = 1/10, signed time matching has risk 7/10, below the nonnegative risk
71/80. The comparison depends on the post factor, which was stipulated as known here; an
analyst cannot select the favorable matching rule using an unobserved bank counterfactual.
  There is also an important distinction between small mean squared error and a valid
confidence interval. If the remaining bias is not negligible relative to the standard error,
centering a nominal interval at the biased comparison does not acquire coverage from having
lower mean squared error. A defended factor-bias envelope can instead be carried into a
conservative interval, or a different inferential procedure can be justified for a specified factor
and sampling regime. The risk table is a design comparison, not an inference theorem.
   Arkhangelsky and coauthors develop synthetic DiD with learned unit and time weights
for a block design. The inspected original’s formal normality result assumes independent
identically distributed Gaussian rows with a well-behaved within-row covariance, particular
growth conditions, spectral restrictions and sufficiently predictive, dispersed oracle weights. It
does not require independent calendar cells within a row, but its independent-row assumption
excludes an unrestricted shared shock across units. The proof also includes a regularization-rate
condition. Neither the fixed-weight identity (23.24) nor a good numerical pre-fit establishes
those premises.(Arkhangelsky et al., 2021)
   The same original distinguishes unit bootstrap, a jackknife that holds estimated weights
fixed, and placebo-based variance estimation. Its jackknife result uses the theorem’s conditions
and additional restrictions; validity is not inferred simply because the estimator has an influence
representation. The single-treated-unit case also requires separate care: the described jackknife
is not defined there, while the placebo variance argument relies on comparability of untreated
noise across units. This is a substantive reason to retain the inference method in the output,
rather than treating bootstrap, jackknife and placebo as interchangeable settings.(Arkhangelsky
et al., 2021)
   The inspected synthdid documentation requires simultaneous treatment onset and shows a
matrix interface with the number of control units and pre periods. It also describes the saved
interface as beta. A proposed integration can wrap that declared block route. It should reject
direct admission of staggered adoption, then either choose a separately justified cohort design
or state that the block route does not answer the request. A mathematical extension discussed
in a paper does not prove that a saved software interface implements it.(synth-inference
contributors, 2026)
23.5. Uncertainty belongs to the signed calendar contrast                                        327


23.5      Uncertainty belongs to the signed calendar contrast
A bank can have millions of account rows and few independent regional funding shocks. At
the same time, the direction of serial correlation’s effect depends on the signs in the requested
contrast. Consider fixed unit coefficients qi and calendar coefficients rt , each summing to zero.
                                               P     P
A double difference has the scalar form θb = i qi t rt Yit . Suppose its untreated noise is

                              eit = ℓi bt + ϵit ,    Cov(bt , bs ) = Γts ,                    (23.27)

with independent, centered cell errors ϵit of common variance σ 2 , independent of b. The
                              P                                                   P
loadings ℓi are fixed. Let κ = i qi ℓi . The shared component of the contrast is κ t rt bt , so
                                     b = κ2 r ′ Γr + σ 2 ∥q∥2 ∥r∥2 .

This is a finite-calendar covariance calculation, with no large-sample claim hidden in the
notation. If the unit contrast balances the common loading exactly, κ = 0, this particular
                                            P

  Let bt be stationary AR(1), with marginal variance σb2 and correlation ρ|t−s| , |ρ| < 1. For
the gap-h difference r = (−1, 0, . . . , 0, 1)′ ,

                               r′ Γr = Var(bh − b0 ) = 2σb2 (1 − ρh ).                        (23.29)

The covariance enters with a minus sign. For a short difference and positive persistence, nearby
common shocks partially cancel. For a longer gap they cancel less. This observation does
not support ignoring serial correlation; it shows why transferring a variance-of-a-level-mean

This derivation verifies the finite covariance result without constructing a Toeplitz covariance
matrix. It also exposes why the stationary initial-state variance matters. Starting the process
at a known fixed zero state would give a different finite-calendar law.
   For one treated region and one donor, set q = (1, −1)′ and κ = 1. With σb2 = 100, ρ = 4/5
and σ 2 = 1, the adjacent difference has common variance 40 and idiosyncratic variance 4, for
total 44. The gap-three difference has common variance 488/5 = 97.6 and total 508/5 = 101.6.
Both use the same two regions and the same number of observed endpoints. Their uncertainty
differs because of the interval they span, not because one has more customer records.(Causal
banking proposal, 2026cn)
   To examine customer replication explicitly, suppose each region-period outcome is the mean
of n customers with independent unit-variance idiosyncratic errors and the same regional
loading. The idiosyncratic variance of that mean is 1/n, so the two total variances become
40 + 4/n and 97.6 + 4/n. As n increases, the limits are 40 and 97.6. This calculation gives an
economic reason to acquire more independent regions or periods when feasible: an additional
customer in an already observed shock cell cannot remove the common component. It does
not prove that any given additional region is independent, uncontaminated or comparable.
328                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The covariance also interacts with weighting. In the double difference, q contains the treated
and signed donor weights, and r contains post and signed pre weights. Choosing a weight to
balance a factor can reduce κ while increasing ∥q∥2 or ∥r∥2 . The independent-cell variance
formula (23.25) is therefore a special case of a more specific noise law, rather than a generic
cost attached to every synthetic comparison. If weights are fitted from the same outcome
errors, their randomness adds a further issue beyond the covariance of a fixed contrast.
   An inferential route must specify which dimension supplies independent replication and
what remains conditional. Resampling customers does not reproduce a region-level common
shock. Resampling whole units respects within-unit trajectories but does not automatically
reproduce shocks shared across all units. A time-block route needs a defended dependence
regime and enough calendar information; a short fixed calendar cannot be made asymptotically
long by changing the resampling option. The earlier covariance and dependence chapters
provide possible methods. Here the requirement is to evaluate them for the actual signed
target, including its loading imbalance and its information clock.


23.6     A response under feedback is a policy-specific response
A regional time series supplies yet another comparison: forecast the outcome under the existing
operating rule and perturb an action. The intervention must be specified together with the
rule that will react to its consequences. Consider the structural system

                         Yt = ρYt−1 + βAt + ϵt ,      At = kYt−1 + ut .                        (23.31)

The state Yt might be a standardized funding position, and At a signed adjustment in servicing
or funding intensity. The parameters and innovation interpretation are supplied structural
premises. A fitted autoregression does not by itself establish that its residual is an exogenous,
manipulable action shock. We compare differences between paths with the same initial state
and structural innovations, so the additive ϵt cancels in the response calculation.
  Introduce a unit action innovation at time zero, u0 = 1, and set later innovations to zero. If
the operating feedback remains k, substitution into the state equation gives the response

                            Rhmaint = β(ρ + βk)h ,        h = 0, 1, . . . .                    (23.32)

The first state response is β. Its effect on the next action is kβ, which adds βkβ to the next
state response in addition to its inherited persistence ρβ. Repeating this recursion proves the
power in (23.32). The later action responses are kβ(ρ + βk)h−1 for h ≥ 1. A unit innovation is
therefore followed by a sequence of endogenous adjustments; it is not a one-period action path.
  If the bank instead forces A0 = 1 and every later action difference to zero, the response is

                                         Rhopen = βρh .                                        (23.33)

If it replaces the feedback coefficient by k ′ and then introduces the same unit innovation, the
corresponding response is
                                      Rhreplace = β(ρ + βk ′ )h .                        (23.34)
This last calculation assumes that the structural outcome law and innovation meaning survive
the replacement. A rule change that also changes the outcome mechanism needs a different
structural analysis. Moreover, it is the incremental response to an innovation within the
replacement regime; it is not the entire value of switching regimes from an arbitrary nonzero
initial portfolio.
23.7. Value includes the action path and the unobserved tail                                329


   Take ρ = 1/2, β = 1, k = 2/5 and k ′ = −1/5. At horizons zero through three the three
state paths are

                                   Rmaint = (1, 0.9, 0.81, 0.729),
                                   Ropen = (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125),
                                  Rreplace = (1, 0.3, 0.09, 0.027).                     (23.35)

All three have the same impact response. Their four-period sums are 3.439, 1.875 and 1.417.
At USD 100 of margin per state-period and an upfront USD 200 implementation cost, the
resulting net amounts, before charging later action intensity, are USD 143.90, −12.50 and
−58.30. A positive maintained-rule calculation can consequently coexist with a negative value
for the forced one-period action path. The discrepancy is a difference between interventions,
rather than an estimator’s rounding error.(Causal banking proposal, 2026cn)
   For this numerical example the action can be positive or negative without a capacity
bound. A real servicing action may be nonnegative, integer-valued or capped. Enforcing those
restrictions changes the recursion when they bind. Neither the powers above nor a linear
software response should then be presented as the response of the constrained policy without
solving that policy’s state evolution.


23.6.1    Closed-loop fit can leave the replacement response unidentified

Even a perfect fit to the old feedback system need not identify these interventions. Suppose the
observed action is always At = (2/5)Yt−1 , with no action innovation. Consider two structural
worlds:
                                 (ρ, β) = (1/2, 1) or (1/10, 2).                         (23.36)
Both imply Yt = (9/10)Yt−1 + ϵt under the observed rule. With the same initial law and
innovation law they generate the same joint distribution of all observed states and actions.
Yet replacing the feedback by k ′ = −1/5 gives state coefficients 3/10 and −3/10 respectively.
The observed reduced-form persistence and the known old action rule do not separate the
state persistence from the action effect.
   For a known initial state Y−1 = 1 and zero subsequent innovations, the four replacement-rule
states are (0.3, 0.09, 0.027, 0.0081) in the first world and (−0.3, 0.09, −0.027, 0.0081) in the
second. Their sums are 0.4251 and −0.2289, or USD 42.51 and −22.89 of gross margin at
the same conversion. These are state paths after a controller replacement, whereas (23.35)
describes innovation responses within each regime. Keeping that distinction prevents another
target substitution.
   The witness is deliberately a lack-of-excitation case. Exogenous variation in actions, a
defended instrument, a structural restriction on ρ or β, or a new experiment can provide
additional information. A high forecast score under the old controller cannot supply it. An
estimator request should therefore carry both the action-support evidence and the intervention
being asked of the time series. When these are absent, a set-valued answer or refusal is more
faithful to the observed information than a unique replacement-policy response.


23.7      Value includes the action path and the unobserved tail
The same horizon discipline used for the trend budget applies to feedback value. For a
deterministic zero-baseline example, let mh be dollars per state unit, d ∈ (0, 1] a per-period

23.8. Software routes must preserve the comparison                                          331


23.7.1    A conditional truncation budget

An infinite-horizon claim needs a defended tail restriction. Suppose uniformly over a declared
admissible regime |mh Rh | ≤ Crh with known C ≥ 0, r ≥ 0 and dr < 1. Then the absolute
omitted gross benefit after horizon H is bounded by

                                                  (dr)H+1
                                     TB (H) = C           .                             (23.41)
                                                   1 − dr
This follows by applying the triangle inequality to each omitted term and summing the
geometric series. It is an approximation budget conditional on a uniform structural envelope,
rather than a sampling standard error. With C = 100, d = 0.95, r = 0.9 and H = 3, it is about
USD 368.55. Reporting the four observed periods to cents does not reduce this stipulated
omitted-benefit budget.
  For the linear action envelope |∆Ah | ≤ |kβ|rh−1 at h ≥ 1, the omitted quadratic cost after
H ≥ 0 is nonnegative and bounded, if dr2 < 1, by

                                                       dH+1 r2H
                                   TA (H) = qk 2 β 2            .                       (23.42)
                                                        1 − dr2
Consequently, absent further sign information on the margin response, the omitted net value
belongs to [−TB (H)−TA (H), TB (H)]. This uses the known nonnegative sign of the cost instead
of adding a symmetric cost allowance to both ends. If benefits are also known nonnegative,
the lower endpoint can be tightened to −TA (H). Such sign information is another premise; it
is not supplied by the word “benefit.”
  If C = 0, the gross tail is zero at every horizon. For C > 0, an ex ante gross-tail tolerance
ε > 0 and 0 < dr < 1, the smallest admissible nonnegative integer horizon satisfies

                                            log{ε(1 − dr)/C}
                                 H +1 ≥                      .                          (23.43)
                                                 log(dr)

The reversed inequality follows because log(dr) < 0. In the numerical envelope, a USD 10
gross-tail tolerance needs H = 27: H = 26 still has a bound above USD 10, whereas H = 27
is below it. This is a requirement for the chosen envelope, not an instruction to forecast 28
periods (indices 0 through 27) from an uninformative short history. More credible long-horizon
restrictions, a finite contractual decision horizon, or an explicit unresolved value set may be
preferable.
   In statistical use, a simultaneous confidence region for structural parameters can be prop-
agated through finite-horizon value and a tail bound valid uniformly on that region. If the
region includes a parameter with an unbounded adverse tail, its corresponding lower value
cannot be replaced by the value at the stable point estimate. A claim about the region’s
coverage remains conditional on identification, dependence and estimation assumptions; the
deterministic tail inequality supplies none of them. This separation makes it possible to report
parameter, trend, donor, numerical and horizon limitations in their correct units without
calling every budget a confidence interval.


23.8     Software routes must preserve the comparison
The proposal should reuse a mature estimator where its target and sampling conditions
fit. The relevant choice is more specific than “run a panel package.” The required state
includes the rollout calendar, the permitted untreated comparisons, the population and horizon
332                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


weights, and the observation or innovation law. The selected primary documentation supports
three complementary routes below. It is a bounded comparison of inspected versions; the
wider software survey, complete dependency rights and runtime qualification remain separate
obligations.(Causal banking proposal, 2026co)


23.8.1    Cohort estimates followed by trend sensitivity

The first route uses a cohort-aware event-study estimator and passes a correctly normalized
estimate vector with its joint covariance to a trend-sensitivity procedure. The inspected
HonestDiD example for did requires a dynamic event study, a universal base period, consecutive
relative times and a reference period of −1. It constructs covariance from the dynamic influence
vectors and removes the normalized zero coefficient. Its example target vector selects one post
period. A discounted banking total needs an explicitly changed target vector and matching
outcome units, rather than adding the endpoints of several separately reported intervals.
(asheshrambachan contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026co)
   The bridge’s influence-product covariance is not a universal remedy for shared regional
calendar shocks. Its validity depends on the sampling units represented by the input influence
rows and the underlying estimator’s inferential regime. A proposed wrapper must either justify
the joint covariance for the bank’s actual design or decline the requested inferential claim.
Retaining the whole matrix also permits the noisy-slope contrast in (23.11); exporting only
marginal standard errors would lose that possibility.
  The selected eventstudyinteract route is a community Stata estimator. Its saved e(b_iw)
and e(V_iw) describe the weighted estimates; e(b) and e(V) retain the underlying interacted
regression. A subprocess wrapper should export the intended pair, its cohort weights and
support, rather than rely on whichever object a generic post-estimation command reads.
The manual says to exclude periods after the last cohort becomes treated when that cohort
supplies the controls. It also warns that the cited validity result is for balanced panels without
covariates, although the implementation accepts unbalanced data. Admitting the broader
input format does not establish the broader causal or inferential claim.(EventStudyInteract
contributors, 2023)
   We propose wrapping these existing routes when their regimes and rights are satisfied.
Reimplementing their inference in another language has no demonstrated benefit at this stage
and would create new numerical and semantic obligations. Stata runtime rights and the
community package’s unresolved redistribution rights must also remain distinct. Their absence
from this bounded inspection is a reason to defer redistribution, not evidence that the estimator
is scientifically inferior.


23.8.2    Augmented donors and block synthetic DiD

The inspected augsynth dispatcher has separate single-outcome, multiple-outcome and stag-
gered paths. It exposes outcome-model, balance and regularization choices, with some options
specific to the dispatched path. The saved declaration is version 0.2.0 at its recorded source
commit. We propose evaluating the original R path and preserving the dispatcher result, donor
identities, penalty, weight signs and chosen uncertainty method. The entry-point manual does
not establish every downstream implementation or inferential detail; those need inspection
before admission. In particular, the oracle minimizer in (23.17) should not be used as a claim
about the output of its ridge option. (augsynth contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal,
2026co)
  The proposed synthdid route is narrower: the inspected matrix interface uses an untreated-
23.8. Software routes must preserve the comparison                                           333


unit count and a pre-period count with simultaneous treatment onset. The transformation from
long banking observations to that matrix must preserve the meaning of both axes. Dropping
early-treated cells to create a rectangle changes the observed comparison and may change
the population target. For a staggered request, a collection of separately justified cohort
comparisons is an alternative design, rather than a hidden preprocessing trick that makes the
block estimator universal. Its beta-interface status also argues for a version-bound wrapper
before considering a port.(synth-inference contributors, 2026)
   These routes solve related but different balance problems. Augmentation can spend ex-
trapolation to improve unit balance; synthetic DiD also changes the pre-period comparison.
The product identity (23.24), norm penalty (23.25) and contamination radius (23.19) explain
concrete reasons their outputs can differ. They do not provide a ranking until the uncertainty
class, sampling law, common target and actual estimator behavior are specified. We therefore
propose retaining both original engines for matched evaluation. We reject automatic substitu-
tion between their outputs and defer a native port until a measured requirement justifies its
maintenance and verification cost.


23.8.3    A prototype can expose semantic errors before a bank trial

A useful first prototype compares meanings before comparing leaderboard scores. The exact
event-study table supplies a known false-lead reference, including the full design rank and
projection matrix. The curvature laws supply sharp endpoints and a noisy-slope variance check.
The donor and double-weight tables supply known bias, variance and contamination tradeoffs.
The signed-calendar and feedback laws then expose two failures that a purely tabular fit score
can miss: the wrong source of replication and the wrong intervention after a rule change. These
are proposed admission tasks, supported by local authored algebra; no upstream estimator
has been run here. (Causal banking proposal, 2026cn,cl)
   Permitted public panels can make the exercise more realistic by supplying calendar spacing,
exposure sizes, missingness and covariate patterns. Their license, revision date, units and local
identity would be retained. They do not by themselves reveal the untreated outcome of a
treated region. One defensible design overlays explicitly generated potential outcomes on a
permitted public covariate structure, disclosing that the causal truth is constructed. Another
compares descriptive behavior on a real policy episode while preserving unresolved causal
truth. Those designs answer different questions and should be reported separately. Existing
public-data survey entries can be screened for these purposes without treating a dataset’s
availability as scientific validation of the rollout design.
  After semantic admission, a prospective statistical comparison would freeze each engine
and its dependency environment, the common estimand, a fresh generating law and seed,
sample sizes, repetitions, inference methods, stopping rule and failure accounting. Scenarios
would vary treatment-effect heterogeneity, factor extrapolation, donor contamination, calendar
dependence, action excitation and post-change stability. Methods should be compared only
where their targets coincide and their claimed regimes are declared; a justified refusal is an
observable outcome. No favorable preliminary result should be used to revise the final scenario
denominator.
  The resulting report would retain target error, interval coverage under the constructed law,
availability, width, monetary decision loss and observed end-to-end cost. It would also retain
unsupported requests, convergence failures, nonfinite outputs and unresolved rights. Statistical
qualification of one frozen regime would remain different from acceptance of arbitrary panels
or a bank’s actual assignment and shock law. Only after such a prototype demonstrates
useful behavior is a costly authentic-bank trial justified by evidence from this program.(Causal
334                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


banking proposal, 2026cl)
   For the proposed library, CLI and MCP interface, a single result should therefore carry
the same target vector, reference period, supported cells, signed weights, uncertainty method,
sensitivity restrictions and horizon budget. A scalar “effect” field would erase the distinctions
developed here. The transport should also preserve a set-valued result or refusal when
assumptions or support do not admit a scalar claim. This is a proposed semantic contract
for later integration; the documented estimator interfaces and these exact references do not
establish interoperability with another repository.


23.9      Choosing the unit and calendar weights together
The block comparison above evaluates particular choices of weights. A bank designing a
comparison faces a further question: should it improve the donor balance, the calendar balance,
or both? The two choices interact. A residual factor mismatch is a product of their imbalances,
while independent-cell noise is multiplied by both squared weight norms. Optimizing one
axis while holding the other fixed need not reveal the best joint choice. We can solve one
small reference problem completely, including its global alternatives, without claiming that
an estimated synthetic-control routine solves that oracle problem.(Causal banking proposal,
2026cm)
   Use a new symmetric factor table, rather than change the inputs of the earlier comparison.
There is one treated region with loading 2, two donors with loadings 0 and 1, one post period
with factor 2, and two pre periods with factors 0 and 1. The untreated mean in each cell is the
product of its loading and factor, plus unrestricted additive unit and time effects. The outcome
errors in the nine cells are independent, centered and have common known variance s > 0.
A constant treatment effect τ enters only the treated post cell. All choices below therefore
estimate that same τ ; they do not change the population or horizon to improve a score.
  Put donor weights (1 − a, a) on the two donors and pre-period weights (1 − b, b) on the two
pre periods. Both pairs sum to one, even when a weight is negative. In row order treated,
donor zero, donor one, and column order post, pre zero, pre one, the signed contrasts are

               q = (1, a − 1, −a)′ ,    r = (1, b − 1, −b)′ ,

Each contrast sums to zero, so the additive unit and time effects cancel. The coefficient of the

the squared norm of one axis’s contrast. Independence of the nine cell errors gives the exact
risk
                            Rs (a, b) = (2 − a)2 (2 − b)2 + sQ(a)Q(b).                   (23.45)
The first term is squared bias for τ , and the second is its variance. This expression is conditional
on the declared factors and fixed weights. It is a mean squared error, with squared outcome
units. It is neither a confidence radius nor a realized profit. Monetary scaling of an estimation
error would need the exposure and decision loss to be specified separately.
  For any fixed b, this is a strictly convex quadratic in a. Its derivative and unique conditional

The denominator is positive for s > 0. There is a corresponding expression for b∗ (a) by

factor bias is already zero, so the remaining axis minimizes its noise norm. Matching the factor
exactly on both axes spends variance twice without reducing bias below zero. Conversely,
when the other axis retains imbalance, moving a toward the extrapolating value 2 can have a
benefit. Separate coordinatewise convexity does not establish joint convexity or the uniqueness
of a joint solution.

23.9.2     What constraints and exact matching cost

Suppose policy requires nonnegative weights on both axes. Then (a, b) ∈ [0, 1]2 . At s = 1/8, the
first derivative in (23.46) is strictly negative throughout the square. Indeed (a−2)(2−b)2 ≤ −1,
while sQ(b)(2a − 1) ≤ 1/4, since Q(b) ≤ 2 on that interval. Thus ∂R1/8 /∂a ≤ −3/2. The
same bound holds for the other derivative. Increasing either coordinate until it reaches one
strictly lowers risk, proving the constrained global optimum (1, 1). It is not merely the best
point found on a grid.
  The four comparisons on the same nine-cell law are

         Choice                                      a             b Mean squared error
         Best nonnegative pair                       1             1                   3/2
         Exact unit balance, minimum time norm       2           1/2                   9/8
         Exact balance on both axes                  2             2                   9/2
         Unrestricted joint optimum                  pair in (23.49)                     1

The exact-unit solution is also the best choice with a constrained to 2: its zero bias leaves
6sQ(b), minimized at b = 1/2. Requiring both axes to fit exactly multiplies two norms of 6
and gives 36s = 9/2. For the nonnegative pair the residual bias is one, and the variance is
4s = 1/2. The joint optimum accepts some residual bias to reduce the total risk below the
exact-unit alternative. These identities explain the comparisons; observing a small pre-period
residual alone would not do so.
   There is a separate direct check. Each of the nine noise coefficients is qi rj . Enumerating all
29 = 512 independent signs for standardized cell errors gives zero mean and second moment
P       2 2
   i,j qi rj . Adding the squared factor-table contrast recovers the displayed risks. For the
irrational weights in (23.49), multiplying their exact cell coefficients and summing squared
coefficients also gives risk one. Thus neither a floating-point optimizer nor a rounded square
root determines the ranking. (Causal banking proposal, 2026cm)
   The result suggests a useful prototype diagnostic: retain both weight vectors and the declared
noise law when investigating a discrepancy between two synthetic comparisons. It does not
prescribe the oracle weights for an actual bank. Its post factor and loadings are known here; a
real untreated post factor is counterfactual. Learning the weights from noisy pre outcomes
can correlate them with those errors. A contamination class, common shocks, missing cells or
a constraint on extreme weights changes the objective. The earlier signed-contamination and
calendar calculations show concrete ways that the apparent gain can disappear. An estimated
procedure needs its own target-preserving selection rule and uncertainty argument. The global
certificate supplies an exact reference for a deliberately restricted law, with which such a future
implementation can be compared.


23.10       Valuing replacement of the entire feedback rule
The response to a new action innovation within a regime leaves a different investment question
unresolved. A bank may propose replacing the old feedback rule for an already occupied
portfolio, without adding an action innovation. We now compare those entire regimes from
the same nonzero initial state, charging the actions each would actually take. An apparently
accurate model of the old path still leaves an interval of replacement values, because the
observed controller can hide the separate persistence and action-effect parameters.
   Retain the structural outcome law in (23.31), with future structural disturbances and action

For the positive coefficients in the two-rule example, the triangle inequality gives an absolute

at a = 0.98 and k ′ = 0.44 yields a uniform bound of USD 4.3532, below USD 4.36, at H = 80.
The actual largest endpoint tail is about USD 4.3231; cancellation makes it smaller than the
