25.3      Four journeys define four different purchases
The buying unit can be written as (q, e, d, o): a causal question q, a specific edition and update
e, a deployment arrangement d, and an output contract o. Let Aq contain the units whose
assumptions, operations, rights and outputs are adequate for that question. Optimization of
cost takes place only over Aq . Unknown membership is a due-diligence item; it is not coded as
either “cheap” or “incapable.” The same family can supply an admissible analyst tool for one
target and an unresolved production service for another. The following comparisons apply
that distinction to banking decisions rather than award one aggregate vendor score (Causal
banking proposal, 2026cw).


25.3.1     Structural funding: what exactly changes when a rate changes?

For treasury, distinguish a change in posted rate from a change in customer mix and a change
in the bank’s pricing rule. JMP’s binary-treatment report separates ATE from ATET, while
its continuous-treatment report offers a quadratic marginal structural model and a generalized-
propensity-score route. The inspected page explicitly warns that a potential-outcome density
plot does not directly supply a causal effect. These are concrete capabilities against which
the proposal should be assessed. They can support a supplied static comparison under their
assumptions; their existence does not establish an effect of a new dynamic pricing rule in a
dependent balance system (JMP, 2026).
   An acquisition request for this journey should specify a monetary contrast at two stated
rates, a customer population and a balance horizon. If the business question concerns retained
balances for all eligible customers, returning an ATET for customers who actually received the
high rate changes the population. If the rate is continuous, a binary high/low recoding changes
the intervention. A prospective adapter must retain the two evaluated doses, centering and
model form; a quadratic coefficient alone is not the requested contrast. Stata’s static treatment-
effect routes offer another comparator, but their inspected i.i.d., conditional-independence and
362                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


overlap conditions cannot be silently replaced by the bank’s shared-calendar sampling law
(StataCorp, 2026a; JMP, 2026).
   The proposal’s current supplied-moment inverse problem is a different service. Its narrow
reproducible calculation can preserve an ambiguity set, while a commercial report may provide
a developed estimation and diagnostic workflow for a different supported model. Buying an
analyst tool could therefore be appropriate before building a general estimation interface. The
proposed common layer would have to demonstrate a further benefit: that the rate, population,
information law, uncertainty and profit mapping survive a handoff. It cannot claim estimator
superiority from returning a richer envelope around an otherwise much narrower calculation.
   The inexpensive admission case should contain two rate levels with unequal assignment
probabilities and two customer strata with unequal effects. Demand separate ATE and
treated-population outputs; change the target population without changing the fitted outcome
model and check that the aggregation changes. Add a shared-calendar version to establish the
boundary of an i.i.d. procedure. A refusal or explicitly restricted interpretation is the intended
answer to the latter unless a justified dependence-aware route is supplied. This is a proposed
comparison of semantic behavior, not a newly executed vendor study.


25.3.2    Sequential servicing: a seat for analysis or an engine for decisions?

Servicing combines time to resolution, competing exits, repeated actions and cost. Stata’s
inspected survival treatment command excludes delayed entry and multiple-record or time-
varying-covariate data. SAS’s inspected competing-risk route has a different risk set and ignores
specified options when EVENTCODE is active. A purchase justified by a survival feature
name can therefore fail the actual request even if both products are working as documented.
An analyst may legitimately simplify a question to a fixed treatment at baseline; the interface
must make that new question explicit rather than transform sequential records into one row
without a scientific decision (StataCorp, 2026i; SAS Institute, 2015b).
   The buying unit for a fixed horizon should name the event of interest, competing events,
censoring, entry rule, action history and net utility. If repayment and write-off have different
monetary consequences, a survival probability for either exit is inadequate. If eligibility
is learned after the first contact, the policy cannot use it at the first contact. SMILE’s
influence-diagram route is a candidate for supplied-model decision analysis, while Stata’s
prespecified-policy evaluation is a candidate for its documented static setting. They answer
different questions unless the history and causal model have deliberately been restricted to
make them coincide (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024n; StataCorp, 2025).
   A graphical analyst seat can be useful for reviewing a supplied mechanism and utilities
without authorizing a server embedding of the same engine. Conversely, a production license
can permit an operational route whose scientific model has not been justified. The acquisition
dossier must therefore contain both the accepted analysis and the permitted deployment.
A generated two-contact case with an explicit history clock can test feasibility before a
costly experiment. It cannot establish truthful logging probabilities in the bank’s historical
records. The present dispatcher still refuses the proposed sequential-policy identifiers; a licensed
alternative is a capability to investigate, not functionality already added by this chapter.


25.3.3    Discovery to intervention: ownership of the unresolved graph

Discovery procurement has two deliverables: an analyst’s model-building experience and the
mathematical object consumed by an intervention query. GeNIe documents a pattern editor
and random completion to a DAG. BayesiaLab EQ documents equivalence-class search and
25.3. Four journeys define four different purchases                                        363


different treatment of fixed versus forbidden arcs. These features make commercial editors
credible alternatives to building a new graphical front end. They also show why “export graph”
cannot be the entire acceptance criterion. The exported object must retain what the search
did not resolve and what the analyst supplied (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024e; Bayesia, 2026b).
   In a deposit-rate example, the procurement packet should distinguish an edge oriented by a
time restriction, an edge implied by a conditional-independence procedure, an edge asserted by
an analyst, and an edge chosen only to produce a usable DAG. A downstream supplied-model
inference engine may need a DAG; that computational need is not evidence selecting one
member of a learned class. The proposed layer can retain the class and evaluate a declared
representative as a scenario, or refuse an unqualified class-wide effect. Its competitive value
depends on making this distinction inspectable without preventing the analyst from using a
productive commercial editor.
   The buying unit also changes between development and repeated scoring. Bayesia’s public
API overview distinguishes modeling and learning from inference configurations. The flattened
feature table does not justify an exact edition-by-operation parity claim. A development
demonstration of a learning command cannot by itself qualify a production inference enti-
tlement to relearn a graph after drift. Separate the learning component, retained model,
update authorization and inference component in the proposed deployment. Request an exact
feature/rights confirmation only for the narrow configuration that survives public semantic
tests (Bayesia, 2026a).


25.3.4     Trustworthy observations: who constructs the variables?

The fourth journey concerns the objects delivered to every engine: rows, identities, fields,
states and times. A node called “arrears” can denote a balance known before contact, a revised
accounting figure published later, or a post-contact outcome. Matching a column name to a
network node does not establish any of those meanings. A commercial inference engine can
correctly process the wrong time slice. Buying more sophisticated inference therefore does not
resolve the observation problem.
  The proposed common service’s strict clock is a useful narrow boundary, but it accepts
declared times and cannot authenticate them. Similarly, record linkage and missingness
analysis from the preceding chapter require their own sampling and truth assumptions. This
journey’s purchasing unit includes a conversion specification: customer or account identity,
row inclusion rule, state mapping, measurement units, decision time and source publication
time. The commercial feature census has not established a general engine that reconstructs
those meanings from banking extracts. That is a recorded scope gap, not an inference that no
vendor offers data preparation.
   For a public/generated admission case, permute node order while preserving labels, then
permute labels while preserving numeric positions. An adapter should accept a valid explicit
permutation and reject an ambiguous one; it should not reject all reordered data. Include a
retrospectively revised field with a publication time after the action. The same values should
lead to a different eligibility disposition when their information clock changes. These are
observable and affordable semantic tests. Later owner evidence is needed to decide whether
the recorded clock and identity are truthful.
364                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


25.4     Graph discovery and model construction

25.4.1    Equivalence is a deliverable

GeNIe’s PC documentation returns a pattern and describes a significance threshold, maximum
adjacency and a time-limit setting. Its Bayesian Search route is a score-guided hill-climbing
procedure with restarts and a structural prior. The pattern editor identifies directed, unresolved
and possible hidden-common-cause arcs. Create DAG chooses directions randomly when a fully
directed network is required. These are useful capabilities, but the final random representative
is not new observational evidence. The proposed product must store both the pattern and any
selected representative, with the selection seed and reason visible to the consumer.
  SMILE makes the boundary concrete in code. Its PC call returns a DSL_pattern, can
be interrupted by a progress callback, and reports an interruption code. A time limit is
checked after an iteration, so it is not the same as a hard external wall-time guarantee. Pattern
coordinates follow the data-set variable order. A wrapper must validate an explicit permutation
and reject an ambiguous or inconsistent matrix-to-name mapping (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024m,l).
   BayesiaLab’s EQ description supplies a different comparison. It searches equivalence classes,
treats fixed arcs as normal arcs, and takes forbidden arcs and temporal indices into account.
Thus two fields with similar names can have opposite effects on the search. The integration
contract should carry the restriction kind, time index and class representation separately. A
license or REST call that returns a network is not evidence that the restriction was interpreted
as intended.
   The banking consequence is immediate. Suppose a deposit-rate graph has an unresolved
rate–balance orientation. One representative says that the rate changes balances; another says
that a balance shock changes the quoted rate. Both can fit the same observational law. The
proposed service should return an equivalence class or a refusal to answer an intervention query.
A commercial editor may be the best analyst-facing component, while the shared library owns
the typed class, provenance and refusal semantics. Building another graphical editor would
need a separate business case; porting SMILE is not an open-source option because its manual
describes proprietary development and deployment licenses (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024j,k).


25.4.2    The latent and supplied-model distinction

Bayes Server documents causal optimization, an evidence-to-abduction-to- intervention coun-
terfactual workflow, and criteria such as back-door, front-door and instrumental-variable routes.
Its guide says that some helper functions are available from version 10 and that the worked
calculation can be performed from 9.4. This is strong evidence of a documented abduction
workflow. It is not a complete domain theorem for every graph, nor an execution of the
local service. The request must state whether the output is a population intervention or an
individual structural counterfactual, and which exogenous-variable model couples the factual
and alternative worlds (Bayes Server, 2026a).
  BayesiaLab supplies graphical surgery, likelihood matching and contribution analysis in
the inspected pages. Stata supplies treatment effects and a developed one-mediator workflow.
These are valuable alternatives for specific targets. Their assumptions remain part of the output:
Stata’s manual names i.i.d. sampling, conditional independence and overlap; its mediation
manual addresses treatment–mediator and mediator–outcome confounding restrictions. An
adapter that returns a coefficient while dropping those conditions is a semantic failure even if
the numerical call succeeds (Bayesia, 2026h,g; StataCorp, 2026a,b).
  The buying route is therefore conditional. Reuse a commercial engine for a supplied
25.5. Effects, IV/RD and the limits of a command menu                                       365


model when its edition exposes the required intervention or abduction operation and its data
movement and deployment rights are acceptable. Integrate an open method when its source,
license, numerical representation and target semantics are compatible. Build the missing
graph-class and assumption ledger in the common library. Reject a direct port when the
license, endpoint meaning or hidden-state contract cannot be preserved. These are distinct
decisions; “use the package” is not one of them.


25.5     Effects, IV/RD and the limits of a command menu
Stata’s treatment-effect reference documents ATE, ATET and potential-outcome means
using regression adjustment, inverse-probability weighting, augmented weighting and match-
ing. Its caveats explain why i.i.d. sampling, conditional independence and overlap matter.
The cate postestimation path evaluates a prespecified treatment-assignment policy. JMP’s
causal-treatment documentation similarly defines positivity, consistency and conditional ex-
changeability, while its uplift and treatment personalities address distinct estimands. These
capabilities set a high baseline for estimation. A new common service must justify its cost by
preserving target identity, evidence, clocks, uncertainty and cross-tool failure semantics, not
by adding another estimator name (StataCorp, 2025; JMP, 2026, 2025).
  The IV/RD row is especially important for procurement. Stata’s weak-instrument postesti-
mation describes confidence sets that can be finite, disconnected, unbounded, whole-line or
empty; its grid and simulation controls are exposed. SAS/ETS SYSLIN supplies 2SLS, LIML,
K-class, SUR and 3SLS system alternatives. SPSS and JMP provide narrower equation or
model-implied instrument paths. A bridge that serializes only a point estimate loses exactly
the result that is most decision-relevant when the instrument is weak. The bridge should
preserve the set components, search bounds, grid, seed, covariance choice and whether an
empty set means model rejection or numerical noncoverage (StataCorp, 2026g; SAS Institute,
2015a).
   For a credit threshold, the business request may be a local complier effect, an all-applicant
effect, or a reduced-form jump. The same columns and cutoff do not identify all three. The
proposed acquisition comparison should execute a small public/generated fixture in which
exclusion holds, then a negative control where eligibility has a direct outcome effect. A
commercial command can be the reference implementation for the first fixture; it cannot make
the second restriction true. The cost of a licensed command is justified only if the workflow
preserves that distinction and reports the negative control.


25.6     Time, panels and survival
GeNIe documents dynamic Bayesian networks and parameter learning for an existing dynamic
structure. Its parameter-learning page says that the structure is not learned by that procedure
and explains the node-and-time-slice column mapping. SMILE’s dynamic tutorial distinguishes
initial from transition tables, lag order, slice count and temporal evidence indices. SAS/ETS
and Stata provide VAR, SVAR, VARMAX and Granger-style operations, while SPSS TCM
uses “causal” in the Granger-predictive sense. Mplus provides intensive longitudinal and latent
dynamic models. These are substantial tools, but a predictive lag, a supplied transition model
and an intervention effect are different targets (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024a,b,c; StataCorp, 2026c;
SAS Institute, 2026a; IBM, 2026a).
  The adapter must preserve sampling interval, time origin, state ordering, calendar shocks,
contemporaneous restrictions and the intervention regime. A state array with swapped
366                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


categories can pass type checks and reverse a servicing action. A VAR test on shared monthly
observations can be a useful diagnostic while failing to identify a rate intervention. The
proposal should buy or reuse supplied-model temporal inference when it meets those fields
and build a common refusal when the question asks for an unsupported change of regime.
   Survival tools provide another concrete baseline. Stata’s inspected stteffects documenta-
tion excludes delayed entry, time-varying covariates and multiple-record data in that command.
SAS PHREG documents counting-process records and competing-event output, but some
options are ignored under its EVENTCODE route. SPSS, Statistica, Minitab, JMP, NCSS
and Mplus each provide useful narrower conversion or reporting functions. The local reference
dispatcher returned completed unsupported responses for the three authored fixed-treatment,
competing-incidence and sequential-policy identifiers. This establishes a present implemen-
tation gap and a route to a matched public/generated bridge; it does not rank vendors or
prove their absence of other methods (StataCorp, 2026i; SAS Institute, 2015b; JMP Statistical
Discovery, 2024; Causal banking research project, 2026an,ao).


25.7     Policy value, uplift and decision analysis
Stata’s estat policyeval evaluates a prespecified treatment-assignment probability. GeNIe
and SMILE influence diagrams compute expected utility for a supplied model with decision
nodes, information and costs. JMP uplift emphasizes treatment differences in partitioning.
Amazon Personalize documents train/test recommendation metrics, including average rewards
at rank. These capabilities should be compared on aligned targets, not on the shared word
“policy”.
  For a binary action, a prespecified static policy has value

                           V (π) = E{π(X)Y (1) + [1 − π(X)]Y (0)}.                           (25.1)

For a sequential policy with history Ht , logging probability bt and target policy πt , the
trajectory weight is
                                        TY−1
                                             πt (At | Ht )
                                  WT =                     .                        (25.2)
                                             b (At | Ht )
                                         t=0 t

The second object requires action histories, positivity and an outcome clock. It cannot be
obtained by placing the last action in a static treatment column. An influence diagram answers
a supplied-mechanism utility question; a recommendation metric evaluates a predictive ranking.
The service must retain which object was requested.
   Azure Personalizer is a historical comparator. Its archived documentation describes Rank
and Reward calls, contextual and action features, delayed reward, and a service that does not
maintain individual user histories. It also records that new resources stopped in 2023 and the
service retired on 25 August 2026. The migration recommendation to an open project does
not establish estimator or feature parity. AWS metrics and a retired hosted policy service
cannot be treated as evidence of a causal-policy guarantee (Microsoft, 2026a; Amazon Web
Services, 2026a).
   The proposed route is to keep a static policy adapter, a sequential off-policy research module
and a supplied influence-diagram adapter separate. First use a public or generated trajectory
fixture to test clocks, logging probabilities, costs, action support, failure denominators and
independent evaluation. Only then consider a licensed engine trial. A model that refuses a
sequential target is preferable to a static score silently substituted for it.
25.7. Policy value, uplift and decision analysis                                                    367


25.7.1     Information parents can change the affordable policy

The SMILE influence-diagram manual supplies an unusually concrete acquisition require-
ment. After inference, the returned matrices may be indexed by unobserved decision
nodes and by chance nodes that should have been observed before a decision. It provides
GetIndexingParents to recover those indices. Chance-node entries are then posterior probabil-
ities for each policy; decision entries are expected utilities for outcomes and policies; value-node
entries are expected utilities for policies. An integration that buys access to the matrix but
exports only a scalar has discarded part of the result’s meaning (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024n).
   Consider a generated servicing decision with equally probable histories h0 , h1 and actions 0
(no contact) and 1 (contact). Stipulate net utilities in USD per customer:

                 u(h0 , 0) = u(h1 , 0) = 0,        u(h0 , 1) = 10,   u(h1 , 1) = −30.            (25.3)

The histories can represent eligible and ineligible contact contexts; the amounts already include
contact costs. If the history is available before acting, a deterministic policy is the pair (a0 , a1 ),
with value
                               V (a0 , a1 ) = 12 u(h0 , a0 ) + 21 u(h1 , a1 ).                 (25.4)
The four values for (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1) are respectively 0, −15, 5 and −10. The best feasible
history-dependent policy contacts only at h0 and has value 5. If history is unavailable until
after the decision, only the two constant policies are feasible, with best value 0. Randomizing
contact independently of history with probability r has value −10r and cannot improve that
value. Taking the largest matrix entry, 10, is neither the best population value nor a feasible
unconditional policy value. The exact four-policy enumeration is a project derivation, not a
SMILE run (Causal banking proposal, 2026cv).
   For this stipulated utility model, purchasing a perfectly timely history feed has gross value
at most USD 5 per customer before feed, review and deployment expenses. Buying a faster
decision engine does not create this information. A feed that becomes available after contact
has zero policy value here, even when it has the same data contents. With noisy history, the
posterior contact benefit must be positive; if p is the conditional probability of h0 , that benefit
is 10p − 30(1 − p), so contact requires p > 3/4. The purchased signal needs an information
clock and calibrated meaning for p, not merely an accuracy percentage.
   This example defines a specific acceptance case for a commercial adapter. Export parent
identifiers, state order, observed/unobserved status, decision ordering and policy indices with
the utility matrix. Reconstruct all four policy values and the restricted two-policy value
outside the engine from that export. Then intentionally withhold the history and require
the feasible policy set to shrink. If the wrapper reports value 5 for a decision that cannot
observe history, the correct response is to reject that integration for the requested deployment.
The experiment tests the preservation of documented information semantics; it does not rank
SMILE’s optimizer against other optimizers or validate the stipulated utilities.
  An alternative acquisition is a static prespecified-policy tool when the bank can truly
observe the relevant covariates before the one decision. Stata’s documented policy probability
supplies that narrower comparison. A supplied influence diagram remains useful when the
bank wants to inspect mechanisms and decisions together. A future sequential estimator is
needed when the question concerns a learned policy under repeated, uncertain assignment.
Those alternatives should compete only within their supported target and information class.
Their different purchase costs cannot compensate for a missing predecision variable (StataCorp,
2025; BayesFusion, LLC, 2024n).
368                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


25.8     Language, deployment and semantic loss
SMILE’s C++ engine and its documented wrappers for Java, Python, R, .NET and COM are
access paths to one proprietary engine. The licensing page separates academic and commercial
development, server deployment and end-user redistribution. Bayesia’s API page separates
Java modeling and inference from REST inference, describes customer-hosted model files for
one configuration and hosted models for another, and prices production by simultaneously
loaded model instances. The phrase “Java API” or “Bayesia API” therefore does not name a
single acquisition unit (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024j,k; Bayesia, 2026a).
  The request contract should include:
1. a target and population with unit, horizon, currency and sign convention;
2. a graph or supplied model with endpoint marks, restriction types and unresolved-class
   representation;
3. treatment or action identity, assignment/logging law and observation clock;
4. estimator, uncertainty object, numerical controls, seed and refusal state;
5. artifact hashes, dependency versions, license entitlement, data location, interruption status
   and recovery identity.
   The consumer should see whether the result is documented, locally observed, project-derived
or proposed. A wrapper should preserve an interrupted SMILE learning call as incomplete,
preserve Bayes Server’s intervention rather than ordinary evidence, and preserve Stata’s
disconnected confidence set. It should not coerce a vendor error or an unsupported target into
a null estimate.
   The recommended integration pattern is a narrow adapter plus a native semantic ledger.
For a proprietary engine, the ledger records the license, model location, wrapper version,
serialization and permitted deployment. For an open-source package, it records the commit,
license, dependency graph, source anchors and whether the package can be adopted, wrapped,
ported or rejected. The common CLI and MCP surfaces expose the ledger and request
envelope; they do not make proprietary code open or transform a predictive metric into a
causal estimand.


25.8.1    Entitlements determine the architecture that can be quoted

For SMILE, the inspected license page separates development from deployment, and server
deployment from distribution of end-user programs. This creates at least three different cost
inquiries for a proposed banking product: analysts building a prototype, a centrally hosted
calculation service, and applications distributed to consumers. The existence of a Python or
R wrapper does not collapse these distinctions. An academic development license is not the
planning assumption for a commercial bank; a server integration needs its own applicable
entitlement. No clause inspected here authorizes porting the proprietary engine. The feasible
proposed route is a licensed adapter, with an open-source alternative considered separately
(BayesFusion, LLC, 2024k).
   Bayesia’s overview describes another architecture. It distinguishes Java deployment with
model files on customer servers from a hosted REST configuration whose model files reside on
Bayesia servers in France. It also states that the Java route validates credentials with a license
server and requires a permanent Internet connection. Those documented dependencies must
enter a deployment comparison even when all model files stay local. Model residency and license
connectivity are different properties. The public table’s extraction loses visual feature markers,
so the exact edition-function matrix and contractual guarantees remain unresolved. The explicit
prose does support inquiring about model residency, network dependence, loaded-instance
25.9. Scheduling a licensed engine                                                            369


capacity and learning versus inference (Bayesia, 2026a).
   Stata illustrates why concurrent users and concurrent engines must not share one field.
Its license-options page defines an identified single user and a network license for a specified
number of concurrent users within a single site. It describes annual and perpetual arrangements.
This is evidence about the published user-license categories, not confirmation that unattended
service accounts, remote MCP clients, geographic replication or redistribution are covered.
The proposal should use a licensed analyst workflow as a candidate reference and keep an
unattended service route pending the relevant terms. Counting API workers as “users” would
be an unsupported legal and operational assumption (StataCorp, 2026f).
   These distinctions change the quote request. It should state the legal deployment entity,
exact edition/update, development users, runtime users or instances as applicable, sites, model
residency, permitted data movement, offline needs, recovery replicas, consumer access and
expected model churn. An edition list without those quantities does not price the workflow.
The public originals establish which questions matter; they do not provide binding permission
or numeric prices. This is why the financial examples below use transparent hypothetical
terms rather than convert an undocumented seat price into a server cost.


25.8.2    Version replacement is a scientific change

An upgrade can add a needed helper without preserving an operational contract. Bayes Server’s
inspected example says that its counterfactual calculation is possible from version 9.4, while
the illustrated abduction helpers arrive in version 10. A prototype that manually constructs
the older calculation and a workflow that invokes the later helper have different reproducibility
and review costs, even if both answer the same supplied structural question. The acquisition
dossier should preserve the structural coupling, evidence removal and intervention steps, then
test whether a replacement produces the same declared result. Matching a button name is
insufficient (Bayes Server, 2026a).
   Retirement has a similar consequence at the service boundary. The inspected Azure
Personalizer pages record retirement on 25 August 2026, before the literature cutoff. They
describe Rank/Reward and explicitly say that the service does not maintain individual user
information or history. A migration candidate must therefore reconstruct whatever external
history the old workflow used, its reward delay and assignment logging. A replacement
recommendation engine can preserve a ranking interface while changing the evaluation problem.
Treat the old service as a historical design comparator, and price migration, requalification
and export retention separately from a recurring engine fee (Microsoft, 2026a).
   For SAS EVENTCODE, the ignored-option list makes the upgrade/translation test particu-
larly observable: parse the actual effective procedure and covariance settings, then compare
them with the request. If an integration asserts that an ignored RANDOM statement supplied
a random-effects fit, the problem lies in the integration’s claim. Preserving the original request
alongside the effective invocation enables a reviewer to see that mismatch. A successful numeric
result does not authorize relabeling the effective model (SAS Institute, 2015b).


25.9      Scheduling a licensed engine
Bayesia’s production description makes simultaneous loaded model instances a license quantity.
A simple planning model is useful before a quote arrives. Let job i have supplied load-and-
inference duration di , and let m be the number of permitted instances. For independent jobs
370                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


all available at time zero and a nonpreemptive schedule, the makespan is
                                                                   X
                            Tm =            min            max           di .                   (25.5)
                                   assignment to m instances j≤m
                                                                   i∈j

This is a workload assumption, not a measured vendor rate. Three planning jobs with durations
7, 5 and 4 take 16 units on one instance and 9 units on two instances by placing the 5 and 4
jobs together. The calculation tells the prototype to measure model-load time, queueing and
failure recovery. It does not establish that a production license permits that schedule or that
the engine scales linearly.
   There is a simple lower-bound check on this reference: every schedule needs at least the
longest job time, 7, and at least the average assigned load, 16/m. For two instances, a
makespan below 9 would require each instance to carry exactly 8 units because the durations
are integers and total 16. No subset of {7, 5, 4} sums to 8. The partition {7}, {5, 4} attains
9, proving optimality for this three-job instance. Three instances attain 7. A deadline of 8
therefore requires three under these assumptions; a deadline of 9 needs two. This is a useful
prospective quote distinction even though none of these durations is an observed product
timing (Causal banking proposal, 2026cv).
  The vendor’s loaded-model language also exposes a limitation of the simple job formula.
A warm model that is idle between requests can still consume a licensed instance. Let Ik (t)
indicate that model instance k is loaded at time t. The proposed entitlement constraint is
                                   X
                                       Ik (t) ≤ m   for every t.                                (25.6)
                                   k

This counts simultaneously loaded instances, not daily request volume or physical servers.
In the simple three-job reference each job loads, computes and unloads within its stated
duration. If models are retained between jobs, their occupancy intervals must be extended. If
loading and unloading are costly, the policy can trade repeated startup against scarce instance
slots. The correct evidence is a trace of load, readiness, request start, completion and unload
events, with license failures retained. A thread count alone cannot recover this trace. Exact
concurrent-query behavior within an instance remains an edition/runtime question; it is not
assumed by the model (Bayesia, 2026a).
   For example, retaining one model throughout a quiet period can leave only m − 1 slots for
the other models even while that first model performs no inference. A benchmark that reports
only CPU utilization can miss this binding constraint. Conversely, sequential loading may
satisfy a one-instance license while violating the decision deadline. A bank choosing between
those routes should measure the requested deadline and refusal/fallback outcome together,
then ask what capacity is needed for the same supported workload. A larger license has no
demonstrated value merely because more cores are available.
   SMILE’s time-limit semantics introduce a different scheduling issue. The manual checks
elapsed search time after an iteration completes. Without a bound on the remaining iteration,
setting the nominal limit to the bank’s deadline does not prove that the result arrives by that
deadline. An external wrapper may enforce a wall-time stop, but it must mark the learning
result as interrupted and retain the last valid artifact separately from a completed graph.
Killing the process cannot convert a partial search into an accepted scientific answer. The
prototype should include a deadline at an iteration boundary and one during an iteration; the
latter is precisely the case a simple elapsed-time setting can fail to resolve (BayesFusion, LLC,
2024m).
   The same ledger must include model transfer, data residency, license-server availability,
retries, operator review and retirement. A cheaper per-instance license can be dominated by
25.9. Scheduling a licensed engine                                                            371


a long load time or by the cost of converting a pattern, state ordering or uncertainty object.
Those terms belong in the workflow cost, not in an unqualified engine benchmark.


25.9.1    Buying capacity when models stay resident

The production-instance description has a further implication that a throughput table misses.
Requests can revisit an already loaded model, while retaining that model consumes a slot
between requests. An acquisition decision therefore depends on the model-retention policy as
well as the number of licenses. The Bayesia overview explicitly allows sequential loading and
unloading to reduce the simultaneous-instance requirement. It does not specify the latency of
these operations, a caching policy, or a guarantee that one model instance can serve concurrent
requests. Those are quantities to measure. The following reference isolates residency while
keeping actual product behavior unresolved (Bayesia, 2026a; Causal banking proposal, 2026cx).
   Consider a single worker receiving requests for immutable model versions from a finite set.
Loading a model consumes five abstract time units, inference consumes one, and eviction is
instantaneous. No model is loaded initially. Requests are processed in their declared order,
with no prefetch and no overlap of loading and inference. The bank buys capacity for m
resident models, including idle ones. These assumptions deliberately exclude parallel speedup:
the question is whether buying an additional slot saves reloads. A model name includes its
parameter and schema version; a revised balance-response network is a different object even
when an analyst gives it the same display name.
   Write the ordered model requests as x1 , . . . , xK , and let S be the resident set just before
a request. A hit occurs if xt ∈ S. A miss requires loading xt and, if |S| = m, selecting an
eviction. For a known batch, let Jt (S) denote the smallest number of remaining loads from
time t. Retaining unused models is free apart from capacity, so an optimum can delay an
eviction until the slot is needed. The recurrence is
                        JK+1 (S) = 0,
                            Jt (S) = Jt+1 (S),          xt ∈ S,                             (25.7)
                                                                    ′
                            Jt (S) = 1 +       min           Jt+1 (S ),      xt ∈
                                                                                / S,
                                           S ′ ∈Em (S,xt )

where Em (S, x) is {S ∪ {x}} if |S| < m, and is {(S \ {y}) ∪ {x} : y ∈ S} if |S| = m. Thus every
candidate next set contains the requested model and respects the purchased capacity. The
recurrence is exact by conditioning on the next eviction and then optimizing the remaining
suffix. It is not an estimator of a future workload. Under the stated serial model, a schedule
with N loads has completion time
                                          T = K + 5N.                                     (25.8)
Changing the load or inference duration replaces those coefficients; overlapping operations or
concurrent calls require a different state and time model.
   Take the six-request batch (A, B, C, A, B, C). One slot requires six loads and finishes at
36. Three slots load each distinct model once and finish at 21. With two slots, the following
resident sets attain four loads:

                   {A},    {A, B},    {A, C},         {A, C},           {B, C},   {B, C}.   (25.9)

Load at requests 1, 2, 3 and 5; requests 4 and 6 are hits. Completion time is 26. At least
four loads are necessary: the first three distinct requests each require a load, and loading C
in the third request with capacity two evicts either A or B. Both are requested again, so at
least one further load is unavoidable. This lower bound and the witness establish the exact
372                                                                    Causal analysis for a universal bank


two-slot optimum. A separate enumeration of all feasible resident-set paths gives the same
result, including paths that voluntarily evict early (Causal banking proposal, 2026cx).
   The offline optimum needs information about the remaining batch. A familiar online rule
evicts the least recently used resident model. For the same two-slot sequence its resident sets
are {A}, {A, B}, {B, C}, {C, A}, {A, B}, {B, C}. Every request is a miss, so it takes 36, exactly
the one-slot time. The extra license has supplied storage capacity but this policy has not
converted it into a time saving. The distinction is commercially material: a demonstration that
knows the complete batch cannot support a streaming service-level promise for an unspecified
eviction policy.
   Reordering requests to group identical models would answer a different scheduling problem.
It may be legitimate for independent overnight reports; it may be impossible when the next
servicing request depends on an earlier decision or when each request has a deadline. The
acquisition case must say whether such reordering is permitted. Likewise, preloading all three
models before starting the stopwatch both consumes capacity and incurs work. Excluding that
preparation would favor the larger resident configuration for the wrong reason. The reference
starts with an empty resident set so the full preparation cost is visible.


25.9.2    A workload law and a deadline produce different purchases

An expected-cost quote needs a workload law. Suppose, only for this example, that each of
the six requests independently chooses A, B or C with equal probability. There are 36 = 729
equally likely batches. This is an authored finite law, not an inferred distribution of bank
demand. It permits both complete enumeration and an independent probability calculation
for the online least-recently-used rule.
  For one slot, the first request always loads and each later request differs from its predecessor
with probability 2/3. For three slots, loads equal the number of distinct requested models.
Therefore
                                         13                                665
                  EN1 = 1 + 5(2/3) = ,           EN3 = 3{1 − (2/3)6 } =         .          (25.10)
                                          3                                243
With two slots, before request t ≥ 2 there is only one resident model exactly when all the
preceding requests are equal. That event has probability 32−t . Conditional on it, the next
request misses with probability 2/3; otherwise there are two resident models and the next
independent request misses with probability 1/3. Hence
                                         6 
                                             1         1 2−t           769
                                         X                     
                             EN2 = 1 +             +     3         =       .                       (25.11)
                                         t=2
