The independence of the next request from the resident state is essential to this calculation.
Changing model frequencies or making the next model depend on previous outputs changes
the law. Exhaustive evaluation of all 729 batches matches these three rational expectations
exactly; it is not Monte Carlo evidence with an estimated standard error (Causal banking
proposal, 2026cx).
  Now assign an illustrative allocated capacity charge of USD 0, 120 and 300 per six-request
planning batch to one, two and three slots. These are incremental accounting assumptions,
not a vendor’s billing units or quotes. Price a time unit at USD 20, including the stipulated
common preparation and waiting cost. For a known batch, the objective is the charge plus
20Tm ; for the specified random online workload, it is the charge plus 20ETm . The comparison
25.9. Scheduling a licensed engine                                                             373


is
                      resident slots         1          2          3
               known-batch optimum time     36         26         21
                                                                     .                     (25.12)
                 known-batch total USD     720        640        720
                 online mean total USD  1660/3 135220/243 168560/243
Thus the known batch favors two slots; the random online workload favors one, with expected
cost approximately USD 553.33 against USD 556.46 for two and USD 693.66 for three. The
small expected difference between one and two is a property of these supplied numbers. It
would be irresponsible to regard it as a measured procurement margin without observing the
workload and costs.
   A hard deadline is a separate constraint. Over the finite support of six-request sequences,
one slot and two-slot least-recently-used scheduling both have worst completion time 36. Three
slots have worst completion time 21, because there are at most three distinct models. A
requirement to finish every supported sequence within 30 units therefore selects three among
these online configurations, despite its higher mean cost. For the known batch, the exact
two-slot plan finishes at 26 and is eligible. The facts available before purchase decide whether
that cheaper plan is a relevant comparator.
   This is also a limitation of any deterministic online two-slot policy under an unrestricted
adaptive arrival model. An adversary observing the resident set can always request a missing
one of the three models, forcing a load at each of the six requests. That argument does not
assert that bank arrivals are adversarial. It shows why a worst-case claim cannot be inferred
from an average or a prescient batch schedule. If requests are random and independent, use
that declared law. If the bank requires a deadline only with a specified probability, estimate
that tail under an appropriate workload model and report the failed fraction. Do not silently
reinterpret “every request” as “the average request.”
   The example has deliberately held scientific acceptance fixed across slots: all model versions
and outputs are identical and no inference is skipped. An apparent speedup obtained by
retaining an old model after an approved parameter update changes that condition. If A
becomes A′ midway through a batch, the residency identity and load count must change. If the
policy changes the model selected after observing an output, future requests are endogenous to
the earlier computation and the independent uniform calculation no longer applies. A prototype
should retain those version and decision events so that the capacity estimate corresponds to
the actual approved analysis.


25.9.3    What the capacity prototype must reveal before a quote

The loaded-instance model identifies a small set of observations with direct acquisition con-
sequences. For each permitted configuration, measure loading, license validation, readiness,
inference and unload times separately; keep resident versions and model-file locations through-
out the trace. An engine that runs quickly after loading can still be unsuitable for frequent
model changes. A route with customer-resident model files can still depend on the documented
license-server connection. An interrupted or unlicensed load must remain in the assigned
workload, with its actual fallback or unresolved deadline; it is not a zero-time successful request
(Bayesia, 2026a).
   Two comparisons should then be reported. A known-batch reference measures what a
sufficiently informed scheduler could attain under the same capacity and ordering constraints.
A deployable online policy measures what the proposed service can attain using only information
available at each request. The gap between them is a scheduling opportunity, not evidence that
the vendor engine is inefficient. Original loaded-model traces allow the bank to ask whether
374                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


an additional instance or a better retention policy would address the observed bottleneck. A
mean CPU time without such traces cannot distinguish those purchases.
   License and runtime failures require a further state. The finite time formula assumes every
required load is permitted and finishes in its stipulated time. If validation is unavailable with
no known upper delay, this model supplies no finite deadline guarantee. The response is to
keep that operational input open, evaluate an allowed fallback and avoid quoting unsupported
availability. The same separation applies to a SMILE search interrupted during an iteration:
extra licensed capacity does not turn an incomplete graph into a completed scientific result.
A capacity proposal should preserve the completed/incomplete state while measuring its
operational cost (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024m).
   Finally, allocate recurring capacity charges to a planning workload only once. A license
shared by funding and servicing analyses is a common fixed resource; charging its full annual
fee independently to each journey overstates total cost, while omitting one journey’s occupancy
understates contention. The prototype should report joint resident intervals and the rule for
allocating their expense. A price negotiation can then use both a scientifically matched output
requirement and a concrete instance quantity. The proposal’s immediate deliverable is this
testable purchasing model. Actual durations, permitted concurrency, deployment rights, prices
and bank workload remain observations to obtain after the narrow prototype shows merit.


25.9.4    Extra instances do not remove a shared licensing dependency

The inspected Bayesia API description separates model-file location from license validation:
a Java configuration can retain model files on customer servers while validating credentials
with the vendor’s license server when launching an instance. It states a permanent connection
requirement. This has a specific acquisition consequence. A proposal for several local replicas
must explain which dependencies those replicas share. Local data residency does not, by itself,
imply independent recovery or offline operation (Bayesia, 2026a).
   Consider a deliberately narrow recovery experiment. All replicas are initially unloaded, and
a required model must become ready during a stated recovery window. Suppose validation
must be available in that window, and at least one local worker must be able to load the model.
Let C indicate common validation availability and Rj local readiness for replica j. Write
P(C = 0) = q and P(Rj = 0) = p. In this authored model the Rj are mutually independent
and independent of C. The success event is
                                 m
                                 [
                     {C = 1} ∩       {Rj = 1},     Am = (1 − q)(1 − pm ).                 (25.13)
                                 j=1

The formula follows by taking the complement of all local workers failing, then applying the
stated independence from validation. It concerns a cold recovery request. It is not a statement
that disconnecting the license server terminates a currently loaded engine or makes every
ordinary query fail; that behavior is not established by the inspected page.
   With stipulated p = 1/10 and q = 1/50, one, two and three replicas have success probabilities
.882, .9702 and .97902. Ignoring the shared validation gate would report .9, .99 and .999
instead. The difference matters to a capacity purchase: a two-replica calculation that drops
the common dependency appears to meet a .99 target but actually does not meet it in this
very model. Increasing m cannot solve that problem, since
                                   Am ≤ 1 − q = .98 < .99.                                (25.14)
The probability calculation is reproduced by summing every common/local readiness combina-
tion for each of the three capacities (Causal banking proposal, 2026ct).
25.10. Exact hypothetical cost and route choice                                                375


  For a general desired probability a, the same model requires q ≤ 1 − a before replica count
can be sufficient. When q < 1 − a and 0 < p < 1, a finite sufficient count satisfies
                                                  a
                                       pm ≤ 1 −      .                                 (25.15)
                                                1−q
At q = 1 − a, the right side is zero, so no finite count with p > 0 attains the boundary. These
conditions do not estimate p or q; they identify which measurement or architectural change
could alter a purchase decision. A second local machine cannot resolve an unavailable common
credential path. A different permitted validation arrangement, a genuinely ready standby or
an alternative engine may change the event structure, but each requires its own documented
rights, scientific equivalence and operating evidence.
   The standby distinction is especially easy to obscure in a benchmark. Keeping a model
already loaded changes the recovery experiment and can consume a licensed instance during the
quiet period. Starting the standby only after failure changes its readiness time and can expose
the shared validation path. Neither arrangement is universally cheaper or more reliable from
the public description alone. A quote should specify whether the required capacity includes
retained standby models, when validation occurs and what recovery behavior the vendor
actually supports. A performance comparison should count the preparation and occupancy of
that exact arrangement.
   The independence assumption also needs scrutiny. Replicas on one host can share a process
supervisor, memory pressure and storage. Replicas on different hosts can still share a network
route, model store or license service. If local readiness is perfectly common rather than
independent, adding replicas leaves local success at 1 − p, making the cold-recovery probability
(1 − q)(1 − p) for every m. The appropriate input is a joint failure model, not a list of machines.
This is a practical reason to preserve configuration and dependency identity alongside observed
failure counts.
   The inexpensive prototype can first exercise the common layer against a declared unavailable-
validation response and an interrupted model load. It should retain the recovery request,
each attempt, elapsed time and the eventual fallback or unresolved result. Such fixtures can
demonstrate correct accounting and refusal before a paid engine is available. They cannot
establish actual license-server uptime or vendor failover behavior. A later permitted trial
should inspect those behaviors using the exact contracted edition and recovery arrangement.
A broad availability claim waits for observations from the relevant workload and time horizon.
   This dependency calculation belongs in the commercial comparison because it can change the
item being purchased. A capacity-only quotation may offer more instances without addressing
the binding common recovery condition. A proposed open or commercial alternative must
preserve the same causal outputs before its different recovery architecture is economically
comparable. The useful procurement conclusion is conditional and specific: price the supported
configuration that can satisfy the required recovery experiment, and record when the current
evidence cannot identify such a configuration.


25.10       Exact hypothetical cost and route choice
To make the acquisition decision reviewable, consider three routes for n assigned requests in
one planning year. The values below are deliberately round and hypothetical:
      CB (n) = 420000 + 1.8n,                            build the common service,         (25.16)
      CL (n) = 190000 + 5.6n,                      licensed adapter and conversion,        (25.17)
      CH (n) = 285000 + 3n,           hybrid: common ledger plus licensed engine.          (25.18)
376                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


The fixed terms include engineering, review and deployment preparation. The variable terms
include request preparation and operation. They do not include an invented vendor quote.
The exact pairwise crossings are
           230000   1150000                 95000   475000                135000
   nLB =          =         ,       nLH =         =        ,       nHB =          = 112500.
             3.8      19                     2.6      13                    1.2
                                                                                          (25.19)
Thus the licensed route is cheapest at low volume under this model, the hybrid route is cheapest
in the middle, and building the common service is cheapest at sufficiently high volume. The
ordering is a consequence of the assumed costs, not a recommendation to purchase any named
product.
   At volumes 10,000, 50,000 and 150,000, the exact costs in USD are respec-
tively (246000, 315000, 438000) for licensed, hybrid and build at the first volume;
(470000, 435000, 510000) at the second; and (1030000, 735000, 690000) at the third.
The route minimizing maximum regret over these three scenarios is hybrid: its regret is
USD 69,000, compared with USD 340,000 for licensed and USD 192,000 for build. This is a
minimax decision over a declared volume set, not an expected bank cost. Minimizing the
largest absolute cost instead selects build: its largest cost is USD 690,000, against USD 735,000
for hybrid and USD 1,030,000 for licensed. A committee must choose its objective before
using the table. The exact enumeration is reproduced in the accompanying S8 calculation
record (Causal banking proposal, 2026cv).
   Semantic admissibility comes first. If a licensed route cannot preserve a disconnected IV
set, a graph class, or a sequential policy’s logging law, its cost is not comparable to a build
route that can. The route is then rejected for that target regardless of its nominal price. The
prototype should measure the fraction of requests that require conversion, refusal or human
review and replace the planning terms with observed quantities.


25.10.1     A quote ceiling for a genuinely comparable configuration

Suppose the hypothetical hybrid envelope excludes a new annual deployment charge z ≥ 0,
with all other expenses held fixed. It remains competitive with both alternatives exactly when

                     z ≤ zmax (n) = min{135000 − 1.2n, −95000 + 2.6n}.                     (25.20)

At 50,000 requests the admissible increment is at most USD 35,000. Across continuous
nonnegative volume, the largest such ceiling occurs where the two terms agree, n = 1150000/19,
and equals USD 1185000/19, approximately 62,368.42. Outside the interval from 475000/13
to 112500 requests, hybrid is already more costly than another route even with z = 0. At
integer request counts the continuous maximum is an upper bound; it need not be attained.
These are affordable-price ceilings under assumed equal service, not estimates of a vendor’s
willingness to sell (Causal banking proposal, 2026cv).
   A quote for an analyst seat cannot be inserted as z for a server deployment. Nor can an
instance fee be multiplied by customer count when the contract counts loaded models. First
choose the configuration and feasible schedule, then enter its charge in the correct fixed or
occupancy-dependent term. If the quote changes the route’s permitted geographic use, history
retention or model-learning operations, reassess admissibility before comparing cost. The cost
surface makes this negotiation specific: it identifies the required entitlement and the largest
incremental price consistent with the stated volume and alternative routes.
   Shared costs need the same discipline. If the bank already operates a source and assumption
ledger required by every route, its sunk acquisition cost does not become a saving unique
to hybrid. If building that ledger is still necessary in every route, include its incremental
25.11. The value of a compatibility signal                                                   377


cost in every relevant envelope. Likewise, a manual fallback needed after an unsupported
request must be charged to the assigned population. Earlier cost accounting develops these
principles generally; here their role is to prevent a favorable commercial comparison obtained
by assigning common scientific review to only one alternative. The proposal needs observed
workflow accounts before any of the displayed cost inequalities can support a procurement
decision.


25.11       The value of a compatibility signal
The uncertain acquisition fact may be compatibility with the required information and
uncertainty contract. At 50,000 assigned requests, suppose that a common licensed engine has
a good or bad compatibility state. Both licensed routes share that state. Their annual costs,
in USD, are
                                           good      bad
                                     B 510000 510000
                                                         .                           (25.21)
                                     L 470000 720000
                                     H 435000 535000
The bad-state additions pay for conversion repair, replacement or fallback that restores the
same scientific acceptance. A route with an uncorrected scientific error is inadmissible; these
are not prices for tolerating wrong causal answers. Build is compatible in both states by
assumption. This is an acquisition scenario, not a measured advantage of our present prototype.
   Let the prior good-state probability be 3/5. Expected costs are USD 510,000, 570,000
and 475,000 for B, L, H respectively, so the no-test choice is hybrid. A proposed fixture has
sensitivity 19/20 and false-positive probability 1/20 for the common compatibility state. The
four joint probabilities for good-positive, bad-positive, good-negative and bad-negative are .57,
.02, .03 and .38. Bayes’ rule therefore gives
                             59                      57                     3
                    P(+) =       ,   P(good | +) =      ,   P(good | −) =      .         (25.22)
                             100                     59                     41
For a posterior probability p, the route costs are 510000, 720000 − 250000p and 535000 −
100000p. Licensed is dominated by hybrid throughout 0 ≤ p ≤ 1, since their difference is
185000 − 150000p > 0. Hybrid beats build exactly when p > 1/4. Thus a positive signal retains
hybrid and a negative signal selects build. Using the joint probabilities avoids rounding the
conditional expectations:

                 Csignal = .57(435000) + .02(535000) + .41(510000) = 467750.             (25.23)

Gross information value is USD 7,250. A USD 5,000 test has net value USD 2,250; a USD 15,000
test has net value minus USD 7,750. Perfect state information would select hybrid in the
good state and build in the bad state, for expected cost USD 465,000 and value USD 10,000.
This upper bound rules out any USD 15,000 experiment justified only by this one annual
decision. Separate enumeration of all nine signal-contingent pairs of routes confirms this
optimum (Causal banking proposal, 2026cv).
   This example connects the commercial architecture to experiment design. Testing the R and
Python wrappers of the same SMILE core does not supply two independent observations of a
core semantic defect. Wrapper-specific serialization defects need separate states or conditional
error laws. Similarly, a public fixture with known answers can reveal whether graph marks or
utility indices survive conversion, while it cannot authenticate deployment rights or estimate a
bank’s future mixture of requests. The probabilities above are stipulated properties of a signal
378                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


about one acquisition state. They are not a claim that 95% sensitivity on generated examples
transfers to a bank.
   A prospective measurement must distinguish failure at the engine, wrapper, licensing,
data-conversion and human-review levels. Count every assigned fixture, including unavailable
and unsupported cases. Before increasing the budget, recompute the choice with every feasible
alternative, including doing the narrow task with an existing analyst tool. The experiment is
valuable only through the decision it can change, at the scale and time horizon to which its
information applies.


25.12      Adoption decisions and remaining competitive gaps
The comparison yields six concrete decisions.
1. Reuse a commercial editor for analyst graph construction when the bank accepts
   the edition, licensing and model-export boundary. Keep the unresolved class and source
   evidence in the common ledger.
2. Integrate a licensed engine only for a named supplied-model, intervention or inference
   profile whose wrapper, error and deployment behavior pass a matched public/generated
   fixture.
3. Adopt open-source components when the original source, license, dependency rights,
   coordinate convention and uncertainty object can be preserved. A package’s presence in a
   catalog is not a runtime result.
4. Port selectively only for a narrow algorithm whose semantics, numerical tolerances and
   adverse cases can be reproduced. Proprietary SMILE or hosted vendor implementations
   are not porting candidates.
5. Build the semantic ledger and refusal layer because it spans graph classes, target
   clocks, uncertainty, artifacts and licenses rather than one estimator. This is the proposed
   product’s defensible common capability, still unqualified at bank scale.
6. Reject a route for a target when it changes the estimand, drops unresolved structure,
   cannot preserve an uncertainty set or lacks a lawful deployment path. Rejection is a
   successful proposal outcome.
  The gaps remain substantial. The local service has no general discovery or sequential-policy
runtime; no commercial engine has been executed here; exact edition parity, paid prices,
embedding rights and support terms remain unknown for many families; and arbitrary latent
graphs, dependent learners, authentic assignment truth and bank economics remain open. A
complete census across all 17 areas requires additional primary manuals and owner inputs.
The present chapter narrows what should be measured and purchased; it does not claim that
the competitive survey is closed.


25.13      A prototype-to-purchase protocol
The next public/generated comparison should freeze one target from each of four journeys:
a graph-class intervention query for discovery, a weak-IV funding set, a competing-event
servicing conversion and an observation identity/clock map. Include a fixed-history policy
value as an additional servicing case. For each target, freeze the input schema, unit, clock,
graph/model, method, uncertainty object, license mode, seed, resource budget and stopping
rule. Run the common ledger, a selected open-source reference and a documented commercial
route when accessible. Report semantic equivalence, refusal/unsupported counts, numerical
error, uncertainty shape, preparation and review time, memory, queueing, recovery and full
25.14. Conclusion                                                                          379


cost.
   The study must include negative controls: a randomly oriented graph, a transposed node
matrix, an unsupported delayed-entry survival record, a nonpositive logging probability, a
direct-effect IV violation and a recommendation metric presented as though it were a causal
value. A system passes only when it preserves the refusal or identifies the changed target. The
full denominator includes unavailable originals, failed conversions and manual reviews.
   An accepted public/generated result would justify a narrow paid trial. It would not justify
a bank deployment. The paid trial would bind the exact edition, entitlement, data residency,
service account, operating platform and publication rights, then repeat the frozen matched
protocol. Authentic bank assignment, audit truth, accepted loss and institutional economics
remain later inputs. The prospective cases and their source-specific acceptance conditions are
recorded separately from the exact arithmetic (Causal banking proposal, 2026cu).


25.14      Conclusion
Commercial alternatives already provide meaningful graph, model, estimator, survival, policy
and deployment capabilities. The proposal’s gap is not a lack of commands; it is the lack of a
common contract that keeps target meaning, ambiguity, uncertainty, numerical state, data
clock, rights and refusal visible across those commands. A hybrid acquisition route is a useful
planning default under the displayed hypothetical costs, while a cheap compatibility signal
can change a route only under a declared signal law. The immediate work is therefore the
public/generated matched protocol and the semantic ledger. Prices, runtime parity, bank truth,
independent acceptance and ROI remain open evidence, as the proposal must say plainly.


25.15      Commercial Bayesian and hidden-state engines: what a
           posterior can justify
A servicing decision may depend on a credit state that the bank cannot directly observe. A
missed payment, account balance and contact history provide evidence about that state, but
the proposed action changes a mechanism rather than merely revealing another measurement.
A useful commercial comparison must therefore separate four questions: what state is plausible
given information available now; what parameters are plausible within a specified model; which
model restrictions the observations identify; and what happens when the bank changes an
action. An accurate answer to the first two questions need not answer the last two.
   The relevant commercial landscape includes graphical-model engines, statistical estimators
and general numerical environments. Three complete Stata command manuals add detail
to the previously inspected GeNIe/SMILE, Netica, BayesiaLab and Mplus profiles. These
five supported families allow a substantive comparison, while SAS, EViews, HUGIN, Bayes
Server and commercial numerical environments remain candidates requiring further matched
technical evidence. The comparison retains the 7 October 2026 literature cutoff. The Stata
copies have July 2026 PDF metadata and release-19 example routes, but later retrieval does
not authenticate their exact cutoff-era bytes or an installed licensed build. The older sources
retain their stated manual families and mutable-page limitations. None of these qualifications
licenses a claim that an unevaluated product lacks a feature.
380                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


25.15.1    Supplied-model computation and the missing causal restriction

Let A ∈ {0, 1} denote a servicing action and D ∈ {0, 1} a subsequent default. Consider two
deliberately small, fully specified mechanisms. In the selection mechanism, U ∼ Bernoulli(1/2)
is an unobserved favourable credit state, N ∼ Bernoulli(1/5) is independent noise, and

                                 A = U ⊕ N,       D = 1 − U.                            (25.24)

The exclusive-or operation flips its first binary argument when N = 1. In the causal mechanism,
an independent action A ∼ Bernoulli(1/2) replaces the first equation, and D = (1 − A) ⊕ N .
Both mechanisms give exactly the same observable table:

                                         D=0 D=1
                                   A = 0 1/10 2/5                                       (25.25)
                                   A=1    2/5 1/10

Consequently, both yield P (D = 1 | A = 0) = 4/5 and P (D = 1 | A = 1) = 1/5. Under an
intervention that replaces only the action equation, however, the selection mechanism retains
default risk 1/2 for either action. The causal mechanism has risks 4/5 and 1/5. The identified
contrast within each stipulated mechanism is therefore different even though every observable
cell agrees. This is a project derivation by complete finite enumeration, not a finding about
actual customers.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bl)
  With an assumed loss of USD 1,000 per default and action cost USD 100, the net value of
universal action relative to no action is USD −100 under selection and USD 500 under the
causal mechanism. More observations from this same law cannot distinguish those values. If
w is the prior probability of the causal mechanism in a two-model analysis with these fixed
parameters, equal likelihoods leave its posterior probability equal to w for every observed
sample. The posterior expected margin is

                 V (w) = 600w − 100     USD,      V (w) > 0 ⇐⇒ w > 1/6.                 (25.26)

Priors w = 1/10 and w = 9/10 imply USD −40 and USD 440. These numbers expose the
decision’s sensitivity to a causal assumption that the likelihood cannot learn in this example.
They do not prohibit Bayesian decisions under declared assumptions; they require the source
and consequences of those assumptions to remain visible.
   BayesiaLab’s inspected documentation distinguishes observation from intervention and
names graph surgery and likelihood matching. Its identification discussion requires causal
information expressed in a DAG before estimation. This is a useful conceptual strength
for an adapter. It does not mean that drawing the action arrow or invoking graph surgery
establishes that the bank’s graph is true.(Bayesia, 2026j,i) An agent could help enumerate the
two mechanisms, identify which records might distinguish them and draft a public experiment.
It must retain both until justified restrictions or new information resolve their difference. A
natural-language statement of confidence cannot replace that missing evidence.


25.15.2    State inference must preserve the decision clock

The supplied state model may nevertheless be valuable for prediction and decision support.
GeNIe’s inspected DBN overview represents a stationary discrete-time stochastic process.
Its discrete-DBN learning page fits parameters by EM in an already specified structure; the
selected page explicitly excludes learning the dynamic structure. Time-indexed columns must
match node identifiers, and existing network evidence is ignored during that parameter-learning
25.15. Commercial Bayesian and hidden-state engines: what a posterior can justify             381


operation. These are concrete semantic requirements, not interchangeable user-interface details.
(BayesFusion, LLC, 2024a,b)
   SMILE’s C++ tutorial distinguishes initial and transition conditional-probability tables,
temporal lag order, the number of unfolded slices and integer outcome indices. A flattened belief
array is ordered by slice and outcome. A proposed Python, Java or R wrapper must preserve
those mappings before its output can be compared with a native model. A matching array
shape is insufficient if the meaning of outcome zero or the initial slice changes. (BayesFusion,
LLC, 2024c)
    Stata’s documented sspace procedure estimates linear state-space parameters by maximum
likelihood using Kalman or diffuse-filter likelihoods. Its general form separates a latent state
zt , measured variables yt , exogenous inputs xt , wt and disturbances:

                                    zt = F zt−1 + Bxt + Cεt ,
                                                                                          (25.27)
                                    yt = Hzt + Gwt + Jνt .

The coefficient matrices are time invariant in this documented profile. The stated likelihood uses
Gaussian, serially uncorrelated disturbances with state and observation errors uncorrelated with
each other. The documented robust variance option and stationary/nonstationary initialization
methods address different statistical and numerical choices; they do not certify that a bank
action placed among the regressors is exogenous. A proposed adapter must retain the declared
covariance structure, model constraints and initial-state method. (StataCorp, 2026ad)
   The postestimation interface makes an especially important distinction: one-step predictions
use past information, filtered states use past and current information, and smoothed states use
all sample information. Its prediction sample can change the recursive state estimates. The
bank’s information set must therefore include availability times, not merely a date column.
(StataCorp, 2026ae)
   For an exact example, let a hidden distress state H remain constant for two dates, with
P (H = 1) = 1/2. Conditional on H, independent indicators X0 , X1 equal H with probability
3/4. On observing X0 = 1, the filtered probability is 3/4. If the later observation is X1 = 0,
retrospective smoothing gives

                                                      (3/4)(1/4)
                P (H = 1 | X0 = 1, X1 = 0) =                            = 1/2.            (25.28)
                                                (3/4)(1/4) + (1/4)(3/4)

Suppose a separate, stipulated causal model says an action prevents default with probability
1/10 when H = 1, has no effect otherwise, costs USD 60 and avoids USD 1,000 when successful.
Its filtered expected margin is USD 15; using the later smoothed probability gives USD −10.
The latter is a legitimate retrospective calculation, but it was unavailable when the action was
chosen. The example assumes that the causal benefit law is known; filtering does not identify
that law.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bl)
   Observability is another distinct obligation. In a noise-free two-state model with F = (9/10)I
and H = (1, 1), the observability matrix formed by H and HF has rank one. The initial
states (1, 0) and (2, −1) generate the same output (9/10)t at every date, but their first-
minus-second component contrasts are one and three. The null direction (1, −1) remains
invisible. Adding a prior can regularize or select a state representation; it does not make the
contrast observable from these measurements. New measurements, constraints justified by the
application, or a decision defined only on observable combinations are substantive alternatives.
State observability, parameter identification and causal identification each require their own
argument.
382                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


25.15.3    A posterior, a prediction error and a simulation error answer dif-
           ferent questions

Stata’s bayesmh provides adaptive Metropolis–Hastings estimation with explicit likelihoods
and priors. Its manual cautions that allowed combinations need not produce a proper posterior,
and that no single diagnostic establishes convergence. Multiple starting points, all model
parameters and requested functions need attention; apparent mixing can conceal multimodal
pseudoconvergence. Chain count, burn-in, adaptation, thinning and random seeds must
therefore be retained in a reproducible specification. The documented defaults are starting
configurations, not universal adequacy guarantees. (StataCorp, 2026ac)
   Netica’s inspected learning text instead describes counting, EM and conjugate-gradient
parameter fitting, with prior information supplied through preexisting tables and experience.
Its objective includes both data likelihood and prior terms, and local optima remain possible. A
fitted table should not be relabeled a sample from a full parameter posterior.(Norsys Software
Corp., 2026a) The Mplus 8.1 addendum supplies a complementary Bayesian dynamic-SEM
profile, including latent centering and outcome versus residual lag distinctions. Its missing-
covariate rule can remove observations unless the covariate is modeled as an outcome. A
servicing comparison must preserve that modeling decision and its observation set. The
addendum alone does not supply a complete selected release’s prior, sampler and licensing
specification.(Muthen and Muthen, 2018)
  Uncertainty must be named before being compared. For a parameter θ, training information
D and a future outcome Y , total variance is
                            Var(Y | D) = E[Var(Y | θ, D) | D]
                                                                                         (25.29)
                                           + Var(E[Y | θ, D] | D).
The first term describes conditional outcome variation; the second propagates parameter
uncertainty. For θ ∼ Uniform(0, 1) and Y | θ ∼ Bernoulli(θ) with no data, these terms are 1/6
and 1/12, totaling 1/4. For two future outcomes conditionally independent given their shared
θ, the variance of their count is 2(1/6) + 4(1/12) = 2/3. Treating the probability as fixed at
its posterior mean 1/2 gives 1/2 instead. The shared unknown parameter induces dependence.
(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bl)
   The selected sspace postestimation manual explicitly states that its reported prediction
RMSE includes disturbance variation but does not account for parameter-estimation error. It
must therefore be labeled accordingly. An adapter could add a justified parameter-propagation
layer, but its result would be an additional construction requiring its own assumptions and
tests. Neither layer automatically represents graph uncertainty or uncertainty about the action
mechanism.(StataCorp, 2026ae)
   Monte Carlo error is separate again: it measures finite simulation error in a posterior
summary. The bayesmh manual distinguishes effective-sample-size and batch-means MCSE
calculations. Its saved dataset also compresses repeated states into rows with chain, iteration
and frequency fields. Frequencies are required when summarizing these rows.(StataCorp,
2026ac) For values 0.1 and 0.9 with frequencies nine and one, the posterior-sample mean is
0.18, whereas the unweighted row mean is 0.5. A CSV conversion that retains parameter values
but drops frequencies silently changes the result. This exact arithmetic is an export-contract
example, not a native execution test.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bl)

25.15.4    From numerical tolerances to a conditional decision bound

An approximate belief need not support the same action as its reference. Suppose the exact and
approximate probabilities of a beneficial state are 0.61 and 0.59, an action produces USD 100
25.15. Commercial Bayesian and hidden-state engines: what a posterior can justify            383


in that state and costs USD 60. The expected margins are USD 1 and USD −1. A small
probability discrepancy can matter near a decision threshold even when average predictive
scores look similar.
   A conditional bound clarifies what an approximation contract would need. Let bt and ebt be
exact and approximate marginal state laws under the same fixed policy. Define total variation
as ∥b − eb∥TV = 12 s |b(s) − eb(s)|. If the reward at each date has range at most R, and the
                  P

marginal discrepancy is at most ϵt , then
                                              −1
                                             TX
                             |V − Ve | ≤ R         γ t ϵt ,   0 ≤ γ < 1.                 (25.30)
                                             t=0

To see this, subtract the reward minimum, bound each expected-reward difference by its range
times total variation, and apply the triangle inequality to the discounted sum. With R = 100
dollars, ϵt = 0.02, γ = 0.9 and T = 12, the bound is 2(1 − 0.912 )/(1 − 0.9), approximately
USD 14.3514. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026bl)
   This argument assumes the marginal error bounds. A one-step transition approximation, a
sampler stopping rule or agreement on one benchmark does not establish them. Nor does a
bound for one fixed policy automatically cover the regret of a different policy selected using
approximate beliefs. Deriving propagation under a specified transition law, verifying it on
known-law public examples, and separating policy-selection error are the next scientific steps.
The proposed product should report these limits instead of attaching an unqualified confidence
label to the action value.


25.15.5     Commercial comparison and an executable proposal route

The vendors have different documented strengths. Stata supplies explicit state/observation
equations, initialization options, information-set choices, Bayesian diagnostics and persistent
simulation exports. GeNIe/SMILE supplies graphical DBNs and concrete native temporal
representations. Netica supplies parameter-learning alternatives with latent or incomplete data.
BayesiaLab distinguishes observation, intervention and identification assumptions. Mplus
supplies a Bayesian dynamic-SEM modeling route. The proposal currently has exact authored
references and semantic requirements; it has no qualified native adapter for these profiles. Its
proposed contribution is to preserve causal meaning and refusals consistently across the library,
CLI and MCP, including the agent’s translation of a business question into a model.
   The appropriate reuse route is a conditional, isolated licensed worker with a versioned
exchange contract. A request must identify its task, decision time, outcome horizon, units,
observed and latent variables, action mechanism and admissible information. A returned
result must distinguish filtered from smoothed states, process from parameter uncertainty, and
posterior from Monte Carlo variation. It must preserve native diagnostics, chain frequencies,
parameter names, initialization and failed calculations. Replacing a vendor’s engine or porting
its mathematics is a separate rights and validation decision; public documentation is not a
redistribution entitlement. Prices, commercial deployment rights and measured operating costs
remain unavailable in this comparison, so no saving or superiority is asserted.
   SAS’s selected MCMC PDF transfer was incomplete; EViews and HUGIN technical endpoints
failed. Those attempts neither establish their capabilities nor prove absence. Complete
selected-release MCMC/SSM manuals, official state-model help, HUGIN DBN and intervention
documentation, Bayes Server’s versioned SDK contracts, and MATLAB/Wolfram toolbox-
specific originals are concrete recovery targets. Broader complementary searches must also
test whether the shortlist misses a product family. These source obligations can proceed
independently of public prototype design.
384                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The first prototype comparison can use the finite laws above, supplied-state models with
known parameters, and deliberately misspecified alternatives. Before execution, freeze the
query, information clock, causal assumptions, uncertainty components, monetary inputs and
admissible errors. Compare exact enumeration with a licensed native inference path; test a
timestamp violation, an unobservable contrast, a frequency-loss export, posterior impropriety
and a policy near its decision threshold. Record both correct answers and justified refusals. Only
after such comparisons show merit should the proposal request costly bank-specific experiments.
This route develops useful public evidence while retaining the unresolved assumptions and
commercial terms.


25.16       Commercial network tools: spatial impacts, exposure
            designs and switchbacks
A branch intervention can affect customers outside the treated branch, while a borrower’s
funding choice can propagate through guarantees and counterparties. Commercial software
already offers several relevant routes, but they answer different questions. A spatial regression
estimates a response under a supplied weight matrix and model; an exposure experiment
compares outcomes under an assignment design; a switchback changes a population’s treatment
over time. The proposal must compare these routes at the level of their targets, information
and assumptions. A graph interface or a feature called “impact” is not a common causal
estimand.
  The selected primary documentation supports concrete profiles for Stata, SAS/ETS, ArcGIS
Pro and Statsig. Their strengths include supplied-network estimation, spatial data preparation,
diagnostic output, experimental assignment and analysis services that our proposed library
has not implemented. The comparison therefore asks which original engines or services merit
a public prototype, and which semantics the proposed common interface must preserve. It
does not claim existing product parity. (StataCorp, 2026x; SAS Institute, 2024; Esri, 2025b;
Statsig, 2025b)


25.16.1     Define the intervention before comparing an impact

Let Y be an n-vector of branch outcomes, a a vector of intervention levels, and W a supplied
matrix whose entry Wij weights the influence of unit j on unit i. This receiver-row convention
differs from the source-row adjacency used by some discovery packages. For a stipulated linear
structural equilibrium, consider

|ρ|r(W ) < 1, where r(W ) is the spectral radius, also gives the convergent propagation expansion

      P

without supplying those intervention premises. An endogenous treatment, omitted common

estimator. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026as)

25.16.2     Weights, identities and uncertainty are substantive choices

Stata distinguishes scalar normalization from row normalization. Dividing W by a common
scalar and changing spatial coefficients correspondingly can preserve the model. Normalizing
each row separately generally changes its meaning. The manual also refuses a sample smaller
than the matrix’s unit set unless force is requested, warning that removing units changes spatial
connections and normalization. Its maximum-likelihood robust covariance is described for
nonnormal independent and identically distributed innovations; the heteroskedastic GS2SLS
option relaxes identical distribution while retaining independence. None of these choices
supplies arbitrary residual network dependence. (StataCorp, 2026x)
  The exact three-branch star
                                                                    
                             0 1 1                      0 1/2 1/2
                       W⋆ = 1 0 0 ,           Wrow = 1 0    0                        (25.33)
                                                              
                             1 0 0                      1 0    0

illustrates the distinction. With ρ = 1/4, β = 10 and γ = 0, a unit intervention at branch 1 has
responses (80/7, 20/7, 20/7) under W⋆ and (32/3, 8/3, 8/3) under Wrow . In contrast, replacing
W⋆ by W⋆ /2 and ρ by 1/2 preserves the original response exactly. The two row conventions
describe different propagation assumptions. An agent must not select one merely to match a
package default. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026as)
   SAS/ETS’s selected SPATIALREG manual, labeled 2023.10 and dated August 2024, docu-
ments a broad cross-sectional model family including SAR, spatial Durbin, error and moving-
average specifications. Its default row standardization replaces missing weights with zeros;
NONORMALIZE instead refuses missing off-diagonal entries and treats diagonal entries as zero.
A missing relationship is not scientifically equivalent to a known absent relationship. The
SPATIALID field aligns observations with the matrix, but numeric noninteger IDs are truncated
for matching. The proposed interface should use validated immutable identifiers and an explicit
missing-tie policy before dispatch, preserving all exclusions and conversions. (SAS Institute,
2024)
  The selected SAS SAR likelihood uses independent normal innovations. It offers Hessian,
outer-product and QML covariance choices, with Hessian as default and additional restrictions
when certain likelihood approximations are selected. Stata’s default impact delta method

conditions on regressors; its unconditional option includes their sampling variation and has
sample-selection restrictions. These documented distinctions are useful requirements for an
adapter, but do not by themselves prove identification or useful finite-sample coverage. (SAS
Institute, 2024; StataCorp, 2026v)
  Full parameter covariance must also survive extraction. In the two-branch reference,

   Stata’s spatial-panel route further requires strongly balanced panels. Its fixed-effects

25.16.3     Exposure support is a property of the experiment

For a different route, let Zi be treatment assignment and let Ei (Z, G) summarize the assign-
ments of unit i’s neighbors in a declared network G. An exposure response Yi (z, e) assumes
that this summary retains the relevant treatment interference. Even if the graph is measured
perfectly, the assignment design may never generate some required (z, e) combinations. For two
connected borrowers with exactly one treated, the only possible exposures are (1, 0) and (0, 1),
each with probability 1/2 for a given borrower. The cells (0, 0) and (1, 1) have zero probability.
Direct effects at zero neighbor treatment cannot be recovered by weighting observations into a
cell the experiment never visits. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026as)
   Independent half-probability treatment assignments instead give each exposure cell prob-
ability 1/4. With known positive probabilities πi (z, e) = Pr{Zi = z, Ei = e}, an authored
finite-population mean reference is
                                            n
                                         1X    1{Zi = z, Ei = e}Yi
                             µ
                             b(z, e) =                             .                       (25.35)
                                         n i=1       πi (z, e)

Under consistency for the declared exposure mapping and the known assignment law, lin-
earity of expectation yields the mean potential outcome for that cell. Enumerating all four
25.16. Commercial network tools: spatial impacts, exposure designs and switchbacks               387


assignments for the stipulated law Yi (z, e) = 5 + 2z + 3e gives expected means 5, 8, 7 and 10
for (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1) respectively. The direct contrast at e = 0 is 2, and the spillover
contrast for untreated units is 3. This verifies a point-mean identity. It supplies neither a
useful variance estimate from two borrowers nor a general confidence interval; joint exposure
probabilities, dependence and the sampling/design law remain necessary. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026as)
   Statsig’s selected cluster-unit documentation gives a different, concrete service: assign at
organization level and analyze user revenue using a specified one-to-many organization/user
relationship. Its ratio treatment accounts for numerator-denominator covariance with the
delta method. That can address the distinction between assignment and analysis units, but
does not establish that all interactions lie within organizations, that treatment cannot alter
the denominator, or that the desired exposure cells have positive probability. Those questions
must remain in the proposed experiment contract. (Statsig, 2025c)


25.16.4     Switchbacks change interference and time together

Statsig’s legacy technical documentation describes switchbacks in which populations or regions
switch treatment by time window. It documents event attribution using exposure timestamps,
unit IDs and an attribution window; bucket-level and variant-level metrics; separate resampling
of treatment and control buckets 10,000 times; and percentile confidence intervals. Configura-
tion includes schedules, window lengths and burn-in/burn-out exclusions, with randomized
bucketing described as an advanced feature. These are substantive capabilities for a public
experimental comparison, not merely a network label. (Statsig, 2025b,a)
   Changing everyone in a region together can reduce one form of simultaneous cross-treatment
interference while introducing an important time comparison. For an authored law Yt (z) =
100t + 2z, observing control at t = 0 and treatment at t = 1 gives an observed difference
of 102 although the immediate causal effect is 2. With carryover Yt = 2Zt + 4Zt−1 under
an alternating schedule, treated windows follow control and yield 2, while control windows
follow treatment and yield 4. The observed difference is −2, the immediate effect is 2, and
the sustained treatment effect is 6. Resampling the same contaminated windows cannot
create missing assignment or washout information. These are explicit counterexamples to an
unrestricted interpretation, not claims of an observed Statsig failure. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026as)
   The prototype should therefore declare the policy target, randomization of start phases and
schedules, carryover horizon, attribution overlap and effective resampling unit. Discarding
exposures during burn periods is not by itself a demonstration that all associated outcomes
are free of earlier treatment. Adjacent buckets or shared regional shocks require a justified
dependence treatment. The saved September 2025 documentation also lists profile limits,
including unavailable time-series and dimension breakdowns and unavailable CUPED and
sequential testing for that legacy switchback profile. Those statements must not be promoted
to claims about current commercial availability. (Statsig, 2025a)


25.16.5     A comparison that can guide the first prototype

For an initial equilibrium-model prototype, Stata and SAS provide documented original engines
with different model, covariance and weight policies. ArcGIS offers a geographical workflow and
a Python surface, with an impact convention that needs explicit reconciliation. Statsig supplies
an experimental alternative when population/time assignment is the intended intervention.
A rational first comparison chooses a declared target and then asks which of these profiles
388                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


actually supports it; it does not rank unlike outputs by one accuracy number. Our present
implemented contribution is the exact authored references. Model fitting, licensed execution,
native covariance behavior and service integration remain proposed capabilities.
  The public prototype can begin with the two- and three-branch laws above, generated
assignments, missing-tie perturbations and explicit carryover. It should compare target
preservation, refusals, graph and sample identities, uncertainty definitions and economic
decisions before scale. Public empirical datasets can test import, geography and workflow
behavior, but their observed network alone supplies no intervention truth. Actual runtime,
memory, analyst effort, licensing, data movement and upgrade costs must be measured rather
than inferred from documentation. Commercial adapters should preserve the original engine
where justified; porting a proprietary algorithm is neither necessary nor supported by the
present evidence.
   Coverage remains incomplete for the exact editions and interference targets of Optimizely,
EViews, IBM SPSS and the commercial probabilistic-network families. The requested Op-
timizely route returned a general homepage, which supports no technical capability claim.
Supplied Bayesian networks and ordinary pooled regression must not stand in for an unin-
spected exposure estimator. Their next steps are concrete: identify the exact procedure and
version, acquire the original technical specification and rights terms, and compare its target
with the same public reference. None is classified as lacking a feature merely because its
original has not yet been reviewed. These unresolved profiles and unknown prices limit the
market comparison while allowing the supported prototype designs to proceed.


25.17      Commercial missing-data workflows and transfer be-
           tween bank populations
A bank may obtain a credible intervention estimate in a pilot and still make a poor decision
when it extends the intervention to another branch. Customers may differ, follow-up outcomes
may be missing, and the software used to complete the records may report uncertainty for
a different quantity from the proposed decision. A useful commercial comparison therefore
follows the complete question: which population receives which action, when is the outcome
measured, why is it unobserved, and which assumptions connect the observed records to the
decision? Imputation, uncertainty combination and population transfer are separate steps. A
feature called “missing values” establishes none of those connections by its name alone.
   The selected primary documentation provides concrete comparators. Stata’s mi family
manages multiple completed datasets and their analysis; SAS/STAT’s MI and MIANALYZE
procedures separate generation and combination; IBM SPSS Missing Values exposes impu-
tation and output-specific pooling. The inspected IBM edition is 31.0.2. The SAS HTML
identifies version 14.1, whereas the Stata manuals contain release-19 example-data paths and
July 2026 PDF metadata. These identities delimit the comparison; later retrieval does not
authenticate every byte as the edition available at the literature cutoff. Exact licensed builds,
current entitlements and broader commercial coverage remain unresolved. EViews, Mplus
and commercial graphical tools remain leads requiring matched technical originals for this
particular target. StataCorp (2026aa); SAS Institute (2026e); IBM (2026c)


25.17.1    Missingness assumptions precede record completion

Let A be a binary action, X covariates recorded before that action, Y (a) the monetary
outcome under action a, and R an indicator that the outcome is observed. The record contains
25.17. Commercial missing-data workflows and transfer between bank populations                 389


(X, A, R, RY ), with a separate missingness mask so that an absent outcome is never mistaken
for a zero. Consistency connects an observed outcome to Y (A); treatment exchangeability and
positive treatment probability are additional causal assumptions. For the particular problem
in which only Y is missing, a conditional mean restriction sufficient for response adjustment is

                 E[Y | X, A, R = 1] = E[Y | X, A],         P (R = 1 | X, A) > 0.           (25.36)

The stronger familiar MAR restriction makes response independent of the missing outcome
conditional on the observed variables. When covariates are also missing, the pattern-specific
observed information and imputation model must be specified again; equation (25.36) is not a
general multivariate recipe. Administrative censoring, a variable undefined for a customer,
and an outcome lost through nonresponse need distinct observation models.
   Stata’s substantive manual and the SAS assumptions chapter distinguish MAR from MCAR
and describe ignorability using MAR together with distinct parameters for the data and
missingness models. They also explain why an assumption about unobserved values cannot be
verified by inspecting only the observed values. The SAS profile adds distributional restrictions
for particular regression and MCMC procedures. These restrictions must accompany a
procedure name. A good fit to observed records, a plausible-looking imputed distribution or
rejection of an MCAR diagnostic does not establish MAR. StataCorp (2026ab); SAS Institute
(2026c)
   An exact example makes the investment consequence visible. Let a latent response type H be
equally likely to be zero or one, randomize A independently of H, and set R = H. All customers
have Y (0) = 0. Responders have Y (1) = 10. In one complete-data law, nonresponders have
Y (1) = −10; in a second they have Y (1) = 10. The observable joint distribution of (A, R, RY )
is identical in both laws: each action-response cell has probability 1/4, and observed treated
outcomes equal 10. Yet the complete-population effects are respectively 0 and 10. At an
assumed action cost of USD 4, the margins are USD −4 and USD 6. More imputation draws
from one selected model cannot distinguish these worlds. The project reference enumerates
the complete laws and verifies equality of their observed distributions. It does not assert that
either law describes actual bank records.Causal banking proposal project (2026bf)
  A transparent sensitivity parameter writes the unobserved treated mean as 10 + δ, keeping
the control mean zero. The resulting target is

                              τ (δ) = 10 + 12 δ,    V (δ) = 6 + 12 δ.                      (25.37)

For the illustrative restriction δ ∈ [−20, 0], value ranges from −4 to 6 and changes sign at
δ = −12. The interval is supplied as a sensitivity restriction, not learned from the missing
outcomes. The SAS sensitivity chapter documents a pattern-mixture approach in MI and
explicitly says that the selection-model approach is not supplied by that procedure profile. A
result that changes under a plausible MNAR scenario establishes dependence of the decision
on assumptions; it does not establish which scenario is true. Exact syntax and later-release
capabilities need their own evidence. SAS Institute (2026g); Causal banking proposal project
(2026bf)


25.17.2     What the three documented workflows preserve

Stata offers four MI storage styles while retaining the original data as m = 0 and the completed
datasets as m = 1, . . . , M . Variables can be regular, imputed or passive, with passive variables
representing algebraic functions of other variables. The introduction also states that extended
missing values .a through .z persist as hard missing in the documented profile. An interchange
layer that maps every absent value to an ordinary numeric null could therefore change what
390                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


the engine is asked to impute. Maintaining the missingness reason and role is part of the
statistical contract. StataCorp (2026aa)
   For chained equations, Stata documents a default burn-in of ten iterations, ordering from the
most to the least observed variable, configurable conditional models and saved trace summaries.
Perfect prediction produces an error unless an explicit augmentation option is requested. The
manual discusses incompatible conditionals and dependence of results on specification, order
and burn-in. These are useful controls, but a chosen default is not a proof of convergence or of
adequacy for a causal estimand. For example, an imputer that omits a treatment interaction
needed by the analyst can erase the heterogeneity needed for the branch-transfer decision even
if marginal summaries look reasonable.StataCorp (2026y,ab)
  There is a stronger reason to retain the conditional specifications themselves. Consider
binary U, V with proposed conditionals

                      P (U = 1 | V = 0) = P (U = 1 | V = 1) = 21 ,
                                                                                          (25.38)
                      P (V = 1 | U = 0) = 14 ,    P (V = 1 | U = 1) = 43 .

For any positive binary joint distribution, the odds ratio calculated from either pair of
conditionals must agree. Here the first specification requires odds ratio 1 and the second
requires 9, so no such joint distribution exists. Nevertheless, alternating draws can have
stable distributions. In the cell order (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1), a scan updating U then V
has stationary law (3, 1, 1, 3)/8; reversing the scan has stationary law (1, 1, 1, 1)/4. Direct
multiplication verifies each invariant distribution. Thus an apparently stable trace does not
demonstrate compatibility of the supplied conditionals. This exact constructed example is
a diagnostic design, not an observed failure of a particular vendor’s implementation.Causal
banking proposal project (2026bf)
   SAS supplies a related but separately versioned workflow. Its MI overview distinguishes
sequential methods for monotone patterns from multivariate-normal MCMC and fully condi-
tional specification for arbitrary patterns. FCS uses separate conditional models rather than
beginning with an explicit common multivariate model. The completed datasets are analyzed
using the relevant complete-data procedures, and MIANALYZE reads parameter estimates
together with standard errors or covariance matrices. It notes an additional assumption for
multivariate Wald inference and special treatment for quantities such as correlations and ratios.
The proposal therefore needs a typed collection of estimates and covariance matrices, not just
a filled table. The recovered HTML contains equations as images that are outside this text
inspection; the numerical pooling formulas below are grounded in the readable Stata manual.
SAS Institute (2026e,f,d)
   IBM’s manual makes another important distinction. Multiple Imputation accepts analysis
weights in summaries and imputation models, but it does not explicitly handle strata, clusters
or other complex sampling structures. The manual also says that Complex Samples procedures
do not automatically analyze MI datasets in this profile. Frequency weights and analysis
weights have different semantics; noninteger frequency weights are rounded. Passing a final
sampling weight therefore does not establish a cluster-aware covariance calculation. Stata
documents a survey-prefix analysis route, but that alone also leaves the imputation model’s
treatment of the sampling design to be justified. IBM (2026c); StataCorp (2026z)
   SPSS chooses a monotone method when the pattern permits it and otherwise uses FCS.
Automatic FCS uses ten iterations; the manual provides history output for convergence
assessment. Main effects are the automatic specification, with optional categorical two-way
interactions under selected settings. Scale variables can use linear regression or predictive
mean matching, whose documented default donor count is five; categorical models use logistic
regression. Constraints can cause redraws, and excluding highly incomplete variables removes
25.17. Commercial missing-data workflows and transfer between bank populations               391


them from both imputation and prediction. Reproducing a run requires the same seed, case
order, variable order and settings. These details affect the implied procedure and belong in an
adapter request. IBM (2026c)
   The output variable Imputation_ distinguishes original data from the M completed versions,
and split-file settings control how those versions are analyzed. IBM distinguishes naive
combination, which supplies a pooled parameter, from univariate combination, which can
also supply standard errors, effective degrees of freedom, intervals and missing-information
diagnostics. Support is specific to each output; an unsupported procedure returns no pooled
output. An integration must preserve that unavailability rather than attach a generic confidence
interval to every pooled number. IBM (2026c)
