of the restriction matrix. The fixed-length interval’s finite-sample near-optimality result has
further convexity and symmetry conditions; those do not apply automatically to relative
magnitude or added sign/shape restrictions. Neither a sensitivity curve nor a convenient
Gaussian approximation supplies these assumptions. Reporting a favourable tuning value
after inspecting the curve needs a separately justified selection or simultaneous-inference
rule (Rambachan and Roth, 2023).


25.21.3     Defaults, grids and failed numerical searches

The pinned source exposes substantive distinctions between entrypoints. The unrestricted
smoothness interface defaults to a fixed-length confidence interval and the first postperiod
target. Its automatically selected tuning grid uses a preperiod upper-bound calculation with
significance level 0.05 when multiple preperiods are present, even if the requested interval
level differs. The relative-magnitude interface defaults to the C-LF method, ten tuning values
between zero and two, and 1,000 inversion grid points. The did bridge has a default of 100
grid points and forwards that argument to relative magnitude but not to its smoothness call.
A wrapper should record the executed options explicitly and require deliberate tuning choices
for a decision analysis (Ashesh Rambachan, Jonathan Roth and contributors, 2026b,a).
   At the lower relative-magnitude level, membership is retained at grid nodes after union
across signed preperiod components. Default bounds are plus or minus twenty post-target
standard errors around zero. The inspected high-level path reduces accepted nodes to their
minimum and maximum. This is a numerical summary, not a certificate that the continuous
confidence set is connected, fully searched or bounded. An empty set of accepted nodes on the
coarse grid {−1, 1} is compatible with the nonempty continuous set [−0.2, 0.2]. Accepted nodes
−2, −1, 1, 2 with rejection at zero have hull [−2, 2], which fills a rejected gap. Acceptance at a
search boundary leaves the extent beyond that boundary unresolved. These are elementary
grid counterexamples, not observed outputs from running the package (Ashesh Rambachan,
Jonathan Roth and contributors, 2026b; Causal banking proposal project, 2026bh).
   Solver status creates a different concern. In the inspected population-bound helpers, when
both linear-program statuses are nonzero, the smoothness path returns the unadjusted target
as both endpoints with a warning; the selected relative-magnitude component path makes
a corresponding return without a local warning. The inspected alternative branch does not
separately guard a single failed optimum. These source paths do not prove that any particular
runtime input triggers a failure, but they rule out treating every returned point interval as
certified identification. A proposed adapter must distinguish infeasibility, unboundedness,
convergence failure and an unresolved status. Capturing warnings alone is insufficient if a
helper discards status; a pinned patch or lower-level instrumentation may be required before
admission (Ashesh Rambachan, Jonathan Roth and contributors, 2026b).
   The same principle applies to covariance and restrictions. Nonconformable dimensions
cause refusal, while asymmetry and negative eigenvalues generate warnings rather than a
statistical repair. Fixed-length paths warn that requested sign or shape restrictions are unused.
The initial proposed contract should refuse an unexplained invalid covariance and either
25.22. Native identification engines and the joint meaning of a counterfactual                 405


refuse an ignored restriction or report the executed, weaker restriction explicitly. A silent
positive-semidefinite projection would change the supplied uncertainty model; it needs its own
justification.


25.21.4     Reuse choice and an implementable qualification path

The proposal retains the pinned R implementation as a reference and selects an isolated R worker
as a future integration candidate. Its complete repository MIT licence permits reuse subject
to notice retention and the stated disclaimer. This does not qualify the licences, installation
or numerical behavior of CVXR, GLPK, ECOS and the other imported dependencies. The
pinned maintenance notes describe recent CVXR compatibility repairs, which make a frozen
environment and version-change review especially relevant. A new Python or C++ port
would add optimization and distributional parity obligations without a measured benefit. The
Stata implementation or another port would need its own source and interface review (Ashesh
Rambachan, Jonathan Roth and contributors, 2026b).
   The conversion boundary is equally important. The selected did bridge requires a dynamic
aggregate and universal baseline, constructs covariance from the influence matrix, requires
consecutive event times, and removes the normalised reference coefficient. This computation
alone does not establish that the influence representation has the right bank clustering
or calendar dependence. The selected fixest bridge uses internal model fields to form an
                                                                                 b ′ . The worker
aggregation matrix T , then transforms coefficients and covariance as T βb and T ΣT
must preserve cohort ordering, target weights and the actual covariance selected upstream,
and must qualify compatibility with the chosen versions (Ashesh Rambachan, Jonathan Roth
and contributors, 2026a).
   A bounded prototype should first reproduce population targets and option forwarding on
frozen contrasts; then exercise malformed order, singular inputs, solver terminations, clipped
grids and ignored restrictions. Coverage and decision-value comparisons need prospectively
specified generated panels, sampling laws, tuning choices, failure denominators and resource
budgets. Ordinary DID, prespecified smoothness, relative magnitude and the conservative
projection supply useful matched comparators, with their differing assumptions retained. Total
cost includes event-study fitting, covariance construction, conversion, repeated inversion, failure
investigation and environment support. Only that evidence can justify which R path to build
and whether a later bank experiment is worth its cost.


25.22       Native identification engines and the joint meaning of a
            counterfactual
A lending analyst may ask whether an approval changes repayment, while a servicing analyst
asks whether a borrower who failed under the existing policy would have succeeded under
another action. These questions require different information. A native implementation
can make a symbolic calculation faster, but its language does not turn an observational
conditional distribution into an intervention law or select a coupling between a person’s
potential outcomes. The proposed product therefore keeps graph identification, numerical
evaluation and counterfactual model specification as separate contracts.
   The selected aGrUM 3.2.0 revision is dated 6 October 2026. Twelve authenticated implemen-
tation, wrapper and test originals extend the earlier dispatch review. The build declarations
require C++20 and CMake 3.18; the selected root license statement is LGPL-3-or-later or MIT,
subject to a separate component review. These are historical source declarations, not a report
406                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


that a native build, Python installation or bank interface has passed. The R-backed C++
search core of dosearch supplies a substantive alternative, while other native candidates and
partial-identification engines remain unresolved. The bounded comparison cannot establish
complete C++ market coverage. (aGrUM authors and contributors, 2026; Tikka et al., 2025)


25.22.1     Inspecting recursion without mistaking it for a correctness proof

The native do-calculus source constructs backdoor and frontdoor expressions, then provides a
general recursive identification path. Its branches restrict the graph to outcome ancestors, add
irrelevant remaining variables to the intervention, partition observed nodes connected through
latent co-children, and multiply or marginalize the resulting kernels. A single remaining full
confounded component triggers a hedge exception. The induced submodel keeps observed
identifiers and retains a latent descriptor only when it still has at least two retained children.
These observations identify the algorithmic objects that a comparison must preserve; they
are not a proof that every legal input reaches the mathematically intended branch. (aGrUM
authors and contributors, 2026)
   Two details deserve explicit qualification before reuse. The conditional-query path builds one
modified graph after removing incoming edges to intervention nodes and outgoing edges from
every conditioning node, then tests candidate promotions within that graph. A comparison
must establish the appropriate multi-variable graph surgery and the conditional query after
each promotion. Separately, when an accumulated kernel is present, the first topological
factor is constructed as a joint-probability AST rather than the numerator expression just
calculated from that kernel. Whether that branch is reachable with a distinct marginal, or
is equivalent under the implementation’s invariant, requires a proof-aligned fixture. Neither
observation alone warrants announcing a software defect. Both are precise obligations that a
root README or successful simple adjustment example would miss. (aGrUM authors and
contributors, 2026)
   The numerical layer has its own boundary. A formula’s identified predicate checks whether
an expression root exists. Evaluation then requires an observational Bayesian network, so
a structure-only answer and an evaluable answer are different states. Division of expression
trees delegates to tensor division. The selected files do not settle zero-denominator support
handling, finite arithmetic or an uncertainty statement. The Python convenience wrapper
retains the model on the returned tensor and maps an unidentified formula to a None numerical
answer; complete exception and lifetime conversions still need direct inspection and execution.
Preserve an expression with its graph, variable domains and support conditions instead of
returning an unqualified floating-point success. (aGrUM authors and contributors, 2026)
   For example, let approval A and repayment Y be binary. In one authored lending world,
U ∼ Bernoulli(1/2), A = U and Y = U ; in another, A ∼ Bernoulli(1/2) and Y = A. Both
observed laws put mass 1/2 on each of (A, Y ) = (0, 0) and (1, 1). Replacing the approval
equation gives an average intervention contrast of zero in the first world and one in the second.
Deterministic assignment in the first world also means that the observed law does not provide
all conditional treatment comparisons. The example is a supplied structural construction,
not a discovered bank graph. Its purpose is to prevent an association or unsupported engine
return from being presented as identified repayment benefit. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026aa)
25.22. Native identification engines and the joint meaning of a counterfactual                  407


25.22.2     Why individual root updates need a joint abduction contract

The selected counterfactual builder starts from the observational Bayesian network, collects
parentless nodes excluding interventions and declared latents, conditions the original network
on the observed profile, and fills each selected root’s conditional-probability table with its
individual posterior. It then calculates an intervention in the reconstructed model. The
constructor used for reconstruction does not copy the separate original latent descriptors or
spurious-arc declarations. Accordingly, graph identity also belongs in the conformance test.
More fundamentally, replacing several root marginals does not in general retain their posterior
joint dependence. (aGrUM authors and contributors, 2026)
  Consider a completely declared servicing example. Before an action, roots U and V are
independent fair bits; A is an independent fair action. Let success under action a have one of
two structural response functions:

                         Ystable (a) = 1{U = V },
                         Yswitch (0) = 1{U = V },    Yswitch (1) = 1{U ̸= V }.              (25.59)

Every observed pair (A, Y ) has probability 1/4 in both worlds; each world also has P {Y (a) =
1} = 1/2 for both actions. Thus even the two marginal intervention laws do not choose between
these cross-world response functions. For the profile A = 0, Y = 1, however, the roots must
agree. The joint posterior puts mass 1/2 on (U, V ) = (0, 0) and 1/2 on (1, 1), while each
separate root posterior remains a fair bit. Consequently,

                                          P {Ystable (1) = 1 | A = 0, Y = 1} = 1,
                                          P {Yswitch (1) = 1 | A = 0, Y = 1} = 0,
                   X
                         1{u = v}P (u | A = 0, Y = 1)P (v | A = 0, Y = 1) = 12 .            (25.60)
                   u,v

The last expression is the result of imposing separate posterior root marginals; it is not the first
world’s joint conditional probability. In the switch world the same product reconstruction also
gives 1/2 for inequality. The exact finite enumeration tests this semantic distinction without
executing an upstream package. A native run is still required to establish the behavior of the
installed representation, graph and wrapper on this fixture. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026aa)
   If the declared payoff is USD 100 for success less a USD 20 action cost, the three respective
success probabilities imply USD 80, USD −20 and USD 30. These are conditional values
for the specified profile and action, not an incremental return against a measured current
workflow. They are assumed monetary consequences of a semantic choice. A product cannot
substitute the middle probability 1/2 because it looks numerically stable: it must preserve
the joint abduction distribution, state a sufficient factorization condition, return a justified
set over admissible couplings, or refuse the requested individual answer. Additional marginal
intervention observations alone do not resolve this constructed coupling ambiguity. (Causal
banking proposal project, 2026aa)


25.22.3     A reusable boundary and a concrete qualification route

The inspected native tests are useful starting specifications. They include manual back-
door/frontdoor expression comparisons, selected direct-do-calculus numerical comparisons,
a hedge evaluation exception, ID/IDC smoke tests and a salary counterfactual fixture. The
selected conditional smoke tests verify that an expression builds and evaluates; they do not
independently establish its multi-variable causal meaning. A parity check against the same
408                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


builder also cannot replace a separate structural oracle. None of these upstream tests was run
in this source review, and the coupled-root example is a new authored reference, not a claim
about existing upstream coverage. (aGrUM authors and contributors, 2026; Causal banking
proposal project, 2026aa)
   For dosearch, the already pinned R/C++ source makes a different tradeoff. Its native entry
accepts directed and bidirected graph information, a collection of known distributions, a target
and search options through Rcpp. The loop can return when its time budget expires; the
returned identifiable flag depends on whether a target distribution was found. The inspected
result does not separately certify search exhaustion. Therefore preserve a discovered formula
and derivation when available, but retain unknown or time-limited status when search failure
has not been proved to imply nonidentification in the stated problem class. Start reuse through
the supported R boundary; a stand-alone C++ port would additionally require extraction of the
Rcpp interface, environment, representation and rights obligations. A shared implementation
language is insufficient evidence that the two engines deliver an interchangeable service. (Tikka
et al., 2025)
   The proposed conformance program first fixes the query, graph class, observed or experimen-
tal input law, domains, support and information clock. It then compares direct and shortcut
identification on independently enumerated small models, tests multi-variable conditioning
and nested kernels, exercises nonidentification separately from unsupported methods, and
tests numeric availability and support-zero behavior. Counterfactual tests additionally retain
structural response functions and joint posterior dependence; a graph with ordinary conditional
tables is not silently promoted to a unique cross-world model. Finally, the same signed query
and typed result cross the native, Python and process boundaries, with ownership and excep-
tions checked. Retain aGrUM and dosearch as conditional comparators and defer executable
admission until those trials pass in their declared regimes. Other candidates, original proof
alignment, full component rights and general partial identification remain open; this bounded
source review does not close them. (aGrUM authors and contributors, 2026; Tikka et al., 2025;
Causal banking proposal project, 2026aa)
Chapter 26

Reusing causal software across
languages without changing the
question

26.1     What must a port preserve?
An original implementation, a language binding and a new implementation of the same
published method are different assets. For a bank, their comparison begins with a decision:
which result will inform a rate change, eligibility rule or servicing policy? The artifact that
must survive may be a graph class, a vector of treatment contrasts, a joint uncertainty law or
an explicit refusal. A port that reproduces a point estimate while changing its population or
resampling unit has not reproduced that decision problem.
   The immediate proposal is to reuse original-language implementations where their scientific
profile and dependencies fit. A native port needs a separate case: a demonstrated interface,
deployment or resource constraint and an equivalence argument for the specific computation
being replaced. This chapter develops those obligations from inspected R, Python, Java and
C++ sources. It does not claim that the proposed workers have been built or that similar
algorithm names establish parity.
  Let Fv (x, u) be version v of a source computation, with scientific input x and explicit random
input u. A candidate Gw in another language accepts an encoding E(x); its result is decoded
by D. An exact coupled reference would require

                                D{Gw (E(x), T (u))} = Fv (x, u)                            (26.1)

for every admitted x, u, where T maps the random inputs. The equality must include result
status, target identity and uncertainty, not just numeric fields. It is often stronger than a
useful implementation needs. A numerical profile can instead specify a justified error bound for
a named output, while a stochastic profile can require equality or an appropriate comparison
of joint output laws. These alternatives need to be selected explicitly; agreement on one seed
is not evidence of any universal equality.
  The four languages expose different engineering choices, but no language determines scientific
validity. R pcalg offers source-visible FCI/RFCI paths and conversion routines. Python
CausalML exposes target columns, shared control fits and row-bootstrap implementation. Java
Tetrad stores graph endpoints attached to nodes and implements distinct search branches.
Native aGrUM contains FCI/PAG code and is also accessible through bindings. The proposal
should preserve these originals as comparison references, then decide whether to call, bind,

                                              409
410                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


port or reject the selected profile. Source inspection is the evidence available here; it remains
distinct from an upstream runtime trial (pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024a;
uber/causalml, 2026; cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026c; agrumery/aGrUM, 2026a).


26.2     A branch comparison is part of the method
The inspected pcalg Possible-D-Sep code has a concrete branch: after a supplied conditional-
independence test, it removes an edge when p ≥ α. A missing test value is first replaced by the
numeric value of the NAdelete option. The same path has search-size and conditioning-order
limits. Translating the outer FCI name while changing any of these branches can change the
graph, even with identical input data (pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024a).
  Suppose a proposed numerical replacement returns pe with |pe − p| ≤ ϵ. If p ≤ α − δ or
p ≥ α + δ for δ > ϵ, the threshold decision agrees. At an exact tie, replacing ≥ by > disagrees
even when ϵ = 0. At α = 1/20, the values .0499, .05 and .0501 give delete decisions (0, 1, 1)
under the inspected rule and (0, 0, 1) under a strict comparison. This finite reference concerns
branch semantics; it does not establish that a particular dataset produces those test values.
   The margin argument extends to an adaptive algorithm only with care. At each step,
suppose the source and replacement have the same current graph, visit the same candidate
test, and their numeric error is bounded by ϵj . If the source comparison is separated from
its threshold by more than ϵj and ties/order are handled identically, the next branch agrees.
Induction then preserves the entire trace for that input. Without those conditions, a first
disagreement can change the next conditioning set, so a bound on the original sequence of test
values no longer controls the replacement sequence. A maximum error in a final matrix is not
a substitute for this trace-level argument.
   The appropriate public/generated fixture should therefore retain the visited node pair,
conditioning set, test status, effective threshold and branch decision. Include exact ties, near
ties and missing values. With NAdelete=true, the inspected replacement of a missing value is
1, which triggers deletion at the stated threshold; with false it is 0, which does not. That is a
source-defined policy for an unavailable test, not evidence of independence or dependence. A
bridge should retain the unavailable-test diagnostic even when it reproduces the source branch.
A new policy that refuses the graph is permissible as a separately declared wrapper behavior,
but it must not be reported as exact source parity.
   Search caps need similar treatment. The pcalg path can skip a Possible-D-Sep search
because the candidate set exceeds its configured maximum. Increasing that maximum in a
C++ port changes the algorithm’s effective search, although it may make sense for a new
profile. Java Tetrad and aGrUM have their own inspected traversal, filtering and orientation
paths; their source details cannot be collapsed into “FCI with the same alpha.” Candidate
generation, conditioning subsets, order, selection assumptions and stopping rules all belong
in a matched-method claim. The proposed first reuse route is the original implementation
with explicit controls. A port follows only after the exact selected profile has a meaningful
comparison oracle (pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024a; cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026c;
agrumery/aGrUM, 2026a).


26.3     Preserving the joint random computation
CausalML’s inspected T-learner code sorts non-control treatment labels, fits one control
model, and exposes that model as a shared reference for each treatment group. This is useful
computational reuse. It also means that uncertainty in the control fit can be shared across
26.4. Rows, clusters and the law of a bootstrap                                               411


treatment contrasts. A port that independently refits the control for each action has changed
the joint computation, even if each individual contrast has the same marginal distribution
under an illustrative law (uber/causalml, 2026).
  To isolate the issue, let UA , UB , UC be independent, equally probable −1 and +1 errors in
three fitted response means. Define two treatment contrasts using one control:

                             DA = UA − UC ,        DB = UB − UC .                          (26.2)

Each has mean zero and variance two; their covariance is one. The difference DA − DB =
UA − UB has variance two because the control error cancels. A replacement using independent
                                     ′ = U −U               ′
UC,A , UC,B instead has contrasts DA       A      C,A and DB = UB − UC,B . Each marginal is
unchanged, but their covariance is zero and the difference variance is four. Enumerating all
eight shared-control tuples and all sixteen split-control tuples verifies
                                            !                                  !
                                       2 1                                2 0
               Cov{(DA , DB )⊤ } =         ,             ′
                                                   Cov{(DA    ′ ⊤
                                                           , DB ) }=          .            (26.3)
                                       1 2                                0 2

The example is an authored random law, not a claimed variance formula for CausalML or an
observed vendor comparison.
  A bank comparing two offers needs the joint contrast or a justified conservative alternative,
not merely two separately correct marginal intervals. Reusing a fitted control object can preserve
shared randomness; serializing it as two independent fit instructions does not. Conversely, an
implementation that intentionally refits each contrast might be appropriate under its declared
method, but it is a different comparator. The source-derived reuse decision should name object
sharing, fit data, random state and target rows together.
   Equal integer seeds in R, NumPy, Java and C++ do not by themselves establish equal
random draws. Even within one implementation, changing iteration order can allocate the
same random stream to different units or model components. A proposed coupled comparison
should supply explicit resample indices, fold assignments and permitted tie-breaking draws
whenever the original API supports that control. Randomness inside a learner needs a separate
identity and rule. When exact coupling is unavailable, compare the required joint law under a
justified statistical design; do not infer failure from ordinary Monte Carlo differences or infer
success from two equal averages.
  The distinction is particularly important for a proposed original-language worker. Passing
a model object by reference can retain sharing within one process, while a worker boundary
may require an immutable fitted artifact or an explicit fit identifier. The common request
can refer to that identity without prescribing a generic Python pickle or Java object stream.
The scientific obligation is to preserve which fit is shared. Transport and serialization are
implementation choices to qualify after that obligation has been stated.


26.4      Rows, clusters and the law of a bootstrap
The inspected CausalML bootstrap draws row indices with replacement. One helper accepts
a supplied seed for its random-index generator; another accepts an RNG or uses NumPy’s
global state. Both slice features, treatment and outcome with the same index vector. That
alignment is essential, but it does not turn row resampling into household, panel or calendar
resampling (uber/causalml, 2026).
  Consider two observed account clusters, each containing two identical rows. The first cluster
has outcomes (0, 0), the second (2, 2). The empirical mean is one. A four-row bootstrap
412                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


samples from (0, 0, 2, 2) independently four times. Its conditional mean remains one and its
mean variance is 1/4. A two-cluster bootstrap instead draws two whole clusters from the two
available clusters and retains both rows in each selected cluster. Its mean also has conditional
expectation one, but variance 1/2. The first result follows from averaging four variance-one
empirical draws; the second from averaging two such independent cluster means.
   The finite distributions are especially transparent. Four-row resampling has 44 = 256
equally likely index tuples; cluster resampling has four equally likely cluster tuples and mean
values (0, 1, 1, 2). Agreement in the returned mean conceals a factor-of-two variance change.
Neither conditional bootstrap distribution is automatically a valid sampling approximation for
bank data. The example shows that silently changing the resampling unit during a port is a
change in the uncertainty procedure, even before asking whether that procedure is scientifically
justified.
   For longitudinal servicing, a language boundary should therefore carry the declared sampling
unit and resampling identity, not infer them from the number of rows in a data frame. If the
original API supports only row resampling, the first adapter can explicitly support independent-
row targets and refuse the requested dependent uncertainty. A new whole-account or calendar
resampling method needs its own assumptions and validation. It should be presented as a
method extension rather than silently enabled as “the same bootstrap in R.” Changing a seed
cannot repair an incorrect sampling unit.
   Failed resamples are part of that contract. A bootstrap sample can omit a treatment
arm; deleting those replicates changes the conditional law from the declared row bootstrap.
Stratifying by arm also changes the law and may be useful only as a declared procedure. The
comparison needs all planned replicates, valid-result indicators, diagnostics and aggregation
rules. A port that returns an interval from a selected successful subset may look more
reliable than a source that exposes failure, while answering a different question. The proposed
acquisition decision is to preserve the original resampling path first and qualify any new
dependent-data method separately.


26.5      Endpoint types and stable identities
A graph transfer has to preserve where each mark is attached. Write an edge between stable
node identifiers i and j as

                         eij = (mi , mj ),    mi , mj ∈ {◦, tail, arrow}.                   (26.4)

The subscripts name the endpoint, not the array position. Thus a circle at i and an arrow at
j remains a different object from an arrow at i and a circle at j. A complete graph object
also contains the node universe, absent edges, isolated nodes, edge multiplicity rules and any
separate selection or latent-couple annotations. Those items are not recoverable from a list of
directed arcs alone. An unresolved endpoint is a scientific result, not a request for the receiving
library to choose a convenient direction.
   The inspected sources illustrate why a common label vocabulary is insufficient. The selected
pcalg export covers seven endpoint pairs and therefore supplies no basis to assume that an
arbitrary endpoint object round trips. Tetrad endpoints are enum members attached to
graph nodes; the selected lookup uses node identity and returns null if the requested node
is absent, despite a comment that promises an exception. aGrUM’s PAG code exposes a
mark at a destination node, while its generic mixed-graph conversion checks arrowheads and
can collapse circle/tail distinctions. A bidirected PAG edge becoming two arcs is another
information change. This is a warning about specific inspected helpers, not a defect claim
26.6. Observation clocks and row identity                                                    413


about every aGrUM API (pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024a; cmu-phil/tetrad,
2026c; agrumery/aGrUM, 2026a).
  Define a versioned, partial translation ϕv→w from the source representation to the receiving
representation. It is valid only on a stated domain Gv,w , and on that domain must satisfy

     decodew (ϕv→w (G)) = G     up to a declared bijection of stable node identifiers.     (26.5)

The equality includes marks at both endpoints, edge existence, isolated nodes, and every
annotation the requested operation needs. If the receiver has no representation for a star, null,
circle or selection annotation, the transfer must return an explicit unsupported-result status.
Mapping an unfamiliar endpoint to a circle, dropping a latent-couple list, or fabricating a
missing edge is not a neutral fallback. A partial map is useful: it defines which requests are
safe to send and gives a precise refusal boundary.
  The first comparison suite should generate all node-label permutations for small labelled
graphs, include isolated and reordered nodes, and exercise each endpoint pair supported by
both source and destination. It must distinguish an absent edge from an edge whose mark is
unknown. It should round-trip every admitted graph, then assert refusal on each unsupported
case. A graph that matches only after sorting internal integer indices has passed a serialization
convenience test, not the label-permutation invariant. Stable identifiers must be explicit and
unique; display names alone may be duplicated or normalized by a library. A source API
keyed by object identity must first resolve each object against the saved node map, before the
graph is serialized.
  This contract also prevents a false interpretation of package conversion helpers. A helper
may be correct for the subset it implements, while a caller uses it outside that subset. The
admission response therefore carries the source graph class, receiver class, translated and
unrepresented marks, node-map digest, and any lost annotations. The downstream effect query
can then refuse to treat a partially represented graph as an identified set. Graph conversion is
not itself causal identification. Even an exact endpoint round-trip preserves only the supplied
graph object, not the assumptions that made the graph scientifically credible.


26.6     Observation clocks and row identity
The row-bootstrap example has an analogue in the design matrix itself. The inspected Tetrad
lag utility creates rows by shifting positions in a data table; its selected method accepts the
dataset and lag count, not a subject ID or physical timestamp. For a bank panel ordered as

                                 (A, t1 ), (A, t2 ), (B, t1 ), (B, t2 ),

a one-row lag assigns the preceding account’s t2 record to account B at t1 . That transition
is not part of either customer’s history. The source method can still be appropriate for one
regularly sampled series, but the port must not silently reuse it on stacked accounts. This
boundary follows from the inspected row construction; it is not a claim that every Tetrad time
series route lacks subject awareness (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026d).
   Before a worker receives a temporal table, the caller must state the observation unit, subject
key, timestamp or ordered event index, gap rule, calendar/irregularity policy, and treatment of
resets and overlapping windows. The adapter must either construct within-subject sequences
under that rule or refuse to create lags. The model clock and inferential sampling unit are
separate fields. A customer is not automatically the sampling unit: uncertainty may instead
resample branches, campaigns, calendar blocks or randomized clusters. Row counts cannot
substitute for either concept.
414                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   For funding, an event ordered at origination cannot be joined to an outcome that occurs
before the funding decision merely because a later table contains it. For servicing, a time-varying
action requires its decision timestamp, available history and censoring or competing-event
status. These are caller scientific inputs; a bridge can check their declared shape and order, but
cannot certify that a timestamp is truthful or an account ID correctly linked. The response
must retain the declared clock and preprocessing map so a reviewer can tell whether a package’s
row position matches the intended bank history.


26.7      Which original should be reused?
The evidence supports a narrow portfolio of original-language references, not one universal
engine. These are prospective route choices based on inspected source, not successful local
builds, matched runtime results or bank validation.
   For latent discovery in R, pcalg is the direct first reference for the selected FCI/RFCI
behavior because the pinned source exposes the search, missing-test, threshold and endpoint-
conversion paths. The proposed route calls a pinned R worker with explicit controls and retains
its diagnostics. The package declares GPL (at least version 2), requires R 3.5 or later, links
Rcpp/RcppArmadillo/BH and imports additional graph packages. Dependency resolution and
distribution rights for the complete environment remain to be checked. A C++ rewrite is not
justified by a wish for one runtime; it first needs an actual deployment constraint and must
pass the trace and endpoint suite (pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024b,a).
   For heterogeneous data, rCausalMGM is a separate R candidate, not a drop-in replacement
for pcalg. Its inspected FCI-Stable documentation specifies a mixed-data initial graph and
orientation options, but also says that rows with missing values are dropped; its selected profile
and assumptions must travel with the response. Its native implementation is wrapped for
R through Rcpp and declares GPL-3 plus Rcpp, survival, BH, Armadillo and RcppThread
requirements. Admit it only for an explicit complete-case target profile until missingness
handling and the exact mixed-data test are separately qualified. It is not a standalone C++
library contract merely because some algorithm code is in C++ (cran/rCausalMGM, 2026).
   MIIC is another distinct model family. The inspected package presents R and C++ sources,
a C++14 compiler requirement, Rcpp, and OpenMP flags delegated to the R build. It declares
GPL (at least version 2) and exposes information theoretic, latent, and stationary temporal
modes. Preserve MIIC as a comparative candidate where its source assumptions and output
semantics match the question; do not translate its ‘latent’ option into a generic PAG or report
its graph as an effect estimate. A direct C++ port is not established by the inspected R
wrapper. Scale and application claims are not measurements of the target banking workload
(miicTeam/miic_R_package, 2026).
   For uplift-style effect estimation in Python, CausalML’s pinned release is a useful original
reference for a selected binary T-learner profile. The root license notice is Apache-2.0, but the
source declares Python 3.11 or later and eighteen direct requirements; transitive dependencies
and deployment rights have not been closed. Keep model fits and row bootstrap inside its
Python worker, carry shared-control fit identity explicitly, and treat learner randomness
separately from the resampling generator. This does not admit dependent account-level
uncertainty, and other estimators do not automatically share this contract. Matching a CATE
column without target rows and shared fit does not preserve the bank contrast (uber/causalml,
2026).
  For Java graph work, pinned Tetrad is a candidate where its graph/search profile is needed
and its GPL/dependency terms are accepted. The selected library POM declares Java release
26.8. An admission contract for each worker                                                    415


21 and a substantial dependency set. The same pinned README describes Python and
R entry routes as new and nonstandard, with a Java 25 requirement. This is a separate
wrapper environment, not a contradiction to resolve by guessing. Invoke one pinned artifact
or one pinned wrapper stack, record which was used, and do not mix them as interchangeable.
Stable node IDs and endpoint marks belong in the request before either path is admitted
(cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026b,c).
   For C++, aGrUM’s native FCI/PAG path is a plausible comparator when deployment
calls for a compiled graph worker. Its inspected traversal, orientation and endpoint methods
identify a distinct implementation profile. The source includes a dual LGPL-3-or-later/MIT
statement for aGrUM, alongside warnings that third-party code has separate copying terms.
The review has not resolved those dependencies, built the pinned library or qualified its PAG
against another implementation. Test the native profile on its own merits through a narrow
adapter; do not claim that the C++ function ports pcalg FCI because both are called FCI
(agrumery/aGrUM, 2026a).
   These choices distinguish three actions often conflated in a software survey: adopt an original
implementation behind its native worker; bind existing components while preserving their
artifacts; or port selected logic only after a measured need and bounded equivalence domain.
Begin with original R and Python workers for selected profiles, keep Tetrad and aGrUM as
cross-check candidates, and retain MIIC and rCausalMGM as distinct discovery families. No
package is rejected as scientifically useless; each is rejected as a universal substitute where the
inspected source supports a narrower claim. Keep native reimplementation deferred until its
benefit exceeds maintenance, validation, rights and migration costs (Causal banking proposal,
2026dc).


26.8      An admission contract for each worker
The proposed boundary is a versioned request/response contract, not a generic claim that
packages can be hidden behind one function. The request names the target population, action
or graph question, outcome and units, information cutoff, observation clock, row and sampling
units, variable ontology, missingness policy, identification assumptions, method controls, seed
sources and coupling, and requested uncertainty object. A source profile adds exact package
and dependency identities, representable graph/effect domain, timeout and resource limits.
Fields absent from a source API must be marked unsupported or applied by a reviewed
pre/postprocessor; they must not be silently ignored.
   The response returns request identity, status, target identity, point or set result, uncertainty
type and sampling law, source/runtime identity, translated node map or fit IDs, diagnostics,
omitted rows/replicates, effective controls and structured refusal. A successful process exit
does not mean a scientific result exists. An empty confidence set, unsupported graph mark,
failed resample, timeout and missing assignment field are distinct outcomes, not null, zero or
an empty list.
   Conformance has five levels. First, schema checks establish request and unit completeness.
Second, exact fixtures establish representations, branch conditions, row maps and unsupported
cases. Third, numeric fixtures test declared tolerances on admitted regular cases. Fourth, ran-
domized outputs are compared under shared-input coupling or a predeclared joint-distribution
comparison. Fifth, the pinned environment is installed, built, restarted and faulted under
recorded resource limits. A pass at one level does not imply a pass at the next. The p-value
tie and shared-control laws are gates for selected levels, not production qualification.
  For adaptive graph search, retain candidate edges, conditioning sets, CI-test status, effective
416                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


threshold and decisions. For effect workers, retain action labels, target rows, fit reuse,
resampling indices, failed replicates and aggregation. For temporal workers, retain pre-lag row
maps and subject/calendar boundaries. Run the same cases through pinned source and bridge.
If the native package cannot expose an intermediate, output-level comparison may still be
possible, but missing diagnostics are a blind spot and cannot support a branch parity claim.
   Freeze acceptance criteria before comparisons. Exact discrete fields and refusal statuses
require exact agreement on the declared domain. Numeric fields need a justified tolerance and
a recorded consequence near decision boundaries. Distributional criteria specify joint quantities
and reference law before draws. Operational criteria include reproducible installation, assigned-
request success, latency, memory, restart and failure accounting. Unsupported requests and
failed calls remain in the denominator. A retry that retains only successful cases cannot inflate
reported availability.
   An evidence manifest pins source release, environment lock, compiler/JDK/R/ Python
versions, build logs, transitive dependency identities, license texts, source-to-output hashes and
exact fixtures. Security and supply-chain review are separate from semantic parity. A notice
does not clear a transitive license, and a process boundary alone does not settle redistribution
rights. Resolved environments and bank deployment terms are missing, so these acceptance
claims remain open.


26.9     A banking consequence of shared computation
Suppose retention must choose between offers A and B against one shared control. Let θbA and
θbB be incremental margins and kA − kB their operational cost difference. The decision uses
                                   b = θb − θb − (k − k ).
                                   ∆     A    B    A   B

The shared control error can cancel in this difference; a port that fits independent controls
discards that covariance. Under the illustrative Rademacher law, the variance is 2 under
a shared fit and 4 under split fits. More directly, the shared law puts probability 1/4 on
a positive contrast difference; the split law puts 5/16 there. These stipulated laws are not
estimates of CausalML. They show why matching marginal means may still change a threshold
or regret decision; exact example and enumeration are recorded separately from upstream
execution (Causal banking proposal, 2026cz).
   If a bridge preserves only marginal CATE vectors, it cannot reconstruct which control fit was
shared or whether joint covariance changed. It must return marginals with a warning or refuse
the paired choice; it must not imply independent errors. First replay a public/generated request
with a shared fit identifier and exact target rows, then examine a predeclared dependent-bank
simulation. Port only if that route changes a decision-relevant measure and the native API
cannot satisfy the operating constraint.
  This provides a falsifiable reason to integrate: preserve one specified bank target and its
uncertainty, not build a unified API for its own sake. Evidence may favor the native worker,
explicit refusal or a narrow port. It does not assume one language or bridge will win (Causal
banking proposal, 2026cy).


26.10      A joint-law boundary for port decisions
The shared-control example gives a decision-relevant reason to retain joint randomness. Let
ZA and ZB denote the two offer scores after subtracting the same control score, and compare
26.11. Composing a numerical bridge across an adaptive calculation                             417


a bridge that independently redraws its control for each offer. Under the finite Rademacher
construction, exhaustive enumeration gives
                                        
                                        1/4
                                        
                                               d = −2,
                  Pr(ZA − ZB = d) =       1/2   d = 0,           (shared control),          (26.6)
                                        
                                        
                                        1/4    d = 2,

and                                   

The total variation distance of these two laws is 1/8, and the probabilities of a strictly positive
difference are 1/4 and 5/16. A bridge can therefore change the probability of selecting A
even though both individual offer contrasts have the same marginal variance. These are exact
authored laws, not a variance estimate or an execution of CausalML (Causal banking proposal,
2026db).
  The corresponding numerical rule is also local to a declared decision. If a source score s and
replacement score se satisfy |se − s| ≤ ϵ, then a threshold decision agrees whenever |s − c| > ϵ.
At equality the bound cannot certify the branch. For a finite action set with source values va ,
replacement errors bounded by ϵa , the source maximizer a∗ remains selected when

                                  va∗ − max∗ va > ϵa∗ + max∗ ϵa .                           (26.8)
                                        a̸=a              a̸=a

Without that gap, the replacement may choose a different action; its regret is nevertheless
bounded by 2ϵmax under a uniform error bound. This makes a porting claim testable at the
level of the bank decision rather than at an arbitrary number of decimal places. A result close
to the boundary must carry the interval or return an indeterminate-selection status.
   For a language bridge, the finite law and the deterministic gap rule form two different
admission tests. The first asks whether shared inputs, fit objects and resampling units preserve
a joint output law. The second asks whether a known numerical discrepancy can alter a
selected action. Passing one does not repair the other. The protocol should report both,
together with the source population, output status and refusal boundary. A bridge that cannot
expose shared-fit identity can still return marginal estimates, but it cannot claim the paired
offer decision is equivalent. Likewise, a graph endpoint map that rounds a near-threshold
p-value cannot call an adaptive search path identical without the trace and margin evidence
above.
   The extension narrows the proposed integration decision. Native workers remain the default
when they satisfy the declared profile. A port earns a trial only when its operational constraint
is demonstrated, its admitted domain is bounded, its exact and joint-law fixtures pass, and
its decision-boundary errors are disclosed. Otherwise the scientifically correct output is a
refusal or a native-worker recommendation. No software count or common API can replace
this evidence (Causal banking proposal, 2026cy,dc).


26.11      Composing a numerical bridge across an adaptive calcu-
           lation
The decision to port one routine becomes more demanding when its output is an input to
the next routine. Consider a servicing analysis that transforms observations, fits an outcome
418                                                                   Causal analysis for a universal bank


model, evaluates an offer contrast, and uses that contrast to choose a subsequent diagnostic.
Comparing only the final mean discards the mechanism by which a small arithmetic difference
can change the diagnostic selected. Conversely, requiring identical machine bytes at every
stage can reject a useful implementation without showing any difference in the decision. A
proposal for a bridge needs a compositional statement between these extremes. The following
constructions are project derivations; their exact finite references do not execute an upstream
causal package (Causal banking proposal, 2026da).
   First fix the scientific input and a particular sequence of branches. Let the source states
satisfy zi = fi (zi−1 ), for i = 1, . . . , m, and let the decoded bridge states be zei = fei (zei−1 ). A
state includes the quantities needed by later stages, not merely the displayed estimate. All
norms and units below must be specified: a bound on a probability cannot be inserted as if it
were a bound on a monetary contrast. Suppose both states remain in a declared domain Di−1 ,
the source map has Lipschitz constant Li there, and the bridge has a uniform local discrepancy
∥fei (z) − fi (z)∥ ≤ ϵi for z ∈ Di−1 . If ∥ze0 − z0 ∥ ≤ e0 , the triangle inequality gives
                                                              m
                                                              Y            m
                                                                           X           m
                                                                                       Y
                  ei = Li ei−1 + ϵi ,      ∥zem − zm ∥ ≤ e0         Li +         ϵi           Lj .    (26.9)
                                                              i=1          i=1        j=i+1

The empty product is one. The proof proceeds by comparing fei (zei−1 ) first with fi (zei−1 ), then
with fi (zi−1 ). Induction proves the recursion and its expanded form. The domain condition
is substantive. A source trajectory inside a well-conditioned region does not show that its
perturbed trajectory stays there. The implementation needs a containing domain or an explicit
failure when the next enclosure leaves it.
   For a transparent arithmetic example, take z0 = 0.12, f1 (z) = 2z + 1 and f2 (z) = z/10. The
source result is 0.124. Let input discrepancy be at most 0.001, stage-one error at most 0.002,
and stage-two error at most 0.0001. The composed bound is 0.0005, attained when these three
errors have the positive sign. Simply adding the three error allowances gives a different and
less informative quantity because it ignores amplification and contraction. These constants
are stipulated for the example. They are not certificates for a learner, a matrix inverse or a
floating-point library.
  An adaptive search adds a second obligation. Suppose stage i branches on gi (zi−1 ) ≥ ci ,
where the source comparison function has Lipschitz constant Mi and the bridge’s direct
comparison error is at most ηi . The common branch is certified only if
                                    |gi (zi−1 ) − ci | > Mi ei−1 + ηi .                              (26.10)
This condition must be applied inductively on the actual common history. After an uncertified
branch, the two runs can ask different questions, so the next same-function comparison may
not exist. One cannot continue adding local errors as if the branch sequence had remained
fixed. The appropriate output is a set of possible paths, a return to the original engine, or a
declared lack of equivalence. Equality at the boundary also requires preserving the source’s
strict or non-strict comparison convention.
  This distinction matters for discovery because a conditional-independence decision determines
which later conditioning sets are inspected. It also matters for model selection: an apparently
negligible change in a diagnostic can select a different learner with a different uncertainty
construction. For these cases a useful porting experiment retains the intermediate state
enclosures and branch margins. Comparing final graphs without these traces does not explain
why agreement occurred, while a differing graph does not by itself identify an arithmetic defect.
The source may itself be close to a decision boundary. The reuse choice should therefore
depend on a declared profile of stable paths, not a promise that all data admit the same
numerical certificate.
26.12. Conditional laws, hidden state and adaptive calls                                         419


26.12       Conditional laws, hidden state and adaptive calls
Randomized software requires a statement about the law of a sequence of calls. Let Hi =
(X1 , . . . , Xi ) be the decoded history after call i, including statuses, fitted-object identities,
branch choices and any persistent random state needed by the next call. On finite state
spaces write Ki (x | h) and K    fi (x | h) for the source and bridge conditional distributions of
the next result given the same history h. If the initial histories have the same law and every
reachable conditional kernel agrees, multiplication of conditional probabilities gives the same
joint path law. Equality of one-call marginals is insufficient because it does not determine
these conditional probabilities.
   For example, a source draws one fair bit B and returns (B, B) in two related calls. A bridge
starts a fresh worker for each call and returns two independent fair bits. Each call has the
same marginal distribution. The source returns agreeing bits with probability one; the bridge
does so with probability one half. Direct enumeration gives joint total variation distance 1/2.
The missing state is the shared bit. The analogy in a bank analysis is a fitted control model or
common bootstrap draw that must be reused across offer contrasts. Assigning a seed to each
request is not enough if the definition of a request has silently split a shared computation.
  For approximate kernels define δi = suph 12 x |Ki (x | h) − K  fi (x | h)|, where the supremum
                                                 P

covers all common histories reachable while comparing the two implementations. On a given
common history, the distributions can be paired so that they return the same value with
probability x min{Ki (x | h), Kfi (x | h)}, at least 1 − δi . Put their common masses together,
             P

then distribute the residual masses to complete this pairing. Repeating this construction until
the first disagreement yields

The first inequality follows because every event has the same indicator when the coupled paths
agree. The second follows by expanding the probability of at least one disagreement. This is a
sufficient bound, often conservative; it does not assert that a measured discrepancy in a few
requests bounds the supremum over histories. If the initial laws differ, an additional initial
coupling factor is needed.
   Adaptive stopping fits the same argument when the horizon is bounded in advance. Add a
stopped state that repeats itself through the remaining calls, and include the stopping decision
in the kernel. A cap on conditioning-set size or on iterations then has an explicit role. With
an unbounded horizon, one additionally needs a summable error allocation or a controlled
tail for the number of calls. Stopping after apparently favorable numerical results cannot be
justified by applying a fixed-horizon bound only to completed paths.
   The path bound and the arithmetic bound answer different questions. Tiny shifts of
continuous numerical outputs can have disjoint point masses and total variation one even
when their metric distance is tiny. For continuous states, one can instead couple numerical
discrepancies in a specified metric and use the margin condition to certify a common discrete
branch. To bound the probability of a branch error, one must supply the probability mass
within the relevant margin and the probability that the arithmetic certificate fails. A density
or margin bound is an extra assumption, not a consequence of observing a small error on
one input. Thus the proposal should retain both the numerical enclosure and the conditional
law of the discrete choices, using each only on the domain where its assumptions have been
established.

26.13       When retries select a different statistical result
A language bridge can preserve every successful arithmetic call and still change the reported
statistical law through its failure policy. Fix one scientific request. Let Y denote the result that
an ideal computation with random input would produce, with law P . Let S indicate whether
that attempt completes and returns a usable result, and write q(y) = Pr(S = 1 | Y = y). This
representation does not assume a failed attempt actually calculated or logged its      R

It describes the joint law required to reason about selection. Assume 0 < q̄ = q(y)P (dy).
Among successful attempts the reported law is

or zero covariance for that particular mean. Zero covariance does not establish equality of
whole distributions.

independent-attempt premise itself fails.

Completed results are weighted by qK , not by q. If q(y) > 0 almost surely, this selection
vanishes as K grows without limit, although expected cost can be unbounded. If q(y) = 0 on a
positive-mass region, those results never appear. Retaining a seed cannot repair a deterministic
lack of memory, an unsupported data type or a nonterminating algorithm. Even conditional
independence can be inappropriate when retrying retains the same defective process state.
   Take a stipulated score error Y ∈ {−1, 1} with equal probabilities, q(−1) = 1/4, and
q(1) = 1. This is a selection example, not an empirical claim about causal software. With two
attempts, exhaustive enumeration of signs and four equally likely operational states gives

       Procedure                    Completion Pr(Y = 1 | return) Returned mean
