qualification needs the chosen edition, licensed environment, actual execution and complete
prices; later bank acceptance needs authentic bank questions, truth and owners. The proposed
contract supplies a concrete route for those stages while preserving uncertainty about their
outcomes. It does not establish that any sibling repository or commercial platform has already
adopted the causal library.


39.9     Scenario controls must preserve a fixed scientific workload
The previous orchestration comparison motivates a closer question for a nightly bank offer
analysis: which requested effects survive a partly failed scenario? Dataiku’s detailed official
manuals describe useful controls for handling failures, testing a flow and initiating another run.
Their current technical text supports a more precise comparison than an index of scenario
features. The observations below concern the saved DSS 15 and DSS 14 manuals acquired
after the 7 October 2026 cutoff. They establish documented mechanisms, with the historical
qualification developed below; they do not establish an executed adapter or an exhaustive
account of the product. (Dataiku, 2026d,g,f,b)


39.9.1    A tolerated operating error leaves a scientific question

The step-control manual specifies sequential execution until the first failure or completion
of all steps. Some steps, including Build/train, can downgrade an error to a warning and
let later steps run. An example uses Ignore failure when attempting to kill another scenario.
Individual steps can be disabled with Never, run with Always regardless of previous failures, or
use conditions on earlier failures, the current outcome or variables. The documented scenario
outcomes are SUCCESS, WARNING, FAILED and ABORTED. These distinctions are useful:
cleanup can still run after a failure, and a later diagnostic need not be lost. They leave the
application responsible for deciding whether its requested causal effects have actually been
returned. (Dataiku, 2026d,b)
   Let Q be the declared set of cohort requests, wq their fixed population weights with
P
  q∈Q wq = 1, τq the cohort’s mean potential-outcome contrast between contact and no contact,
and cq the incremental cost of contacting a member. The declared all-contact policy has
incremental net value, in dollars per member,
                                            X
                                     VQ =         wq (τq − cq ).                                (39.5)
                                            q∈Q

For the following exact authored construction, cohort effects are stipulated truth, not estimates
whose identification or precision has been established. There are two equal-weight cohorts,
39.9. Scenario controls must preserve a fixed scientific workload                               661


with τA = 10, τB = −30 and cA = cB = 1. No contact has zero incremental value and cost.
Thus
                         VQ = 21 (10 − 1) + 12 (−30 − 1) = −11.                  (39.6)
If the effect for cohort B is missing after a failed or skipped step, averaging the available cohort
instead reports Vavailable = 9. The apparent improvement of 20 dollars comes from changing
the population. It reverses the financial sign without any sampling noise. A tolerated error
that leaves the same effect missing creates the same arithmetic problem. These are constructed
missing-output illustrations; they are not recorded Dataiku run outcomes. (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026bs)
  The proposed scientific ledger keeps two requested effects and one returned effect in every
such illustration. It retains the failure, skip or tolerated error as a distinct disposition, the
declared weights and the missing result. It can describe the available cohort’s value for that
cohort, but cannot rename it the original population value. Assigning zero to a missing effect
would add a substantive assumption. Even renormalizing costs to the returned cohort would
change the all-contact policy being evaluated.
   An explicit range can communicate a limited answer. If a separate substantive argument
justifies τB ∈ [−50, 50], with cohort A’s effect and the costs still stipulated, the original target
obeys
                                   VQ = 4 + 21 τB ∈ [−21, 29].                                (39.7)
This identified set follows from assumed bounds, rather than statistical confidence. It gives no
guarantee of a positive net return. The route to a sharper answer is to recover the missing
effect, defend tighter bounds or declare a different policy and population explicitly. Reporting
only the successful cohort cannot supply the lost information. (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026bs)

39.9.2     A trigger observes its rule, not a complete causal snapshot

The trigger manual distinguishes initiation from execution. Several active triggers are evaluated
independently; any true condition can promote a scenario for execution, which need not start
immediately. For filesystem datasets, change detection uses filenames, lengths and modification
times, with an optional marker file. A dataset-change trigger does not detect SQL data changes;
a SQL-query trigger compares the query’s output. The suggested row count or maximum-
column query is a useful proxy, whose adequacy depends on the scientific request.(Dataiku,
2026g)
  For example, two fixed records can retain both row count and maximum date while cohort
B’s stored contrast changes from −30 to 30. In the same stipulated equal-weight population,
net value then changes from −11 to 19. A count-and-maximum-date proxy cannot distinguish
these two tables. This is a logical counterexample for that chosen query, rather than a claim
that SQL triggers cannot use a stronger query or that the platform loses changes. The proposed
adapter should bind the relevant data snapshot and information clock, with a change rule
appropriate to those dependencies. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026bs)
  By default, Suppress triggers while running is enabled: a second trigger can go unevaluated
during a long run. If suppression is disabled, an evaluation finishing while the scenario is still
running is ignored. For eligible tracked events, the manual describes disabling suppression,
enabling Delay runs and disabling Squash delayed runs to retain a run per trigger. It also warns
that serial scenarios accumulate delayed runs if arrival throughput exceeds service throughput.
Squashing limits the delayed queue to at most one run and can cancel an intermediate run.
Time-based, manual and hidden Run another scenario triggers are excluded from run delaying.
(Dataiku, 2026g)
662                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


  These controls support different operational objectives. A latest-snapshot analysis may
deliberately combine changes, whereas a predeclared event study may need every eligible event
and its clock. The latter requires a durable event/request record and reconciliation against
the declared workload. Trigger counts alone cannot certify that denominator, and every raw
data change need not be a scientific event. The application must define the relationship
before choosing suppression or squashing. This is a proposed contract to qualify, rather than
demonstrated event completeness.


39.9.3    Existing tests help define a bounded integration experiment

The scenario-step manual documents checks and data-quality rules: the step fails when at
least one selected check fails, and rule outcomes become variables for later steps. It also
documents project pytest selection and a flow integration test that swaps in stable reference
inputs, rebuilds outputs and compares them with reference datasets. These mechanisms
could support a prototype comparison using public or generated data. A causal extension
would need reference targets, weights, information clocks, refusals and uncertainty alongside
ordinary output comparisons; the documentation does not show that such an extension has
been executed. (Dataiku, 2026f)
   Run another scenario waits for completion and takes the child’s outcome. The manual says
the initiating step’s user is used regardless of the child scenario’s Run as setting. A proposed
adapter must therefore preserve the observed run identity together with the scientific request,
then test the relevant configuration. This narrow documented behavior does not establish the
whole authorization model. Similarly, a Clear step deletes dataset or folder contents; persistent
scientific evidence must have its own deliberate retention arrangement.(Dataiku, 2026f)
   The economical next experiment is a small fixed manifest containing complete, failed,
skipped and tolerated-without-effect requests. Check the returned scientific ledger, weights
and source identities before measuring retries or runtime. Pair this with two data versions
that share a selected trigger proxy but differ in a scientific dependency. A successful native
experiment would support only its frozen release, configuration and manifest. Its merit should
be established with public/generated inputs before purchasing a large bank study. No native
execution, licensed entitlement or measured commercial cost is asserted here.


39.9.4    The cutoff requires a patch identity, not just a major version

The current release index lists DSS 15.0.0 on 14 August 2026 and DSS 15.0.2 on 24 September
2026, both before the client cutoff. It lists DSS 15.1.0 on 8 October and DSS 15.2.0 on 15
October, both later. DSS 15 therefore cannot be dismissed as entirely post-cutoff. Equally, its
current major-version manual cannot silently stand for the exact 15.0.2 technical bytes. The
DSS 14 release index lists 14.7.5 on 24 September. Its inspected step-control body matches
the DSS 15 body, which supports a current textual comparison but does not authenticate the
historical patch revision. (Dataiku, 2026e,c,d,b)
   Release-index headings for Agent Skills and MCP server do not establish their detailed
behavior. Those claims need the relevant primary technical text and edition. The detailed
scenario review narrows one earlier source omission; exact cutoff originals for the selected
commercial manuals, SAS Viya, Domino, Posit and complementary market coverage remain
to be investigated. Rights, prices and native qualification remain separate questions. This
comparison supports reuse of documented orchestration mechanisms as candidates, while
requiring an explicit scientific workload before an integration is accepted.
39.10. Commercial execution platforms and open client contracts                              663


39.10      Commercial execution platforms and open client con-
           tracts
A bank’s overnight causal analysis may run in an established execution platform while its
scientific meaning remains the responsibility of the proposed library. A useful commercial
comparison therefore follows the actual boundary: submission, observation of a remote job,
interpretation of its terminal state, recovery and custody of its outputs. The open clients
supplied by SAS, Domino and Posit reveal concrete integration choices. Their selected source
revisions precede 7 October 2026. They authenticate client and SDK behavior visible in source,
not every feature of a licensed server, a supported deployment combination, or a successful
native trial. (SAS Institute, 2026h; Domino Data Lab, 2026; Posit PBC, 2026a,b)


39.10.1    Completion is one coordinate of a scientific result

Let q denote an immutable scientific request, a a run attempt, v a code revision, d a data
snapshot and e an execution environment. The requested result has a declared estimand,
population, information time and assumptions. An execution record is a different object: it
says which attempt ran which inputs, whether it terminated, and which artifacts it produced.
A proposed acceptance rule can make these requirements explicit:

                       A(q, a) = T (a) S(a) B(q, a, v, d, e) E(a) C(q, ra ),              (39.8)

where each factor is a zero–one indicator. Here T means terminal, S means an allowed
successful execution state, B means a verified binding between request and execution identities,
E means the required result artifacts ra exist, and C means the result passes the stated
scientific contract. The last factor may require an explicit nonidentification or refusal result;
a numerical effect need not exist for every valid request. These are proposed application
semantics, not a claim that a vendor implements this particular rule. A successful process exit
supplies evidence for only part of the conjunction.
   This distinction matters even when all arithmetic is exact. Suppose a funding decision has
a stipulated incremental response coefficient bv , capital exposure of USD 1,000 and cost of
USD 20. For two revisions that encode different supplied assumptions, take b0 = 3/100 and
b1 = 4/100. Their net values are

                V0 = 1000(3/100) − 20 = 10,         V1 = 1000(4/100) − 20 = 20.           (39.9)

Both calculations can exit successfully. Substituting the second revision while describing the
run as a replay of the first changes the answer by USD 10. This is an authored identity
example with stipulated coefficients, not an estimated causal effect or a measured vendor
failure. Recording a code commit alone also leaves the data snapshot, configuration, dependency
versions and randomization state to be specified. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ch)


39.10.2    Domino: versioned restart and distinct polling predicates

The selected Domino Python client exposes useful controls for this boundary. Its job submission
payload includes a commit identifier, main-repository Git reference, environment identifier
and hardware selection. Its restart method defaults to requesting the original input commit;
the alternative requests the current version. The stop method separately accepts a flag asking
to commit results. These are meaningful strengths for controlled experimentation, but the
selected client source does not establish complete data and environment immutability or the
licensed server’s interpretation of every field. (Domino Data Lab, 2026)
664                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Two polling interfaces in the same source have different visible predicates. The legacy
blocking run helper resets its consecutive status-read retry count after a successful read. It
waits for an output commit and then requires the reported status to be Succeeded. The
newer blocking job helper raises on executionStatus == Failed and passes isCompleted
to the polling library as its success predicate. Its defaults specify a five-second poll interval
and a 6,000-second polling timeout, with selected request exceptions ignored during polling.
(Domino Data Lab, 2026)
   These observations justify a precise question rather than an accusation of a product defect.
A supplied hypothetical response whose completion flag is true and whose execution status
is neither Failed nor Succeeded satisfies the newer local predicate. It would fail a proposed
explicit Succeeded allowlist. This is a logical witness about the inspected expression; it does
not show that the server actually emits such a response. Resolving that question needs the
supported server state schema and its version. An adapter should preserve both fields, the
raw response, job identity and output binding until the mapping is justified. It must also
distinguish failure to observe a job before the deadline from proof that the remote job has
stopped. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026ch; Domino Data Lab, 2026)
  For the proposal, the preferred route is a narrow client wrapper that keeps Domino’s
execution and revision controls and adds the scientific request contract. Reimplementing the
entire scheduler has no demonstrated advantage. The wrapper remains a proposed integration:
supported API routes, exception mapping, actual terminal states, output custody and fault
behavior still need their own inspection and registered public or synthetic trials.


39.10.3     Posit Connect: tasks, jobs and schedules have different meanings

The inspected R client declares development version 0.12.1.9000. Its task object normalizes
an incoming identifier when necessary. The poll_task implementation waits for the task’s
finished field, checks the final numeric code, raises on nonzero code and attaches an optional
result to the task object. The function exposes a wait interval but no overall deadline parameter.
This describes the local function signature and loop, not the absence of time limits elsewhere
in the server or transport. An integrating worker should impose an explicit observation budget
and retain the remote task identity for reconciliation. (Posit PBC, 2026a)
   Job records carry additional context: content and bundle identifiers, start and end times,
execution status, exit code and, where available, cluster and image information. The selected
documentation distinguishes Active, Finished and Finalized on newer servers and identifies
missing fields on versions earlier than 2022.10.0. The implementation also normalizes older
timestamp and identifier representations. A consumer must not treat missing historical fields
as verified empty values or infer a successful scientific result from the label Finished. A bundle
identifier is useful provenance, but its mapping to the request’s code, data and configuration
still needs evidence. (Posit PBC, 2026a)
   Scheduling adds another boundary. The inspected schedule-update method is marked
experimental, converts start and next-run times and calls unversioned schedule endpoints.
Thus the R package’s source commit, the server API behavior and the schedule’s information
clock are separate versioning questions. In banking, a job scheduled after a ledger cutoff must
not quietly use records first available after the intended decision time. The proposed adapter
should preserve that time explicitly and reject ambiguous timestamp conversion. This is an
application requirement, not a finding that Posit violates it. (Posit PBC, 2026a)
   The R client is therefore a plausible integration route for R-based estimation and reporting.
Its task, job and schedule objects should remain distinct in the library/CLI/MCP contract.
Porting the client wholesale to another language would add an API-maintenance obligation
39.10. Commercial execution platforms and open client contracts                                665


without yet proving better scientific fidelity. A worker boundary with typed results is the more
limited candidate to test first.


39.10.4     Posit Launcher: reuse the scheduler boundary with explicit state

The Launcher Go SDK addresses a different layer. Its official guide describes a plugin connecting
Workbench or Connect to a scheduler using length-prefixed JSON over standard input and
output. Bootstrap reconciles current jobs, heartbeats detect an unresponsive plugin, and
multiple Launcher instances require a common view of job state. The guide gives Go and
product-version prerequisites. These are documented design contracts of the pinned SDK;
they are not a measured availability or recovery guarantee. (Posit PBC, 2026b)
   The testing guide offers a useful structure for proposed qualification. It separates universal
invariants, product request sequences and individual control scenarios. Examples cover
nonempty job identifiers, distinct IDs for two submissions, retrieval and filtering, terminal-state
nonregression, launch, stop, kill and cancel. Profiles allow scheduler-specific terminal states
and exit codes; unsupported suspend/resume can be skipped. An integration must interpret
the selected profile and skipped cases rather than collapse the entire suite to one portable
success claim. These tests are documented upstream facilities; no passing execution is asserted
here. (Posit PBC, 2026b)
   For a bank with an accepted scheduler, adopting this bridge boundary is more plausible than
reproducing an execution platform inside a causal library. The library would still own causal
request identity and result validation. The platform would own job dispatch and resource
management. A prototype comparison should test stale state after restart, duplicate submission,
status-stream interruption and missing output, including the cost of state reconciliation. A
failed bootstrap or missing shared state must remain visible as an operating failure, not be
translated into a zero causal effect.


39.10.5     SAS: preserve experimental scope and explicit timeout outcomes

The sasctl project exposes Python module and command-line access to SAS Viya. Its selected
Workflow class states that its partial implementation is experimental and can change without
notice. The comment refers to the documentation situation in September 2022; it does not
establish whether public workflow documentation exists at the proposal cutoff. Submission
selects an enabled definition, maps supplied values to declared prompts and includes their
declared types and versions. Naive datetime values are converted using local timezone when
possible, with a UTC fallback if they remain naive. A banking adapter should require an explicit
timezone before submission rather than let the worker host silently define the information
clock. (SAS Institute, 2026h)
   A separate score-execution method exposes another concrete control issue. It returns the
strings completed or failed on those reported states. Its timeout test is inside the polling loop,
while the loop guard itself limits elapsed time; there is no explicit return after the loop. A
supplied zero timeout therefore skips the body and reaches Python’s implicit None return. For
a positive budget, the timeout branch can be reached if time crosses the threshold during an
iteration, but a later failed loop guard can also end the loop without that explicit timeout
result. This is source-level control-flow reasoning, not a timed experiment against SAS. (SAS
Institute, 2026h; Causal banking proposal project, 2026ch)
   The proposed wrapper should validate a positive observation budget, normalize all completion
paths into typed states, retain execution identity and logs, and require a separately verified
result binding. An unrecognized or absent polling return is an unresolved observation, not
666                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


permission to use stale scores. Reusing the open client selectively is a candidate; depending
on its experimental workflow service without versioned qualification is not yet a supported
product commitment.


39.10.6    Retries, rights and a costed prototype choice

Recovery can change value when a retry repeats a charge or an externally visible action. In an
exact illustrative servicing example, suppose one useful contact produces a stipulated USD 12
gain and every attempted delivery incurs USD 7. If there is at most one useful gain, net value
after n charged attempts is

                       V (n) = 12 − 7n,     V (1) = 5,     V (2) = −2.                   (39.10)

The sign changes solely because of the assumed duplicate cost. A repeated analysis job need
not incur this contact cost; the example concerns a workflow that crosses into a paid or
externally visible action. It motivates separate request and attempt identities, reconciliation
before resubmission and an idempotency key at the side-effect boundary. It establishes no
vendor failure rate, bank return or economic superiority. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026ch)
   The selected connectapi license is MIT; the Launcher root license provides an MIT-style
grant unless supplied under a commercial agreement. The Domino and sasctl client roots
include Apache 2.0 texts. These source licenses are relevant to proposed client reuse. They do
not supply an entitlement to a commercial server, a supported edition, a complete dependency-
rights review or a price. Consequently the commercial comparison should price an actual
deployment and support arrangement separately from the open wrapper. (Posit PBC, 2026a,b;
Domino Data Lab, 2026; SAS Institute, 2026h)
   The practical proposal is to compare narrow wrappers around established execution services
using the same public or synthetic scientific workload. Record installation and maintenance
effort, queue and compute time, output validation, failed attempts, recovery and any billed
actions. Preserve every requested case in the denominator. Qualify client and server versions,
explicit failure states, output custody and clock semantics before drawing an economic conclu-
sion. Historical Dataiku technical-version gaps and wider market coverage remain separate
survey obligations; these four inspected profiles neither establish market completeness nor
erase those limits.
Chapter 40

What language models contribute to
causal knowledge

40.1     Four different objects called causal reasoning
A banker asking why deposit balances fell can be asking for an explanation of a recorded event,
an estimate of a feasible rate intervention, a prediction of next month’s balance, or a diagnosis
of an observation error. A fluent answer can move between these objects without announcing
the change. The useful starting point for evaluating language assistance is therefore the object
being produced: a proposed scientific question, evidence about a causal model, a formal
calculation conditional on that model, or a recommendation under a specified loss. Success at
one object supplies no automatic guarantee for the others.
   The early frontier argument proposes using language models to organize domain knowledge,
draft graphs, critique assumptions and suggest robustness analyses. It also records the ability
to reproduce recognizable public data and distinguishes transforming known information
from discovering a new causal structure.Kıcıman et al. (2023) This distinction is particularly
consequential in banking. A familiar statement about interest rates can be useful prior
knowledge, but the effect of a particular bank’s deposit offer depends on its population,
competitors, eligibility rules and information clock. A remembered relationship does not
determine that intervention effect.
   Formal benchmarks introduce a second object. CLadder constructs questions from known
causal structures with different verbalizations. Its results concern answers to those generated
questions, including historically specified models and prompting methods.Jin et al. (2023)
Such a benchmark can reveal failures to distinguish observation from intervention. It cannot
establish that a model elicits the right variables from an unfamiliar bank process, measures
them correctly, or returns calibrated uncertainty after fitting to dependent data. These are
additional stages of the proposed product.
   Third, a language model can propose a causal mechanism for numerical analysis. Model
Discovery Agent illustrates a separation between executable mechanism proposals and numerical
fitting, evidence approximation and experiment design. Its finite predictive evaluations
explicitly do not establish causal identification.Murphy (2026) A mechanism may predict well
because several observationally equivalent models predict equally well. The bank must still
justify which intervention the model represents and which new experiment would distinguish
economically different mechanisms.
  Finally, workflow assistance concerns selection and coordination of established operations.
Causal-learn+ describes assistance with diagnosis, assumptions, method selection and inter-

                                              667
668                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


pretation while retaining algorithm outputs and graph ambiguity.Zheng (2026) This is a useful
architectural direction. It changes the analyst’s interaction with numerical tools; it does not
make a method’s premises true. The following chapters keep these four contributions separate
while studying how they can work together.


40.2      Text supplies a different information channel
Write D for the observed numerical records, K for inspected documentary or expert evidence,
and M(D, K) for the models consistent with the declared interpretation of both. For target
ψ, a set-valued answer is

                             Ψ(D, K) = {ψ(M ) : M ∈ M(D, K)}.

This notation does not assert that finite data identify the population law or that a statistical
confidence procedure has been supplied. It describes which models the analysis intends to
consider. Statistical uncertainty about the law must subsequently be propagated through the
model set.
  Additional reliable knowledge may exclude a model that the observed distribution alone
cannot exclude. A contract establishing that an invitation was randomized, for example,
has a different evidential role from a predictive correlation. But a model-generated sentence
repeating that randomization is common practice does not establish what happened in the
bank’s historical process. The analysis must identify the original source, the relevant population
and dates, the interpretation of its claim, and the person or measurement that supports it.
   This also explains why retrieving more documents need not improve discovery. LACR
combines background knowledge, retrieved documents and optional numerical information,
and includes an UNKNOWN response. Its reported retrieval effects differ across benchmarks,
with adverse as well as favorable outcomes. Zhang et al. (2024b) Retrieval changes K; it does
not certify K. Documents may concern a different treatment definition, contain an association
stated as a cause, or duplicate the same original assertion. Ten repeated documents are not
ten independent confirmations of an edge.
   An appropriate evidence object therefore retains the claim, source passage, date, domain,
units and proposed role. A passage may justify a variable definition without justifying an
arrow. A process document may establish that one action occurs before another without
excluding a common cause. A source about another bank may suggest a hypothesis while
leaving transport assumptions unresolved. These roles determine the strength with which K
can restrict the model class.


40.3     Discovery methods use language judgments in different
         ways
Three broad routes recur in the inspected literature: direct graph or relation prediction,
refinement of numerical discoveries, and priors or constraints used within a search.Wan et al.
(2024) The distinction matters because it locates where a wrong assertion enters the calculation.
   In direct conditional-independence elicitation, chatPC obtains language-model judgments
from descriptions and context. Its statistical calculation concerns the proportion of YES/NO
model responses.Cohrs et al. (2024) Repeated answers can measure response variability under
a prompt. Without a separate argument, they are not repeated draws of the bank variables
40.4. Temporal discovery is not a change of vocabulary                                       669


and do not yield a sampling test of independence in the bank population. A highly stable
wrong answer can therefore be more dangerous than a visibly variable one.
   Soft guidance provides a different failure boundary. The inspected CD-UCT method
combines language and mutual-information scores to guide graph search without excluding
otherwise valid DAGs. Language-only priors are not uniformly beneficial in its reported
comparisons.Darvariu et al. (2024) Ancestral-path constraints can likewise enter through a
soft log-prior penalty, with reported degradation under inaccurate prior information.Ban et al.
(2023) Softness leaves room for the numerical criterion to resist the suggestion, but it does not
establish that the final graph probabilities are calibrated.
   Hard restrictions can be scientifically appropriate when backed by a genuine design fact.
They are more consequential when inferred from prose: deleting a candidate model deletes
every effect value that only that model permits. Statistical Causal Prompting converts model
outputs into forced, forbidden or unknown prior knowledge using method-specific mappings.
The inspected examples include failures as well as improvements.Takayama et al. (2024) The
interface must expose both the original assertion and the conversion rule, so a reviewer can
determine whether a numerical threshold has quietly become a scientific exclusion.
   Noisy language priors can also guide a sequential allocation of questions over edges while
retaining PAG representations.Verma et al. (2025) This is closer to a budgeted information
problem than to asking for a finished graph in one prompt. Its relevance to a bank still depends
on whether the supplied knowledge applies to the observed regime, whether latent structure is
represented correctly, and whether the retained ambiguity survives into the effect query.


40.4      Temporal discovery is not a change of vocabulary
A statement that collections activity affects arrears omits the action time, available history,
response horizon and possible feedback. Expanding a variable name into a paragraph does not
supply these missing indices. A temporal graph needs explicit time labels and a rule governing
contemporaneous edges, lag limits, hidden histories, stationarity and interventions.
   RealTCD combines a language-derived initial adjacency with numerical score optimization
over temporal graphs and intervention targets. Its setup includes causal sufficiency, a known
observational regime, finite lag and a DAG on unrolled variables; its identification statement
has further stated premises. The inspected real-system assessment lacks a ground-truth DAG
and evaluates selected relationships through expert rules.Li (2024) These qualifications prevent
a graph score from being read as a general guarantee for a bank’s latent, irregularly observed
time series.
   The Large Causal Models work is an adjacent numerical foundation-model route, not
simply a conversational language-model interface. The inspected model assumes additive
noise, stationarity, no latent confounders and no contemporaneous effects, and does not detect
or correct violations of these assumptions.Kougioulis et al. (2026) Distinguishing the two
routes avoids treating the shared word “model” as a common scientific contract. One supplies
semantic proposals; the other learns a temporal mapping under a training distribution and
structural restrictions. Either can be useful within its declared regime.
   For sequential servicing, a credible workflow starts with the decision history and feasible
intervention. It then asks whether the discovery output expresses the required variables and
whether a policy effect is identified over every retained graph. An automatically generated
lagged graph cannot resolve unrecorded private information merely by assigning it a latent-node
name.
670                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


40.5     Interactive systems and agents add a review problem
CausalChat combines graph suggestions, user editing and numerical updates. Its small nonex-
pert study uses a fixed sequence of interfaces. Zhang (2024) Such evidence can motivate better
interfaces, but it does not isolate every learning, ordering or expertise effect. The proposed
bank evaluation needs qualified reviewers, an explicit task distribution and a comparison that
records the time and information supplied by people.
  Debating agents provide another review structure. MAC uses affirmative, negative and
judge roles; its inspected comparisons also report a competitive single-agent route for simpler
graphs at lower cost.Le et al. (2024) Several personas can share the same mistaken premise or
model knowledge. Agreement among them is not automatically independent corroboration.
Their usefulness should be measured through detected errors, retained correct alternatives,
decision consequences and total cost.
   The oci-agent study instead emphasizes an accountable human principal over actor/critic
workflows and deterministic causal libraries. Its critic can decline analyses with poor over-
lap.Chou et al. (2026) The relevant outcome then includes correct refusal and what remains
possible for the requested population. Reporting only completed analyses would hide precisely
the difficult cases in which an agent’s judgment matters most.
   An evidence-auditing agent faces a similar boundary. ARGUS audits reported support
for assumptions rather than adjudicating their truth. Its retrieval and abstention tradeoffs
and small human-label pilot leave substantial generalization questions.Zhang et al. (2026a)
In banking, an omitted document, a contradicted assumption and an assumption whose
truth is unknown require different responses. A documentation score should not become an
identification certificate.


40.6     An evidence standard for the proposed banking product
The synthesis supports a modular research program. Language assistance proposes questions,
variables, graph alternatives and evidence links. Formal operations check declared structures
and calculate identified functionals or sets in supported regimes. Numerical procedures estimate
those objects with their own sampling and approximation arguments. Human and institutional
evidence supply facts about assignment, ownership and feasibility that neither interface can
manufacture.
   Each interface needs an explicit refusal or unknown state. A retrieved passage with the
wrong unit should fail target review. A graph class outside a backend’s domain should return
unsupported. A valid but uninformative effect set should remain visible. A conflict between
textual and numerical evidence should retain both sources for investigation instead of selecting
whichever yields a cleaner answer.
   CausalDS makes narrated mechanisms, observations and private scoring objects separate
parts of a benchmark, and its results distinguish symbolic answers, uncertainty, abstention
and cost.Leban and Sun (2026) The proposed evaluation adopts that separation as a design
principle. It does not borrow a published model score as evidence for the local prototype. The
next chapters develop the translation, diagram, discovery, workflow and economic consequences
of this architecture; its empirical value still requires independent mechanisms and an actual
declared backend.
40.7. From a frontier result to a banking capability                                           671


40.7      From a frontier result to a banking capability
The inspected literature gives reasons to invest in better assistance, but it does not yield a
single ranking of causal systems. A system that extracts relations from documents, a system
that answers a supplied structural-model question and a system that chooses a treatment
policy may all receive a score called causal accuracy. Their inputs, permissible assumptions
and correct outputs differ. A product proposal must recover these differences before it uses an
experimental result to select software or allocate development effort.
  For this purpose, describe an evaluation claim by

                                      E = (T , I, A, O, B, L),                              (40.1)

where T is the task distribution, I the information supplied to the system, A its scientific
assumptions, O the oracle or adjudication rule, B the tool, repair and human budget, and L
the loss used to score its output. This is a proposed comparison vocabulary, not a theorem
that these quantities are observed without error. It asks a practical question: which parts of
the published experiment would remain the same in the proposed banking use? A change in
any component requires an argument or a new experiment before the original score can carry
the same interpretation.
   For example, a graph provided in the prompt belongs to I. Correctly calculating a back-door
formula from it tests conditional reasoning. Inferring that graph from account and contact
records is a different task with different assumptions. Likewise, a human who repairs a mistaken
join changes the combined workflow’s information and cost. The repaired answer can be
valuable, but attributing its correctness entirely to the model would misdescribe the product
being evaluated. This motivates an explicit comparison of the strongest available alternatives
rather than an agent-only leaderboard.


40.7.1     Favorable and adverse results locate different opportunities

The earliest broad frontier analysis treats language models as a channel for domain knowledge
and a possible aid to graph construction, critique and robustness analysis. It also probes
memorization and prompt sensitivity. These observations motivate assistance with familiar
concepts while warning that a recognizable public dataset can supply information absent
from a fresh bank problem. Neither renaming a variable nor recalling a benchmark answer
establishes a new identification result Kıcıman et al. (2023).
   CLadder gives a more controlled formal task: generated questions from specified causal
structures with alternative verbalizations. That design isolates important distinctions among
association, intervention and counterfactual reasoning. The supplied structure and generator,
however, are part of the experimental information. A bank workflow must also determine
whether its variable, treatment and population definitions support that structure. The paper’s
remaining language-to-formal-tool problem is therefore central to the proposed product, not
an incidental user-interface issue Jin et al. (2023).
   Two comparisons show why the proposal should retain nonagent and smaller-model baselines.
In CausalEval, adding function calls improves the reported GPT-4o CLADDER point score
from 69 to 76 relative to ordinary chain-of-thought, but reduces its e-CARE score from 90 to 73.
These are outcomes from the named historical configurations and samples. They demonstrate
variation across tasks, not a general tool penalty or benefit. In the inspected relation-extraction
study, the DDI F1 values for Single-Prompt C and PubMedBERT are 67.4 and 87.9. The
task concerns binary pairwise relations and the fine-tuned system receives labeled training
examples. The result supports considering supervised extraction where the document domain
672                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


and annotation budget are suitable; it does not compare whole causal pipelines at equal total
cost Yu et al. (2025a); Susanti and Holsmoelle (2025).
   Retrieval has similarly mixed consequences. LACR combines background knowledge, docu-
ments and optional numerical information. Its ASIA skeleton F1 falls from 1 to approximately
.73 when documents are added, while other reported cases benefit. Documents can add an
applicable mechanism, introduce a conflicting definition or repeat the same unsupported
assertion. The scientific question is which information changed and why it was relevant, rather
than how many documents entered the prompt Zhang et al. (2024b).
   Auditing assumptions is another promising but restricted task. ARGUS assesses the reported
support for difference-in-differences assumptions, uses injected flaws as local ground truth and
explicitly avoids adjudicating causal truth. Its five-paper human-label pilot and in-sample
calibration do not establish the error rate on a new collection of studies. A bank can use such
an assistant to find missing discussion or contradictory passages while keeping assignment,
parallel trends and measurement facts open to scientific assessment Zhang et al. (2026a).
   CausalCollab makes the longitudinal issue concrete. It defines an incremental stylistic effect
in sequential human–model interactions under explicit positivity and sequential exchangeability
premises. Its intervention mixes text versions through a specified functional construction. A
proposed collections-message rewriting policy is not automatically that intervention: it must
define which actual messages are delivered, to whom, and after which history. Model-generated
counterfactual edits or outcome labels in an evaluation remain generated evidence. The
theorem’s premises, the estimator’s approximation and the operational rewriting policy must
be reviewed separately Zhang et al. (2024a).
  These results favor a portfolio of bounded roles. Template-driven formalization, supervised
extraction, retrieved evidence, formal graph algorithms and numerical causal estimators can
each be a baseline or component. A language model is valuable where it reduces a measured
bottleneck while preserving the meaning of the task. Its presence is not a requirement for every
component. The architecture chapter develops how to enforce those boundaries in handoffs;
the question here is what evidence can justify selecting them.


40.7.2    Task composition can reverse a published ranking

Let sak be method a’s success probability on task stratum k and wk the proportion of eligible
                               P
requests in that stratum, with k wk = 1. Under a common success definition, the overall
probability is                                X

                                                 k

Even when every sak is known, ranking methods requires w. A pooled score from one benchmark
mixture is not a mixture-free property of a system. When the strata use incompatible outcomes,
they should first remain separate rather than be forced into this formula.
   As an arithmetic illustration, use the two reported CausalEval point-score pairs just discussed.
Give CLADDER weight w and e-CARE weight 1−w. The FunctionCall-minus-chain-of-thought
difference is
                            ∆(w) = .07w − .17(1 − w) = .24w − .17.                           (40.3)
It changes sign at w = 17/24 ≃ .7083. At equal weights the difference is −.05; at w = .8 it is
.022. This reweighting uses published point scores solely to illustrate composition. It supplies

mechanism-level dependence would be needed for an uncertainty calculation Yu et al. (2025a);
Causal banking proposal project (2026i).
40.7. From a frontier result to a banking capability                                               673


   The same principle applies to missing tasks. If all evaluated requests assume an observed
confounder set, the experiment cannot establish performance on latent-confounding requests,
whatever their future bank frequency. If the support and weights of the intended workload are
unknown, report stratum-level results and plausible planning mixtures. A later public or bank
intake sample can estimate the mix. Changing the weighting after observing which method
wins would instead change the decision rule being evaluated.
  The task family should be the meaningful sampling unit. Paraphrases from the same
mechanism, multiple prompt seeds and repeated tool calls share information. The repeated-call
variance example in the evaluation chapter explains why their count cannot simply replace
the count of independent mechanisms. For a matched comparison, pair methods on the
same held-out mechanisms, preserve all retries and report uncertainty at the level where the
evaluation law supplies independence. No variance estimate can be recovered from a published
average alone.


40.7.3     Component correctness must compose through conditional events

Suppose a request passes five stages: correct formulation E1 , observation construction E2 ,
identification E3 , numerical execution E4 and reporting E5 . By the chain rule,
                                                                             
                                   5
                                   \                    5
                                                        Y               \
                            P         Ej  = P (E1 )         P Ej |         Ek  .            (40.4)
                                j=1                     j=2             k<j

This identity does not require independent stages. It does require that each factor refer to the
same workflow and condition on all relevant preceding successes. Marginal accuracies reported
in five unrelated papers are not those conditional probabilities. They may concern different
data, expert information and definitions of success. Multiplying them would manufacture an
end-to-end claim from incompatible experiments.
    For an exact planning example, conditional probabilities (.96, .95, .90, .97, .98) yield .78025248.
If these numbers are instead only marginal success probabilities in a common request population,
the joint success is bounded by
                                                                 

                                       X           5
                                                   \
                                         c 
                      max 0, 1 −
                                    P (Ej ) ≤ P     Ej  ≤ min P (Ej ),                       (40.5)

                                 j=1              j=1

giving .76 to .90. The lower bound follows from the union bound for failures; the upper
follows because joint success implies every individual success. Two authored populations of
100 requests attain the endpoints. In one, failure sets of sizes 4, 5, 10, 3 and 2 are disjoint,
leaving 76 complete successes. In the other the failure sets are nested inside the ten largest
failures, leaving 90. Both have exactly the same stage marginals Causal banking proposal
project (2026i).
   For the proposal, this means stage tests diagnose where to improve, while a separate
composition test measures the completed request. A syntactically valid graph can propagate a
wrong population through every later stage. A correct estimator may precisely calculate the
wrong target. Conversely, several stages can fail on the same small subset, so adding their
failure counts overstates the number of affected requests. Record per-request transitions and
preserve the joint history needed to distinguish these cases.
