41.12.2     Use heterogeneity to understand weight sensitivity

The paper separates effect heterogeneity from the distance between targets. Define the
covariance-metric heterogeneity and distance by
                                            1/2
                           ′   −1
   H(θ) = min(θ − 1γ) Σ             (θ − 1γ)        ,   dΣ (λ, w) = {(λ − w)′ Σ(λ − w)}1/2 .   (41.13)
                γ

The minimum centers the effects at their generalized least-squares constant. Since (λ−w)′ 1 = 0,
subtracting any constant leaves the target difference unchanged. Cauchy–Schwarz in the
whitened coordinates gives the paper’s sharp bound

                                       |τλ − τw | ≤ H(θ)dΣ (λ, w).                             (41.14)

A banking interpretation follows directly: populations can disagree little because effects are
nearly homogeneous, because their weights are close in the relevant metric, or both. None
of these statements checks confounding. In the example with Σ = I2 , the centering constant
is 2, H 2 = 32, and d2Σ = 1/2. The squared bound is 16, exactly the squared effect difference
(0 − 4)2 . This attained witness checks the stated geometry.
   Minimax-bias weights minimize the maximum covariance-metric distance to Λ. For the
two-group class at ϵ = 2/3, the first coordinate ranges from 1/4 to 11/12. With identity
covariance the center is 7/12, with effect 8/3 and worst-case effect deviation 8/3. This is
the center of the stipulated oracle range [0, 16/3]. It illustrates the geometric compromise,
but minimizing this bias radius need not minimize total interval length, and the compromise
weights need not be the population the sponsor wishes to serve. A precision or robustness
preference is a decision input; an assistant should expose it rather than silently substitute it
for the business target.


41.12.3     State which confidence event is protected

The paper constructs a one-sided upper confidence bound Uβ on H(θ), with error budget β,
from the generalized least-squares residual statistic. Under the exact experiment its square
has a noncentral chi-square law with K − 1 degrees of freedom and conventional noncentrality
H(θ)2 . The paper’s notation indexes this distribution by heterogeneity itself. A software
conversion must reconcile that notation with the noncentrality accepted by a numerical library.
Confusing H and H 2 would change the bound. The source also specifies a zero-bound branch
when the observed statistic is sufficiently small; arbitrary root finding without that branch
would not implement the stated procedure.
696                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank

                                                        √
  Let Rw = maxλ∈Λ dΣ (λ, w), Bβ = Uβ Rw and sw = w′ Σw. The paper’s two-sided interval
uses the folded-normal critical value c1−α (b), defined as the (1 − α) quantile of |N (b, 1)|:
                                      h                      i
                                Cw = w′ θb ± c1−α (Bβ /sw )sw .                          (41.15)

This combines sampling variation with a confidence bound on target disagreement. The
heterogeneity bound, class optimization and critical-value calculation each require their own
numerical checks.
  Proposition 6 of the selected original establishes

               Pr{λ′ θ ∈ Cw } ≥ 1 − α − β    for every fixed λ ∈ Λ and every θ.          (41.16)
                θ

This uniform statement about each fixed target differs from the event that one interval contains
every target together. Appendix C.1, Proposition 7, gives the two-sided simultaneous guarantee

                          Pr{λ′ θ ∈ Cw for all λ ∈ Λ} ≥ 1 − 2α − β.                      (41.17)
                           θ

The one-sided simultaneous guarantee is 1 − α − β. With α = β = .05, the stated lower
guarantees are 90% for each fixed target and 85% for the simultaneous two-sided event. They
are lower bounds, not assertions that actual coverage equals those numbers. To allocate a
5% budget to the latter event one possible choice is α = .0125, β = .025. Reporting “95%
confidence” without stating the event and both budgets would conceal a substantive change in
protection.
   This distinction matters for agents that inspect many customer mixes before selecting a
favorable one. A guarantee for every preassigned target does not automatically guarantee
coverage of a target selected from the same results. Simultaneous protection can protect such
a selection within a fixed admissible class, under its assumptions and its actual confidence
budget. It does not license learning the class from outcomes without further justification, nor
does it correct other forms of model or treatment selection.


41.12.4    Move to feasible estimation without discarding the conditions

The source develops asymptotic extensions with a uniform central limit theorem, consistent
covariance and weight estimates, eigenvalue bounds and regularity for estimated classes. These
conditions are material for dependent banking panels, where covariance estimation is part
of the scientific argument. The main asymptotic development keeps K fixed. A growing-K
appendix requires separate technical assessment before use here. Treating a large collection of
sparse branch effects as though it automatically satisfied the fixed-dimensional experiment
would bypass that issue.
   Estimated classes introduce another boundary. Consistency of a class does not ensure
that it contains every fixed target on the limiting boundary in a given sample. The source’s
Proposition U8 uses a containment condition; an enlarged class with fixed positive slack is a
sufficient route in its example. Remark 8 explicitly distinguishes the theorem for any fixed
δ > 0 from applications reported at δ = 0. The observation that δ = .0001 leaves displayed
intervals unchanged is a numerical rounding observation, rather than a proof of the theorem
at zero slack. A proposed implementation must state which class, containment argument and
slack it actually uses.
  For event studies, the required inputs are the group-time effect vector and its full joint
covariance, with compatible aggregation definitions. An interval for each event time does not
automatically become simultaneous protection across all event times. The paper’s public-data
41.12. Whose effect is the assistant being asked to estimate?                                  697


applications illustrate its authors’ results; without acquiring and inspecting their data, code and
terms, they do not establish a replication or a ready software bridge. A bounded comparison
should first use public known-law group effects, verify the oracle geometry, exercise covariance
and class-boundary failures, and then compare the feasible procedures on matched targets.
   The proposal should offer three explicit choices: commit to a substantively justified fixed
population; report a sensitivity range over declared weights; or add a justified robust confidence
construction when sampling uncertainty also matters. The library, CLI and MCP representa-
tions must carry the group definitions, weight role, full covariance, class, target-selection rule,
confidence event and budgets. A language model can help elicit these fields and explain their
consequences. It cannot infer missing population truth from well-written prose or turn a valid
interval for one target into evidence for another.
Chapter 42

Four banking translations before
formal causal analysis

A request such as “Should we improve retention?” is not yet a causal question. The action
may be a rate offer, a service contact, a product change or a budgeted policy. The unit may be
an account, customer, household or branch. The outcome may be balance retention, funding
cost, repayment or relationship value. An assistant should expose these alternatives and ask
for the missing decision; a formal engine cannot repair a target chosen incorrectly before the
graph is built. The four translations below keep the business motivation while making different
estimands visible. Their formal discipline follows the separation of a target trial, its eligible
population and its observed emulation in Hernán and Robins (2020); the banking choices
themselves are proposals, not observations.


42.1      Deposit pricing: acquisition, retention or net funding cost
Suppose a treasury manager considers a 25-basis-point deposit-rate increase. Translation A
asks for the effect of offering the rate to every eligible account on thirty-day average balance.
Translation B asks for the effect on balances among accounts that historically received similar
offers. Translation C asks for net funding cost, including paid interest, incentive expense,
repricing of existing balances and any value assigned to retained relationships. Translation D
asks for a fixed-budget allocation policy that chooses which accounts receive the offer. These
are four populations or outcomes, not four estimators of one effect.
   Let U be the account, P the accounts eligible under the written rule, A the offer, and
Y B (a) = H −1 H
                P
                  d=1 Bd (a) the average daily balance over H = 30 days, measured in dollars.
The corresponding balance-time outcome is S(a) = HY B (a), measured in dollar-days. The
all-eligible balance target is EP [Y B (1) − Y B (0)]. A monetary value target instead specifies
a valuation M (a) in dollars and compares EP [M (1) − M (0) − {C(1) − C(0)}], where C(a)
is monetary cost outside M (a). Costs already inside M (a) must not be subtracted again.
If Y C (a) already contains net funding cost, the objective is to minimize EP [Y C (a)] and a
negative EP [Y C (1) − Y C (0)] favors the offer. The policy target additionally requires a feasible
policy class and an explicitly costed comparator. A realized post-offer balance may enter the
monetary outcome but is not automatically a pre-offer policy weight. A customer identifier
does not establish economic ownership when accounts are shared or linked. Section 42.7 derives
a dimensionally consistent valuation and its alternatives.
  For example, let W be the frozen pre-offer balance and segment record, e(W ) = Pr(A = 1 |
W ), and ma (W ) = E(Y B | A = a, W ). If consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity

and the declared no-interference boundary hold, the all-eligible target has the identifying
expression                        Z

This equality is conditional on the assumptions; a fitted model cannot verify them. If offers
are absent for a high-balance stratum, restricting the integral to 0 < e(W ) < 1 changes its
averaging measure. Likewise, a policy π(W ) under a monetary expense budget B asks for
EP {Y C (π(W )) − Y C (π0 (W ))} subject to EP [C(π(W ))] ≤ B. The target needs a specified
comparator π0 , a cost convention and an availability clock before any optimization result
has a business meaning. The target-versus-estimator distinction is reproduced in the project
reference (Causal banking research project, 2026h).
   A valid clock records when rate eligibility, customer status and balance information were
available to the offer system. A statement generated after the decision cannot be used as if it
were known before it. Diagnostics include overlap by eligibility stratum, repricing spillovers,
concurrent campaigns and whether the offer itself changes future eligibility. A narrower overlap
target can be useful, but the report must display the excluded accounts and say that the
original all-eligible target remains unresolved.
   Consider two equally common eligible strata with conditional effects of 2 and 8 balance units.
Their all-eligible effect is 5. If the offer probabilities are 0.1 and 0.5, overlap weights e(1 − e)
are 0.09 and 0.25; their normalized average is (0.09 · 2 + 0.25 · 8)/(0.09 + 0.25) = 109/17 ≈ 6.41,
not 5. This is exact authored arithmetic, illustrating why a desirable stable-overlap answer
cannot be substituted for the requested all-eligible effect. The example asserts no bank offer
probabilities.


42.2      Arrears servicing: offer, acceptance or dynamic policy
A collections manager asks whether an early restructuring review should be offered to an
account entering arrears. Translation A targets an offer at the first qualifying arrears date.
Translation B targets acceptance among customers who take up the review. Translation C
targets the effect of a fixed sequence of contacts. Translation D targets a dynamic policy
that uses evolving hardship and payment history. Acceptance is downstream of the offer; it is
not the same intervention. A static binary ATE cannot silently answer a longitudinal policy
question.
   Let Xt contain information available at the decision time, At the offer, Lt+1 later hardship
information and Y discounted net recovery over 180 days. A total-effect question should not
condition on a post-offer descendant Lt+1 as an ordinary baseline covariate. A policy question
needs the action history, availability of each Lt , censoring and a comparator policy. If several
accounts share a household or collection team, account rows are not automatically independent
units. A field entered on day 11 cannot govern a day-10 action even if its event date is day 9.
  For a two-decision example let H0 = X0 and H1 = (X0 , A0 , L1 ), with a regime g = (g0 , g1 )
where A0 = g0 (H0 ) and A1 = g1 (H1 ). Its target is V (g) = E[Y (g)] on the declared first-arrears
cohort. Sequential exchangeability, consistency, positivity along the regime and a justified
censoring law are needed for a longitudinal identification formula. For the discrete case, write
h = (x, g0 (x), l), p(x) = Pr(X0 = x) and

                            mg (h) = E[Y | H1 = h, A1 = g1 (h)],
                          pg (l | x) = Pr(L1 = l | X0 = x, A0 = g0 (x)).
700                                                                   Causal analysis for a universal bank


Then the longitudinal formula is
                                      X
                            V (g) =         mg (x, g0 (x), l) pg (l | x) p(x).
                                      x,l

The formula illustrates the clock: L1 may guide A1 , but cannot retroactively guide A0 . It also
shows why a coefficient from a regression that conditions on L1 cannot be relabeled the total
first-offer effect. This is a project specialization of the longitudinal identification argument in
Hernán and Robins (2020).
   Failure cases are substantive. A model that predicts acceptance can be accurate while
answering no offer-effect question. A model that trims accounts with poor overlap and continues
to report an all-account effect changes the population. A missing policy-history component
is an unsupported target, not a zero effect. The remedy is to return a typed alternative or
refusal and request the missing policy, clock or population decision.


42.3      Credit underwriting: approval threshold or feasible deci-
          sion rule
A credit team may ask whether lowering an approval threshold changes loss. Translation A is
the effect of offering credit to applicants between the old and new thresholds. Translation B is
the effect on repayment conditional on approval. Translation C is the effect on portfolio loss
including volume, utilization and capital cost. Translation D is a policy value under a capacity
or risk budget. Approval is an action selected by a threshold, while repayment is observed
only under selected applicants; conditioning on approved cases changes the target.
   The unit is an application at the decision date. The action must specify amount, term and
price, not only a binary approval label. Potential outcomes include repayment, loss, utilization
and capital usage over a fixed horizon. A threshold change can alter composition, interference
through capacity and future collection intensity. The information contract must distinguish
bureau vintage, application-time fields, later delinquency and revised labels. Diagnostics
include support around the threshold, manipulation or anticipatory behavior, policy feasibility,
missing outcomes and whether the threshold is a rule or a human override.
  A regression discontinuity or instrumental design requires its own continuity, exclusion
and assignment assumptions; a predictive score does not supply them. If the target is an
approval-policy value, the report should retain the policy constraints and loss function rather
than output a conditional repayment coefficient. A public or generated threshold mechanism
can test translation and clock preservation before requesting bank outcome truth.
   To see the selection issue, let D(z) denote approval under threshold policy z and let Y (1)
denote repayment under a specified offered loan. The mean E[Y (1) | D(z) = 1] describes
the applicants selected by z; it is not E[Y (1)] for all applicants. Changing z can change
that conditioning population even if no individual repayment response changes. Near a score
cutoff c, the discontinuity lims↓c E(Y | S = s) − lims↑c E(Y | S = s) may have a local causal
interpretation only under the design’s continuity and manipulation restrictions; it is not
the portfolio effect of moving the entire threshold. A threshold policy must count declined
applications with their opportunity cost and define the loan terms and missing counterfactual
repayment law. The local-design distinction is consistent with the audited discontinuity and
target-trial sources (Hernán and Robins, 2020).
42.4. Branch campaign: donor counterfactual or randomized rollout                               701


42.4      Branch campaign: donor counterfactual or randomized
          rollout
A branch manager asks whether a campaign increased new accounts. Translation A is a
single-branch time-series counterfactual using unaffected donors. Translation B is a panel
effect across branches with staggered launch dates. Translation C is a cluster-randomized
rollout. Translation D is the value of changing campaign intensity under a constrained budget.
The outcomes, donor assumptions and uncertainty objects differ.
   For a treated branch Yt , donor series Xt and intervention date T0 , a structural time-series
method predicts Yt (0) from pre-period history and controls. It requires controls unaffected
by the campaign and a stable relationship after T0 . Perfect pre-period fit does not establish
either restriction. Shared marketing, customer migration or national pricing can contaminate
donors. A randomized rollout addresses a different question with a different cost and design;
panel methods require their own assignment and trend assumptions. The inspected structural-
time-series and synthetic-control sources use unaffected predictors and design information in
their respective comparisons (Brodersen et al., 2015; Abadie et al., 2010); neither makes a
pre-period fit diagnostic a proof of post-period donor invariance.
   An exact construction makes the risk concrete. Let At = 1 on four campaign days,
Xt = x0t + 15At and Yt = 100 + 2x0t + 20At . The pre-period relationship is Y = 100 + 2X.
Continuing it post-period gives a contrast of −10 per day, although one structural law has a
true campaign effect of 20 and a contaminated donor. A second law produces the same twelve
observed rows and a true effect of −10 with an unaffected donor. No estimator can distinguish
these laws without a restriction or experiment. With a stipulated USD1 value per application
and USD20 cost, the four-day net values are +60 and -60. These are authored mechanisms,
not bank evidence.
   In the first law, the observed post-period contrast is Yt − (100 + 2Xt ) = 20 − 2(15) = −10,
while the counterfactual holding the donor’s untreated path fixed is Yt (0) = 100 + 2x0t and
the true effect is 20. In the second law, define an unaffected donor x    e0t = Xt and an outcome
Yt = 100 + 2x e0t − 10At . Every observed (At , Xt , Yt ) row is then identical across the two laws,
including the eight pre-period and four post-period rows, yet the effect is −10. At USD1
per application and a single USD20 campaign cost, 4(20) − 20 = 60 and 4(−10) − 20 = −60.
The sign of the investment decision is therefore not identified from these rows alone. The
contrasting laws are reproducible algebra, not a claim that either mechanism occurs at a bank.


42.5      The formulation record and formal handoff
The declaration uses the same Q = (U, P, A, π, π0 , Y, H, ν, ℓ, I) as the preceding formulation
chapter: unit, population, feasible actions, policy, comparator policy, outcome, horizon,
averaging measure, loss and information clock. A fixed action is a constant policy; A0 in the
servicing example denotes the first action, not a second notation for the comparator. It should
preserve candidate questions when the business sentence is ambiguous. A schema check verifies
fields and types; a semantic check compares them with the brief and dictionary; a formal check
applies the supplied graph and method. A passed schema is not causal truth, and a failed
backend is not nonidentification.
  The order of handoff matters. First, freeze Q and the candidate alternatives with a human
owner. Second, attach each proposed graph arrow to a source, temporal ordering and an
uncertainty label. Third, ask the formal engine which estimand, if any, follows from the
supplied graph and assumptions. Fourth, run estimators only for supported targets and return
702                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


precision, sensitivity and refusal states. An arrow suggested by retrieval is a hypothesis until
its substantive owner accepts it; conversational consistency is not graph accuracy (Kıcıman
et al., 2023; Sng et al., 2024). Formal reasoning benchmarks and narrated synthetic cases help
check the translation boundary, but their scores do not validate bank assignment truth (Jin
et al., 2023; Leban and Sun, 2026).
   The deterministic baseline is an analyst interview plus fixed arithmetic and graph fixtures.
An assisted system can retrieve evidence, draft alternatives, propose a graph and prepare typed
calls. It should be scored on target fidelity, clock fidelity, preserved ambiguity, valid abstention,
numerical correctness only when the target is identified, and complete failure accounting. All
requests belong in the denominator, including refusals and unsupported policies. Public data
and generated structural mechanisms are appropriate proposal evidence; authentic bank truth
and live provider performance remain later conditional evidence.
   The immediate prototype should compare the four translations against the structured
baseline using fixed prompts, scenario-level splits, adverse cases and a stopping rule. A later
bank study is justified only if the prototype isolates a decision-relevant uncertainty and makes
its value of information plausible. No fluent report can substitute for a population decision,
assignment record, clock or expert acceptance.


42.6      Contextual causal language and the intervention a bank
          will buy
A causal sentence in a service note is useful evidence about what was said, but the intervention
a bank will buy requires an additional scientific argument. Zhao, Yan and Hu’s Contextual
Causality with Large Language Models: A Survey, inspected in its 18 September 2026 arXiv
version, separates semantic, intervention and counterfactual tasks within textual context. Its
page 3 explicitly distinguishes intervening in a textual description from manipulating the
underlying data-generating process. The paper’s semantic “identification” of causal relations
should therefore be read as a language task, rather than statistical identification of an effect.
The authors state that their text-only taxonomy organizes causal concepts and does not extend
causal theory.(Zhao et al., 2026)
   For banking translation, the useful outputs are candidate entities, proposed temporal
relations, alternative explanations and the passages supporting each proposal. An analyst may
translate “customers stayed after we called” into an action, outcome and eligible population.
The same note may omit that relationship managers called customers they already expected
to retain. A language model can make both possibilities explicit. A fluent restatement, or a
correct answer to a question about the note, cannot determine which mechanism generated
the observations.


42.6.1    The same observed relationship can reverse the investment decision

An exact authored pair of causal laws isolates the missing information. Let U ∼ Bernoulli(1/2)
be an unobserved account state, and let the natural binary contact rule be A = U . Let Y (a)
be gross monetary response under assigned contact a. Consider

                          M1 : Y (a) = 100a,        M2 : Y (a) = 100U.                        (42.1)

Both laws generate exactly

                      P (A = 0, Y = 0) = 12 ,      P (A = 1, Y = 100) = 12 .                  (42.2)
42.6. Contextual causal language and the intervention a bank will buy                       703


In M1 , contact causes the gross response. In M2 the latent state causes both natural contact
and response, and contact has no effect. Under an intervention the distribution of U remains
unchanged. Hence the average gross effect is USD 100 in the first law and zero in the
second.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026bp)
   At USD 10 per contact, changing from no contact to contacting every eligible account has
incremental net value                             (
                                                    90,   M1 ,
                          E{Y (1) − Y (0)} − 10 =                                    (42.3)
                                                    −10, M2 .
All values and mechanisms here are stipulated; they are not bank observations or outputs
of an LLM. The target compares two fixed policies, all-contact and no-contact, rather than
comparing either policy with the natural contact rule. The witness proves that the displayed
observed law alone cannot identify this decision. It does not prove that every useful causal
question is unidentified.
   An assistant should preserve both graph possibilities when the supplied evidence cannot
distinguish them. A new randomized contact assignment with adequate support would
distinguish these two gross-response laws under its design assumptions. Observing the latent
state alone does not create the missing within-state contact variation because A = U under
the natural rule. Alternatively, a justified exclusion of the latent common-cause explanation
would change the model class, but that restriction needs evidence. Repeatedly asking the
same model to rewrite the same observations does not add either source of information. The
proposed business-to-graph flow should report the unresolved distinction and the experiment
or restriction that could resolve it.


42.6.2    A survey can guide the evaluation design without qualifying every
          cited method

The survey discusses hallucinated or neglected relations, complex contexts, multiple-choice
shortcuts and limitations of external knowledge and agent coordination. These are the survey
authors’ synthesis of their cited work; those originals require separate inspection before
their empirical claims can support a package decision. Table 3 draws many representative
benchmarks from news, Wikipedia, stories, human questions and agent traces, and includes
FinCausal 2020. The presence of financial text is not evidence of contact-policy identification
or monetary utility in banking. Pages 8–9 call for extrinsic decision quality, finer evaluation
and longer agent horizons. This is a research agenda, not an authenticated exhaustive absence
result. (Zhao et al., 2026)
   A public or generated prototype can evaluate the resulting proposal before bank access.
Supply notes with controlled omissions, negation, reversed chronology and conflicting explana-
tions; separately score relation extraction, clock preservation, graph alternatives, unsupported
restrictions and appropriate refusal. Pair identical observations from the two laws above
and check that an assistant does not invent information to force a unique effect. When
an assignment design or restriction is supplied, evaluate the changed answer and its stated
dependence on that premise. These proposed tests assess different tasks from factual question
answering. Their known-law monetary scoring is conditional on the authored mechanisms and
cannot establish actual bank value.


42.6.3    Text measurement must preserve the causal question

A servicing analyst may ask an assistant to extract financial distress from call notes and then
adjust for the extracted score when comparing repayment plans. This can be useful work.
704                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


It also combines three different claims: that the score measures distress, that the note was
available before the plan decision, and that conditioning on the score removes the relevant
confounding. An accurate summary of the note establishes none of the latter two claims. A
later note may describe a reaction to the plan; a note written only after a complaint may select
on both treatment and outcome. The proposed formulation interface must attach a time and a
measurement interpretation to each extracted variable before adding it to an adjustment set.
   Keith, Jensen and O’Connor review text used to measure otherwise unobserved confounders.
Their discussion explicitly distinguishes confounders, colliders and mediators and asks whether
one document can encode several of these at once. It also identifies error in measured con-
founders as an unresolved problem. A richer language representation can improve measurement,
but the review provides no guarantee that a representation eliminates confounding. The appro-
priate comparison therefore includes simple dictionaries, supervised extractors, human-coded
measurements and a language model, with the same permitted document dates and the same
effect target. Keith et al. (2020)


A reproducible example of residual confounding

Consider the following project-generated population model. The intervention intensity A and
later loss Y are standardized continuous quantities; these are illustrative units, not calibrated
bank measurements. True predecision distress is U , while W is an imperfect score extracted
from a predecision note:

                   A = U + εA ,       W = U + εW ,       Y = τ A + U + εY .

   All four disturbances are mutually independent and centered Gaussian. The variances
of U, εA , εY are one, while Var(εW ) = s ≥ 0. The true effect of increasing A by one is τ .
Conditional on W , the residual variance of U is v = s/(1 + s). Residualizing both A and Y on
W therefore gives the population regression coefficient

                                             v         s
                               βA|W = τ +       =τ+        .
                                            1+v     1 + 2s
   The second term persists with an infinite sample. It is not estimation noise that a larger
language model, an accurate propensity fit to W , or a narrower regression interval automatically
removes. With the stipulated τ = −1/5, exact covariance calculations give the following values.

          Text-score noise variance s True effect Adjusted population coefficient
          0                             −1/5         −1/5
          1/4                           −1/5         −1/30
          1                             −1/5         2/15
          4                             −1/5         11/45


   The score with s = 1 leaves enough confounding to reverse the sign. This example is
independently reproduced by solving the population covariance normal equations and by
residual variance decomposition. It demonstrates a specific failure mechanism under a stated
law, not a claim that all text adjustment fails. A successful extraction study must measure the
relevant error and evaluate how it affects the causal target. If a proxy-correction method is
proposed, its additional measurement assumptions and available validation information must
be stated rather than inferred from predictive accuracy.
42.6. Contextual causal language and the intervention a bank will buy                          705


Freeze the measurement rule before evaluating its effects

Egami and colleagues make the measurement rule itself explicit. Let g map a document into a
category or vector. For a textual outcome, E[g(Y (1)) − g(Y (0))] is a target defined by that
particular rule. Searching over rules using the same treatment assignments and documents later
used for effect estimation can induce dependence and select apparent effects. Their proposed
separation of codebook discovery from effect estimation addresses that problem, while their
text-as-treatment discussion imposes a further sufficiency restriction on the representation.
Egami et al. (2018)
   For a language-based measurement pipeline, the rule includes the model version, prompt,
retrieval corpus, preprocessing, extraction schema and response aggregation. Freezing only a
classifier filename while changing the prompt after reading the effect estimates does not freeze
g. The prototype should develop the rule on a designated development set, record its identity,
and evaluate it on held-out units. If several calls concern one customer or conversation, those
calls should remain together in the split. This is a proposed implementation of the separation
principle, not a claim that sample splitting alone ensures valid inference for dependent histories.
   The held-out review asks whether the labels retain their intended meaning, whether extrac-
tion errors differ by treatment and outcome, and whether missing documents have a defensible
observation model. It must preserve negative findings. Rewriting the measurement rule to
rescue a disappointing effect requires a new evaluation set or an explicitly exploratory analysis.
Neither a fixed rule nor a held-out set supplies unmeasured assignment information or repairs
a post-treatment adjustment error.


Formulate competing explanations before selecting a diagram

Geraldo Bastías proposes building diagrams from the assumptions actually used in a study,
preserving several models where the assumptions do not determine one. His workflow checks
identification within each model, derives observable implications, and distinguishes missing
relationships from missing variables. This is a methodological contribution to diagram review,
not an implemented LLM discovery algorithm. It supports an assistant that makes assumptions
inspectable rather than treating a familiar design label as sufficient. Geraldo Bastías (2024)
   For the servicing example, a short initial brief can leave open whether distress caused
the plan assignment, whether a later complaint caused a note to be recorded, and whether
the proposed outcome is arrears, loss or customer welfare. The assistant should construct
separate compatible diagrams and show how each changes adjustment or identification. It
can check timing contradictions and derive conditional-independence implications. Passing
those checks does not establish that an omitted common cause is absent. Where the diagrams
imply different effects, the useful output is the unresolved choice and the evidence that could
distinguish it.
   These requirements permit immediate public and generated evaluation. A public document
corpus can supply realistic language, while a declared generator supplies assignment, document
timing, measurement error and outcome truth. Simple extraction and fixed numerical workflows
provide baselines. The evaluation must vary mechanisms that are difficult for the chosen
extractor, including selective note availability and notes written after treatment. Keith and
colleagues specifically caution that authors can choose semi-synthetic confounders their own
method can easily recover. Freezing adverse mechanisms and separating their construction
from final method selection addresses that concern more directly than adding familiar domain
vocabulary to a favorable simulation. Keith et al. (2020)

42.7     From a balance response to a monetary decision
The deposit example exposes a difficulty that arises before any estimator is chosen. A balance
is a stock, its accumulation over time is an exposure, and the financial benefit of that exposure
depends on a valuation convention. These quantities cannot be interchanged because they
all contain a currency unit. The assistant must obtain a complete statement of the business
target: does treasury want additional deposits, lower expense for a fixed funding requirement,
or a relationship-value objective that includes services beyond funding? Each question can be
legitimate. Only the second is answered by the funding-cost construction developed here. The
construction and all numerical values in this section are authored, exact illustrations. They
supply a reference for testing a proposed translator, not observed bank economics (Causal
banking research project, 2026ba).
  Let Bd (a) be end-of-day eligible balance under offer a on day d, where a = 0 is the stated
existing offer and a = 1 is the proposed offer. Fix a horizon of H days and a day-count
denominator D. Define
                              H                         H
                           1 X                          X
                    B(a) =       Bd (a),       S(a) =         Bd (a) = HB(a).                (42.4)
                           H d=1                        d=1

The units are dollars and dollar-days respectively. With a constant annual valuation rate q,
the monetary amount assigned to the balance-time is qS(a)/D dollars. The rate, denominator,
daily measurement convention and horizon are part of this definition. For example, substituting
a last-day balance for an average balance changes the outcome even if the two amounts happen
to agree in a stable illustrative account. A genuine proposal needs the product’s actual accrual
convention; the example fixes D = 365 without claiming that this convention applies to every
deposit contract.
   Suppose, for the moment, that treasury has the same exogenous daily funding requirement
Fd under either offer and can cover the residual Fd − Bd (a) at a supplied rate qd . This
construction assumes 0 ≤ Bd (a) ≤ Fd ; excess deposits would require a separately specified
investment or disposal rule. Let rd (a) be the deposit rate, and let K(a) be the monetary
expense outside interest: for example a stipulated communication charge. Ignoring discounting
in this short-horizon construction, define

Here N is net funding cost and V is the saving relative to funding the entire requirement at

value is exactly ∆V = E[V (1) − V (0)] = −E[N (1) − N (0)]. Maximizing V and minimizing

expense must be netted as K(1) − K(0), not automatically as K(1): the comparator itself
may incur expense, and cancelling a campaign may save it.
  This identity depends on the reference funding requirement and valuation path being
common. If the offer changes lending volumes, the institution’s marginal funding rate, or the
capacity to raise substitute funds, those objects acquire potential-outcome indices and the
common-reference term no longer cancels. An assistant cannot preserve the simple identity
while quietly adding those effects to its narrative. It must expand the target, state the
additional intervention and equilibrium assumptions, or present the fixed-requirement result

as a narrower answer. Likewise, relationship benefits should be represented by a separately
specified monetary outcome, not attached to a balance effect through an unexplained positive
adjective.


42.7.1    Repricing existing balances can reverse the conclusion

Under constant rates, write r1 = r0 + δr and ∆S = S(1) − S(0). Subtracting the two value
definitions gives the pathwise identity
                                      (q − r0 )∆S − δrS(1)
                    V (1) − V (0) =                        − [K(1) − K(0)].              (42.7)
                                                D
The first term values additional balance-time at the old spread. The second charges the higher
deposit rate to all balances receiving it, including balances that would have remained without
the offer. It is not restricted to newly attracted deposits. An equivalent decomposition uses
the new spread on ∆S and the rate increase on S(0). Both produce the same cash difference;
adding both repricing terms would count part of the cost twice. These identities hold for each
pair of potential balance paths, so taking expectations requires no independence between the
two paths.
   Consider an exact thirty-day example. The comparator holds USD100,000 every day at
a 2% annual rate; the offered rate is 2.25%, and its balance is USD110,000 every day. The
stipulated substitute funding rate is 5%. Operating expenses are USD4 under the comparator
and USD8 under the offer. Thus ∆S = 300,000 dollar-days and the added average balance is
USD10,000. The additional old-spread value is 1800/73 dollars and the repricing charge is
1650/73 dollars. Their difference is only 150/73 dollars. Subtracting the incremental USD4
expense gives
                               1800 − 1650           142
                        ∆V =                 −4=−         ≃ −USD 1.95.                    (42.8)
                                    73                73
The offer attracts balances while increasing net funding cost. The reference also constructs the
complete daily ledger for a stipulated USD150,000 funding requirement and reproduces the
opposite-signed cost difference by summation. That second calculation checks the accounting
identity instead of merely repeating the printed formula. Treating the USD10,000 stock
increase as a USD10,000 benefit, forgetting existing-balance repricing, or subtracting USD8
instead of the incremental USD4 each answers a different question.
   The all-eligible mean effect remains a population target. A deterministic balance path here
makes the arithmetic transparent; a causal analysis must identify or bound the distribution
of paths under both offers. Identifying the mean balance contrast alone is sufficient for this
linear, fixed-rate valuation only when the other required expectations and costs are supplied.
It is not a claim that a regression coefficient identifies the complete financial response of a
deposit portfolio.


42.7.2    Marginal funding cost and an explicit valuation boundary

Another reasonable business question is the annualized incremental expense per unit of extra
balance-time. For a positive expected balance-time change, under the same constant-rate
convention define
                               r1 E[S(1)] − r0 E[S(0)] + DE[K(1) − K(0)]
                      rinc =                                             .               (42.9)
                                              E[S(1) − S(0)]
This is a ratio of portfolio expectations, not the mean of customer-level ratios. The latter can
be undefined for accounts with no balance response, give large influence to tiny denominators,
708                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


and change the aggregation question. The incremental cost rate also differs from the offered
deposit rate. In the example it is 1571/30000, or about 5.237%, despite the 2.25% offered
rate. It includes paying more on existing balances and spreading the incremental operating
expense over the new balance-time. With positive expected ∆S, ∆V is positive precisely when
q > rinc . If that denominator is zero or negative, the displayed ratio is unavailable or loses this
comparison interpretation; the original monetary difference remains the appropriate object to
inspect.
   This comparison is useful even when a bank has not yet supplied a valuation rate. Instead
of inventing a price, the proposal can report the break-even rate or a sensitivity interval. If
the same example permits q between 4% and 6%, its value ranges from −742/73 to 458/73
dollars, roughly minus USD10.16 to plus USD6.27. There is no uniformly preferred offer over
that stipulated set. An owner who accepts the funding model can resolve the economic choice
by supplying the relevant rate and cost convention. This is a missing business input, distinct
from an unidentified balance response. Uncertainty about both should be kept visible rather
than folded into one unexplained error bar.
  For a set of admissible causal laws P and valuation specifications Q, the corresponding
proposal can report

                    V = {EP [Vq (1) − Vq (0)] : (P, q) ∈ A},      A ⊆ P × Q.                (42.10)

The joint admissible set A matters. If liquidity conditions affect both the response and the
marginal rate, independently combining marginal endpoints may create impossible scenarios or
omit admissible dependence. The interval above deliberately varies only a deterministic rate
while holding the response law fixed. It is an economic sensitivity calculation, not a confidence
interval, a Bayesian posterior, or a general sharp bound. The formulation should state which
of those objects the user is requesting before selecting a downstream numerical tool.


42.7.3    Timing and nonlinear valuation require more than a mean

Balance-time suffices only for a constant linear valuation. With a supplied time-varying path
qd , the gross monetary effect is D−1 d qd E[Bd (1) − Bd (0)]. As an exact two-day example,
                                      P

compare additional balances of (200, 0) with (0, 200) dollars. Both have average additional
balance USD100 and exposure 200 dollar-days. At rates (0.10, 0.01) their gross values are
20/365 and 2/365 dollars. A translator that passes only the mean balance to the valuation
engine loses the information needed to distinguish these cases. Discount factors, when required,
must similarly attach to the appropriate cash-flow dates; they cannot be appended after
aggregation if the timing information was dropped.
   A nonlinear valuation needs still more information. Suppose a hypothetical gross value rule
is m(B) = 0.01 min(B, 100) dollars and a comparator has zero gross value. A balance fixed at
USD100 has expected gross value USD1. A balance of zero or USD200 with equal probabilities
has the same mean balance but expected gross value USD0.50. With incremental expense
USD0.75, their net values are USD0.25 and minus USD0.25. The mean balance response does
not identify which decision is favorable. This example is deliberately stylized; its purpose is to
distinguish E[m(B)] from m(E[B]), not to suggest a bank’s valuation schedule.
  Where costs depend on utilization, default, or other post-offer quantities, those quantities
belong in the monetary potential outcome. Their joint distribution can matter. Using the
realized balance to calculate interest is legitimate outcome construction; using that same
post-offer balance as a pre-offer targeting feature is a clock violation. Similarly, conditioning
on it to estimate an ordinary total effect generally changes the question. The declaration
must identify the role a variable plays, rather than labelling a field universally permitted or
42.8. Measurement and selective notes can change the target                                 709


forbidden. The target-trial and time-varying treatment distinctions already developed from
Hernán and Robins (2020) provide the inherited framework; the cash-flow mappings here are
project-specific definitions.


42.7.4    Consolidation and feasibility are part of the intervention

The business unit determines what counts as additional funding. If an offer moves USD10,000
from one account to another account at the same bank, the receiving account’s effect is positive
while the consolidated balance change is zero. Repricing the receiving account can nevertheless
increase expense. For mutually exclusive account balances under a fixed consolidation map, the
bank-level outcome sums the account paths before applying the bank-level valuation. Shared
accounts must not be counted once for each linked owner. When the intervention changes
ownership, currency composition or legal availability, a fixed consolidation map itself becomes
an assumption to reconsider. An identifier matching exercise cannot choose the economic
boundary on the owner’s behalf.
   This also changes treatment definition. A rate offered to one account may alter another
account’s balance or a household’s other offers. The potential outcome may then depend on
an allocation vector, not just an account’s own binary action. A feasible policy must respect
the shared budget and the permitted unit of allocation. Account-level exchangeability and
a no-interference assumption are substantive restrictions on that target, not conveniences a
language model can infer from a rectangular dataset. If these restrictions are not defensible,
the proposal can retain a cluster or portfolio question with its additional requirements.
   A budget needs an equally clear comparator. An absolute expense constraint E[K(π)] ≤ B
differs from an incremental constraint E[K(π) − K(π0 )] ≤ B. A capacity constraint on the
number of contacts is a third object and may not be expressible as either monetary constraint.
The policy π can use only the declared predecision history; the comparator π0 must satisfy its
own declared feasibility conditions. The proposed assistant should present these alternatives
in the business brief and carry the accepted choice into the formal query. Optimization before
that choice can produce a precise answer to an unstated problem.


42.8     Measurement and selective notes can change the target
The cash-flow argument generalizes to language-derived outcomes. A rule g that converts a
servicing note into a distress indicator defines an observed measurement, not automatically
the underlying distress variable. The inspected discussions by Keith and colleagues and Egami
and colleagues separate measurement from causal identification and distinguish a learned text
representation from the scientific target (Keith et al., 2020; Egami et al., 2018). The proposed
translator must say whether the owner wants the effect on recorded distress, on a fixed coding
rule’s output, or on latent distress. Those outcomes can differ even when the extraction system
executes exactly as specified.
   Let a binary underlying outcome have intervention-specific mean µa = Pr(Y (a) = 1). For a
fixed binary measurement rule, define its sensitivity sa = Pr(Y ∗ = 1 | Y = 1, do(A = a)) and
specificity ca = Pr(Y ∗ = 0 | Y = 0, do(A = a)). By the law of total probability, when these
conditional rates are defined,

                   µ∗a = sa µa + (1 − ca )(1 − µa ) = (sa + ca − 1)µa + 1 − ca .        (42.11)

This is an exact project derivation, not an imported guarantee for an LLM. If sensitivity and
specificity are common across interventions, the measured contrast equals (s + c − 1)(µ1 −
710                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


µ0 ). Recovering the underlying contrast by division requires those error rates to be known,
transportable and s + c − 1 ̸= 0. If the sum is one, the measurement contains no marginal
information about the binary outcome through this channel. If it is less than one, its direction is
reversed. Assuming ordinary attenuation without checking the channel is therefore unjustified.
   For example, set true outcome risks to 2/5 and 1/2, a true effect of 1/10. With common
sensitivity 4/5 and specificity 9/10, the measured effect is 7/100. Now retain those control
error rates but use treated sensitivity 1/2 and specificity 19/20. The measured effect becomes
−21/200, reversing the sign. All probabilities remain valid. The change could represent
different document content or extraction errors after the offer; the example makes no claim
that this occurs in a bank. Its implication is that pooled classification accuracy cannot
determine the causal error. A validation design needs outcome truth and enough treatment-
specific information to support the proposed correction, including the population and document
mechanism to which the rates are transported.
   Missing notes introduce a separate problem even when every available note is coded perfectly.
Let A and predecision distress U be independent Bernoulli variables with probability 1/2,
and define Y (a) = U for either action. The intervention has zero effect. Let R indicate
a note available for analysis, with probability 3/4 when A = U and 1/4 otherwise. Every
action–distress combination has positive note availability, so this example does not depend on
a cell with zero support. Exact enumeration gives
                                        3                                    1
              Pr(Y = 1 | A = 1, R = 1) = ,         Pr(Y = 1 | A = 0, R = 1) = .            (42.12)
                                        4                                    4
The observed-note contrast is 1/2 despite random assignment and a zero effect in the full
population. Selecting notes conditions on a common effect of action and distress. A correct
event timestamp, perfect extraction and randomized treatment do not remove that selection
mechanism.
   An oracle that knows U and the note probabilities can reweight each selected cell by the
inverse of its selection probability and recover mean distress 1/2 in each arm. This verifies
the construction; it is not a proposed correction when distress is precisely the unobserved
quantity the notes were meant to measure. The useful handoff identifies what is missing: a
justified observation model, independent validation measurements, or a narrower target that
the owner actually accepts. It must not quietly replace the eligible population by customers
with convenient documentation.
   These examples distinguish three repairs. Correcting a unit or comparator is a specification
repair. Estimating a measurement channel needs suitable validation information. Correcting
selective availability needs a defensible observation law and support. A language model can
locate definitions, propose alternatives and flag contradictions in each case, but those actions
do not provide the missing scientific information. Multiple defensible diagrams and their
different identifying consequences should survive the formulation stage, consistent with the
inspected argument for explicit assumption-based modelling in Geraldo Bastías (2024).


42.8.1    A proposal evaluation that isolates the translation error

A useful public and generated evaluation can freeze a set of business briefs that share language
while differing in one decision-relevant fact. For funding, pair a balance target with a net-cost
target; then vary whether the comparator incurs expense, whether repricing covers old balances,
and whether valuation is time-varying or nonlinear. For measurement, vary common versus
differential error and complete versus selective notes. The exact mechanisms above supply the
expected mathematical answer, while public dictionaries can supply realistic field names and
42.9. Which servicing policy does the business sentence describe?                                    711


documented units. Public text alone supplies neither assignment truth nor a bank’s marginal
funding rate. An evaluation should preserve that distinction explicitly.
   The reference response should contain the target, the necessary outcome components, the
sign convention, the information that is absent, and the reason an alternative interpretation
would change the answer. A numerical score is appropriate only when the brief supplies enough
information to determine it. For an unspecified q, reporting the break-even rate and the
unresolved valuation choice can be correct; inventing a rate to produce a confident investment
recommendation is an error. For selective notes with unknown selection probabilities, reporting
the selected contrast as the full-population effect is an error even when the subtraction is
exact.
   The comparison should use the same briefs, dictionaries, permissible source material and
answer schema for a structured analyst baseline and an assisted workflow. Separate the
underlying mechanisms used for development from those used for final evaluation, and keep
ambiguous, unsupported and failed requests in the denominator. This section provides exact
authored reference families, not a completed provider comparison. A useful prototype result
would identify which translation failures become less frequent and at what review cost. That
result can support a later decision to purchase authentic banking validation; it cannot supply
such validation in advance.


42.9      Which servicing policy does the business sentence de-
          scribe?
A request to improve early servicing can leave the later action rule unspecified. That omission
is more consequential than a missing estimator option. An initial review may change a
later condition, and a subsequent contact may respond to that condition. Comparing first-
stage actions while holding the later action fixed therefore differs from comparing complete
operating policies. The longitudinal formula developed earlier makes this distinction precise;
the following finite construction shows the numerical consequence. It specializes the inherited
sequential-intervention framework of Hernán and Robins (2020) to an authored example, with
no empirical claim about how an actual servicing review affects hardship.
   Let A0 denote an initial action, L1 a later adverse-state indicator, and A1 a follow-up action
taken after observing L1 . Stipulate Pr(L1 = 1 | do(A0 = 0)) = 1/4 and Pr(L1 = 1 | do(A0 =
1)) = 3/4. The initial action has a direct benefit but increases the chance of the costly later
state in this deliberately adverse model. Define net recovery, in hypothetical dollars, by

                                 Y (a, l, b) = 100 + 20a − 40l + 30bl − 10b.                      (42.13)

The last term is the follow-up cost and is already included in the outcome. There is no
additional initial cost in this construction. The structural model uses an independent uniform
disturbance to generate L1 at the stated probabilities, and the outcome is then deterministic
given the actions and state. These declarations supply the causal law for the example; observed
historical conditional frequencies would not by themselves supply the same law.
   For a fixed initial action a, let g a take the follow-up action precisely when L1 = 1. In that
state, follow-up adds USD20 net; when L1 = 0 it subtracts USD10. The adaptive rule is
consequently optimal within this specified two-action second-stage class when the state is fully
observed and there is no shared capacity constraint. Its value is
