   This calculation supplies a clear reason to prefer a generated prototype now. It can verify
the likelihood update, target preservation, action threshold and complete outcome accounting.
It can introduce dropout, shared shocks or worlds outside the two-model family and test
whether the workflow reports the changed assumptions. An actual bank experiment is justified
only when its feasible action, observation law, transfer population and cost could resolve a
consequential uncertainty. The present calculation cannot supply those inputs and does not
authorize or perform an experiment.
   A retrieval-only query has zero value for discriminating these two worlds if its response law
is identical in both and it conveys no new applicable restriction. Its likelihood ratio is one and
the posterior remains q. Retrieval may still improve variable definitions, reduce clerical effort
or reveal a genuine distinguishing fact. Those are separate benefits to model and measure.
Repeating a prompt until it favors the preferred graph does not reproduce the experiment
analyzed in Equation (45.7).
   The comparison also explains why full graph recovery is sometimes unnecessary. When
every retained model recommends the same feasible action over the relevant cost range, further
orientation may have little decision value. When two models differ on a consequential action,
the useful query is the one that separates them under an admissible information mechanism.
An agent can help formulate that query and show which assumptions drive its value. The
proposal’s initial objective is this reviewable connection from discovery to a decision, with
numerical and semantic limits preserved.


45.26        A correlation screen can discard a nonlinear cause
The proposal should also evaluate what happens before the formal discovery engine is called.
A marginal correlation screen may reduce the number of candidate pairs supplied to an agent,
but its omissions constrain everything downstream. The inspected Augur procedure uses a
Spearman screen before language judgments. Its reported forecasting performance does not
establish that this screen retains all intervention-relevant mechanisms (Zhiqing Cui, Binwu
Wang, Qingxiang Liu, Yeqiang Wang, Zhengyang Zhou, Yuxuan Liang and Yang Wang, 2025).
An exact project example shows the distinction without making any claim about an executed
45.27. Information gain and decision value can choose different queries                        783


Augur benchmark.
  Let X ∼ N (0, 1) and E ∼ N (0, 1) be independent, and set
                                         Y = X 2 − 1 + E.
Then E(Y | X = x) = x2 − 1, so X and Y are dependent, but
         Cov(X, Y ) = E(X 3 ) − E(X) = 0,          Var(Y ) = E(X 4 ) − E(X 2 )2 + 1 = 3.
The population Spearman correlation is also zero. To see this, the joint law of (X, Y )
is unchanged when X is replaced by −X. Since the normal distribution function obeys
Φ(−X) = 1 − Φ(X), the expectation of (Φ(X) − 1/2)(FY (Y ) − 1/2) is equal to its negative
and hence is zero. The independent Gaussian error makes the outcome continuous, so the
usual continuous-rank interpretation applies. Neither a Pearson nor a Spearman population
threshold bounded away from zero retains this pair on the basis of its marginal correlation.
   The intervention response is not zero: replacing X by x gives E{Y | do(X = x)} = x2 − 1.
Moving from zero to one changes the mean by one; moving from minus one to one changes
it by zero. Thus even the phrase “the effect of X” is incomplete without the intervention
contrast. In a banking scenario, X might be a standardized deviation from a reference pricing
point and the response might be curved. The example does not establish that such a curve
applies to deposits. It identifies a specific failure regime that a discovery proposal should cover
(Causal banking proposal, 2026n).
   A deterministic feature H = X 2 − 1 would reveal the association in this law: Var(H) =
Cov(H, Y ) = 2. That feature is a useful model representation, but it does not make H an
independently manipulable business action. It maps X and −X to the same value. The
interface must retain the original action, the transformation and the intervention contrast.
Discovering relations among engineered features can change the graph’s variables and its
feasible interventions. An agent should not relabel those features as independently adjustable
levers.
   Several remedies have distinct costs. Retaining all candidate pairs avoids this particular
screen but increases search and testing burden. A nonlinear dependence screen can detect
other features of the joint law, subject to its sampling assumptions and power. A scientifically
motivated feature family can make a restricted functional model plausible, but choosing
features after examining the final evaluation sample changes the procedure being assessed.
A language proposal of a nonlinear relation can be retained as a hypothesis without being
treated as verified evidence. The public prototype should compare these alternatives with
the same initial information and report which candidate relations were removed before graph
search began.


45.27       Information gain and decision value can choose different
            queries
Model disagreement or expected entropy reduction can be useful ways to select a new experiment.
The inspected Model Discovery Agent uses a disagreement surrogate for information gain
within its candidate mechanism pool (Murphy, 2026). The banking decision adds another
requirement: the acquired information must concern something that can change a feasible
action. A high information score need not meet that requirement. The following project
example makes the difference exact.
   Let a candidate world have two independent binary properties, R and S. Assume Pr(R =
1) = 1/10 and Pr(S = 1) = 1/2. Only R affects the offer decision: offering gives five units
784                                                                Causal analysis for a universal bank


when R = 1 and minus three when R = 0; not offering gives zero. Property S concerns
another graph feature that does not affect this target. The current expected offer value is
5/10 − 27/10 = −11/5, so the current action is no offer. Perfect observation of R would allow
offering only in its favorable state, with expected value 1/2. Perfect observation of S cannot
change the action and has decision value zero.
   Nevertheless, a query revealing S removes one bit of world uncertainty, while a query
revealing R removes only h2 (1/10) ≃ .468996 bits, where h2 (p) = −p log2 p − (1 − p) log2 (1 − p).
Maximizing entropy reduction over the full candidate world therefore prefers the decision-
irrelevant query. This is a difference between objectives, not a computational failure. It can
arise even when the candidate probabilities and the query likelihoods are exactly known.
  Now consider an informative but imperfect query Z about R, with Pr(Z = 1 | R = 1) = 4/5
and Pr(Z = 1 | R = 0) = 1/5. A positive answer gives posterior probability 4/13, and a
negative answer gives 1/37. Both are below the offer threshold 3/8, so the optimal action
remains no offer for either answer. This query has positive mutual information about R,
namely h2 (13/50) − h2 (1/5) ≃ .104818 bits, but zero value for this decision. Information that
changes beliefs can still be too weak to cross a relevant action threshold.
  A more accurate query has true-positive probability 19/20 and false-positive probability
1/20. Its positive posterior is 19/28 and its negative posterior is 1/172. Offering only after a
positive answer now gives ex ante value
                                 1 19          9 1             17
                                                    
                              5             −3             =      = .34.
                                10 20          10 20           50
This remains below the perfect-information value .5. A query cost of .1 per comparable future
decision would leave planning net value .24 under these stipulations. The same priced irrelevant
query has negative net value. The probability and cost assumptions are authored inputs, not
measured calibration or vendor prices (Causal banking proposal, 2026n).
   The lesson for an agent is precise. Retain a model-discrimination objective when scientific
understanding is the declared target. For a specified banking action, propagate candidate
worlds into utilities and ask whether the query can change the preferred action. If several bank
decisions share the graph, the utility may include several uses; their populations and weights
need to be stated rather than silently inferred. Customer constraints and acquisition costs
also belong in this calculation. Optimizing information gain is not wrong, but its connection
to investment value must be demonstrated.
   The prototype can implement these finite reference problems before conducting any expensive
experiment. It should reproduce the different query rankings, preserve the posterior update
and explain the dependence on the prior and loss. If a language-only query is assigned a
likelihood, that likelihood requires its own evidence; model confidence is not a substitute. A
correct implementation of this arithmetic would demonstrate decision accounting in a declared
finite problem. It would not establish that the candidate-world set includes the bank’s true
mechanism or that a real proposed query has the stipulated reliability.


45.28      From language guidance to a defensible discovery deci-
           sion
Language assistance can make a discovery workflow more useful by clarifying variables, locating
applicable knowledge, comparing algorithms and exposing conflicting assumptions. Its strongest
proposal is a supervised route from meaning to an explicitly restricted causal model. The
decisive question is whether that route improves the intervention decision while preserving
45.28. From language guidance to a defensible discovery decision                              785


what the observations cannot distinguish. A graph that is more fluent, more stable under
repeated prompting, or easier to fit need not answer that question.
   Consider a bank choosing a one-unit increase in a standardized deposit offer A at the start
of a month. Let Y be a standardized measure of the following month’s retained balances.
The population consists of accounts eligible when the offer is set; post-offer behavior cannot
become baseline information by renaming a column. For the example below, account histories
are independent, there is no interference, and the decision compares do(A = 1) with do(A = 0).
These are stipulated conditions for a calculation, not properties inferred from a real bank.
Shared branches, calendar shocks, selection and equilibrium responses would require a different
observation model.


45.28.1     A clock-compatible ambiguity that more observational data cannot
            remove

Two centered Gaussian structural models illustrate the information problem. In the first, the
offer changes the outcome:

          A = UA ,     Y = 12 A + UY ,      UA ⊥ UY ,      Var(UA ) = 2,   Var(UY ) = 23 .

  In the second, a pre-offer latent condition H affects both variables:

               A = H + V,        Y = H + W,           H, V, W independent N (0, 1).

  Both mechanisms respect the recorded order of offer and outcome. Both produce the same
nonsingular observed distribution,
                                             !!
                                     2 1
                      (A, Y ) ∼ N 0,              ,      E(Y | A = a) = 12 a.
                                     1 2

   The covariance determinant is three, so this ambiguity does not depend on a degenerate
observed table. Nevertheless, the intervention contrast is 1/2 in the first model and zero in the
second. Causal sufficiency would exclude the second model by assumption. The clock alone
does not exclude it. A language system that interprets the phrase “offer response” as proof of
a direct effect has supplied a scientific restriction that was absent from the numerical data.
   There is also an exact limit on a forced choice based only on these observations. If an
algorithm selects the first model with probability q, its success probabilities in the two worlds
are q and 1 − q, because the input distribution is identical. Their sum is one and the smaller
is at most one half, for any observational sample size. This statement includes randomized
algorithms. It does not say that all causal discovery is impossible; it identifies the information
missing in this particular comparison. An applicable assignment restriction or an intervention
could distinguish the worlds. A repeated description of the same observed association cannot.
   This distinction determines the numerical baseline. A PC analysis under causal sufficiency
and the stipulated order answers a conditional question. A latent-aware analysis must retain
the possibility of common causes. Neither method should be scored as wrong merely for
declining to select a single DAG when its declared model class permits both mechanisms. For
these two stipulated worlds the compatible effect values are {0, 1/2}. That pair is not an
exhaustive identified set over arbitrary latent models, and it is not a finite-sample confidence
set. A prototype should retain those qualifications in the returned object. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026x)
786                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


45.28.2     What the reported gains do and do not support

The available studies motivate several distinct product options. Retrieval can supply missing
definitions or restrictions; soft priors can guide a limited numerical search; statistical prompt-
ing can make existing numerical evidence intelligible; and debate can organize competing
explanations. The appropriate comparator changes with the role. A retrieved definition is
compared with a dictionary and a documented expert rule, whereas a search prior is compared
with the same numerical algorithm and resource budget.
   The primary results also preclude a single claim of uniform improvement. LACR’s retrieved-
document condition reduces ASIA skeleton F1 from 1 to 0.73, while additional knowledge
improves CORONARY. Its reported perfect orientation score is conditional on recovered true-
positive edges. Missing and false edges therefore remain outside that particular denominator.
(Zhang et al., 2024b) Darvariu and colleagues report useful combined mutual-information and
language priors, especially with limited search, but mutual information alone performs best
on Child in the reported comparison. Keeping positive search support is useful; it does not
calibrate the probability of a causal effect. (Darvariu et al., 2024)
   Statistical prompting is similarly task dependent. In Takayama and colleagues’ Table 3,
the Sachs PC baseline has F1 0.44, the language condition without the statistical prompt has
0.52, and the two statistical-prompt conditions have 0.29 and 0.27. Other algorithm/dataset
combinations improve. These are comparisons within the authors’ experiment, not local
replications or evidence that one algorithm always dominates. Their lower fit criterion and
their closer-to-reference graph are different outcomes. (Takayama et al., 2024)
   Cohrs and colleagues report query-order agreement of 0.510 and 0.870 for their two model
configurations, and a data-based method has higher SACHS F1 than either language method.
Their answer-proportion null concerns the response process. Even a correctly calibrated test
of that null would not automatically test conditional independence in the bank population.
(Cohrs et al., 2024) The response-count calculation developed earlier in this chapter supplies a
separate finite-binomial counterexample; it should be reused as a diagnostic, not represented
as a new model experiment.
  The newer multi-agent comparison combines algorithm selection and code execution with
graph debate. Its inspected version reports that additional debate rounds can degrade Survey
and Auto results and that the complete workflow consumes 16–25 times the tokens of standard
baselines. Those findings support a bounded single-round comparator and full cost accounting,
without establishing bank economics. (Le et al., 2024) The 2026 argumentation approach
makes conflicts explicit but retains hard semantic constraints after an irreversible preliminary
skeleton reduction. Its synthetic descriptions are generated with access to the true graph
and its runtime comparison omits external model latency. These limits motivate neutral
descriptions, misleading-description controls and complete timing. (Li and Russo, 2026)
   Exposure and semantics require separate tests. The accessible-corpus study by Feng and
colleagues links relation frequency to performance and examines contradictory statements and
context changes. Its scope does not establish the behavior of every closed model. Moreover,
a changed context may genuinely change the causal claim. A fixed-world paraphrase test
must preserve the population, timing and intervention; a changed-world test must change its
reference answer accordingly. (Feng, 2024) Contradiction reduction and graph agreement are
useful diagnostics, but neither is a substitute for effect truth. The inspected hallucination
study explicitly retains that distinction. (Sng et al., 2024)
   Barakati and colleagues provide a domain application that usefully exposes the translation
problem. Their materials study maps microscopy-derived unit-cell descriptors to literature
terminology, queries relationships using LangChain and a language model, and reruns gCastle
45.28. From language guidance to a defensible discovery decision                              787


PC with required and forbidden relations. The stated response schema includes insufficient
information. This is a concrete architecture for connecting measurements, terminology and
candidate restrictions. Its comparison chiefly discusses agreement between inferred pathways
and prior LiNGAM findings. Agreement does not establish an intervention oracle, and spatial
unit cells are not automatically independent samples. The abstract uses the term fine-tuning,
whereas the inspected methods describe querying literature and give no reproducible training
recipe or checkpoint. The proposal should therefore retain the documented workflow without
inferring a trained artifact or calibrated effect uncertainty. The linked repository is a separate
reuse lead requiring its own revision, rights and execution review. (Barakati et al., 2025)


45.28.3     Missing answers and recorded identity are part of the causal inter-
            face

Tracing the pinned research code reveals obligations that are less visible in a method name. In
the selected causal_GPT interface, the pure PC wrapper reads variable descriptions and stored
language answers. Its numerical pvalue method pools the two query orders, then converts a
decision to zero or one. A missing stored row returns zero. The advertised weighted-vote branch
also returns zero beside an unfinished implementation marker. Thus unavailable evidence,
an unsupported aggregation method and a dependence decision can share one numerical
representation. These observations concern the inspected source, not measured frequencies in
an installed package. (IPL-UV causal GPT contributors, 2024)
   The hybrid path contains a genuine numerical fallback for queries outside the selected
language-variable/conditioning scope. Within that scope it collects unanswered queries, uses
temporary decisions while assembling them, and requests their answers in the surrounding
driver. That driver also saves result metadata with fixed model and temperature strings despite
accepting different values as arguments. For example, a configured model B at temperature
0.2 would still receive the inspected record’s fixed model label and temperature 0.6. This is a
literal assignment trace, not an API call. A comparison cannot be reproduced reliably if result
identity and actual configuration can diverge. (IPL-UV causal GPT contributors, 2024)
   The proposal should therefore adopt the useful separation of language and numerical query
channels while replacing the ambiguous interchange. A language-answer object needs the target
statement, operational definitions, source evidence, model revision, settings, parsing status and
an explicit unknown state. A statistical test object needs its observations, null, sampling law
and calibration. A pending query must not be published as a completed dependence judgment.
Unsupported weighted voting should refuse until implemented and checked. Result identity
should be populated from the actual request and response, with missing metadata retained as
missing.


45.28.4     A token score does not have the same meaning in three discovery
            engines

The five pinned LLM-and-SCD notebooks expose a complete research route from an initial
graph and bootstrap summaries through two prompts to constrained rediscovery. In a selected
collection cell, the code sums the first token’s top-five probability mass only when the token is
exactly Yes or yes. It separately accumulates No or no. It does not identify all semantically
equivalent strings or turn the unreported mass into an explicit uncertainty object. The resulting
score is a property of the prompted token distribution, not a probability that an edge exists in
the bank. (Masataka Takayama and contributors, 2024)
  An exact authored example makes the parsing boundary visible. Suppose the five tokens
788                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


have masses 0.96, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005 and 0.005, assigned to Yes, No, a newline, I and It. The
literal affirmative score is 0.96. Change only the first token to a leading-space Yes; the exact-
string collector assigns affirmative score zero, although a whitespace-normalized semantic class
still has mass 0.96. These are constructed input distributions, not observed endpoint outputs.
They show why unrecognized formats and truncated token lists need explicit treatment before
any scientific constraint is created. Simple normalization would fix this example but would not
establish causal calibration or solve multi-token answer semantics. (Causal banking proposal,
2026x)
  The conversion then magnifies a parsing choice. The selected notebook marks a score
below 0.05 as forbidden, above 0.95 as required, and the interval between them as unknown.
Consequently the two constructed representations above become opposite hard constraints.
At exactly 0.95 the notebook returns unknown, while the inspected paper’s Algorithm 2 uses
an inclusive upper threshold. The 0.05 boundary is unknown in both. The notebook commit
predates the inspected paper revision, so the discrepancy is a version-alignment obligation,
not evidence about the authors’ later experimental execution. (Masataka Takayama and
contributors, 2024; Takayama et al., 2024)
   The target backend introduces another semantic choice. The PC conversion creates required
and forbidden directed-edge objects; exact search receives an allowed supergraph, in which a
high score permits rather than forces an edge. The proposed pinned DirectLiNGAM target
documents directed-path prior knowledge. Its meaning must be checked against the notebook’s
direct-impact question and the chosen matrix convention. For a chain A → M → Y , no
direct A → Y edge exists, but an A-to-Y directed path does. Converting “no direct impact”
to “no directed path” rules out this chain and its mediated effect. A common matrix with
numbers −1, 0, 1 does not make these three contracts interchangeable. (Masataka Takayama
and contributors, 2024; LiNGAM project, 2026b)
  Notebook dependency installation is not locked to a reproducible environment. The separate
cycle-conversion notebook also passes the data positionally into a constructor whose first
parameter is random_state in the later inspected target, before calling fit with the data.
Compatibility must be established at an actual chosen dependency revision; this source
comparison does not demonstrate what ran in the historical notebook. Acyclic conversion and
choosing among repaired constraints by fit on the same observations are further parts of the
adaptive procedure, and must accompany any later uncertainty claim. (Masataka Takayama
and contributors, 2024; LiNGAM project, 2026b)
   LLM-CD offers a useful alternative representation. The inspected evaluation checks generated
relations against directed reachability. Its backend wrappers serialize ancestral constraints
separately from absent edges and, for one backend, order constraints. This is consistent with
the primary paper’s distinction between ancestral priors and local adjacency. The paper also
states that the factorization of path priors is approximate and that their common strength
is problem dependent. (LLM-CD contributors, 2025a; Ban et al., 2023) Adoption still needs
a bounded adapter: the selected wrappers use shared working paths and shell calls whose
exit status is not checked before parsing, then remove intermediate files. A nested backend
license does not resolve missing root-project terms. The proposed adapter should retain typed
constraints, use isolated run directories, check process results and preserve all scientific inputs
and outputs. Its terms and dependency boundaries must be resolved before enabling it.


45.28.5     A public and generated prototype with a decision criterion

A useful first prototype has two stages. Deterministic semantic fixtures check missing answers,
unsupported methods, token variants, exact threshold boundaries, graph endpoint preservation,
45.28. From language guidance to a defensible discovery decision                             789


cycles, edge-versus-path conversion and request/result identity. These tests are cheap and
have known expected answers. They establish an adapter contract; they do not estimate live
model quality. Only then should the team profile a matched discovery experiment and register
its final design.
  The experiment should split by mechanism family. Repeated numerical samples, variable
names, retrieved packets and prompts belong inside a mechanism’s cluster. The Gaussian
pair above is a compulsory ambiguity case, accompanied by causally sufficient, non-Gaussian
and latent cases with explicit clocks. Generator truth and effect oracles remain outside the
prompts. Natural descriptions, neutral renamed descriptions and deliberately misleading
descriptions are crossed with no retrieval, applicable original evidence, wrong-domain evidence
and contradiction. Removing meaningful definitions changes the information supplied, so the
comparison must say when it tests robustness and when it tests the value of information.
  Each language arm needs the same numerical inputs and a declared comparator: a dictio-
nary/clock baseline; PC or FCI under the appropriate assumptions; score or non-Gaussian
methods within their qualified regimes; language-only proposals; and soft or hard guidance
with declared strength and refusal rules. Final graphs alone are insufficient. Record class
and endpoint retention, invalid outputs, valid abstentions, conditional effect-set retention and
width, and downstream action regret under known truth. Include every requested case in the
denominator, including parse failures, timeouts, empty outputs and conflicting constraints.
Measure total calls, tokens, retries, numerical resources, latency and adjudication effort.
   Before final runs, freeze versions, rights, splits, targets, sample sizes, replication counts,
tolerances, primary paired comparisons and multiplicity treatment. Development profiling
may set resource caps; it cannot become an unannounced final experiment. Prompt variants
and prior strengths must not be selected on the final mechanisms. An optional live model
experiment needs the chosen endpoint’s actual revision and measured costs, but none of these
design steps requires bank data or a paid experiment now.
   The banking example supplies a transparent economic threshold. Stipulate USD 200 per
outcome unit and USD 60 for the unit offer increase. Net values are USD 40 in the direct-
effect world and minus USD 60 in the latent world. If a planner assigns probability p to the
former, the expected net action value is 100p − 60. Because the observed likelihood is the
same, additional observational records alone cannot update those odds within this two-world
comparison. At p = 0.9 the expected value is USD 30, while perfect knowledge would produce
USD 36 by taking the action only in the favorable world. Thus USD 6 per decision is an
upper bound on the expected value of any information experiment under those assumptions.
At p = 0.5 it is USD 20. A real noisy experiment supplies less information and incurs costs;
neither number is bank ROI or an authorized spending budget. (Causal banking proposal,
2026x)
   The resulting recommendation is to reuse typed evidence, explicit conflict handling and
bounded search guidance as design references; to defer enabled package integration until the
specified contracts are verified; and to reject automatic conversion of response agreement into
causal confidence. The unresolved scientific task is to justify useful graph/effect uncertainty
for the complete adaptive procedure in declared regimes. The small-language-model discovery
lead currently has metadata but no acquired original; its methods cannot support a technical
comparison yet. Broader literature coverage and that original remain explicit survey work.
They do not prevent the proposed public/generated prototype from testing the concrete
semantic and decision boundaries established here.
790                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


45.29      Expert-guided graph ensembles and their intervention
           limits
A bank building a diagram from several discovery algorithms will often face agreement about
a relationship but disagreement about its direction. The methods may also miss different
relationships because they use different scores, tests and structural restrictions. Asking a
domain expert to resolve selected disagreements is a plausible use of an assistant. The design
question is what the expert is being asked, how its answer changes the graph, and whether the
resulting graph supports the bank’s intervention query.
   Tench and Demeester propose a dynamic expert-guided ensemble that distinguishes adjacency
from orientation. It counts how many component graphs contain any edge between a pair,
considers pairs in descending frequency, and adds directed edges subject to an acyclicity check.
A lower adjacency threshold determines which pairs are eligible. For eligible pairs without a
strict majority, it asks the expert whether a plausible causal relationship exists. A separate
threshold controls when direction votes suffice and when expert orientation is requested. The
procedure uses equal component weights and a finite query budget. This is greedy graph
construction; the term model averaging does not establish a Bayesian posterior over causal
models. (Tench and Demeester, 2026)


45.29.1    An expert’s causal ordering is not a direct edge

The source deliberately permits an expert to answer about a direct or indirect causal path.
This is weaker than knowing whether two nodes are adjacent in the full graph. In a stipulated
offer–uptake–balance chain O → U → Y , changing the offer may affect balance through uptake
even though O → Y is not a direct edge. An expert can answer the path question correctly
while accepting a spurious direct connection proposed by a component method. The paper
recognizes this distinction in its simulated expert and compares it with an expert that knows
direct edges. (Tench and Demeester, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026al)
   The proposed bank interface should therefore carry the proposition being elicited: adjacency,
ancestry, orientation conditional on adjacency, or a temporal exclusion. It should also permit
insufficient knowledge. A reply about plausible ancestry cannot silently become proof of a
direct edge, and a forced binary answer cannot represent every legitimate uncertainty state.
The set of variables matters: marginalizing uptake changes the observed-variable graph even
when the underlying mechanism is unchanged.
  The method’s output is a DAG. Its component comparison includes FCI, while its noisy
benchmarks can contain latent confounding. A directed output cannot by itself retain every
bidirected or unresolved endpoint in a latent graph. Before an adapter is proposed, the
conversion from each component’s graph type must be explicit, with unsupported endpoints
preserved or refused. Acyclicity checks alone do not establish compatibility with an input
equivalence class or identify an intervention in the presence of hidden common causes. (Tench
and Demeester, 2026)


45.29.2    Frequency, diversity and structural compatibility

For one binary question, suppose eleven voters each have probability 3/4 of being correct.
Under independent errors their majority is correct with probability
                        11

If all eleven instead copy the same 3/4-correct signal, majority correctness remains 3/4. These
are two authored probability laws with the same individual accuracy. They show why individual
competence alone cannot justify improvement toward certainty. The paper itself acknowledges
that algorithms share data and often share statistical principles. Its discussion motivates
diversity, but does not estimate a calibrated graph probability from vote frequency. (Tench
and Demeester, 2026; Causal banking proposal project, 2026al)
  Even individually valid DAGs can produce incompatible edge majorities. Consider the three
graphs

                                    G1 = {A → B, B → C},
                                    G2 = {B → C, C → A},                                 (45.9)

Each is acyclic, yet every edge of A → B → C → A has frequency 2/3. A greedy acyclicity
rule must discard or reconsider an edge. Its result can depend on tie handling and earlier
choices. Returning one DAG makes the output structurally admissible under that rule, but
it neither preserves every component claim nor proves which disputed edge is false. (Causal
banking proposal project, 2026al)


45.29.3     The reported evidence is informative and conditional

The main experiments use seven benchmark network structures with synthetic categorical
samples, clean and corrupted versions, four sample sizes from 100 to 100,000, and twenty
column orderings. The principal simulated expert is correct on 70% of existence questions and
90% of orientation questions. Thresholds of zero for adjacency and 0.9 for orientation, with a
budget of twice the node count, were selected using separate randomly generated networks.
The paper reports broad gains in its graph scores, alongside a precision–recall tradeoff and
varying comparison denominators when algorithms fail or return undefined precision. These
are reported experiments; they are not newly reproduced results in this proposal. (Tench and
Demeester, 2026)
  The real-model appendix is narrower than the simulated-expert study.             It uses
gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07 on five clean networks, excluding Pathfinder because its variable
names lack the needed semantics and Formed because many edges represent diagnostic rather
than causal relations. Expert responses are cached across seeds and sample sizes. Both
argument orders are queried, with disagreement causing a fallback to component voting.
The reported per-response orientation and existence accuracies are not the accuracy of that
combined fallback policy. (Tench and Demeester, 2026)

            Reported case             Orientation accuracy Existence accuracy
            Mean across five networks                93.3%              66.4%
            Property                                 83.9%              43.9%
            Alarm                                    82.8%              52.2%

Property’s existence accuracy falls below the paper’s better-than-random expert assumption.
A useful mean therefore cannot replace domain-specific evidence, and accuracy on all possible
pairs need not equal accuracy on the difficult pairs selected adaptively by an ensemble. Cached
responses also do not become twenty independent expert realizations because the numerical
algorithms are rerun twenty times. The appendix’s near reconstruction of the Asia network
raises a memorization concern; unsuccessful recall of another full network cannot establish
that its concepts or fragments were absent from training. (Tench and Demeester, 2026)
792                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The source states that it supplies no formal graph-recovery guarantee and has not empirically
qualified continuous or mixed observations. Its cost discussion includes component discovery,
expert requests and structural-distance scoring. The proposed comparison should likewise
retain timeout, memory and invalid- output denominators, distinguishing a conditional score on
successful outputs from all-request performance. The source’s proposed imputation sensitivity
analysis does not supply the missing runtime results or a bank operating cost.

45.29.4    Resolve the printed query contract before reuse

The prose says that a fixed budget bounds queries and exhausted decisions fall back to majority
voting. The printed Algorithm 1 leaves two details unresolved. For an existence query, the
counter increment lies inside the branch reached only when the expert accepts the connection.
With three eligible minority connections, budget one, and three rejections, a literal trace
makes three expert calls while the printed counter remains zero. Separately, when an accepted
adjacency has two legal directions, neither reaches the orientation threshold, and no budget
remains, the printed conditional chain has no final branch adding the majority direction. An
example with direction votes 3/4 and 1/4, threshold 9/10 and budget zero therefore leaves the
edge unassigned under the printed chain. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026al)
   These are specification discrepancies, not verified defects in the released implementation.
Resolving them requires an immutable source version and its tests and call logs. A proposed
adapter should count every attempted external call, distinguish logical questions from the
two argument-order requests, account for retries and invalid answers, and define the behavior
at exhaustion. Caching needs a key that binds the variable meanings, full request, model
snapshot and relevant settings. Otherwise a cost-saving cache can silently reuse evidence for
a different scientific question. The method and data lead in the paper are useful acquisition
routes; package names and reported license labels are not sufficient permission or provenance
for direct adoption.

45.29.5    A selected graph still has to answer the intervention query

For a separate exact example, consider two standardized observational summaries X, Y whose
temporal ordering has not been established. Let ρ = 3/5. The following two zero-mean
Gaussian structural models use independent errors within each model:

                                       Var(ϵX ) = 1,   Var(ϵY ) = 1 − ρ2 ,

                           M2 :        Y = ηY ,   X = ρY + ηX ,
                                       Var(ηY ) = 1,   Var(ηX ) = 1 − ρ2 .

Both imply covariance 3/5 1 and hence the same observational distribution. Their effects
on the mean of Y of increasing the intervention level of X by one unit differ:
                                           3
                                  τ (M1 ) = ,      τ (M2 ) = 0.                          (45.11)

More algorithms fitted to the same distribution do not identify the missing direction. Truthful
temporal restrictions, suitable experiments or independently justified structural knowledge can
eliminate a candidate; that extra information must be stated. The example does not override
a known banking information clock. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026al)
  Suppose a one-unit increase in Y is provisionally valued at USD 100 and the intervention
costs USD 40. The two compatible margins are USD 20 and USD −40. Treating a 90% graph
45.30. Domain knowledge as evidence for a causal graph                                        793


vote as probability for M1 gives effect 27/50 and margin USD 14, but the vote has supplied
no probabilistic calibration that warrants that calculation as expected value. A decision
under unresolved model ambiguity must retain the compatible effects or adopt an explicitly
justified probability model. This is an authored planning illustration, not evidence of model
performance or bank returns. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026al)
  The proposal should therefore retain expert-guided averaging as a candidate for generating
and reviewing diagrams. A public prototype comparison can use known generated mechanisms,
withheld domains, correlated component failures, wrong expert assertions, budget exhaustion
and incompatible graph endpoints. It should compare static aggregation, selective expert
queries, a numerical method without expert input and a workflow that preserves unresolved
graph classes. The outcomes should include the correctness of the intervention answer,
supported refusal, retained ambiguity, all physical requests and total review cost. Graph scores
remain useful diagnostics, but qualification of an intervention service requires its own evidence.


45.30       Domain knowledge as evidence for a causal graph
A collections manager considering a payment holiday needs to distinguish a plausible story
from an intervention that improves customer outcomes. A language model may suggest that
financial strain affects delinquency, that servicing changes financial strain, and that earlier
delinquency affects the servicing offer. Each statement needs a population, a time index,
a variable definition and an evidential basis. Joining the three statements without those
qualifications can create a cycle whose meaning is unclear. A retrieval system can help locate
the underlying evidence, but a retrieved sentence does not by itself establish an invariant
structural mechanism. Two recent clinical studies make the promise and the limitations of
this assistance concrete.


45.30.1     Graph elicitation and the meaning of completeness

Aziz and Brookhart study a hypothetical comparison of statins with no treatment for preventing
cardiovascular disease. They run four prompting strategies on GPT-4o and a zero-shot strategy
on GPT-o1, with three separate conversations per configuration. Two author reviewers assess
consistency, acyclicity, source accuracy, completeness and prompt adherence. This is a study
of fifteen outputs in one familiar clinical scenario, rather than an estimate of performance over
a population of banking questions. The original was published on 30 October 2025.Aziz and
Brookhart (2025)
   Its completeness criterion asks whether the graph contains seven groups of variables drawn
from an ASCVD risk score. This is a useful check for conspicuous omissions, but it does not
validate the graph’s arrows or establish that its adjustment set identifies the statin effect.
Predictors can have different causal roles: a pretreatment common cause, a mediator and a
selection variable cannot be treated interchangeably simply because each predicts the outcome.
In a bank, a strong arrears predictor measured after a servicing offer may be an outcome of
that offer. Including it in a list is different from correctly deciding whether to adjust for it.
   Table 1 and the article’s accompanying text report fourteen acyclic graphs and seven graphs
containing six of the seven criteria. The seven-of-fifteen count does not support the abstract’s
“more than half” wording. Race is absent from all fifteen outputs. That is a reproducible
observation about the study’s criterion; it does not establish a universal requirement to insert a
particular attribute into every causal model. A social attribute’s role needs an explicit account
of the processes it represents and the target population. Blindly adding a variable to improve
a checklist score could conceal the same scientific problem as omitting it.Aziz and Brookhart
794                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


(2025); Causal banking proposal project (2026bg)
   The study also separates producing citations from producing reliable evidence. One-shot
outputs supply sources but include nonexistent references and incorrect titles, dates or author
details. Chain-of-thought outputs give explanations without sources in all three runs. The
GPT-o1 zero-shot configuration consistently supplies references and code, yet one code output
needs manual repair. Its third run is described as supplying nine sources and then assessed
using denominators of six; the original outputs are needed before aggregating that run’s
citation accuracy. The source assessments described in the paper use title and abstract review,
which is weaker than checking that primary methods and results support a particular causal
arrow.Aziz and Brookhart (2025)
   One instruction-based output contains arrows in both directions between statin use and
cholesterol. The authors correctly identify the need for temporally indexed nodes if feedback is
intended. The banking counterpart is Dt → At → Dt+1 , where Dt is delinquency information
available before action At . Collapsing Dt and Dt+1 into a single “delinquency” node loses
the information clock. A graph assistant should request that missing distinction rather than
silently reverse an arrow to satisfy a syntactic check. The study supports a brainstorming and
source-checking role; it supplies no validation of a bank effect estimator.


45.30.2     Retrieval helps under a particular reference and query

Lin and colleagues combine language models, retrieval and observational discovery for chronic
low back pain. Their February 2026 medRxiv original is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed result.
They use baseline observations from 1,868 participants and a fourteen-variable expert reference.
Crucially, the authors explicitly state that this reference contains cycles and is not a DAG.
The reference was developed from clinical expertise and a literature synthesis; it is a declared
comparison target, not observed intervention truth.Lin et al. (2026)
   The three knowledge systems share Mistral 7B-Instruct v0.3. Ordinary retrieval supplies
document chunks selected by vector similarity. Knowledge-graph retrieval extracts entities
and relations, merges entities, forms communities and retrieves entities, attached relations,
community summaries and supporting text. The paper describes 600-token chunks with 100-
token overlap, an 8,000-token retrieval budget, and a pipeline involving constrained extraction,
a graph database and community clustering. These are descriptions of the authors’ system;
they do not establish that its dependencies are pinned, licensed for the proposed distribution
or operationally integrated here.Lin et al. (2026)
   Both retrieval systems use the same source articles that the experts used to construct the
comparison graph. This is an informative test of reconstructing an aligned body of knowledge.
It does not measure performance when the literature is incomplete, contradictory, selected
by a different team, or independent of the reference adjudicators. The authors discuss this
alignment explicitly. Their argument that the model predates publication of the expert graph
also does not by itself authenticate the model’s training corpus or exclude related earlier
content. The appropriate extension is a deliberately held-out reference and document design,
not a declaration that contamination has been ruled out.
   For the data component, the paper describes hill climbing with local generalized linear models,
BIC scores and 500 bootstrap samples. A thresholded consensus graph forms the initial model.
The system then combines its edges with the knowledge system’s proposals and asks a further
direction question when both directions are suggested. Plausibility, association, temporality
and a direct causal query are separate prompt conditions. Their relative performance matters
as much as the strongest result.Lin et al. (2026)

reason to recover the original edge records, not a reason to invent corrected results.


45.30.3     Direct edges, indirect effects and feedback need different objects

The chronic-pain plausibility and temporality questions explicitly allow a relationship “through
one or more intermediate variables.” Their answers therefore need not describe direct adjacency
among the measured variables. For the chain

                          A −→ M −→ Y,          E = {(A, M ), (M, Y )},                     (45.12)

A is an ancestor of Y even though (A, Y ) ∈   / E. A positive indirect-effect answer cannot be
inserted as a direct edge without changing the graph and possibly its conditional independences.
Conversely, when a variable is unmeasured, a projected graph may legitimately have different
edge semantics. The interface must state which object it is constructing. The paper’s source
text is sufficient to identify the mismatch that needs checking; it is not sufficient to reconstruct
every edge’s intended semantics.Lin et al. (2026); Causal banking proposal project (2026bg)
  Taking a union of proposed edges also has no universal accuracy guarantee. Starting from
the correct two-edge set in equation (45.12), adding the false edge Y → A produces two true
positives, one false positive and no false negatives. Thus
                                            2 TP       4
                                F1 =                  = < 1.                                (45.13)
                                       2 TP + FP + FN  5
It also creates a directed three-cycle without any reciprocal pair. Resolving only two-way pairs
would not remove it. This exact example does not assert that the paper’s code necessarily
produces such a failure. It shows why the observed nonnegative changes in its result table
cannot be promoted to a theorem that combining knowledge and data always improves the
graph.Causal banking proposal project (2026bg)
796                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


   There is a further distinction in the observational comparison. Moralization drops arrowheads
and connects parents of a common child. For A → M ← B, it adds the A–B link even though
that link is absent from the original skeleton. Consequently, the paper’s moralized-graph
comparison is not simply a comparison of adjacencies after ignoring direction. Good agreement
on that object cannot identify a unique causal ordering. Similarly, a cyclic expert reference
and a DAG learner require an explicit account of the representation mismatch before their
distance is interpreted as scientific error.
   A useful banking representation retains the proposition type, time horizon, population,
supporting span and evidence strength for each proposed relation. It distinguishes a direct
cause from an ancestor, an association, an ontological relationship and a modeler’s assumption.
A type hierarchy or a semantic link in a knowledge graph is not automatically a causal edge.
Hard constraints can narrow the graph search when justified by an information clock or design
rule. Uncertain literature claims should remain revisable evidence; treating them as inviolable
constraints can exclude the true graph. When sources conflict, returning the alternatives
preserves information that forced orientation destroys.


45.30.4     Identical records can support opposite investment decisions

An exact illustration explains why better graph agreement alone is insufficient for a product
decision. Let A denote a centered, standardized servicing intensity and L a centered loss index,
where one loss unit is stipulated to equal USD 100. Consider two authored Gaussian structural
models. In the first, all exogenous variables are independent and

                 A = UA ,      L = − 12 A + ε,     Var(UA ) = 1,     Var(ε) = 34 .          (45.14)

In the second, U, ηA , ηL are mutually independent centered Gaussians, each with variance 1/2,
and
                                A = U + ηA ,     L = −U + ηL .                         (45.15)
Both models imply exactly the same centered bivariate Gaussian observed law:
                                        !                   !
                                     A            1   −1/2
                                 Var        =              .                                (45.16)
                                     L           −1/2  1

In the first model, replacing the action equation by a one-unit higher intervention lowers
expected loss by one half unit. In the second, replacing the action equation leaves U and L
unchanged, so the effect is zero. The observed regression slope is −1/2 in both. No amount of
replication of this observed joint law distinguishes the two intervention effects. The Gaussian
loss index is an illustrative local model, not a claim that realized bank losses can have an
unrestricted negative support. Causal banking proposal project (2026bg)
  Suppose the higher action costs USD 20 per eligible customer over the declared horizon,
with no other monetized effects. Its modeled incremental margin is

                  V = −100{E[L | do(A = a + 1)] − E[L | do(A = a)]} − 20,                   (45.17)

which equals USD 30 in the first model and USD −20 in the second. Retaining both models
therefore retains the range [−20, 30]. Under a separately declared subjective weight w on the
first model, expected margin is 50w − 20, positive only when w > 2/5. A language-model
vote fraction, retrieval score or graph F1 is not that probability. The practical task is to find
evidence that can distinguish the models: an admissible randomization, a justified additional
measurement, or an independently supported restriction. More fluent explanations of the same
observed correlation cannot do so.Causal banking proposal project (2026bg)
45.31. Factual support in a causal assistant                                                 797


45.30.5     A public evaluation and a concrete integration decision

The proposal should first test graph assistance on public documents and generated cases with
declared causal laws. The evaluation needs two distinct targets. One is reconstruction of a
specified expert account, for which alternative adjudicators and documented disagreements are
legitimate evidence. The other is recovery of causal implications under a known data-generating
law. Conflating these targets would reward agreement with an expert even when the expert’s
graph is incomplete. The Gaussian pair above provides an inexpensive refusal case: a system
given only the shared observed law should retain both effects unless the task supplies additional
identifying information.
   Cases should also include indirect-only relations, long cycles, feedback requiring time
expansion, unmeasured common causes, contradictory papers and evidence that is silent about
direction. Keep the adjudication documents separate from the retrieval corpus for the primary
test; report same-corpus reconstruction as a different condition. Hold out domains as well
as individual documents. Match source access, context allowance and reviewer effort across
data-only, expert-only, ontology-assisted, LLM-only, ordinary-retrieval, graph-retrieval and
combined systems. This tests whether constructing a knowledge graph is worth its additional
extraction, maintenance and review cost.
  Measure source identity and span entailment, variable/time alignment, direct-edge and
ancestral accuracy, equivalence-class retention, abstention, valid identification and decision
consequences separately. Repeat prompts and seeds; do not treat correlated edge votes from a
shared corpus as independent experts. Record graph-building tokens, query tokens, latency,
correction effort and maintenance alongside numerical scores. An 8,000-token context cap does
not equalize the cost of building the two retrieval systems. The public study should predeclare
thresholds for useful assistance and costs before inspecting the held-out results. There is no
measured financial benefit in the two clinical papers that can set those thresholds for a bank.
   For implementation planning, adopt the evidence-provenance pattern and the separation of
variable definition, relation proposal and graph validation. Integrate retrieval behind a typed
interface only after pinning the underlying corpus, software, model and rights. Retain the
ordinary-retrieval comparator; the results do not justify porting an entire graph-retrieval stack
in advance of a matched benefit test. Reject unconditional union, compulsory orientation
and silent conversion of an indirect relation into a direct edge. The chronic-pain appendix’s
Boolean answer schema and fallback to general knowledge lack an explicit abstention channel;
the proposed interface should supply one. Lin et al. (2026)
   The same reviewed request can pass through a library call, CLI or MCP tool. It should carry
the target, variable clocks, corpus identities, proposed relation types and permitted operations,
and return evidence-backed alternatives and identification status. Retrieved prose is evidence
to inspect, not an instruction that authorizes another tool call. A cycle or unsupported edge
should produce a specific unresolved result that downstream estimation preserves. These are
proposed contracts, not demonstrated cross-repository integrations. Public prototype merit
must precede an expensive experiment with private bank data.


45.31       Factual support in a causal assistant
A retrieved explanation of a lending policy can be well supported by its cited document
and still leave the causal question unanswered. The document may describe association,
concern a different customer population, or rely on an unverified assignment assumption.
Wang and colleagues’ survey of factuality organizes evaluation and improvement around
knowledge, retrieval and domain specificity Wang et al. (2023). Its selected arXiv edition is
798                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


useful background for designing evidence assistance. Its taxonomy and surveyed examples
should not be read as independent validations of each underlying method or as a theorem
about causal diagrams.
   The survey scopes factuality around determinable, undisputed facts. A causal proposal
frequently includes a different type of claim: whether a servicing offer would change default,
whether selection creates a spurious association, or whether a time-indexed edge is needed.
These questions can remain disputed even when dates, document quotations and variable
definitions are correct. The assistant therefore needs an explicit distinction between what a
source says, whether that statement is warranted outside the source, and whether it supports
the proposed causal role for the population and time in question.


45.31.1    Match the evaluation to the claim

The survey distinguishes rule-based, neural, human and language-model evaluation. Lexical
overlap and semantic similarity can help locate likely support, but neither is sufficient for
entailment. “The offer causes repayment” and “the offer does not cause repayment” share most
words while disagreeing on the decision-relevant proposition. Even a citation that accurately
supports the first sentence may describe a randomized intervention in another setting or an
author’s unsupported interpretation of a regression. Checking attribution and checking causal
identification answer different questions.
   Atomic claim checking offers a useful design discipline: split the output into claims whose
support can be examined. For example, an assistant might assert that treatment preceded the
outcome, an instrument predicts treatment, its exclusion restriction holds, and the estimated
effect exceeds cost. The first two may have direct documentation or statistical evidence.
Exclusion usually requires a structural argument; an effect-above-cost claim additionally needs
the target population, units, uncertainty and cost assumptions. One global “factual” score
cannot make these evidence types interchangeable.
   A proposed evidence record should therefore retain the exact source span, edition, scope and
claim role; distinguish quotation from project inference; and preserve a conflict or unsupported
status. Human reviewers can assess scientific assumptions, but the survey also discusses
subjectivity and inconsistency in human evaluation. Model judges introduce their own bias
and domain limitations. Agreement among judges that share the same document, training
exposure or prompting pattern is not an independent scientific replication. Calibrating a judge
for citation entailment would still leave causal identification and monetary decision quality to
be assessed separately.


45.31.2    Retrieval and structured knowledge help under stated conditions

The survey identifies failure routes involving missing or conflicting information, misleading
evidence, distraction and misinterpretation. This suggests concrete proposal requirements.
Evidence search should preserve contradictory passages and their populations, intervention
definitions and dates. Retrieval should allow “insufficient evidence” rather than making
general knowledge completion an obligatory final step. An assistant should explain when a
source settles a definition, offers a mechanism hypothesis or reports an identified effect under
assumptions. Increasing retrieved volume does not by itself resolve disagreement among those
roles.
   Structured knowledge can improve entity and query mapping. For banking, this could
distinguish an application score from a post-decision monitoring score, or connect two names
for the same branch. A knowledge-graph relation such as “associated with”, “measured after”
45.32. An autonomous discovery workflow and the limits of its authority                       799


or “mentioned together” is still not a direct causal edge. An indirect mechanism should not
silently become a direct edge among observed variables. Temporal feedback requires explicit
time indexing or an appropriate cyclic model, rather than an acyclic drawing that hides the
feedback. The assistant’s contribution is to expose candidate interpretations and supporting
evidence so that graph assumptions can be reviewed.
  The survey discusses debate and interactive retrieval as strategies described in the literature.
Those accounts motivate candidate workflows, not verified superiority of a multi-agent imple-
mentation in this proposal. Several agents repeating an unsupported premise may amplify
confidence without adding information. A useful design would require an independently sourced
challenge, record the unresolved disagreement and retain an abstention route. Its merit must
be measured against simpler retrieval and human-assisted baselines at matched evidence and
review budgets.
   The survey’s financial examples mainly concern language tasks. In that context “causal
language model” can denote autoregressive next-token modeling. That architectural term does
not identify an intervention effect. Financial text accuracy, sentiment prediction and financial
question answering may help prepare evidence, while a causal bank decision still requires an
intervention, target population, information clock, identification argument and uncertainty.
Domain fluency is useful only when those roles remain visible.


45.31.3     An evaluation that can justify a prototype

Public evaluation can test these distinctions before private bank experiments. Freeze known-
law causal cases and separate documentary corpora, including negated statements, obsolete
policies, contradictory populations, indirect relations and observationally equivalent causal
explanations. Compare simple retrieval, structured retrieval and proposed agent workflows
with matched documents and budgets. Hold out documents and domains, and give adjudicators
the actual claim definitions rather than asking for an undifferentiated plausibility score. These
are proposed studies, not completed live-model evaluations.
   Report evidence retrieval and entailment, entity/time mapping, graph-role errors, identifica-
tion/refusal, target-weight preservation and decision loss separately. Known-law cases establish
ground truth by construction; public observational data can test reproducibility and practical
relevance but need their own identifying assumptions. Neither should be labeled authentic
bank qualification. Include adversarial cases where every quoted sentence is accurate but the
causal conclusion or target population is wrong. Count corpus curation, retrieval, repeated
model calls, adjudication and maintenance when comparing costs.
   In the proposed CLI and MCP workflow, evidence status should accompany the claim into
the causal analysis request. Retrieved text supplies evidence, not tool authorization. The
result should distinguish supported premises, unverified assumptions, identified or unidentified
effects and the population to which an interval refers. This would allow the assistant to explain
why a proposal needs more information or a narrower claim. The survey supports the need
to examine these evidence failures; actual reliability and economic merit remain empirical
questions for the bounded public prototype.


45.32      An autonomous discovery workflow and the limits of its
           authority
An analyst who can run a discovery algorithm still faces a substantial sequence of choices:
expressing the question, checking the observation clock, choosing an admissible method,
800                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


configuring it, interpreting its graph and communicating what the graph permits. Causal-
Copilot addresses much of this sequence in a single agent workflow. Wang and colleagues
describe natural-language input, data diagnostics, algorithm selection and configuration,
execution revision, graph refinement and report generation. This is a useful architectural
comparison for the proposed banking assistant. Its value lies partly in organizing work that
a numerical discovery routine leaves to the analyst. The extent of that automation and the
causal authority of its output require separate examination.(Wang et al., 2025b)
   The evidence considered here has two distinct versions. The paper is arXiv:2504.13263v2,
dated 21 April 2025. The inspected repository snapshot is commit a31aa7c, dated 15 May 2026.
Both precede the literature cutoff, but the later source has not been established as the code
that produced the paper’s experiments. Paper results below are author-reported results; source
findings describe particular static paths in the later snapshot. Neither supplies a reproduction
of the other. This distinction permits a useful component assessment without attributing
a later implementation choice to an earlier experiment.(Wang et al., 2025b; Causal-Copilot
contributors, 2026)


45.32.1    Translating a retention question into a causal request

Suppose a manager asks, “Which retention offers prevent withdrawals?” Causal-Copilot’s
input and preprocessing modules offer a concrete starting point: parse a natural-language
objective and constraints, inspect the supplied data, and allow the user to revise the request.
Its subsequent modules filter and rank algorithms, configure execution and revise errors.
The paper also describes an interactive graph revision loop and a generated PDF report; its
web interface is an author-described interface rather than a deployment tested here. These
capabilities show why the proposal needs a complete analyst journey, including intelligible
reasons for method selection, rather than a collection of numerical commands.(Wang et al.,
2025b)
   For the retention request, a proposed causal contract must go further than extracting the
words “offer” and “withdrawal.” Let X denote assignment of a specified offer before a decision
deadline, and let Y indicate retention over a fixed subsequent horizon. The population must
specify eligibility at that deadline. A receipt date, an acceptance date and an assignment
date can produce different treatments; an account balance observed after an offer can be
a consequence of treatment rather than an admissible adjustment variable. Multiple offers
require either a specified version or an explicit policy. The assistant should expose these
alternatives and ask for the information that determines the intended contrast. A fluent
question-to-graph translation does not establish the timing or truth of the underlying variables.
   The selected source makes part of the selection process concrete. A user-chosen algorithm
bypasses the filtering step. Otherwise, the filter sends the query, data statistics, supplied
knowledge, resource information and the requested DAG or CPDAG form to a temperature-
zero language-model selection step. Such a prompt can organize alternatives and enforce an
output preference. It cannot make an observationally undetermined direction identifiable
merely because a DAG was requested. The proposal should retain the candidate class, rejected
alternatives and assumptions that justify the selection. User authority to choose an algorithm
is likewise distinct from evidence that its assumptions hold.(Causal-Copilot contributors, 2026)
  The proposed contract would therefore distinguish a documented business fact, a modeling
assumption, a statistical diagnostic and an agent suggestion. For example, an audited
assignment rule may justify an independence premise; an apparent lack of linear association
cannot certify it. A suggested latent “relationship strength” variable may explain selection,
but naming it does not measure it. In the eventual CLI or MCP request, these distinctions
45.32. An autonomous discovery workflow and the limits of its authority                       801


need structured fields that survive the call to a numerical engine and its returned report. They
are proposed additions to this library, with semantic and runtime qualification still required.


45.32.2     Stable association can support incompatible decisions

The distinction between workflow assistance and identification has a small exact demonstration.
Let U and V be independent, with U ∼ Bernoulli(1/2) and V ∼ Bernoulli(1/10). Write ⊕ for
binary exclusive-or. Consider two stipulated structural worlds:

                                A : X = U,     Y = X ⊕ V,
                                                                                          (45.18)
                                B : X = U ⊕ V, Y = U.

In world A, the offer changes retention. In world B, the hidden customer state U precedes
both assignment and the later outcome, producing selection without an offer effect. These are
mathematical examples, not observed banking mechanisms or fitted Causal-Copilot models.
Both induce the same strictly positive observed distribution:
                                             9                              1
                     P (0, 0) = P (1, 1) =      ,   P (0, 1) = P (1, 0) =      .          (45.19)
                                             20                             20
Consequently, E(Y | X = 1) − E(Y | X = 0) = 4/5 in either world. An intervention replacing
the equation for X leaves Y = U unchanged in world B. In world A, it gives retention
probabilities 9/10 and 1/10. The interventional contrast is therefore 4/5 in A and zero in B.
Enumerating the four (U, V ) atoms reproduces both the observed law and these effects. The
pair demonstrates nonidentification in a class admitting both worlds; it is neither a general
sharp effect bound nor a statement about an actual discovery run.(Causal banking proposal,
2026bt)
  Now condition on six independent observations comprising three (0, 0) pairs and three (1, 1)
pairs. In an ordinary iid empirical bootstrap of size six, the covariance of X and Y is positive
whenever both types appear. It vanishes only for either of the two constant-type resamples.
Hence
                                                             31
                     P∗ {Cov(X,
                          d       Y ) > 0} = 1 − 2(1/2)6 =       = 0.96875.                (45.20)
                                                             32
Here P∗ is conditional resampling probability, not probability that a causal direction is true.
Exhausting all 66 = 46,656  index resamples gives 45,198 positive covariances. The conditioning
event has probability 63 (9/20)6 = 531441/3200000 under either observed law, so it is a possible

sample with an explicit probability. The stability calculation concerns a covariance sign; it does
not claim that any specific upstream algorithm returns an edge with that frequency.(Causal
banking proposal, 2026bt)
  With a stipulated USD 100 contribution per incremental retained customer and a USD 30
expense per assigned offer, the contrast against withholding is

       ∆A = 100(4/5) − 30 = 50,        ∆B = 100(0) − 30 = −30 USD per offer.              (45.21)

The same observed data can thus favor opposite actions in the two admitted worlds. More
confident repetition of the association does not select between them. A useful assistant should
identify what would change this conclusion: a credible assignment experiment, defensible
additional restrictions, or new information that excludes a world. Which information is feasible
remains a banking design question. Bootstrap stability is still useful for describing sampling
sensitivity under a declared resampling law; its interpretation must stop at that law.(Causal
banking proposal, 2026bt)
