45.32.3     What the reported discovery comparisons establish

The paper’s synthetic experiments supply known graphs and vary the generating conditions.
They provide evidence about selection and discovery within those conditions, including favorable
settings and substantive alternatives. The default tabular row in Table 2 reports Causal-Copilot
F1 of 0.900, compared with 0.920 for PC, 0.910 for FCI and 0.920 for GES. In the sparse
row, its 0.820 is below GPT-4o’s 0.830 and FCI’s 0.840. These countercomparisons matter
when evaluating an adaptive selector: automation can be useful without dominating each fixed
method. They do not support a universal superiority claim. (Wang et al., 2025b)
   The financial scenario is generated, with 50 nodes across three financial domains; the reported
Copilot F1 is 0.650 ± 0.130. Financial vocabulary does not turn this known-truth simulation
into an authentic bank validation. The temporal Table 3 is explicitly linear and stationary. Its
default row gives 0.673 for Copilot, 0.695 for PCMCI and 0.733 for DYNOTEARS. The table’s
n = 5000 row reports 0.668 for Copilot, whereas the adjacent prose says 0.649. The very-large
row labels p = 100, whereas part of the prose says p = 1000. These two disagreements remain
unresolved; no raw output or experiment-bound configuration is supplied by this assessment
to reconcile them. (Wang et al., 2025b)
   The evaluation description on physical page 47 imposes a twenty-minute runtime cap,
describes a best-DAG conversion for tabular predictions and evaluates temporal summary
graphs while excluding diagonal entries. Such conventions change the evaluated object. A
summary adjacency can record that some lagged relationship exists while losing which lag
matters. Excluding a diagonal also excludes a variable’s own autoregressive relationships
from that graph score. Completion under a runtime cap is relevant operational evidence,
but an unavailable run and an incorrect completed graph are different outcomes. A banking
comparison should retain both, specify the scored graph object, and examine the intended
intervention query rather than infer effect quality from a summary F1 alone.(Wang et al.,
2025b)
   The later source supplies a precise example of why the conversion convention needs an explicit
name. In evaluator.py, entries [i, j] = 1 mean j → i, and the default is sample=False. The
default metric method calls a helper that consults true_graph when orienting ambiguous
predicted edges. Its alternative sampling branch also selects using minimum SHD against truth.
The integrated tabular benchmark constructs the default evaluator and reaches this helper; its
temporal branch instead calls direct binary scoring. This is truth-assisted benchmark evaluation
in the inspected paths. It is not evidence that a deployed discovery procedure receives the
unknown true graph, and it has not been bound to the 2025 experiments. (Causal-Copilot
contributors, 2026)
  For two nodes, hold fixed a single legal asymmetric undirected prediction and consider
opposite one-edge true DAGs. Both directions are compatible with this unoriented prediction.
With ordered off-diagonal binary F1, a truth-assisted conversion can attain one in both worlds.
A conversion fixed to one direction before seeing truth attains one in one world and zero in
the other. Under a stipulated equal weighting of the worlds,
                                                              1
                                F 1assisted = 1,    F 1fixed = .                           (45.22)
                                                              2
This authored enumeration isolates the information used by the score; it is not an estimate of
the paper’s score inflation. An optimistic compatibility score can answer a legitimate question
about whether an ambiguous output contains the truth. It should be reported as that question,
alongside ambiguity and a declared prediction rule, rather than interpreted as a direction the
algorithm selected without truth.(Causal banking proposal, 2026bt)
45.32. An autonomous discovery workflow and the limits of its authority                        803


45.32.4     A graph-refinement invariant needs an executable guard

Physical page 7 of the paper states that LLM recommendations are soft suggestions and
may not override high-confidence bootstrap decisions. That is an intelligible division of
authority. A source-level assessment must ask whether the reachable editing path enforces
it, including the representation of opposite directions of the same pair. In the later snapshot,
bootstrap_recommend identifies high directed frequencies at 0.9 or above and low frequencies
at 0.1 or below. Low ordered entries also enter its “middle” collection. The LLM evaluation
combines that collection and deduplicates it as unordered pairs. Its prompt distinguishes two
directions, answer C for no relationship and answer D for unknown. (Wang et al., 2025b;
Causal-Copilot contributors, 2026)
   Consider a conditional static witness using the source’s receiver/source matrix convention.
Stipulate a raw 0 → 1 edge and twenty bootstrap results, nineteen in that direction and one
in the reverse direction:
                                        !                           !
                                    0 0                  0  0.05
                             G=         ,       B=               .                         (45.23)
                                    1 0                0.95  0

Set uncertain-edge frequencies to zero. The forward ordered entry is high; the reverse entry is
low and therefore also enters the middle collection. Unordered deduplication makes the pair
eligible for LLM examination. In the inspected quality_judge path, fixed_pairs is empty.
If an answer C is accepted for this pair, the resulting forbid entry reaches an edit that sets both
entries of G to zero. A separately authored finite translation of these expressions reproduces
the mutation. (Causal-Copilot contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026bt)
  The conditions in this witness are essential. The bootstrap collection and accepted answer
are stipulated, not observed model outputs. The main program reaches the judge and its
quality path, but no upstream process or background knowledge implementation was executed
here. The witness stops immediately after the LLM mutation; later KCI pruning and cycle
handling are not simulated. It therefore identifies an unguarded intermediate edit under stated
inputs, rather than claiming a reproduced final graph failure. It also does not establish that
the 2025 implementation violated the paper’s rule. (Causal-Copilot contributors, 2026; Causal
banking proposal, 2026bt)
  A proposed repair would encode protection on unordered pairs before any edit:

                                P = {{i, j} : i ̸= j, Bij ≥ 0.9},

The equality refers to both ordered entries for the protected pair. Applying this rule blocks the
same conditional deletion in the authored reference. A full integration would have to define
the precedence of user changes, statistical constraints and subsequent pruning, then verify the
invariant at each relevant boundary. Protecting an edge implements an authority rule; it does
not prove that the protected edge is causally correct. The two-world example already shows
why such a proof cannot follow from frequency alone. (Causal banking proposal, 2026bt)


45.32.5     Temporal semantics, runtime scope and component adoption

Temporal support requires following the path that is actually called. The inspected bootstrap
helper has an iid row branch and a temporal branch with block size ten and block starts
sampled without replacement. That is a particular resampling scheme, not automatically
a justified time-series bootstrap. More directly, the inspected judge calls the helper with
ts=False, even though the helper offers a temporal branch. The program wrapper can preserve
804                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


returned lag matrices, and the state declares raw, revised and lagged fields. Storage capacity
does not establish that the judge resamples, edits and reports the same temporal object.
(Causal-Copilot contributors, 2026)
   For a servicing query, an edge Xt−1 → Yt and an edge Xt−5 → Yt imply different feasible
intervention times. Summarizing both as X → Y can be useful for an overview while being
insufficient for the requested policy. A proposal integration should preserve lag, endpoint
type, observation clock and the declared summary operation in its result. It should select a
resampling law justified for that target and explicitly refuse a temporal confidence claim when
only an iid route is available. Whether a fixed block size and without-replacement scheme
have suitable behavior depends on the assumed dependence and asymptotics; the inspected
branch alone supplies neither a theorem nor a qualification study.
   Runtime claims also need a boundary. The inspected benchmark timer encloses
Programming.forward, rather than the whole natural-language, diagnostic, selection,
refinement and reporting journey. Its source also replaces missing values with zero, a
preprocessing choice whose causal consequences depend on the missingness mechanism.
Default pytest settings exclude integration, LLM and LaTeX markers; this is evidence of
declared tests and selected exclusions, not absence of tests. The requirements contain pinned
entries alongside an unpinned huggingface-hub. An environment lock, end-to-end runtime
measurement and semantic acceptance suite therefore remain necessary before a reproducible
runtime comparison. (Causal-Copilot contributors, 2026)
   The bounded adoption decision is to use the workflow decomposition as an architectural
reference and assess components behind explicit contracts. Question parsing, method explana-
tions and report drafting are candidates for adaptation with evidence-linked inputs and human
revision. A statistical wrapper is a candidate for reuse after validating its graph and temporal
semantics against an independent reference. The truth-assisted evaluator is unsuitable as the
sole operational accuracy score; it can be retained only as a separately named compatibility
diagnostic. The unguarded refinement path requires a repair and invariant checks before
adopting the paper’s authority promise. None of these static decisions qualifies an installed
package. (Causal-Copilot contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026bt)
   The root license grants MIT permissions with a 2026 contributor notice; the inspected
vendored causal-learn notice grants MIT permissions with a 2022 notice. Both require
preservation of the notice and disclaim warranty. These two originals support a bounded
licensing assessment of the inspected files. They do not settle every transitive dependency,
model provider, data asset, deployment or redistribution right. Direct adoption remains
conditional on that complete inventory and on a tested environment; a port would create
an additional numerical and semantic equivalence obligation rather than removing the rights
question.(Causal-Copilot contributors and cmu-phil, 2026)
   The comparison also exposes deficits in this proposal. It has not demonstrated an integrated
Copilot-like business conversation, algorithm selector and interactive graph revision experience.
Nor has it qualified the proposed ambiguity-preserving engine boundary, temporal guard,
evidence-linked report or complete workflow costs. These are concrete prototype objectives. A
first public-data assessment can combine known-mechanism simulations with paired requests
that change assignment knowledge, lag information or the authority to edit a graph. It should
retain refusals, failures, ambiguity and total workflow expense in the denominator, and use
the exact examples above as small reference cases. Such an assessment can justify whether
an expensive bank experiment is worth conducting. It cannot substitute public observational
labels for unknown causal truth or declare a banking product validated.

45.33      Temporal discovery with hidden causes: what an agent
           can add

45.33.1     Start with the intervention, the clock and the hidden alternative

A servicing team observes that a borrower receiving more contact this month has a different
repayment outcome next month. It wants to change contact intensity, not merely forecast the
outcome. Let Xit denote the intensity for borrower i at decision time t, and let Yi,t+1 denote
the subsequent net recovery before contact cost. A useful first target is

                       τ = E{Yi,t+1 (do(Xit = 1)) − Yi,t+1 (do(Xit = 0))}.

Here the expectation is over a declared eligible borrower population and its predecision histories.
A multistage policy requires a separate target that also specifies subsequent actions. Recording
a message after a payment does not make the message a prepayment intervention. Event time,
availability time, decision time and follow-up must therefore be represented separately. An
agent can elicit these distinctions and propose candidate mechanisms. Neither the ordering of
the records nor a persuasive mechanism description establishes exchangeability, the absence of
selection, or a manipulable treatment. (Zheng, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026ax)
  The distinction can be seen without fitting a model. Consider a centered two-wave Gaussian
example, with independent standard normal U, ex , ey :

                                X = U + ex ,       Y = 2U + ey .

The hidden state U can represent persistent financial distress. There is no effect of intervening
on X. A second world has X ∼ N (0, 2) and Y = X + e, where e ∼ N (0, 3) is independent
of X. Its intervention effect is one. Both worlds have exactly the same observed bivariate
Gaussian law, with covariance matrix
                                                     !
                                                2 2
                                          Σ=        .
                                                2 5

The regression slope is one in both worlds; the time order is also the same. More observations
of this law cannot choose the causal effect. If one outcome unit is stipulated to be USD 20
and the added contact costs USD 8, the two net effects are minus USD 8 and plus USD 12. A
language model that labels U “distress” has supplied an interpretation, not an observation of
U or a reason to discard either world. These exact constructions explain why a proposal must
preserve ambiguity until a defensible restriction, proxy, assignment mechanism or experiment
supplies additional information. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ay)
   Time indexing also changes the graph class. The arrows At → Bt+1 and Bt → At+1 are
compatible with an acyclic time-unrolled model. Collapsing time produces the cycle A →
B → A. Likewise, At → At+1 is ordinary autoregressive persistence, not a contemporaneous
self-cycle. An instruction to “repair the DAG” by deleting these arrows would remove valid
candidate mechanisms. The product needs a typed graph carrying lag units, contemporaneous
edges, endpoint marks and latent-variable semantics before it asks an agent to explain or
modify it. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ay,ax)


45.33.2     Five frontier roles that should be evaluated separately

RealTCD uses language-derived meta-initialization within temporal discovery from observa-
tional and interventional regimes. Its unknown-target result is valuable because intervention
806                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


targets need not all be supplied in advance. It nevertheless assumes causal sufficiency. The-
orem 3.1 concerns a global score maximizer under sufficient conditional-density capacity,
intervention faithfulness, strict positivity, finite entropy and suitably small penalties. These
are substantive restrictions on the data and optimization problem. LLM initialization does
not prove that a numerical optimizer reaches that maximizer. A month with unusually many
arrears is not automatically an intervention regime: an unrecorded macroeconomic shock
can change both contact and repayment. For banking, the proposed use is to suggest initial
lagged structures and possible regime targets while retaining a separate register of which
regime assignments are observed, assumed or conjectured. Its reported benchmark advantages
are author results under their designs, not evidence that hidden banking causes have been
recovered. (Li, 2024)
   Sequential Causal Discovery with Noisy Language Model Priors addresses a different problem.
Its sequential axis consists of arriving observation batches; it should not be silently equated
with a fully specified temporal structural model. The inspected formulation allows latent
confounding under a restriction that each confounder affects two observed variables. Language
judgments update edge-level beliefs in a Bayesian-inspired scheme. The authors explicitly
distinguish this from full probabilistic inference over graphs, and leave broader confounding,
calibration and interventional extensions as future work. Their discussion also warns against
transferring standard independent, stationary bandit regret guarantees to the dependent
language-response channel. This is a useful approach to noisy suggestions, but an edge belief
cannot be presented as a calibrated posterior over all banking mechanisms or as confidence in
a policy value. (Verma et al., 2025)
   Large Causal Models provide an essential numerical comparator. They are pretrained
numerical transformers for temporal discovery, not large language models interpreting business
text. The inspected paper assumes additive noise, causal stationarity, no hidden confounders
and no contemporaneous effects. Its limitations section says that the model does not detect or
correct violations of these assumptions; predictions can instead reflect training-distribution
biases. Reported speed and accuracy under its test design motivate a challenger in that
declared domain. They do not justify using the model as a hidden-confounder detector. A
bank comparison should therefore separate the gain from numerical pretraining from any gain
due to language descriptions, expert restrictions or additional information. (Kougioulis et al.,
2026)
   Model Discovery Agent assigns language another role: proposing additions to a mechanistic
hypothesis library. Candidate models are fitted and compared using evidence approximations,
including BIC or tempered sequential Monte Carlo in different settings. The inspected
experiments use open-loop inputs; the method discussion distinguishes these from closed-loop
actions that depend on observed history. The finite-pool interpretation is particularly relevant to
banking. Even exact evidence would give a posterior restricted to the enumerated candidates. In
the implemented search, evidence is approximate, top-pool pruning is deterministic hypothesis
search, and unproposed model mass is not represented. Small residuals can delay further
expansion, and a discarded model can later become relevant. An agent can thus make a model
library more useful without establishing that it contains the true policy-response mechanism.
A servicing application needs an archive of rejected alternatives and challenges that distinguish
their intervention predictions, not only their fit to logged trajectories. (Murphy, 2026)
   The protected-core architecture advocated in Causal Discovery in the Era of Agents supplies
a way to combine these roles. The formal discovery method continues to determine the meaning
of its output; the agent proposes context, retrieval, assumptions and analyses around it. A
CPDAG represents a class of DAGs, and a PAG preserves ambiguity arising with latent or
selection variables. Neither should become a single confident DAG because the report needs a
45.33. Temporal discovery with hidden causes: what an agent can add                          807


diagram. This is an architectural argument and prospective evaluation standard. It is not an
empirical demonstration of safe banking performance, and its causal-learn+ identity is distinct
from the CausalAgent repository inspected below. (Zheng, 2026)
   Evidence against unqualified language assistance belongs alongside these favorable possibili-
ties. The inspected study on integrating language priors reports degradation when priors are
inaccurate, particularly for the temporal Water and Mildew examples. A model’s familiarity
with a variable name can encode the wrong temporal scale, population or intervention. Con-
sequently, a fair comparison must include deliberately reversed or misleading priors, opaque
variable names, and a no-language baseline. Tuning prior strength on the final evaluation
mechanisms would conceal the very failure the comparison is meant to measure. (Ban et al.,
2023; Causal banking proposal, 2026ax)


45.33.3    Additional non-Gaussian information: a useful but restricted route

Shi and colleagues develop a two-wave method that can distinguish some causal alternatives
using higher-order cumulants. Their model is

                           X = β1 U + ex ,      Y = β2 U + ηX + ey ,

with temporal ordering, linearity, independent errors and latent component, and specified
non-Gaussian information. Define the fourth mixed cumulants C31 = cum(X, X, X, Y ),
C22 = cum(X, X, Y, Y ) and C13 = cum(X, Y, Y, Y ). The first statistic is
                                                     2
                                     ∆1 = C31 C13 − C22 .

For this scalar-component model, writing κU = cum4 (U ) and κx = cum4 (ex ) gives

                                 ∆1 = κU κx β1 β22 η(β2 + ηβ1 ).

The proof’s nonzero cumulants and loadings, and the excluded cancellation η = −β2 /β1 ,
matter. Under those conditions the statistic supplies information absent from the Gaussian
example. It does not create information in that example by changing the estimator. (Shi et al.,
2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026ay)
  Two exact checks make the boundary concrete. First, let U take values −1, 0, 1 with
probabilities 1/6, 2/3, 1/6. It is nonnormal, has variance 1/3, and has fourth cumulant
1/3 − 3(1/3)2 = 0. With independent Rademacher errors, X = U + ex and Y = U + X + ey
have a direct effect of one. Nevertheless, C31 = C22 = C13 = −2, so ∆1 = 0; the relevant
third cumulants are also zero. This does not contradict the result with its full nonzero-
cumulant premises. It shows why “nonnormal” alone is an insufficient eligibility test and why
nondetection must remain inconclusive. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ay)
  Second, consider independent Rademacher U, V, ex , ey with

                           X = U + V + ex ,       Y = U + 2V + ey .

There is no direct X → Y path. Direct enumeration of all sixteen equally likely atoms,
independently checked by adding factor cumulants, gives C31 = −6, C22 = −10 and C13 = −18.
Thus ∆1 = 8. After standardizing X and Y , whose variances are three and six, the determinant
is 8/(32 62 ) = 2/81, still nonzero. The two hidden loading vectors (1, 1) and (1, 2) are not
proportional. Although the paper discusses aggregating hidden factors into a global component,
one common scalar component is not automatically an adequate representation of arbitrary
loadings with the required independent errors. This example lies outside that scalar restriction;
it supplies a diagnostic requirement for a proposed banking application, not a counterexample
808                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


under all theorem premises. Multiple forms of persistent borrower distress should not be
collapsed into a single latent score merely because that makes the test available. (Shi et al.,
2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026ay)
   The proposed multiple-testing algorithm standardizes the observations and uses percentile
bootstrap intervals for three statistics with a Bonferroni allocation of α/3. The paper explicitly
treats failure to detect as inconclusive. In one specified weak-signal simulation, reported power
rises from 4.8% at N = 2,000 to 99.5% at N = 200,000. These are useful warnings about
information requirements, not a general sample-size formula for a bank. Calendar dependence,
selection, heavy tails and estimated high-order moments require their own inferential argument.
A bootstrap implementation cannot supply that argument by itself. Moreover, detecting the
presence of a path does not consistently estimate its magnitude. The contact decision still
needs an effect or effect set in recovery units. The appropriate reuse is a narrowly qualified
statistical challenger and assumption diagnostic, with stronger restrictions declared explicitly.
(Shi et al., 2026)


45.33.4     Screening, hierarchy and prediction are complementary evidence

Yu and colleagues illustrate a more modest and practically useful language role in dementia
research: screening thousands of candidate variables using word and document embeddings,
followed by manual review and statistical discovery. This is not evidence that a modern agent
independently discovers a true temporal mechanism. Their pipeline uses a mixed graphical
model skeleton followed by FCI-MAX, temporal restrictions, fifty imputed datasets, and
edge-frequency thresholds of 30%, 50% or all datasets. Manual review restores risk factors
missed by the information-retrieval models. The lesson for a bank is to test the recall of
the variable-screening stage before celebrating a smaller graph: a missed common cause can
undermine the downstream analysis. Agreement across imputations is a stability statistic, not
automatically a calibrated graph posterior or a causal confidence set. The source’s cohort prose
reports 406,837 participants whereas its table reports 406,781; that discrepancy is unresolved,
and no exact cohort-size claim is used to justify a banking comparison. UK Biobank access
requires a researcher application, and the supplementary code has not been inspected here.
Publicly described data should therefore be distinguished from data available for unrestricted
immediate reuse. (Yu et al., 2025b)
   Spatio-Temporal Hierarchical Causal Models offer another adjacent route. The hierarchy
distinguishes units, such as regions, from repeated subunits, such as sensors. Its collapse
arguments take the number of subunits toward infinity while the numbers of units and
time points remain fixed. The stated conditions include convergence of mechanisms and
empirical measures, static unit confounders, neighbor restrictions, a known global ordering of
contemporaneous spatial influence, and common functional mechanisms. The adjustability
result additionally requires observable history to block the relevant backdoor paths. More
observations within a branch cannot establish that premise or make a time-varying unobserved
shock static. A proposed bank use must specify which objects are units and subunits and why
the asymptotic sequence represents the intended decision. (Li et al., 2026d)
   The paper also states instrument-based identification claims that must be read with a
target-specific argument. A valid instrument alone does not identify an arbitrary population
intervention distribution. To see the problem, let an independent binary instrument Z
encourage treatment among a population split equally between compliers and never-takers.
Compliers have Y (0) = 0, Y (1) = 1; never-takers have Y (0) = 0 and either Y (1) = 0
or Y (1) = 1. Both worlds satisfy exclusion, relevance and monotonicity and produce the
same observed (Z, A, Y ) law. The complier effect is one, but the population average effect
45.33. Temporal discovery with hidden causes: what an agent can add                            809


is respectively one half or one. Additional restrictions are necessary before translating an
instrument into the population recovery target. This construction does not purport to refute
every specialized hierarchical result; it prevents a generic IV sentence from being treated as a
universal identification theorem. (Li et al., 2026d; Causal banking proposal, 2026ay)
   The hierarchical paper reports favorable simulation comparisons and traffic applications,
including stress settings with drift or feedback. Such results are useful leads for a prototype.
A finite simulation mean of 4.91 near a truth of five is not itself a proof of unbiasedness,
and observed robustness does not remove the theorem’s assumptions. Its public code lead
is a separate item for version, rights and numerical review. It is also a statistical modeling
contribution rather than a demonstrated language-agent capability. (Li et al., 2026d)
   Augur uses language-generated causal explanations and teacher–student distillation for
discrete trend prediction. Its graph-overlap consensus and summary-to-graph consistency
scores help select training explanations. Agreement among sampled graphs, however, can
reproduce one shared misconception. A narrative can match every edge of an incorrect graph.
The inspected forecasting and explanation results therefore motivate a prediction or explanation
baseline, not a claim of hidden-confounder recovery or identified intervention value. (Zhiqing
Cui, Binwu Wang, Qingxiang Liu, Yeqiang Wang, Zhengyang Zhou, Yuxuan Liang and Yang
Wang, 2025)
   CausalPulse illustrates the difference between a successful workflow and successful causal
diagnosis. In its manufacturing evaluation, reported aggregate operational success reaches
98.73% for PSE, while root-cause Hits@1 is 0.44 and F1 is 0.39. Its reference labels are manually
identified “immediate variables changed” at an anomaly timestamp. Those labels and process-
order rules may be useful for its diagnostic task, but changes can be downstream consequences,
and neither operational success nor those annotations establish a bank’s intervention truth. The
appropriate banking comparison reports workflow completion, diagnostic ranking, identification
and decision performance separately. No one metric can stand in for the others. (Shyalika
et al., 2026)


45.33.5     Inspect the executable boundary before proposing adoption

The pinned LCM source declares package version 0.1.0, Python at least 3.10, an Apache-2.0
root license and six direct dependencies, including NumPy below two and PyTorch Lightning
2.0.8. These declarations do not settle all dependency or checkpoint rights. The advertised
checkpoints support up to twelve variables, lag three and length five hundred; their external
bytes have not been qualified here. The inspected forward path returns a tensor with axes
batch, target variable, source variable and lag index. The example applies a sigmoid, and its
convention maps index l to lag ℓmax − l. For example, index two at maximum lag three means
lag one. A wrapper that reverses source and target or treats the last axis as elapsed calendar
time silently changes the causal claim. (Pinned upstream contributors, 2026b)
  The README’s example contains a concrete masking issue. It loops over the three lag
positions but indexes the two variable dimensions:

for l in range(pred.shape[-1]):
    pred[:, l, l] = 0

For shape (1, 12, 12, 3) this clears nine cells, all lag entries on variable diagonals zero through
two; diagonals three through eleven remain. More fundamentally, valid lagged self-edges should
survive unless the declared model excludes them. The remedy is therefore to decide which
temporal edges are admissible before correcting the index loop. The example’s global min–max
normalization also has a zero denominator for a constant input, and its random padding needs
810                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


explicit seeds, validity semantics and evaluation controls. The inspected loading helper returns
no model on a missing or failed checkpoint and uses a loader path with unrestricted weight
deserialization. Checkpoint identity, loading behavior and failure classification belong in a
prototype contract. These are static-source and exact-coordinate findings, not measurements
from running LCM. (Pinned upstream contributors, 2026b; Causal banking proposal, 2026ay)
   For DMIRLAB’s CausalAgent, the inspected route spans tool selection, MCP dispatch,
the statistical backend, graph extraction, cycle processing and report preparation. Its root
license is MIT; requirements include specified MCP and LangGraph versions as well as lower-
bounded statistical dependencies, so a resolved compatible environment remains necessary.
The MCP module imports the PC function but invokes an OLC function without importing it,
even though that function exists in the backend. A missing binding and an absent optional
CDMIR dependency are different failures. Neither should be described as a scientific conclusion
that hidden causes are absent. The PC path uses Fisher’s Z at level 0.05; a generic tool
description cannot extend that test’s validity to arbitrary data-generating laws. (Pinned
upstream contributors, 2026a)
   Graph conversion introduces another distinction. The PC path retains raw endpoint matrices,
while the OLC formatter documents its own row/column and coefficient conventions. The
downstream cycle detector keeps entries equal to one and transposes them into a directed
graph. If a bidirected endpoint pair is admitted, this projection produces two directed arrows
and a false directed two-cycle. This is a conditional converter example, not an assertion that
ordinary PC outputs bidirected graphs. Undirected and circle endpoints also need explicit
treatment; deleting them is information loss, not resolution of uncertainty. The detector
catches exceptions and returns the same pair as “no cycle.” A validation error must instead be
an explicit unavailable state. (Pinned upstream contributors, 2026a; Causal banking proposal,
2026ay)
   Tracing the caller prevents an incomplete repair recommendation. It does run the cycle
detector again after proposed edits, but only warns if cycles remain and still reports the original
cycle count as fixed. The editing function deletes one matrix entry without a paired-endpoint
contract. In the normal dictionary-result path, a reversed type guard leaves the critical edge
list empty; the emitted revised graph is then an empty list, and the edited working matrix
is not used for that output. The alternate string branch attempts dictionary access on a
string. Independently, the edge evaluator’s prompt placeholders differ from the keys supplied
at invocation and its exception path returns a low-confidence retain default. Correcting only
that prompt would not repair the dictionary branch or the lost edited graph. A bounded
repair must address the entire typed result path and verify the resulting report, while keeping
original and proposed graphs separately available. No live application or language model was
invoked for these observations. (Pinned upstream contributors, 2026a)
   These findings support reference use before integration. Direct adoption is deferred because
target semantics, native behavior, dependencies and weight identities remain unqualified.
Porting entire neural or agent stacks would add maintenance and equivalence obligations
without an established benefit. A narrow adapter is a plausible next step: preserve upstream
numerical methods while owning the clock, graph, failure and evidence contracts. Rejecting
all research use would discard useful challengers, but accepting an MCP response or an acyclic
projection as causal certification would be equally unjustified. The proposed adapter must
round-trip permitted endpoint pairs and lagged edges, distinguish validation errors from
negative findings, and retain every edit’s origin and justification. (Causal banking proposal,
2026ax)
45.33. Temporal discovery with hidden causes: what an agent can add                           811


45.33.6     A public and generated comparison that can resolve useful questions

The first investment should be a bounded prototype using generated truth and suitable public
observations. Public time series can supply realistic clocks, missingness, vocabulary and
forecasting challenges. They supply causal ground truth only when assignment or interventions
are independently documented. Generated structural models supply known intervention
responses and controlled violations. Combining those roles is more informative than declaring
a public observational graph to be the true bank mechanism. It also avoids making expensive
bank experiments a prerequisite for investigating basic conversion errors. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026ax)
   The comparison should have distinct arms: a numerical method without language; the same
method with expert-supplied restrictions; language proposals accepted only through the formal
core; deliberately corrupted priors; and the numerical LCM challenger within its declared
sufficient, stationary, lag-only domain. Mechanism families should vary scalar versus multiple
latent loadings, weak or zero higher-order signal, temporal feedback and contemporaneous
effects, irregular or aggregated clocks, and drift and selection. Identical observations and
information budgets should be used wherever the scientific target permits. An expert arm
given true hidden structure is an information oracle, not a fair practical competitor. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026ax)
   Evaluation units must be independent mechanisms or complete trajectories under a declared
sampling design, not repeated prompts or neighboring rows. Development, calibration and final
evaluation need separate mechanisms. Freeze source and weight identities, variable descriptions,
prompts, prior-strength rules and stopping budgets before the final set. A pilot can estimate
runtime and variance to choose a defensible replication budget; no final qualification dataset or
success rate is claimed here. Report endpoint accuracy and retained-class validity separately
from identification correctness, effect-set coverage, width, availability, decision loss and total
review/computation cost. Unavailable tools, failed fits, timeouts and refusals remain in their
declared denominators. A repaired graph conversion can pass exact native fixtures while
the scientific model remains inapplicable to a particular hidden-confounder regime. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026ax)
   Several remedies are already concrete. Exact endpoint and lag fixtures can detect conversion
loss. Constant-input and padding fixtures can enforce preprocessing eligibility. A missing OLC
binding or backend can produce a typed failure. The dictionary, prompt, structured-response
and output branches can be corrected together and tested with generated results. Public
metadata-screening exercises can measure omitted-variable recall against an independently
curated reference. None of these steps requires pretending that a language-generated latent
label is an observed variable. They should proceed while the broader statistical questions
remain open. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ax)


45.33.7     The unresolved bridge from graph uncertainty to monetary uncer-
            tainty

Let M⋆ denote the true model in a stated model universe and let M
                                                                c be a data-dependent
retained set. Suppose a justified procedure provides

                                      P (M⋆ ∈
                                            / M)
                                              c ≤ αG .

For each retained model, let CM contain the target effects compatible with its assumptions and
an appropriate observed-law confidence set. Suppose the construction also justifies a bound
αE for failure of the true-model effect set under the actual selection and sampling procedure.
812                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


Then the union                                  [
                                         C=          CM
                                              M ∈M
                                                 c
misses the true effect with probability at most αG + αE , by the union bound. Independence
between these two failures is unnecessary once both event bounds are valid. Obtaining those
bounds is the difficult part; using the same data for selection and effect estimation cannot be
ignored. A model universe omitting the true mechanism also invalidates the premise. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026ay,ax)
   For illustration, budgets of 0.03 and 0.02 allow a 0.05 overall failure bound. An exact
hundred-atom construction with three graph failures and two disjoint effect failures attains
this bound. No graph-frequency histogram, low entropy over LLM outputs, or successful DAG
check establishes either premise. Nor does a narrow interval conditional on one selected graph
account for excluded alternatives. In the Gaussian banking example, even infinite observational
data leave both effects zero and twenty dollars available unless extra assumptions are justified.
Conservative uncertainty can therefore remain wide for an informational reason, not because a
numerical solver needs improvement. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ay)
   The known research route is to declare a restricted temporal model family, derive or verify its
retention and observed-law confidence procedure, propagate all compatible effects, and account
for numerical approximation. Exact small models should precede dependent-data studies and
larger learners. General nonlinear latent systems with selection, changing mechanisms and
potentially false language priors are not covered by that route merely because a restricted
example succeeds. Useful finite-sample precision and robustness in those broader regimes
remain open questions. When equivalent models imply opposite decisions, a valid outcome
is an effect set or a request for additional information, rather than a forced point estimate.
(Causal banking proposal, 2026ax)
   An illustrative value-of-information calculation helps decide whether that additional in-
formation merits a later experiment. Suppose, explicitly as a decision-maker’s stipulated
prior, the direct-effect world has probability 3/5. Acting immediately has expected net value
(3/5)12 + (2/5)(−8) = 4 dollars per eligible case. Perfectly distinguishing the worlds before
acting would yield (3/5)12 = 7.2 dollars, so perfect information is worth at most USD 3.2
before its cost. This is an upper bound under the stipulated prior and two-world decision
problem, not an observed bank price or the value of an imperfect trial. A robust decision-maker
who declines to assign that prior may instead retain the net-effect set {−8, 12} and withhold
action under a worst-case criterion. The proposal can explain both decision rules without
inventing institutional preferences. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ay)
   The resulting program is specific about what can be done now: improve semantic contracts,
repair selected adapters in a prototype, test exact counterexamples, and run predeclared public/-
generated comparisons. It is equally specific about what is unresolved: broad graph/effect-set
calibration, model misspecification, useful precision and the information needed to distinguish
observationally equivalent mechanisms. This review recovers three additional primary originals,
but the diffusion-model lead still lacks a securely acquired original and the Earth-science lead
returned HTML rather than a genuine technical PDF. Specialist search saturation, uninspected
supplementary code and checkpoint qualification remain open. These coverage limits do not
prevent the concrete prototype work, and they do prevent a claim of an exhaustive or generally
qualified temporal causal agent. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ax)
45.34. From language suggestions to an identification certificate                            813


45.34       From language suggestions to an identification certificate
An analyst asks whether servicing a delinquent account will increase repayment. An assistant
may propose a graph, an adjustment set or an instrument, yet these are different objects from
an identified effect. The product must preserve the question through each transformation:
which customers, which action, at which time, compared with what alternative, and under
which observation law? A formal engine can answer the resulting mathematical question
conditional on its model. It cannot establish the institutional truth of an assumption supplied
by the language model. This division of responsibility creates a useful role for an assistant
without treating its fluency as a certificate. (Causal banking proposal, 2026v)


45.34.1     Evidence from different tasks should remain distinguishable

CLadder provides formal causal question generation and different verbalizations, helping
separate calculation from familiar real-world associations. Its authors report improvements
from structured CausalCoT prompting and retain the difficulty of turning language into the
right formal inputs. The inspected paper and repository are separate versioned objects; a result
reported for one dataset version is not automatically a qualification of every released generator
template. In particular, a selected repository template places an instrumental-variable ratio
inside an average-treatment-effect query. That label needs its own structural and population
assumptions. (Jin et al., 2023; PyWhy Community and CLadder and CausalDS contributors,
2026)
   CounterBench makes another contribution: 1,000 balanced binary questions about deter-
ministic structural mechanisms, spanning basic, joint, nested and conditional questions. In
the inspected first version, Chen and colleagues report GPT-4o accuracy of 52.5 percent with
standard prompting, 78.8 percent with CausalCoT and 92.0 percent with CoIn. The same
table reports a decrease from 51.8 to 49.8 percent for Davinci. CoIn organizes extraction,
iterative reasoning and backtracking through demonstrations; the description of an algorithm
does not by itself make the model’s generated steps a machine-checked proof. The authors
identify probabilistic mechanisms and hidden confounding as extensions. These favorable
and adverse results are historical paper observations, not measurements of this product or of
current services. The inspected v1 title is A Benchmark for Counterfactuals Reasoning in
Large Language Models; it should not be silently conflated with later title or release variants.
(Chen et al., 2025)
   METER instead aligns three linguistic question families over 4,145 shared contexts. Its first
level concerns causal relations expressed in text, which the paper calls discovery. That task
differs from recovering a graph or equivalence class from an observational law. Intervention
and counterfactual options are generated by a model and then edited and filtered by human
annotators. For GPT-4o the authors report zero-shot accuracies of 87.92, 77.96 and 67.42
percent, with corresponding CoT accuracies of 86.46, 75.14 and 66.18 percent. Its useful
lessons concern shared context, distraction by irrelevant facts, causal reversal and unsupported
statements. Curated semantic labels do not supply a complete formal identification oracle.
Comparing its headline percentage directly with CounterBench would confound the question,
answer space, information and target. (Li et al., 2026b)
   Gendron and colleagues separate graph extraction from evaluating counterfactual mecha-
nisms. Their experiments show that providing the correct graph need not remove mechanism-
evaluation errors. They also acknowledge using model-derived counterfactual values as proxies
for some real-world ground truth. This is a reason to retain independent numerical or logical
references when evaluating a banking workflow. A coherent graph and a confident answer can
814                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


fail at different stages. (Gendron et al., 2024)
   CausalDS moves toward an agent workflow with public scene files, separate private truth,
observation noise and identification-gated questions. It distinguishes population-average
intervention targets from counterfactual targets and conceptual variables from their noisy
measurements. Those distinctions are directly relevant to a bank’s data dictionary. However,
benchmark architecture and the semantics of every implementation branch require separate
inspection. The selected source retains unknown values for missing engines and exceptions,
while returning false with error metadata for invalid target nodes. A negative criterion result
can also survive an unavailable or failed fallback. A consumer that reads only the Boolean can
turn a malformed or unresolved request into a claim of scientific impossibility. (Leban and
Sun, 2026; PyWhy Community and CLadder and CausalDS contributors, 2026)
   Formal proof assistance introduces a further boundary. CausalSmith distinguishes a me-
chanically checked proof from a faithful formalization of the intended statement. A changed
hypothesis, a vacuous definition or an assumed hard step can yield an artifact that fails the
original scientific purpose. The authors’ internal catalog reports 14 accepted, 59 downgraded
and 71 failed runs among 144 recorded runs; the identification and structural-model clusters
contain one acceptance among 94 runs. Reruns count separately. These are not independent
estimates of autonomous research quality: the paper acknowledges the absence of independent
human quality validation and an estimated error rate for statement matching. A valid proof of
the wrong banking target remains the wrong deliverable. (Jiyuan Tan and Vasilis Syrgkanis,
2026)


45.34.2     A valid instrument need not answer the population question

Consider a stipulated servicing experiment. At time zero an eligible population receives a
randomized encouragement Z. Actual servicing A occurs by day seven, and binary repayment
Y is measured by day thirty. Let A(z) denote take-up under encouragement z, and Y (a)
repayment under servicing a. Assume encouragement is independent of the take-up type and
potential outcomes, that it affects repayment only through servicing, and that consistency and
no interference hold. Take-up is monotone: there are no borrowers who accept only when they
are not encouraged. These assumptions define the example; an assistant’s proposed instrument
does not establish them. (Causal banking proposal, 2026w)
  Suppose one quarter of borrowers are always-takers with (A(0), A(1)) = (1, 1), one quarter
are never-takers with (0, 0), and one half are compliers with (0, 1). The two candidate worlds
have the same take-up and differ only in potential repayments:

          Stratum      Probability World A: (Y (0), Y (1)) World B: (Y (0), Y (1))
          Always-taker    1/4             (0, 1)                  (1, 1)
          Never-taker     1/4             (0, 1)                  (0, 0)
          Complier        1/2             (0, 1)                  (0, 1)

Under either world the complete observed joint law of (Z, A, Y ) is the same. For Z = 0, a
quarter have (A, Y ) = (1, 1) and three quarters have (0, 0); for Z = 1, these probabilities are
reversed. Consequently,
                        E[Y | Z = 1] − E[Y | Z = 0]   3/4 − 1/4
                                                    =           = 1.
                        E[A | Z = 1] − E[A | Z = 0]   3/4 − 1/4
The population average effect is nevertheless 1 in world A and 1/2 in world B. Exact enumeration
reproduces every cell and contrast; neither world is fitted to bank data. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026w)
45.34. From language suggestions to an identification certificate                               815


   The reason is visible algebraically. Let C denote the complier stratum. Under the stated
independence and exclusion restrictions, the first-stage difference is P (C): always-takers and
never-takers do not change treatment. For the same reason the reduced-form outcome difference
is P (C)E[Y (1) − Y (0) | C]. Dividing therefore identifies the complier effect when P (C) > 0.
The ratio supplies no new observation of the always-takers’ untreated outcome or the never-
takers’ treated outcome. Here their observed outcomes and the binary restriction permit
a population-effect range [1/2, 1]. Varying the unobserved outcomes, or mixing compatible
subtypes, attains the endpoints and intermediate values in this stipulated class. It would be
incorrect to attach the ratio’s value to the unrestricted population target. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026w)
  The distinction can reverse an investment conclusion. Stipulate a USD 100 value for
repayment and a USD 75 servicing cost per treated borrower. A hypothetical policy treating
everyone rather than nobody then has net value between minus USD 25 and plus USD 25
per eligible borrower. The complier calculation alone gives plus USD 25 and cannot settle
that population policy. This comparison is neither the value of the encouragement policy nor
observed bank ROI; feasibility, actual costs and transport beyond the stipulated population
remain separate questions. The exact example explains why the query’s population must
survive every language, tool and reporting conversion. (Causal banking proposal, 2026w)


45.34.3     Suggestion packages and formal engines have different obligations

The selected pinned PyWhyLLM paths illustrate a useful but limited component. Its public
initialization imports suggestion classes. The main identification suggester delegates backdoor
proposals to confounder suggestions, leaves a frontdoor method unimplemented, and retains a
commented estimand path. A separate simple suggester prompts for IV, backdoor or frontdoor
names and extracts response tags. Protocol classes declare interfaces; the validation suggester
adds prompted critique. None of these selected paths supplies a formal identification certificate.
Its selected unit tests mock model responses and compare extracted lists, establishing intended
parsing behavior rather than live scientific validity. (PyWhy Community and CLadder and
CausalDS contributors, 2026)
   The proposed reuse is therefore a small optional elicitation component. Its outputs should
be candidate variables or assumptions with provenance, subject to schema checks, variable
allowlists, finite retries and review. A package name or a method called validation should
not grant scientific authority. The root MIT notice has been inspected separately from
complete runtime and dependency rights. CLadder and CausalDS likewise need version-specific
generator, observation-model and scorer audits, with their code and data rights kept distinct.
CounterBench and METER currently support the literature argument; adopting their released
datasets requires item-level semantics and rights review. No selected external integration is
enabled by this analysis. (PyWhy Community and CLadder and CausalDS contributors, 2026;
Causal banking proposal, 2026v)
   The formal engine needs a stricter output contract. An identified result retains the exact
query, graph, observation law, assumptions, supported model class, expression and checkable
certificate. A not-identified result needs a compatible counterexample or an applicable complete-
method certificate for the same target and class. Unknown covers insufficient assumptions,
unsupported methods, invalid input, absent engines, timeouts and unverified negative criterion
results. Execution status and scientific status should be distinct fields, with reasons and fallback
history. For example, failure to find a backdoor set may justify trying another identification
method; it does not by itself prove that no observational formula exists. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026v)
816                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   This matters in the inspected CausalDS path. Filtering an IV candidate from a population-
ATE answer avoids one target substitution, but an empty remaining method dictionary becomes
false. When a more general fallback is absent or fails, that result still needs its criterion
scope. Invalid graph-node cases also return false alongside error metadata. The proposed
wrapper should inspect all of those fields and preserve unknown or invalid-request semantics
as appropriate. This is a static source finding and a proposed conversion rule, not an observed
failure of an installed CausalDS runtime. (PyWhy Community and CLadder and CausalDS
contributors, 2026; Causal banking proposal, 2026v)


45.34.4     A public prototype that tests the actual weakness

The smallest useful prototype combines independently enumerated mechanisms with audited
formal-engine outputs. It asks the assistant to translate a banking question, expose its
assumptions, select a supported query and explain the result without changing its scope. Same-
observed-law worlds test whether the workflow recognizes missing information. Paraphrases
and renamed variables test whether it preserves meaning. A changed population or observation
mask should trigger a changed query, while harmless wording should not. Deliberately invalid
graphs, unsupported classes and timeouts test whether uncertainty survives. Private truth
artifacts must remain separate from assistant inputs. (Causal banking proposal, 2026v)
   Report false identification, target substitution, invalid certificates, unavailable results and
the reasons for abstention separately. A high answer accuracy on identified questions cannot
conceal confident answers to unidentified ones. Measure complete costs: formalization review,
tool calls, failed executions, proof checking and human correction as well as model tokens.
These measurements can use public and generated cases before an expensive bank experiment.
They establish whether a prototype merits institutional evaluation; they do not manufacture
assignment truth or stakeholder acceptance. (Causal banking proposal, 2026v)
  The engineering route is concrete. Representative rates of business-to-formal error, reliable
detection of missing assumptions and broad faithful proof translation remain research questions.
A proof checker can reduce one class of error while leaving those questions unresolved. The
product proposal should fund a scoped prototype with explicit failure cases and retain the
unresolved claims, rather than promise that formal syntax alone solves causal reasoning.
(Causal banking proposal, 2026v)
Chapter 46

Choosing the next experiment:
information, decisions and agent
limits

An agent that proposes a plausible causal diagram has not yet answered the bank’s next
question: which additional observation could change a worthwhile decision? A diagram may
contain a dozen unresolved arrows, although only one uncertainty affects whether a particular
retention offer should be deployed. Conversely, an apparently stable effect estimate can conceal
a decisive measurement or selection problem. Experiment selection therefore connects problem
formulation, causal discovery and investment analysis. Its purpose is to spend a limited
information budget on distinctions that matter, while preserving the possibility that none of
the proposed experiments is useful.
   The proposed role of a language model is to formulate competing mechanisms, translate
a question into an admissible design menu, locate observations that could distinguish the
mechanisms, and explain the resulting numerical comparison. A statistical component must
evaluate the observation laws and decision losses. A language model’s confidence, the number
of agreeing agents, and the novelty of an experiment description are inadequate substitutes for
those calculations. This chapter develops that separation using inspected primary literature,
concrete public software interfaces, and an exact banking planning example. The example
establishes a property of its stipulated law; it does not measure language-model ability or the
value of a bank experiment.


46.1     Three different meanings of an experimental action
A real intervention changes an admissible treatment or environment and obtains an outcome
under that change. A simulator experiment changes an input in a specified mathematical world.
A model or expert query obtains an answer from a fallible information source. All three can be
sequential actions, but their observation laws have different meanings. A simulator can reveal
its own response to an offer without establishing the response of depositors. An expert can
state that a variable precedes another without supplying a randomized treatment assignment.
Neither operation becomes a bank intervention because an agent calls it an experiment.
   Let θ index a candidate mechanism, D the information available before design selection,
d ∈ D(D) an admissible acquisition, and Od its returned observation. A Bayesian design
calculation requires p(Od | θ, d, D) and a distribution π(θ | D). For a physical experiment, the
former must represent assignment, adherence, measurement, missingness and the outcome

                                              817
818                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


clock. For a simulated experiment, it is the generator’s observation law. For an expert query,
it is an answer error model, potentially conditional on wording, context and common source
material. Estimating a histogram of repeated answers measures a query distribution; without
additional calibration it does not identify the probability that an asserted causal arrow is
correct.
   Consider a bank deciding whether to offer a fee waiver to a defined group of depositors. The
target is incremental 90-day stable-balance value, net of the waiver, contact and funding costs,
relative to the existing policy. Define the population before contact, use only its pre-contact
information for eligibility, and distinguish the offer from acceptance of the offer. A proposed
prospective study would need an assignment rule and a way to observe both withdrawals and
account closure. A historical query about customers who accepted cannot silently take the
place of that study. Selection, interference across accounts and changes in market rates could
each invalidate the proposed observation law.
   The information clock is as consequential as the treatment clock. A design chosen today
may produce a 90-day outcome before a later cohort’s deployment decision; it cannot inform
today’s irreversible decision before that outcome exists. Transport from the study cohort to
the deployment cohort is then an additional assumption. Delay and the value of waiting belong
in the cost calculation. Public or generated data can test whether an agent respects these
distinctions now, even when conducting the prospective bank experiment would be premature.


46.2     What the primary literature supports

46.2.1    Learning a strategy does not remove its information requirements

Lampinen and colleagues study whether agents can acquire active causal strategies from passive
demonstrations. The positive finding concerns learning how to investigate from examples
of competent investigation. At evaluation, the learner can act and obtain the consequences
needed by the task. Passive training is therefore compatible with active information acquisition;
it is not evidence that an observationally unidentified effect becomes identified without new
assumptions or observations. The paper’s finite graphs and constrained action and observation
spaces also limit transfer to a bank with latent customer states, delayed outcomes and restricted
actions Lampinen (2023).
   This distinction suggests a useful proposal component. Demonstration traces can teach
an agent to ask for the outcome horizon, request a missing assignment variable, or select a
discriminating synthetic intervention. Their training value should be evaluated separately
from the information supplied by the eventual environment. A comparison should hold that
environment and its acquisition budget fixed, and include a numerical or rule-based design
policy that receives the same history. Otherwise a more informative interface can be mistaken
for a better reasoner.
   Verma and colleagues provide a different example: sequential causal discovery with a
language model treated as a noisy expert. Their method combines batches of observational
data with background information obtained through a fixed budget of model queries, using
partial ancestral graphs to retain relevant latent-confounding ambiguity. The inspected
evaluation compares query allocation with random edge selection and reports improvements
in graph metrics. This is evidence about the tested graph-learning setup, not a physical
intervention or a measured gain from a lending decision. Sequential arrival of data batches also
does not by itself supply the treatment-history assumptions required by longitudinal causal
inference Verma et al. (2025).
46.2. What the primary literature supports                                                  819


   The paper identifies open questions that directly affect deployment: the uncertainty over
candidate graphs, calibration of language-model answers, more complex latent confounding,
the incorporation of interventions and sequential theoretical analysis. These limits argue for
retaining ambiguous graphs and for pricing questions according to their possible effect on the
decision. Repeated model answers may share training information and reasoning errors. An
empirical answer frequency is useful operational evidence, but the product should not multiply
it into independent scientific confirmation.


46.2.2    Model discovery and numerical design: gains with important excep-
          tions

The inspected version of Model Discovery Agent combines model proposals with numerical
model comparison and experimental design. Candidate mechanistic models are fit to observa-
tions, and a design component seeks experiments whose predictions distinguish the current
candidates. The paper discusses Bayesian model evidence, approximations including BIC,
sequential Monte Carlo, and disagreement-based surrogates for expected information gain.
Depending on the design space, its implementation uses numerical optimization or evaluates a
finite menu. This combination offers a concrete reason to use a language model: it can propose
representations and mechanisms that a fixed estimator does not enumerate, while numerical
components fit and compare the proposals Murphy (2026).
  The favorable evidence needs its stated denominator and comparison budget. The paper
reports experiments in chemistry, glucose dynamics and neuronal systems; its chemistry
aggregate uses 115 matched evaluable world–seed cells from 171 attempted cells over 54 worlds.
This is a conditional comparison over evaluable cells, not a claim that all attempts succeeded.
The paper also explicitly distinguishes sample efficiency from a compute-matched comparison.
Extra model proposals, optimization, fitting and retries may consume substantial resources
even when fewer environment queries are used. A bank investment argument must record
both kinds of expenditure.
  Adverse findings sharpen the design recommendation. In the paper’s source-location
experiment, a greedy joint-variance heuristic performs worse than random selection, and the
model-information criterion does not show an advantage over random design in that domain.
A numerical-looking acquisition score is therefore not a guarantee of improved information
gathering. The observation model, candidate pool, approximation error and accessible design
menu all affect whether the score is useful. Random and fixed designs remain substantive
baselines; they are not merely weak comparators to be discarded once an agent is available.
  A further limitation is support. Normalized weights over the proposed models sum to one
even when every model omits the mechanism that generated the data. Pruning can make
apparent confidence increase while removing a useful alternative. For the bank, candidate
mechanisms should include policy selection, timing error, measurement changes and null effects
where relevant. An agent should be able to propose a new mechanism after a failed predictive
check. Such revision needs an evaluation rule that prevents unlimited post hoc repairs from
making every hypothesis unfalsifiable.


46.2.3    Scientific judgment, research state and the missing validation step

DISCERN tests a complementary problem: whether agents carry evidence limitations through
scientific reasoning. Its 203 canonical life-science tasks comprise 79 data-integrity tasks, 102
analysis-verification tasks and 22 hypothesis-generation dossiers, across eight tracks and eight
evaluated models. The three levels are independently instantiated and scored. Their outputs
820                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


are not passed through an evaluated end-to-end research pipeline. For a counterfactual dossier,
eligibility depends on eliciting a model prior that conflicts with the supplied evidence Huang
et al. (2026).
   The reported perfect-score rates are 60.8%, 34.2% and 0.6% at the three levels under
their respective rubrics. These are rubric-specific evaluation percentages, not probabilities of
discovering a true mechanism or choosing a profitable experiment. The grading uses human-
designed criteria, deterministic checks with language-model verification and adjudication for
the first two levels, and rubric-based judgment for hypotheses. Three draws of a judging
procedure do not amount to three independent institutions validating an experimental result.
The authors identify task dependence, possible familiarity with public data and residual
grading uncertainty, and do not establish whether the proposed hypotheses lead to useful
follow-up experiments.
   For banking, the relevant failure mechanism is precise. An agent can correctly say that
offer acceptance is selected, yet subsequently recommend deploying the offer as though the
observed acceptance–balance association were a causal effect. Merely counting whether the
word “confounding” appears in a report misses that failure. A useful evaluation checks whether
the limitation changes the next action, narrows the claim, or produces abstention. It also needs
clean controls: an agent that rejects every dataset can appear cautious while destroying valid
opportunities. The proposed experiment-selection evaluation should score both unwarranted
deployment and unnecessary rejection.
   Discovery Foundation Models proposes an explicit, revisable research state, with representa-
tions, hypotheses, evidence, experiment choices and transferable research skills as objects that
can change. Its Zetema description separates proposed expectations from external outcomes
and calls for attributing a failure before promoting a lesson to reusable memory. This is a
useful architectural principle: an invalid measurement should revise the observation model,
whereas a failed mechanistic prediction may require a new hypothesis Yang et al. (2026b).
   The report’s GALILEO discussion describes a structured therapeutic-discovery case and
explicitly locates specialized human-executed assays inside the coupled system. It does not
establish a general-purpose discovery system or broad transfer across domains. The underlying
biomedical original is outside the inspected evidence used here, so the account informs the
proposed architecture without independently validating its biological results. Adopting a
revisable state representation is consequently a design choice; claiming that the proposed bank
agent improves scientific discovery would require a separate controlled evaluation.


46.3      A decision criterion with an explicit option to stop
Let a ∈ A denote a deployment decision and u(a, θ) its incremental value, expressed in a
common unit and at a specified horizon. The value of acting with existing information is

                                   V (D) = max E[u(a, θ) | D].
                                              a∈A

If acquisition d costs c(d, D), its one-step net value is
                                                           
               G(d | D) = EOd |d,D max E[u(a, θ) | D, Od , d] − V (D) − c(d, D).             (46.1)
                                        a∈A

Acquisition is worthwhile under this model only if its best admissible net value is positive.
Costs can include the experiment itself, failed attempts, waiting, analyst effort and computa-
tion. Combining per-customer value with a whole-study cost requires an explicit deployment
population or amortization; otherwise the comparison has inconsistent units.
46.3. A decision criterion with an explicit option to stop                                 821


  Expected information gain asks a different question. For a finite mechanism set, write
H(π) = − θ πθ log2 πθ . Then
         P


                      I(d | D) = H{π(· | D)} − EOd |d,D H{π(· | D, Od , d)}.

This criterion can be appropriate when learning the mechanism is itself the objective. It need
not prioritize uncertainty that changes a particular decision. The target of information gain
matters: information about a nuisance parameter, an effect sign and a full dynamic model
need not have the same economic value. A remedy is to use a decision-relevant target or
evaluate Equation (46.1) directly, while examining the sensitivity of both to their assumed
likelihoods and losses.


46.3.1     An exact fee-waiver planning construction

Suppose two binary variables H and Z index four equally likely planning worlds. H represents
whether the fee-waiver policy is valuable; Z is an independent nuisance feature of the envi-
ronment. Relative to abstention, deploying has value USD 100 when H = 1 and USD −120
when H = 0. Abstention has value zero in either world. These are stipulated, already net
deployment values per normalized deployment decision, not measured customer effects. Each
information acquisition costs USD 5 in the same normalized units. The calculation assumes
that its observation is available before the deployment decision and that the world remains
relevant to that decision Causal banking proposal project (2026a).
   With prior probability p = Pr(H = 1) = 1/2, expected deployment value is 100p − 120(1 −
p) = 220p − 120 = −10. The optimal initial action is abstention. The threshold for deployment
is p > 6/11. Perfect information about H would have gross value USD 50, since deployment
would occur only in the good half of the worlds. That USD 50 is an upper bound under the
stipulated model, not a forecast of a feasible experiment’s return.
   Consider two permitted abstract acquisitions. Design dZ reveals Z perfectly. Design dH
returns a signal S ∈ {0, 1} satisfying
                                                           4
                                    Pr(S = H | H, Z, dH ) = .
                                                           5
The signal has conditional error probability 1/5, independent of Z. This accuracy is an assumed
experiment likelihood. It is not a measured accuracy of an LLM, a hypothetical expert panel
or an actual bank trial. Equal acquisition budgets make the comparison transparent: both
designs use one acquisition costing USD 5.
   The first design learns one bit about the full world but leaves the posterior probability
of H at 1/2. The bank still abstains, so net information value is USD −5. For the second
design, each signal has probability 1/2. A positive signal gives posterior 4/5 and expected
deployment value 220(4/5) − 120 = 56. A negative signal gives posterior 1/5 and expected
deployment value −76, so the bank abstains. Expected terminal value is (1/2)56 = 28 and
net value is USD 23. Full-world information gain is only 1 − h2 (1/5) ≃ 0.278 bits, where
h2 (p) = −p log2 p − (1 − p) log2 (1 − p).


       One-acquisition policy                    Information (bits) Gross USD Net USD
       Maximize information about (H, Z)                     1.000              0    −5
       Maximize deployment value                             0.278             28    23
       Uniform random choice of the two                      0.639             14     9
       Do not acquire                                            0              0     0
822                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


  The random policy chooses between the two designs with equal probability, so its expected
net value is (−5 + 23)/2 = 9. Its expected information gain also averages the two design gains,
conditional on knowing the selected design. An information criterion targeted specifically at
H would select the useful signal in this example. The construction therefore demonstrates
a mismatch between the full-world learning objective and this deployment objective, rather
than a general failure of information-based design. The values follow from exact finite sums,
independently checked by evaluating the realized payoff of the signal-dependent deployment
policy.


46.3.2    Unavailable observations and correlated answers

Now suppose dH returns no observation with probability 1/4, independently of the world, and
every attempt still costs USD 5. On failure the posterior remains the prior and the bank
abstains. Gross expected value becomes (3/4)28 = 21, and all-attempt net value is USD 16.
Restricting the comparison to successful acquisitions would instead report USD 23. Both
calculations can be arithmetically correct, but they answer different questions. A purchase
or investment decision needs the attempted-work denominator. If failure depends on H, the
failure event itself has a likelihood and must enter the posterior; treating it as independent
missingness would be another model error.
   Repeated agreement introduces a separate problem. Suppose five expert answers are perfectly
correlated because they all copy one underlying noisy answer whose accuracy is 4/5. After five
positive answers, the correct posterior remains 4/5. Incorrectly multiplying five independent
likelihoods would produce
                                        (4/5)5        1024
                                         5       5
                                                   =       .
                                   (4/5) + (1/5)      1025
Different prompts or agent identities do not establish independent error channels. The remedy
is to model the shared source, collect evidence from a different measurement or intervention
when feasible, and compare conclusions under plausible dependence structures. A majority
vote cannot create the missing assignment evidence.


46.3.3    A finite stopping rule and the danger of a narrow model pool

Suppose at most two useful signals are available and their errors are conditionally independent
given H. Always purchasing both gives expected terminal value 148/5 = 29.6 and costs
USD 10, leaving net value 98/5 = 19.6. This is below the one-query value of USD 23. A
conditional calculation verifies the stopping decision. After a positive first signal, the best
possible gross increment from a second useful query is 16/5 = 3.2; after a negative signal it is
zero. Both are below its USD 5 cost. A query about Z adds no deployment value at either
history. Thus, for this menu and horizon of at most two, the optimal policy purchases one
useful query and stops. This result does not establish that a myopic stopping rule is optimal
