run. A new run should receive a new execution identity, even if it preserves the same business
question. Conversely, keeping the same model while changing the target population requires a
new scientific identity. Requiring these two distinctions avoids both needless recomputation of
unrelated artifacts and unsafe reuse of results for a changed question. The custody construction
in Section 53.15 describes the narrower local byte and context checks already observed.


48.3     Three orchestration frameworks under inspected revisions
LangGraph offers a state-graph and checkpoint interface. At the inspected revision dated
7 October 2026, its project declares version 1.2.14 and Python 3.10 or later. The selected
compile path accepts a checkpointer. Its interrupt documentation is precise about resumption:
the interrupted node starts again and re-executes its preceding logic. That behavior is useful
for a review step, but an expensive or externally consequential action before the interrupt may
be repeated unless the application separately journals or deduplicates it. The proposed reuse
decision is a conditional Python adapter for state orchestration, with scientific identities and
side-effect records owned by the application. Porting the entire framework is not justified by
the present proposal. The inspected root license is MIT; dependency and deployment review
remains separate. (langgraph contributors, 2026)
   Pydantic AI offers typed tool interfaces and usage controls. The inspected 7 October 2026
revision declares Python 3.11 or later and a dynamic package version; no exact release number
is inferred from that field. Selected tool fields support sequential execution and an approval
condition, but their inspected defaults do not require either. The application must configure
consequential tools explicitly. Request counts can be checked before a model call, whereas
token totals generally arrive with responses; an optional pre-counting path has its own support
and overhead. The selected cost check warns when no cost was calculated and cannot enforce
the stated monetary limit in that case. The proposed decision is conditional reuse for typed
adapters, backed by an application-owned budget ledger and unknown-cost policy. The MIT
notice does not resolve every model or data term. (pydantic-ai contributors, 2026)
   AutoGen’s inspected April 2026 snapshot declares AgentChat 0.7.5 and a pinned core
dependency. Its README describes maintenance mode with no new features; that is a source
declaration, not an independently verified evaluation of any successor product. The selected
AssistantAgent is stateful and expressly not safe for concurrent calls on the same instance. It
can execute returned tool calls concurrently, and reflection can introduce another inference
call. Its save/load methods preserve model context; they do not record the outcome of every
external action. The code notice inspected for AgentChat is MIT while the root documentation
notice is CC-BY-4.0. The proposal retains AutoGen as a comparative architecture and possible
isolated adapter, but does not make it the default controller or treat conversation persistence
as an exactly-once journal. (autogen contributors, 2026)

   The plain controller is the baseline because its admitted operations and failure states can
be enumerated. This is not evidence that frameworks add no value. A framework may reduce
implementation effort for complex state, streaming or human review. That advantage should
be evaluated against the additional dependencies, semantics and operational responsibilities it
introduces. A thin adapter can preserve the application’s causal request and result contracts
while allowing this comparison. No framework should be credited with discovery, identification
or calibrated uncertainty merely because it can call a tool bearing those names.


48.4      Causal packages need decisions at the scientific boundary
The package inventory covers different kinds of reusable material. PyWhyLLM is a hypothesis-
elicitation candidate: its inspected back-door suggestion path delegates to a model, while the
inspected front-door path is a placeholder. A suggested confounder is not a proven adjustment
set. Adopt the idea of source-linked suggestions conditionally, and pass a supplied graph
to a qualified identification engine. Directly porting the entire dependency stack would add
maintenance without resolving that distinction. (pywhy-llm contributors, 2026)
   The inspected CausalAgent package supplies interaction and tool-wrapper ideas, but its
OLC handler’s missing function binding and permissive malformed-output path prevent
default direct adoption of that route. A wrapper must carry typed errors and graph endpoint
semantics. In oci-agent, the useful intermediate objects are specifications, notebooks and
diagnostic reports. Its inspected unrestricted notebook runner has no finite per-cell timeout,
and its selected trimmed AIPW target differs from conventional overlap weighting. Adapt the
specification/report concepts behind bounded operations; do not expose the general runner as
a trusted causal endpoint. These are static source decisions, not measured failure frequencies.
(CausalAgent contributors, 2026; oci-agent contributors, 2026)
  Benchmark software has another role. CLadder and CausalDS are candidates for evaluating
task formulations and answers after their generator/scorer assumptions are reviewed. They
are not engines whose test labels establish the bank’s causal truth. The selected IV-as-ATE
866                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


and unknown-identification boundaries remain reasons to quarantine unsupported cases or
repair a scorer before using it. OntoLearner can contribute structured vocabulary and local
versioned ontology objects, but taxonomy does not certify a causal edge. LCM remains a
deferred execution candidate until weights, terms and its sufficient lagged regime are qualified.
The LLM-CD and LLM-SCD code pathways retain unresolved license or version-alignment
requirements; their papers can still be evaluated as scientific arguments. (cladder contributors,
2024; causalds contributors, 2026; OntoLearner contributors, 2026; LCM contributors, 2026;
LLM-CD contributors, 2025b; LLM-and-SCD contributors, 2024)
   These choices distinguish five useful dispositions. Direct adoption requires the actual
component’s contract, environment and rights to match the use. Conditional integration adds
an adapter and predeclared acceptance cases. Porting reimplements selected semantics and
needs new numerical and error comparisons; source similarity is insufficient. Reference-only
use borrows an idea without claiming executable reuse. Rejection or deferral records the
reason and a concrete reconsideration trigger. A package can receive different dispositions for
its graph representation, estimator and notebook runner. Treating its repository as a single
yes-or-no choice obscures the component that creates the real scientific or operating risk.


48.5     A state invariant for revision and invalidation
Suppose the controller maintains a dependency graph of immutable analysis objects. A result
stores the exact identities of the target, input data, graph, method and execution environment
used to produce it. Define the reuse invariant I(s) to mean that every result presented as
current has matching admitted dependencies and retains its qualification status. Initially, no
result exists and I holds. A transition that creates a result establishes I only after checking
its dependencies. A transition that changes a dependency preserves I by retiring affected
descendants from the current view and requiring recomputation or an explicit stale label. By
induction, those transition rules preserve I for a finite sequence. This is an application-level
argument under the stated rules, not a proof that the current prototype implements an
arbitrary dependency graph or that supplied causal assumptions are true. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026aa)
   The retirement rule should be selective. In a finite illustrative dependency graph, identifica-
tion depends on the target and graph; estimation also depends on data; valuation depends on
the estimate and cost assumptions; the report depends on valuation. A pure observation-clock
diagnostic depends on the data and clock rule. Changing the target horizon invalidates
identification, estimation, valuation and the report, while leaving that diagnostic current if its
own dependencies did not change. Changing costs invalidates valuation and the report without
changing the effect estimate. An exact traversal verifies these sets in the project example. No
claim is made that every real diagnostic is target-independent: if its admissibility rule uses the
horizon, that dependency must be recorded too. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aa)
   This rule protects a banking decision from a subtle error. An agent can produce a plausible
revision to the question after observing a weak result. The old estimate may remain numerically
unchanged and its source files may still pass all hashes. It becomes ineligible as an answer
to the new question because its scientific dependencies changed. The revised target and
the original result should both remain inspectable. The controller must also prevent a later
successful parse, retry or report step from turning a conditional or unverified premise into
a verified one. Such promotion requires new supporting evidence and a separate recorded
decision.
48.6. Recovery includes an unknown outcome                                                   867


48.6     Recovery includes an unknown outcome
Local pure computations and external effects have different recovery contracts. A deterministic
calculation can be rerun with pinned inputs and environment when recomputation is allowed.
A paid model request may have completed and been billed even if its response was lost. A
proposed journal distinguishes prepared, submitted, acknowledged, completed, failed and
outcome-unknown states. A timeout after submission should not be treated as proof that the
provider did no work. The availability of provider lookup or idempotency must be established
for the selected service. (Causal banking proposal, 2026z)
   There is a simple indistinguishability argument. Let history h0 lose a request before the
external service receives it, and let history h1 lose the response after the service completes
the work. If the local journal in each case contains only submitted and the same timeout, its
observable state is identical. A rule depending only on that state takes the same action in
both histories. Resubmission can duplicate work under h1 ; refusing to resubmit can leave
the task unfinished under h0 . Randomization changes the probabilities but cannot guarantee
both no duplication and eventual completion from this information alone. A service lookup,
idempotent external operation or an explicitly accepted duplication policy adds information or
changes the requirement. This finite argument concerns the stated observation model, not all
possible distributed systems. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aa)
   For a causal assistant, the appropriate response may be to retain an unknown provider
outcome while continuing independent deterministic checks or another task. Cancellation
similarly needs a scope: stopping future local work does not prove that an already submitted
remote request was cancelled or its charge reversed. The budget ledger should retain any
reservation whose financial outcome is unknown until reconciliation. The scientific report can
remain incomplete with an explicit reason; filling the missing answer from memory would sever
its evidence chain.


48.7     Shared budgets require reservations
Usage checks on individual calls do not by themselves enforce a shared budget under concurrency.
Let B be a stipulated expenditure ceiling, S settled cost and R the sum of unresolved
reservations. Before admitting request j with a credible upper cost bound c̄j , a controller can
require
                                        S + R + c̄j ≤ B.                                  (48.2)
The check and reservation must be one serialized state transition. If the actual cost cj is no
larger than its reserved bound, completion replaces that reservation with cj ; hence the total
does not increase beyond its admitted level. Starting from S = R = 0, induction preserves
S +R ≤ B. Unknown prices, unbounded usage, excluded fees or provider overcharges invalidate
the premise; they are not resolved by this algebra. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aa)
   An exact illustrative case makes the race visible. Take B = 10 dollars and settled cost S = 6.
Two requests each require a three-dollar upper bound. If each reads the same unreserved
balance, both individually see 6 + 3 ≤ 10, yet their combined cost can reach 12 dollars.
Under serialized reservation, the first makes S + R = 9, and the second is refused because
6 + 3 + 3 > 10. If the first settles at two dollars, S becomes eight and R returns to zero; the
second three-dollar reservation is still inadmissible. The project calculation enumerates both
admission orders and verifies the same conclusion. All amounts are stipulated; they are not
prices of any model. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aa)
  A successful provider response may supply token counts after money has already been spent.
868                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


Accounting can record that cost correctly without having prevented an overspend. Conversely,
a token cap can limit one resource while leaving human review time or a separately priced tool
unbounded. A useful prototype records call counts, known usage, reservations, settled expense
and unknown charges separately. Retries and reflection consume the same shared budget, and
failed requests remain in its total. These proposed controls address the inspected framework
boundaries without claiming that a financial guarantee follows from a field named cost limit.


48.8      Routing is a decision rule, not a model leaderboard
A prospective router can compare eligible backends by expected task loss and full incremental
cost. For task information z, let eb (z) be a calibrated error probability for backend b, ℓ(z) the
loss of the defined error, and cb (z) its expected call and review cost. Under the deliberately
simplified assumption of one relevant error category and a fixed loss for that category, choose
among eligible backends by
                              b∗ (z) ∈ arg min {cb (z) + ℓ(z)eb (z)}.                        (48.3)
                                          b∈B(z)

The eligible set B(z) encodes data-use and capability constraints. An ineligible backend cannot
become eligible by having a low quoted cost. If the set is empty, the workflow returns an
unavailable route or uses an authorized non-model alternative. Real error categories, uncertain
losses and abstention require a richer decision model. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aa)
   For illustration, backend A costs one dollar with error probability .08, and backend B costs
four dollars with error probability .02. Then B has lower expected total cost precisely when
4 + .02ℓ < 1 + .08ℓ, or ℓ > 50 dollars. At loss 100, the stipulated totals are nine and six dollars;
at loss ten they are 1.80 and 4.20 dollars. These numbers explain what a pilot should measure.
They neither rank real models nor justify applying a benchmark-wide error rate to a new
banking population. Costs of adjudication and wrong refusals must be included if they differ
between routes. (Causal banking proposal, 2026aa)
   To evaluate a router, freeze its task strata and eligibility rules before evaluation, give
alternatives comparable information and tools, and retain every assigned case. Selecting the
backend after seeing the correct answer would evaluate an oracle unavailable at deployment.
A simple deterministic form, a single assisted controller and a critic-assisted controller provide
useful alternatives before sophisticated routing. The experiments should measure whether the
extra model work changes target errors, unresolved assumptions, usable results and review
effort. Scientific identification still belongs to the causal model and data; routing changes
assistance, not what the observational law identifies.


48.9      From architectural comparison to a bounded prototype
The proposed adoption sequence begins with the existing fixed-operation controller and
generated inputs. A selected framework can then be placed behind an adapter preserving
the same requests, grants, result types and failure meanings. Offline fixtures test schema and
recovery behavior before an actual model is admitted. A live trial, if justified, needs named
model and service identities, permitted data, measured usage and an independent task rubric.
It can use public and generated tasks to establish whether further bank experimentation
is worth funding. No authentic customer trial is required merely to compare the proposed
interfaces.
   The present comparison remains scoped. Three pinned orchestration frameworks and the
selected causal packages support concrete decisions; they are not a complete census of all
48.10. An adapter must preserve the scientific object                                           869


backends or hosted services. A current commercial-model feature or price comparison requires
inspected official evidence and an applicable version/date. Model terms, deployment rights,
task performance, costs and authentic owner acceptance remain distinct unresolved questions.
The following preserved local implementation provides a concrete baseline against which such
additions can be tested. (Causal banking proposal, 2026z,ab)


48.10       An adapter must preserve the scientific object
Typed input is useful only if the adapter preserves what the fields mean. Consider two
implementations of the same analysis path: a direct local service and a framework-mediated
service. Let x be a valid request with its scientific context, and let F (x) be the result of a
qualified deterministic engine under that context. An adapter encodes the request with E,
sends it through the tool interface, and decodes the response with D. The desired comparison
is semantic:
                                    D{Ftool (E(x))} ≡ F (x),                             (48.4)
where ≡ requires the same target, assumptions, qualification and result meaning, not identical
incidental ordering of JSON fields. For a pure deterministic numerical path it may also require
exact values, or a declared numerical tolerance supported by the computation. For stochastic
methods the comparison must declare randomization and distributional criteria. Passing one
exact fixture does not prove this relation for every request. This is a proposed qualification
relation with explicit domains, not an asserted property of an installed framework. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026y)
   Several superficially convenient encodings cannot satisfy that relation. Suppose an encoder
replaces every finite or unbounded effect set by a pair containing its smallest and largest
endpoints. Then the union (−∞, −2] ∪ [3, ∞) and the whole line both produce the same pair
of infinite endpoints. A downstream decoder receiving only that pair cannot know which input
was supplied. If it returns the union, it is wrong for the whole-line input; if it returns the
whole line, it is wrong for the union as an exact representation. It could return a conservative
outer approximation if the contract explicitly permits loss of precision, but it must label that
transformation rather than claim equivalence. An exact finite representation of endpoint pairs
reproduces this collision in the project example.
   There is a general reason. Let E(x1 ) = E(x2 ) for two scientifically distinguishable objects
x1 and x2 . Any deterministic decoder D has the same output on the two equal encodings.
Therefore both identities D(E(x1 )) = x1 and D(E(x2 )) = x2 cannot hold. Randomized
decoding cannot guarantee recovery of both without additional information either. The
same argument applies when an adapter collapses PAG endpoint types, maps unknown and
nonidentified into one status, or drops which population an effect targets. Before considering
a port, the proposal should inspect whether the receiving schema is expressive enough. More
elaborate retry logic cannot reconstruct information the schema discarded. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026y)
   A refusal state also carries scientific information. A graphical engine can return an identifica-
tion expression, a formal nonidentification result within a specified model class, an unsupported
method, or an operational failure. These states call for different continuation actions. A
framework that treats every returned string as a successful tool result may preserve transport
bytes while discarding that distinction in its next prompt. The adapter should expose a tagged
result and require the next operation to consume an admitted tag. A report can state that a
method is unsupported without claiming the target is unknowable. A timeout cannot become
an estimated effect of zero. These conditions can be tested with authored fixtures before a
model is selected.
870                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


48.10.1     Units, signs and set-valued banking decisions

Unit conversion illustrates a transformation that can preserve meaning when it is explicit.
Let an effect θ be measured in dollars and suppose an interface returns thousands of dollars:
θ′ = θ/1000. An interval or union must be transformed as a set, not only by changing a display
label. More generally, for a nonzero constant a and constant b, let T (θ) = aθ + b. For a closed
interval [l, u], its image is [al + b, au + b] when a > 0 and [au + b, al + b] when a < 0. Infinite
endpoints and each component of a union follow the same ordering rule. Empty and whole-line
sets retain their distinct identities. (Causal banking proposal, 2026y)
   If a set C has coverage at least 1 − α for θ, then its exact image T (C) has coverage at
least 1 − α for T (θ) when T is a fixed known bijection: the events θ ∈ C and T (θ) ∈ T (C)
are identical. An outer enclosure of T (C) can preserve the lower coverage guarantee while
losing precision. A numerical inner approximation has no such automatic guarantee. If the
conversion rate or cost is estimated, the fixed-known-map premise fails and its uncertainty
must be accounted for. This elementary argument explains why representation and numerical
error belong in an adapter contract. It does not validate the original set’s sampling law.
   Take a stipulated offer-minus-no-offer effect set C = (−∞, −2] ∪ [3, ∞) dollars and an
incremental offer cost of one dollar. The net-value set is C − 1 = (−∞, −3] ∪ [2, ∞). Its worst
case is negative and its best case is positive, so this set alone does not justify either robust
acceptance or robust rejection under a sign rule. Reporting only the midpoint of a finite
substitute interval would invent a decision. If a receiving tool instead uses the reverse treatment
contrast, the effect set becomes −C = (−∞, −3] ∪ [2, ∞), but this numerical coincidence in
the chosen example does not make reversing the contrast equivalent to subtracting cost. The
object must retain the target and transformation, not only the endpoints.
   For a less coincidental bounded check, let C = [2, 5] and a positive one-dollar cost. Net
value is [1, 4], so every admitted value supports the offer under the stipulated expected-value
sign criterion. Reversing the effect contrast produces [−5, −2]; it is not [1, 4]. Scaling dollars
into thousands maps the original effect to [.002, .005] and the cost to .001 in those units.
Subtracting a cost of one in the new units would be a thousandfold error. Exact rational
images in the example check the sign, units and component ordering. The resulting conclusions
remain illustrative consequences of stipulated sets and costs, not validated lending advice or
empirical financial benefit. (Causal banking proposal, 2026y)


48.10.2     Porting needs a failure-domain comparison

A port’s acceptance domain should include both supported and deliberately unsupported
requests. In supported cases compare scientific context, endpoint conventions, uncertainty tags,
set topology, estimates and applicable numerical tolerances. In unsupported cases compare the
reason and retained provenance. Test NaN, infinity, missing timestamps, duplicate variable
identifiers, a changed sign convention and a graph with unresolved endpoints according to
the receiving method’s contract. The expected answer may be refusal. A test that merely
requires the port to return something for every case rewards the very semantic substitutions
the product is meant to prevent.
   The comparison should record which differences are representational and which are substan-
tive. Object-key order may be irrelevant to the engine yet consequential to a byte digest; a
normalized serialization can be introduced with an explicit version and migration. Changing
a dependency law from independent accounts to monthly panels is substantive even if the
numerical array is unchanged. A port can preserve syntax and still change inference. These
distinctions motivate a thin typed adapter first, followed by a port only when measured
48.11. Attribute improvements to the component that changed                                    871


operational benefits justify the additional qualification burden.


48.11      Attribute improvements to the component that changed
Comparing an elaborate new agent to an old script can conflate at least three changes: a
stronger backend, better orchestration and access to better causal tools. A product decision
needs to know which component accounts for an observed improvement and at what cost.
A prospective comparison can hold documents, permitted tools, review rubric and total
repair opportunity fixed while varying backend and orchestration. Let b ∈ {A, B} index two
candidate backends and f ∈ {0, 1} a plain controller versus the framework candidate. For
eligible task i, define loss Li (b, f ) to include the predeclared scientific error and operational
failure consequences. Lower loss is better.
   If all four outcomes can be obtained without contamination, a paired task comparison
isolates the framework contrast at each backend. If repeated exposure changes human judgment
or leaks a reference answer, use independent adjudicators, blinded outputs or randomized
assignment with a declared estimand. Neither approach permits tuning the framework on
the final task answers. Tasks that share a generating mechanism are not automatically
independent observations, so task families and their sampling law must be declared before
attaching inferential uncertainty. The prospective construction here is an evaluation design,
not a claim of collected experimental outcomes. (Causal banking proposal, 2026y)
   Write µbf = ELi (b, f ) for the mean under the target evaluation task distribution. The mean
framework contrast, averaging equally over the two backends, is

                             ∆F = 12 [(µA1 − µA0 ) + (µB1 − µB0 )],                         (48.5)

and the analogous backend contrast is

                             ∆B = 21 [(µB0 − µA0 ) + (µB1 − µA1 )].                         (48.6)

The interaction ∆BF = (µB1 −µB0 )−(µA1 −µA0 ) measures how the framework contrast changes
with backend. These are descriptive contrasts of the stipulated factorial task experiment.
Their identification from sampled trials depends on the assignment and missing outcome rules.
Unequal deployment frequencies would require the relevant weights rather than the equal
weights used here.
  An exact example takes mean losses (µA0 , µA1 , µB0 , µB1 ) = (10, 8, 7, 6). Then ∆F = −1.5,
∆B = −2.5 and ∆BF = 1. The framework reduces mean loss by two units with A but only
one with B. The diagonal comparison µB1 − µA0 = −4 mixes both changes; it cannot all
be attributed to orchestration. The average contrasts sum to the diagonal difference, yet
their separate magnitudes carry the investment information. Costs require their own four-cell
measurement, including failed tasks and review effort. The numbers are authored illustrations,
not performance claims about any named framework. (Causal banking proposal, 2026y)
   Availability creates a further denominator problem. Suppose both routes receive 100 tasks.
Route A returns 90 answers with 81 correct; route B returns 60 with 57 correct. B’s correctness
among returned answers is 95 percent, above A’s 90 percent, but its correct-answer fraction
among all assigned tasks is 57 percent versus 81 percent. Neither summary alone settles utility
when correct refusals and harmful wrong answers have different values. If every unanswered
task incurs a stipulated loss of three and every wrong returned answer a loss of ten, A incurs
120 total loss units and B 150. At loss one per unanswered task, the totals become 100 and 70.
The preferred route changes with the actual decision consequences. These exact counts show
why missingness and refusal must be classified before ranking an architecture.
872                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   A properly specified causal task sometimes requires a refusal or a set rather than a scalar
estimate. Such an output belongs in the correct answer category if the rubric calls for it.
Backend refusal for an unrelated service-policy reason, inability to parse, and unavailable
scientific method are different categories. They should remain visible even if a decision maker
later aggregates their losses. The prospective pilot should first establish that the rubric
recognizes these outcomes, then compare useful assistance under that rubric. A subsequent
bank trial can ask whether the resulting architecture preserves meaning and improves decisions
in its own population; the public/generated study cannot silently stand in for that external
question. (Causal banking proposal, 2026y)


48.12      The implemented boundary
The prototype implements a local handoff from a structured business proposal to fixed causal
operations. It accepts an authored fixture or a recorded model output in a provider-neutral
envelope. It does not contact a model endpoint. The envelope contains the question and its
alternative targets, candidate diagrams, proposed operation names and a provenance record.
That record names the provider, model, revision and generation parameters, retains the exact
prompt, and checks the prompt’s SHA-256 identity. The complete proposal receives its own
content identity. A recorded label is provenance supplied by the caller; it is not independent
proof that a particular model generated the bytes.
   This boundary is deliberately useful before a provider is selected. It permits the same
semantic checks to be applied to different proposed backends without making a framework’s
response format the definition of a causal question. It also separates two evaluations. One
asks whether the controller preserves a given declaration and result. The other asks whether a
model produces good declarations from unfamiliar business questions. The executed examples
answer the first. They supply no empirical answer to the second.
   A proposal can request graph review, graphical identification, discovery or a moment-based
effect calculation. These names do not imply that every operation is implemented for every
input. The fixed service implements syntax review, a supplied-DAG back-door attempt, and
a declared Gaussian moment-inversion calculation. Discovery remains unsupported in the
present service. An unsupported operation returns that status; it does not invent an empty
graph or an effect of zero. There is no operation for sending a customer communication,
altering an account or approving a bank action.


48.13      The three identities of a proposed analysis
Three identities control the handoff. The proposal identity describes the complete proposed
content and model record. The declaration identity covers the problem and diagram together,
including every target alternative, evidence reference, assumption, clock and graph revision.
Finally, the execution identity covers prepared requests, the caller’s grant, source code, schemas
and numerical environment. Changing a population while keeping the same diagram changes
the declaration. Changing an implementation while keeping the same question changes the
execution. Neither change can silently reuse an old result as if nothing had changed.
  The declaration validator checks structure and selected semantic constraints. These include
whether referenced evidence exists in the declaration, whether graph endpoints refer to declared
variables, whether a DAG has a directed cycle, whether a proposed history includes a future
decision, and whether a policy uses information before its declared availability. It also flags
unresolved targets, contradicted assumptions, post-treatment adjustment for a proposed total
48.14. A narrow projection with explicit refusals                                             873


effect and conditioning a population on treatment descendants. It does not prove that an
asserted DAG is true or fully recognize every MAG, PAG or CPDAG. A successful declaration
review means that a stated problem can proceed to an appropriately scoped formal analysis.
    Evidence identities receive an additional byte check. Source records reference bounded local
files under the documentation tree; symlink escapes and paths outside that boundary are
refused. The actual bytes must match the declared hash. This catches a changed source or
stale citation record. It does not check whether a source’s scientific assertion is true. The full
source record, declaration and proposal are retained as immutable artifacts so that a result
can be traced back to both the claim and the bytes that supported its review.
   The external grant is a trusted local caller object bound to the declaration identity. It
lists permitted operations, names the reviewer and supplies the sampling declaration and any
numerical inputs. Putting a reviewer’s name into the model response does not create this object.
Requesting a new operation does not extend its permissions. The grant is an application
boundary, not a digital signature or a bank identity service. Institutional authentication and
approval stores remain requirements for a later deployment.


48.14       A narrow projection with explicit refusals
The implemented translator supports an unconditional population ATE for one static binary
action, with intervention one and comparator zero. Its horizon starts at the declared origin.
It retains all variables and requires the graph to account for them. Outcome and target-loss
units must agree. It does not silently convert a dynamic regime, an overlap target, a selected
population or a utility transformation into this static ATE.
   For a supported target, the translator builds the fixed operation’s scientific context and
places the complete original declaration in its source evidence. The smaller operation schema
carries the treatment, outcome, population, units, horizon, assumptions and graph. The
retained declaration carries the detailed measurement lineage and numeric decision/availability
clocks. Thus a consumer can reconstruct the original problem even where the narrow operation
schema has no field for every detail. No synthetic or analyst assertion is upgraded to externally
verified truth during this projection.
   Candidate graphs are processed individually. For the synthetic offer question, the input
includes an undirected CPDAG and its two directed alternatives. The controller preserves
all three candidate identities. Syntax review returns the CPDAG’s tail endpoints intact. A
supported directed graph can receive a conditional back-door result. Another candidate may
be outside the implemented identification method. The overall record stays ambiguous, and
every candidate’s response remains visible. It does not average graph outputs or select the
most convenient result. These alternatives describe possible worlds; the prototype does not
assert their simultaneous truth or estimate probabilities for them.
   The distinction between nonidentification and an unsuccessful implementation attempt is
essential here. Failure of the supplied back-door procedure does not prove that no other valid
identification argument exists. Likewise, refusal to translate the servicing policy does not
prove that its value is unknowable. It records that this controller has no qualified mapping
from that richer target into its fixed service. The full policy, clocks and assumptions remain
available for a future longitudinal adapter.
874                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


48.15      Representative executed paths
Six synthetic local paths were executed and exported with their artifact descriptors and
checkpoint records. The ambiguous funding question is blocked before invoking a tool because
its economic target has not been resolved. The observation example is also blocked: ownership
and selection questions remain substantive. The servicing declaration passes its own chronology
checks but is unsupported by the narrow static translator. These outcomes are useful behavior;
returning a number would answer an unstated substitute question.
   The discovery example reaches actual graph-review and identification tools for each candidate
and preserves ambiguity. A separate directed fixture exercises ordinary conditional execution,
interruption and exact replay. It is an explicit fixture choice of a supplied graph, not a
discovered resolution of the original ambiguous problem. Finally, a weak moment example
reaches the effect service and retains a two-component unbounded set. The mean vector
supplied is (1, 0), the covariance matrix is diagonal with entries 0.01 and 1, and the declared
sample size is 100. The resulting set has two unbounded tails separated by a finite excluded
region. The controller preserves both tails and the service’s joint-confidence label together
with its Gaussian-approximation limitation. It neither replaces the union by a finite interval
nor interprets the zero denominator estimate as a finite causal effect.
   The numerical example checks propagation of a declared mathematical result. It does not
estimate moments from bank observations or prove that the supplied covariance is valid under
dependence. The original scientific gaps concerning persistent maps, latent temporal graphs
and dependent learners therefore remain open. A semantic adapter cannot repair a failed
inferential law by attaching a more complete provenance record.


48.16      Recovery and adverse inputs
The local journal stores each completed tool response under a hash of the full execution identity.
Publication is atomic. On resumption, the controller checks that saved results form a prefix of
the planned operations, that their content hash is unchanged, that each response belongs to
the correct request, and that referenced artifacts still match their bytes. Source verification
also runs before a completed replay. A changed source is therefore rejected even when a result
already exists in the journal.
   In the interruption fixture, the controller stops after saving the graph-review response and
before the identification step. Resumption keeps the saved review and executes only the
remaining identification operation. A later complete replay returns the same record without
reinvoking tools. This is a tested single-host property of the local fixed operations and journal.
It does not establish distributed exactly-once execution, authenticated tamper resistance
against the local operator, or recovery for arbitrary external side effects. Those stronger claims
would require different implementations and trials.
  The adverse tests exercise both content and authority boundaries. They reject unknown
operations, injected command or permission fields, nonfinite model parameters, changed
prompt bytes and a live-mode declaration. A retrieved text fixture tells the system to ignore
checks and execute a shell command; the controller keeps it as source data and performs only
the granted graph review. This verifies the deterministic command boundary. It is not a
measurement of a live model’s susceptibility to scientifically misleading text.
  Other tests change source bytes, corrupt a checkpoint, alter a target after the grant, introduce
a contradicted assumption, or move the servicing decision before L1 is available. Missing
numerical evidence returns a failed calculation without an estimate. The recorded output
48.17. What the next evaluation must establish                                               875


retains the cause of failure. Together with the inherited problem and operation contract cases,
80 checks pass. This is local conformance evidence, not an accuracy percentage for unseen
banking questions.
   The first integration runs also exposed ordinary engineering limits. Some frozen operation
schemas accepted fewer optional fields than the general context schema. Retaining detailed
clocks in the bound declaration supplied a compatible mapping without dropping them. A
256 MiB address-space allowance was insufficient for imported numerical dependencies; the
executed configuration uses the existing runtime’s tested 1 GiB allowance. Both failed runs are
retained in the evidence. Memory ceilings constrain execution; they do not imply measured
peak memory or comparative efficiency.


48.17      What the next evaluation must establish
The prototype creates a stable place to evaluate actual assistance. A model can eventually
propose a target and diagram, but its output must pass the same declaration and permission
boundaries. An evaluation must compare those proposals with an ordinary structured workflow
and with independent reference judgments. It must score target meaning, evidence applicability,
unresolved ambiguity, graph classes and downstream effect conclusions. Faster or more fluent
reports are secondary when the intervention, population or clock has changed.
   The present records contain zero live model calls. Model tokens and prices remain unavailable,
rather than being reported as measured zeros. All examples are synthetic, all graph resolutions
are explicit fixture assumptions, and no customer action is authorized. A real comparison still
needs exact backend versions, approved data custody, original benchmark identities, experts for
business and diagram judgments, and a frozen analysis of every requested case. The controller
supplies traceable inputs and outputs for that work; the missing scientific and institutional
evidence cannot be inferred from its successful execution.
  The local implementation and historical conformance counts in this chapter are bound to
the preserved source, original trials and subsequent six-case replay. They do not constitute
new provider execution. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ab)


48.18      Evaluate the causal contract across the agent’s compo-
           nents
An agent framework becomes useful to the bank when its components can be evaluated against
a stable decision contract. Consider again an arrears servicing offer. A plausible explanation,
a completed sequence of tool calls and a correct causal answer are three different outcomes.
The system might produce a fluent justification while conditioning on a variable recorded
after the offer. It might execute the requested estimator successfully while answering the
effect among treated accounts rather than the effect in the eligible population. Conversely,
a scientifically correct answer might be that the declared observations do not identify the
requested effect. A framework comparison should preserve these distinctions when it chooses
components, evaluation data and metrics.


48.18.1     Architecture is a map of responsibilities, not a certificate

Wang et al. (2025a) organize autonomous-agent architecture into profile, memory, planning and
action, and distinguish architecture from capability acquisition. This is a useful account of the
876                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


survey authors’ taxonomy. It is secondary evidence for the individual systems and experiments
that the survey discusses. Its selected March 2025 revision, including a benchmark table
largely describing 2022–2023 work, cannot establish the current frontier through October 2026.
The taxonomy nevertheless helps specify where a causal assistant’s responsibilities reside.
   A profile can declare a servicing analyst’s remit; it cannot establish the bank’s authority to
change an account’s treatment. Memory can preserve a previous graph and its supporting
sources; retrieval of that graph does not make its assumptions current for another product
or calendar period. Planning can propose an adjustment analysis, a sensitivity analysis or a
request for clarification. The plan needs a mathematical applicability check before execution.
An action component can call a causal engine, but the result must retain the target, graph and
observation definitions used by that engine. These are proposed mappings from the taxonomy
to banking responsibilities, not findings that the surveyed agents already satisfy them. The
state invariant in Equation 48.1 remains the application’s responsibility.
   The survey separates subjective human evaluation from objective metrics, protocols and
benchmarks. Task success, similarity to human behavior and efficiency answer different
questions. Its discussion also recognizes the cost and population bias of human evaluation and
the inability of objective techniques to measure every capability perfectly. In this proposal, a
business reviewer judges whether the question and explanation reflect the intended decision. A
mathematical reference checks whether a result is correct under explicit assumptions. Neither
judgment should silently replace the other. An uncertain or disputed reference requires an
adjudication status; another model’s agreement is not sufficient causal ground truth. (Wang
et al., 2025a)
   The same survey identifies interacting-module prompt fragility, hallucination, knowledge-
boundary problems in simulations and repeated-call efficiency. These motivate concrete
evaluation cases. A retrieved passage can contain an instruction inconsistent with the declared
target. An apparently helpful memory can introduce information unavailable at the decision
time. A simulated analyst can exploit knowledge hidden from the person being represented,
making the simulation’s task success irrelevant to the real information constraint. A correct
final answer can require many failed intermediate calls. These are reasons to inspect complete
traces and information availability, rather than infer banking performance from a general
agent benchmark. The cases are proposed causal evaluations; their frequencies have not been
measured here. (Wang et al., 2025a)


48.18.2    What a general evaluation library contributes

Zhu et al. (2024a) present PromptBench as a modular library for models, datasets, prompts,
adversarial attacks and evaluation protocols. Their four-stage pipeline initializes the data
and model, specifies prompts, defines input/output handling and metrics, and runs the
evaluation. The selected article reports twelve tasks and twenty-two datasets. Its appendices
describe extension hooks for datasets, models, methods and metrics. These are relevant
design mechanisms for a causal-contract evaluator: a dataset could contain versioned business
questions and admissible responses, while a custom metric checks target and assumption
preservation.
   Those mechanisms do not supply the causal reference. For example, a case asking for an
adjustment set needs a declared graph and an appropriate graphical criterion. A case asking
for an effect interval needs a reference identified set or another justified numerical target. A
question whose meaning changes with the timing of a balance variable needs a clarification
reference. Matching a stored phrase without checking these objects would reward superficial
agreement. A proposed adapter should therefore send a typed request to the existing scientific
48.18. Evaluate the causal contract across the agent’s components                            877


boundary and score its typed response, while retaining the prompt, reference version and
execution trace. PromptBench’s extensibility makes that design plausible; no such adapter is
claimed to have been implemented or qualified by this source inspection. (Zhu et al., 2024a)
   The paper’s empirical conclusions also argue against a single preferred prompt. It reports
adversarial vulnerability, prompt-engineering methods that do not outperform the baseline
on every dataset, and remaining weaknesses on selected dynamic tasks. These are attributed
historical results, not a local reproduction or a ranking of present models. Its own limita-
tions discuss incomplete scenario coverage, metric nuance and the quality of datasets and
prompts. A banking comparison should consequently retain the unmodified baseline, prespec-
ify perturbations and report task-specific failures. It should not select a favorable wording
after examining held-out answers and then call that result general robustness. The paper’s
historical comparison with other libraries is likewise an author comparison at that time, not
an independent purchasing table. (Zhu et al., 2024a)
   The proposed reuse disposition is reference use of these evaluation interfaces, followed by
conditional integration if a selected implementation fits the causal request and result schemas.
A pinned code revision, package and dependency rights, environment, input/output behavior
and a matched baseline would have to be inspected before executable adoption. The article’s
CC-BY-4.0 notice concerns the paper; it is not evidence of the software distribution’s license.
Porting the full library would require new evidence that its maintenance cost is justified
relative to a small local evaluator. Rejecting every general evaluator merely because it does not
itself prove identification would also discard potentially useful infrastructure. The appropriate
boundary is to reuse orchestration and measurement only while retaining application-owned
scientific references.


48.18.3     Completion, correctness and the denominator

Evaluation must make unsuccessful execution visible without penalizing a correct scientific
refusal as if it were a crash. For a fixed case i and wording j, let Rij = 1 denote a completed,
interpretable response and Rij = 0 an unanswered execution. Among completed responses, let
Kij = 1 denote correctness under the frozen causal contract and Kij = 0 an incorrect response.
Set Rij Kij = 0 for an unanswered case solely for the following accounting identity. With N
planned requests, define
                 P                   P                      P
                   ij Rij             ij Rij Kij             ij Rij Kij
            C=              ,   J=                 ,   A=    P            ,   J = CA.     (48.7)
                     N                   N                      ij Rij

Here C is completion, J is correct responses per planned request and A is correctness conditional
on completion. The last two expressions involving A apply only when at least one response
is completed; A is undefined if none is completed. These are finite accounting quantities,
not estimates of calibrated causal uncertainty. A correct nonidentification certificate, an
appropriate ambiguity report or a required clarification can count as completed and correct.
The contract must declare when each is appropriate; indiscriminate refusal cannot receive
credit on answerable cases. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026s)
   An exact authored example makes the difference material. Stipulate twenty servicing-
question families, each with two wordings having identical outcomes within that family for
each system. There are forty planned requests. The example specifies the answers directly;
it contains no model calls, framework trials, simulated accuracy or bank observations. Thus
reporting A alone favors the system that completes fewer cases, whereas reporting J alone
conceals its lower error count. Neither scalar settles the banking decision. The full counts
distinguish reduced coverage from increased wrong answers, and task strata can reveal whether
878                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank

                   A             22        2             16 3/5 11/20 11/12
                   B             30        6              4 9/10  3/4   5/6
