Its step-6 expansion is a different expression. Literal evaluation gives

                    {0.22(0.60 − 0.28) + 0.78(0.74 − 0.35)}
                       − {0.57(0.60 − 0.28) + 0.43(0.74 − 0.35)} = 0.0245,                 (50.49)

not the printed 0.0173. These calculations use exact rational arithmetic; they reproduce the
displayed inputs without executing any downloaded program. (Shrestha et al., 2025; Causal
banking proposal project, 2026bd)
   The numerical discrepancy is only part of the issue. The narrative supplies death probabilities
but names the outcome as survival, and its displayed counterfactual notation must be reconciled
with the intended natural indirect effect. Equations (50.48) and (50.49) consequently identify
inconsistencies; neither is declared the corrected benchmark truth. Establishing that truth
requires the intended coding, structural model, counterfactual target and actual generator. A
library can faithfully calculate the wrong expression or use the right expression with reversed
outcome coding. A benchmark protocol must admit a disputed-reference outcome and preserve
it outside the accuracy denominator until adjudicated under a predeclared rule.
   In the banking example, a similar reversal between default and survival could change the
action recommendation. Correctness must therefore be attached to the complete target and
its units, rather than merely to a signed decimal. Independent arithmetic checks are valuable
precisely because they inspect a different failure mechanism from language-model agreement.
They still do not supply the scientific assumptions that make a mediation or intervention
functional appropriate.


50.37.6      A public prototype with separate tests for each claim

The proposal can investigate these methods without first requesting an expensive bank
experiment. Begin with public, known-law cases whose variables, decision times, mechanisms
and targets are fixed before model evaluation. Split by underlying mechanism and document
family, so paraphrases and renamed variables do not leak between development and evaluation.
Retain three related tasks: extract a question and its evidence; determine whether a supplied
model supports the requested target; and calculate that target when it is supported. Include
cases with missing assumptions, contradictory coding and several compatible diagrams, for
which a single effect is not the correct output.
   Compare a no-tool answer, a direct formula checker, calls to a constrained causal library and
a generated-code agent on the same frozen cases. Review source-span fidelity, temporal roles,
missing variables, graph alternatives, identification/refusal, numerical error and final decision
separately. Count invalid code, timeouts, retries and abstentions in declared denominators. A
50.38. What the saved causal-reasoning records establish                                      975


correct final yes/no answer must not conceal an unsupported graph or a wrong estimand that
happened to yield the same sign. Blinded reference adjudication should precede scoring, and
unresolved reference disagreements should be visible.
   The comparison also needs model and tool revisions, seeds or decoding settings, raw
responses, generated programs, dependencies and all failed attempts. Question-level paired
results support uncertainty calculations that respect the shared cases. Token use, tool calls,
latency and human correction time belong in a full workflow comparison. Useful merit means
meeting a predeclared combination of decision quality, justified refusal and total cost; it is not
established by the paper’s accuracy improvement alone. These are proposed public qualification
steps, with no live-model result claimed here.


50.37.7     A proposed CLI and MCP boundary

A request should distinguish a calculation from a proposed interpretation. It should carry
the decision time, eligible population, intervention, outcome coding, horizon, source identities
and spans, graph alternatives, estimand and explicit assumptions. A calculation request
additionally needs its actual probability table or dataset and a declared sampling law. The
response should return the selected target, unresolved conditions, calculation provenance
and a typed disposition. Missing scientific information, conflicting evidence, unsupported
identification, invalid code and numerical failure are different outcomes requiring different next
actions.
   For a generated-code prototype, the proposed execution boundary permits only declared
inputs and bounded computation in a restricted environment. Generated code, dependency
identities and tool inputs must be inspectable, and network access or policy actions must
not be implicit consequences of a calculation. A formula checker or typed library call can
supply a simpler comparator with a smaller execution surface. The paper motivates evaluating
these alternatives; its use of a REPL is not evidence that this proposed interface has been
implemented or qualified. The paper’s repository, full prompts, raw evaluation files and their
reuse rights remain to be inspected before executable adoption. (Shrestha et al., 2025)
   The resulting investment question is concrete: can constrained calculation support improve
a faithfully specified causal workflow on public cases at an acceptable total cost? A positive
result would justify a more expensive prototype or institutional study while preserving the
additional assumptions that authentic banking decisions require.


50.38      What the saved causal-reasoning records establish
The public repository linked by Shrestha and colleagues permits a more precise assessment
of the preceding paper-level questions. Its selected 23 March 2025 commit contains prompts,
inference helpers, notebooks and result tables. Twelve selected files have been checked against
their pinned Git blob identities. The following source and saved-result findings supersede the
preceding section’s unresolved availability statements for those selected materials. They resolve
some reporting questions while revealing why a saved benchmark score and a reproducible,
qualified agent are different claims. No upstream program or model was executed in this
inspection.(Rahul Shrestha and causal-reasoning contributors, 2025)
976                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


50.38.1    Reproduce the score before interpreting the gain

Each of the three RQ3 result tables has 1,000 unique question identifiers. The identifiers,
reference labels, query types and rungs align across variants. Direct comparison of the eight
method-answer columns with their stored labels reproduces all twenty-four subset averages
in Table 4. In particular, baseline, tree and program correct counts are 843, 875 and 925
on commonsensical cases; 824, 865 and 903 on anti-commonsensical cases; and 793, 853 and
896 on nonsense cases. Every selected final-answer entry is either yes or no. This is a replay
of scoring over saved outputs, not a new model evaluation or independent validation of the
reference labels.(Rahul Shrestha and causal-reasoning contributors, 2025; Causal banking
proposal project, 2026be)
   The raw sample includes 138 treatment-on-the-treated questions, resolving the one-item
discrepancy with the paper’s printed count of 137. Its rung counts are 405 association, 197
intervention and 398 counterfactual questions. The paired records also show the errors hidden
by an average gain. On commonsensical cases the program corrects 141 baseline errors but
loses 59 answers the baseline got right. Those counts are 152 and 73 on anti-commonsensical
cases, and 182 and 79 on nonsense cases. Net gains are therefore 82, 79 and 103 correct answers
per thousand, consistent with the reported subset averages. (Causal banking proposal project,
2026be)
  For a proposed banking assistant, the regression cases deserve their own review. A method
that improves average accuracy can still fail on a particular decision category or on cases
where the simpler method succeeds. The records permit paired analysis by question. They
do not supply a sampling justification for treating all paraphrased variants as independent
deployment observations. Uncertainty and decision-cost comparisons should respect shared
question and mechanism identities, and should not interpret repeated reference labels as
independent adjudications.
   Some appendix discrepancies remain unresolved. The five-chain and ten-chain self-
consistency reasoning fields are empty in all three saved tables. Final majority labels cannot
reconstruct individual chain votes or explain the reported vote-pattern totals of 999 and 995.
The selected records likewise do not contain the error-category annotations needed to reconcile
sixty listed errors with a fifty-case description. These limitations concern particular missing
records; they do not negate the twenty-four reproduced accuracy averages.(Rahul Shrestha
and causal-reasoning contributors, 2025; Causal banking proposal project, 2026be)


50.38.2    A numerical target can reconcile while its meaning remains disputed

Question 2883 matches the penguin example in Appendix D.3. Its stored numerical target
is approximately −0.11217602178843022. Applying the displayed step-4 functional to the
record’s unrounded probabilities yields −0.11217602178843015, agreeing to within 10−15 . The
rounded calculation of −0.112 in the preceding section is consequently consistent with the
saved numerical target. The positive expansion printed in the paper is not a reproduction of
that target.(Causal banking proposal project, 2026be)
  This resolves the numerical comparison, not the semantic problem. The stored question still
describes death probabilities while asking about survival, and the stored formal expression still
needs reconciliation with the intended natural indirect effect. Even the saved reasoning string
contains an arithmetic expression inconsistent with its stated result. A scorer can faithfully
compare an agent’s answer with the stored “yes” while leaving these problems untouched.
The original generator, outcome coding, polarity and intended intervention must be inspected
before relabeling the case or calling its reference independently correct.(Rahul Shrestha and
50.38. What the saved causal-reasoning records establish                                     977


causal-reasoning contributors, 2025)
   In a financial application, analogous disagreement could concern whether a field denotes
default, repayment, positive recovery or a negative loss. A small numerical tolerance is useful
after those semantics are fixed. It cannot settle them. The proposed result contract should
retain both the recorded numerical functional and the unresolved interpretation, rather than
silently converting agreement with a stored number into a validated decision recommendation.


50.38.3     The example generator and the displayed graph disagree

The program prompt supplies an illustrative drug-assignment example. Read literally as an
intended generator, it draws assignment A with probability one half, then independently draws
adherence T and low cholesterol Y conditional on A. Its probabilities are

                     P (T = 1 | A = 0) = 0.79, P (T = 1 | A = 1) = 0.43,
                     P (Y = 1 | A = 0) = 0.54, P (Y = 1 | A = 1) = 0.52.

The generated outcome does not depend on adherence once assignment is fixed. Yet the
displayed DoWhy graph contains only T → Y and treats adherence as the intervention.
Assignment, which drives both generated variables, is omitted. The example also contains
explanatory text that is not valid Python inside its purported code illustration. These are
properties of the selected prompt text; the prompt module itself is a Python string, and no
failure rate for generated programs follows from inspecting it.(Rahul Shrestha and causal-

  An exact project calculation isolates the scientific issue independently of syntax. Under the
independent-noise generator just described,

   For the servicing decision, the same failure occurs if an assistant generates offer acceptance
and subsequent loss from distress but passes a graph containing only acceptance and loss
to an estimator. Larger artificial samples would make the associational calculation more

50.38.4     Reference reuse requires a different execution contract

The selected inference helper has a concrete call mismatch: its self-consistency function accepts
four parameters while its caller supplies five. Within the helper, the completion call also omits
the client required by that routine. The tree branch in the common runner is unimplemented,
with tree logic instead appearing in a separate notebook. These observations qualify the
selected source revision. They do not establish which revision or interactive notebook state
generated the saved result tables.(Rahul Shrestha and causal-reasoning contributors, 2025)
    The README recommends installation through a pip requirements command, but the
file is a Conda environment export for macOS on ARM, including Python 3.12, DoWhy 0.8
978                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


and platform-specific build strings. A supported environment cannot be inferred from that
instruction. The notebooks retain fixed-seed sample construction but also partial example
runs, several scoring denominators and model names that do not bind a provider snapshot.
The program runner hands generated code to a REPL; its use of input sanitization does not
establish the proposed resource, network or tool-permission boundaries. (Rahul Shrestha and
causal-reasoning contributors, 2025)
   The repository carries a complete MIT grant for its author’s material. Rights for inherited
benchmark data, dependencies, model access and downstream uses remain separate. The
defensible proposal decision is to retain the prompts and saved records as research references and
reject unchanged executable adoption. A future implementation should repair call and client
plumbing, use strict typed parsing, record invalid outcomes and retries, bind dependency and
model identities, and separate known-law computation from unsupported causal interpretation.
A constrained library call or exact formula checker remains a necessary comparator to arbitrary
generated code. (Rahul Shrestha and causal-reasoning contributors, 2025)
   The next public evaluation can now start from authenticated question identifiers and paired
outputs while retaining disputed references and missing histories. It must still establish its own
frozen execution environment, held-out cases, reference adjudication and full workflow costs.
This closes a source-availability and scoring gap while leaving scientific truth and executable
qualification as explicit, testable obligations.
Chapter 51

Banking decisions, review effort and
the value of assistance

51.1      Value belongs to a decision and an information set
The value of an agent is the change it makes to a feasible decision after including its information,
review and operating costs. Producing a longer report, drawing more edges or executing a
notebook faster can help that decision, but none is the economic target itself. The banking
application must specify the action, baseline workflow, affected population, financial horizon
and loss before comparing systems.
   Let a range over feasible actions and let V (a, θ) be their monetary value under a causal
state θ. An information set I might contain observed data, authenticated design records and
unresolved alternatives. If a justified probability law for θ is available, an expected-value
decision solves
                               a∗ (I) ∈ arg max E{V (a, θ) | I}.
                                               a

This expression is a decision rule conditional on a probability model. A language model’s
self-reported certainty, the frequency of repeated answers, or a fraction of retrieved documents
is not automatically that probability. The distinction matters most when a small change in
the assumed probability changes a lending, servicing or funding action.
   If the evidence instead supports a set Θ(I) without probabilities, the bank needs an explicit
ambiguity policy. For example, a robust rule can maximize inf θ∈Θ(I) V (a, θ). Expected value
and this robust criterion answer different decision questions. The software must preserve the
information needed for either and require the policy to be named. It must not manufacture
a distribution by assigning equal weight to whichever graphs an algorithm happened to
enumerate.


51.2      An exact example of useful and costly information
Consider a stipulated one-customer intervention whose incremental gross return is either
CNY 0 or CNY 400, with intervention cost CNY 300. Suppose the two states have equal prior
probability. These are project assumptions for an arithmetic example, not bank estimates,
elicited probabilities or measured model performance. Acting has expected net return 200 −
300 = −100, so the unassisted expected-value decision is to do nothing, with value zero.
  Perfect information would permit action only in the CNY 400 state. Its expected gross


                                                979
980                                                                      Causal analysis for a universal bank


value relative to doing nothing is therefore
                         1                   1
                         2 max(0, 0 − 300) + 2 max(0, 400 − 300) = 50.

For this action set and loss, no information service can justify an expected payment above
CNY 50 per decision solely through improved action selection. The bound would change if the
service had other validated benefits or changed the feasible actions; neither is assumed here.
   Now stipulate a binary signal that reports “positive” with probability 0.9 in the high-return
state and 0.1 in the low-return state. Each signal outcome has marginal probability 0.5. Bayes’
rule gives posterior high-state probabilities 0.9 after a positive signal and 0.1 after a negative
signal. The conditional net returns from acting are respectively

                       0.9(400) − 300 = 60,            0.1(400) − 300 = −260.

The optimal rule acts only after a positive signal. Its gross expected value is 0.5(60) = 30. An
independent calculation keeps the loss from false positives visible:

                               0.5(0.9)(100) − 0.5(0.1)(300) = 30.
                               |     {z       }    |       {z       }
                              true-positive gain   false-positive loss

The information value is below the perfect-information bound, as it should be.
   Suppose obtaining and checking the signal costs CNY 2 in computation and CNY 8 in
review for every request, including negative ones. The incremental net value is then CNY 20.
Under the additional simplifying assumptions of identical expected value, linear costs and no
discounting, a CNY 50,000 fixed development cost breaks even at 50,000/20 = 2,500 decisions.
These figures are reproduced with exact rational arithmetic. They are a transparent planning
construction, not a price quotation or an ROI estimate for the implemented prototype.
   The threshold for acting is a high-state probability above 300/400 = 0.75. An assistant
that says “90% confident” can cross that threshold without having a calibrated probability.
Review must establish the meaning and reliability of the signal. A syntactically valid report, a
correct posterior formula and an accurate multiplication cannot compensate for an invented
likelihood.


51.3      Refusal can preserve value, but it also consumes resources
If all that is defensible is the set Θ = {0, 400}, robust net value from acting is −300, while doing
nothing guarantees zero incremental value. The robust rule therefore declines the intervention.
This conclusion differs from a claim that the true effect is zero. It expresses how the bank
chooses under unresolved uncertainty and the stated loss.
  A service that exposes the ambiguity can be valuable if the incumbent workflow would act
on a falsely precise estimate. The evaluation must include that incumbent behavior explicitly.
Against an already cautious baseline, the same refusal may add little decision value while still
costing analyst time. A refusal is neither automatically a failure nor automatically a benefit.
  The inspected observational workflow illustrates this problem through critic declines under
poor overlap (Chou et al., 2026). The denominator must include the declined requests, their
review cost and what happened next. Did a reviewer obtain a better design, narrow the
population with explicit authorization, commission an experiment, or simply lose time? Each
path has a different economic implication. Changing to a selected population must also change
the target rather than make the original request appear successful.
51.4. Four banking journeys require different evidence                                         981


51.4      Four banking journeys require different evidence
For a funding decision, assistance can assemble the rate action, balance units, margin horizon
and policy constraints. It can also flag a mismatch between calendar covariance and an
assumed independent sampling unit. Value arises only if these corrections improve a decision
or avert an error relative to the baseline. A conservative interval wider than the bank’s action
threshold may be scientifically defensible and economically inconclusive.
   For sequential servicing, the central object is a policy adapted to information available at
each decision. The total bill includes state measurement, assignment logging, intervention
delivery and customer outcomes, as well as model calls. An agent can help describe a dynamic
regime, but a static ATE translator cannot evaluate it by substituting a single treatment
indicator. The economic study must compare genuinely feasible policies under common
information and count unsuccessful or unavailable evaluations.
   For discovery followed by intervention, a visually simpler graph can conceal alternative
effects. The useful information is whether additional evidence changes the set of financially
acceptable actions. More accurate recovery of irrelevant edges may have little value for the
selected decision. Conversely, one mistaken orientation near the treatment or outcome can
reverse a policy recommendation. Graph accuracy and decision loss should both be reported,
with neither used as a proxy for the other.
   For trustworthy observations, a language system can reconcile field names and suggest
ownership or inclusion questions. The bank must still establish actual linkage, label and audit
truth. Reviewing a source dictionary may prevent a semantic error; it does not supply sampled
identity labels or independent calendars. The cost of obtaining those scientific inputs belongs
in the information budget, and their absence remains a legitimate stop condition for an effect
calculation.


51.5      A complete cost model
For request i, a prospective accounting identity is

            Ci = Ci,model + Ci,retrieval + Ci,numeric + Ci,review + Ci,data + Ci,operation .

The terms represent distinct resource uses, not independently measured values in the current
project. Model cost includes all calls and retries. Retrieval includes acquisition and any
permitted indexing. Numerical cost includes the complete fit, uncertainty calculation and
serialization. Review includes time spent on wrong, refused and unsupported answers. Data
cost includes audits and additional information. Operations include storage, recovery and
support.
   A natural-workflow comparison measures the quality and cost of complete workflows. A
matched-budget comparison holds selected resources fixed to study one contribution. The
two can produce different rankings without contradiction. An agent that improves answers by
using more expert review may be valuable, but the result is about the combined workflow. It
does not isolate autonomous reasoning quality.
   The experimental unit must also match the cost and outcome calculation. Repeated prompts
about one mechanism are correlated observations within that mechanism. Counting them
as independent bank decisions understates uncertainty and can exaggerate the amount of
evidence. Error bars for incremental value should use the prespecified mechanism or decision
clusters and retain the paired comparison wherever both workflows face the same problem.
982                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


51.6     What can be concluded before a live evaluation
The local controller demonstrates preservation of declarations, alternatives, refusals and
numerical set topology in selected authored examples. It makes zero live model calls. Its
measured interface behavior cannot reveal a provider’s accuracy, token use, price or review
burden on unfamiliar questions. Those fields remain unavailable rather than being filled with
zeros.
   Published benchmarks support the design of a prospective evaluation. They cannot be
combined across different model revisions, task distributions and information budgets into
a bank ROI estimate. CausalDS in particular reports divergence between symbolic success,
interval quality, abstention and cost, which supports measuring them separately (Leban and
Sun, 2026).
   The next empirical step requires a specified backend and custody arrangement, actual prices
and budget, independent held-out mechanisms, adjudicators and qualified numerical baselines.
For bank adoption it additionally requires feasible actions, authentic records and accepted
loss thresholds. Until those inputs exist, exact decision examples can check the accounting
and expose threshold errors. They cannot establish that assistance crosses an institutional
investment threshold.


51.7     Full cost and the investment threshold
Cost is an accounting identity before it is a performance result. For request i, retain input,
output and cache tokens with their actual dated prices; numerical compute; retrieval and
storage; tool retries; analyst review and rework; escalation; and any failed-run charges. Add
fixed integration, security and maintenance costs separately. Unmeasured components remain
missing. Token counts alone cannot establish either dollar savings or cost per usable causal
decision.
   An explicitly illustrative price scenario makes the arithmetic concrete. An ordinary review
takes 30 minutes at USD 60/hour plus USD 1 compute, for USD 31/request. Assisted review
takes 10 minutes at the same rate, USD 2 tools, 30,000 input tokens at USD 2/million and
5,000 output tokens at USD 8/million, USD 0.20 retrieval and USD 0.20 expected retry charges.
The assumed token cost is USD 0.10. If 20% of requests additionally require a 30-minute
escalation, expected escalation cost is USD 6 and total assisted cost is USD 18.50. These
prices, times and escalation frequencies are scenario assumptions, not provider quotations or
measured productivity.
   The resulting variable saving is USD 12.50/request before incremental error losses and fixed
costs. With USD 12,500 fixed cost, 1,000 requests reach arithmetic break-even only if all
those assumptions hold and decision quality is otherwise unchanged. If the assisted method
increases a USD 10,000-loss error by 0.1 percentage points per request, the added expected loss
is USD 10 and net saving falls to USD 2.50, requiring 5,000 requests to recover the same fixed
cost. At a 0.2 percentage-point increase, variable net value is already negative. With all other
inputs fixed and no added error loss, escalation probability must be below 37/60 ≈ 61.67% for
positive variable savings. These sensitivities explain why an inexpensive-looking model call is
not a business case. (Causal banking proposal, 2026p)
   The prospective analysis should compare paired decision loss plus cost per requested case,
as well as cost per valid result. The latter ratio needs its numerator and denominator reported;
selective refusal can improve the ratio while reducing service. In bank data the relevant error
loss may be unknown, so the proposal can report break-even surfaces and identify which
51.8. Selective automation must be valued over requested decisions                              983


uncertainty a prototype should resolve. It must not assign invented observed losses to satisfy
an ROI gate.


51.7.1    A study that can be registered after a prototype

The proposed evaluation protocol is a reviewed prospective design, not a registered or executed
study. Its 400 mechanisms, four label/evidence conditions and three repetitions are a planning
allocation. They would generate 4,800 requests per workflow arm, but the independent unit
is the mechanism and repetitions/conditions are nested. For a single Bernoulli proportion,
400 independent observations give an approximate worst-case 95% normal half-width of 0.049.
For a paired difference bounded in [−1, 1], the worst-case normal half-width can be 0.098.
An elementary distribution-free bounded-mean calculation at half-width 0.05 and failure
probability 0.05 requires at least 2,952 independent mechanisms. To see this, the second
derivative of the log moment-generating function of a variable in [−1, 1] is a tilted variance
at most one. Integrating twice gives log E exp{λ(D − ED)} ≤ λ2 /2. Independence and the
exponential Markov inequality then give P (|D̄ − E D̄| ≥ ϵ) ≤ 2 exp(−nϵ2 /2). Solving for n
yields the stated conservative count. This calculation does not choose a final sample size or
justify normal inference in every stratum. (Causal banking proposal, 2026p)
   First use public, development-only examples to measure feasibility and costs for a numerical
baseline, an ordinary analyst workflow, a single assistant, retrieval assistance and a hybrid
numerical assistant. Add debate only as a separate ablation. Cross unfamiliar labels with
held-out mechanism families, misleading retrieval, clock violations, proxy measurement and
nonidentification. Keep an equal-information comparison separate from an equal-resource
comparison; a system receiving a scientific source or more numerical fitting has a different
information or compute budget. For a human study, assign cases and workflow order to avoid
the learning/selection confounding illustrated by CausalChat, and include review, adjudication
and rework time.
   Use the development pilot to choose decision-relevant tolerances, feasible budgets and a
justified final allocation. Before a final run, bind provider/model revision, actual settings, pack-
age/container identities, independent holdout and truth, retrieval corpus, human adjudication
protocol, prices, stopping rules and the analysis script. Freeze paired mechanism-level analyses
and the multiplicity policy. Retain every planned attempt, including malformed, unsupported,
timed-out and unavailable requests. Quality thresholds concern target/clock errors, unjustified
causal claims, calibration where eligible, justified refusal, decision loss and full cost; a single
composite score cannot establish all of them. These are future prototype/experiment inputs,
not reasons to block this literature-and-design proposal.
   The immediate investment is a narrow prototype using public data and stipulated mecha-
nisms. Its purpose is to resolve target errors, unsupported assumptions, tool failures and review
burden before an expensive bank experiment. Hidden evaluation, actual prices, bank-specific
loss and institutional review remain later inputs; the proposal does not invent their outcomes.


51.8      Selective automation must be valued over requested deci-
          sions
An assisted workflow chooses both an answer and whether to act on it. These choices change
the population on which accuracy is reported. Let Ri = 1 mean that request i receives an
automated recommendation and Ri = 0 mean that it is referred to a fallback. Let ai and
bi denote the respective actions, θi the decision-relevant state, and ℓ(a, θ) the loss relative
984                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


to an explicitly specified feasible comparator. If Ci includes all work before referral, Hi the
additional fallback cost and Di the loss caused by delay, a complete per-request accounting
variable is
                     Zi = Ci + Ri ℓ(ai , θi ) + (1 − Ri ){Hi + Di + ℓ(bi , θi )}.
Loss is monetary here only because the example stipulates a monetary mapping. Legal
feasibility, access to assistance and other constraints can instead restrict the allowed actions;
they should not be silently converted into an invented dollar penalty. A comparison estimates
the change in Zi over the same requested population, including requests on which either
workflow fails. An unanswered request has a subsequent action or an unresolved consequence,
not a disappearing row. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ag)
   Consider 100 generated offer decisions: 80 with a USD 100 loss for a wrong action and
20 with a USD 10,000 loss. Workflow A answers all 80 low-consequence requests and ten
high-consequence requests. It makes one error in each group. Workflow B answers 60 low-
consequence and ten high-consequence requests, making three errors in the first group and
none in the second. A’s conditional answer accuracy is 88/90, higher than B’s 67/70. These
are invented counts that define the example, not estimates of either a model or a bank’s error
rate.
  Assume A costs USD 2 and B costs USD 4 for every requested decision. Each referral costs
another USD 40 and resolves the action correctly in this particular construction. Delay costs
USD 5 for a low-consequence referral and USD 50 for a high-consequence referral. The full
accounting is
                        total
                      ZA      = 200 + 10,100 + 400 + 500 = 11,200,
                          total
                         ZB     = 400 + 300 + 1,200 + 600 = 2,500.
B is less accurate among its answers and automates fewer requests, yet has USD 8,700 less
total loss and cost in the constructed portfolio. The fallback is assumed correct, so these
totals are optimistic about review; allowing review errors adds their losses through the same
equation. Equally, the construction does not imply that more referral is always better. Raising
its cost, delay or error rate can reverse the result. The point is that automation coverage and
conditional accuracy do not determine economic value even when both have been measured
correctly. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ag)
   The review decision can be made explicit. Suppose an unreviewed recommendation has
error probability q, a reviewed recommendation has probability r, an error loses L, and review
plus delay costs c. Under this binary-loss model, review improves expected value precisely
when
                                        (q − r)L > c.
For stipulated q = .01, r = .002 and c = 20, the loss threshold is USD 2,500. Reviewing
a USD 100-consequence decision has net value minus USD 19.20; reviewing a USD 10,000-
consequence decision has net value USD 60. The same apparent confidence therefore supports
different review choices. A language model’s stated confidence does not supply q, and
agreement between model and reviewer does not identify r. These probabilities concern
correctness conditional on the target population and routing rule; they require suitable labels
and a separately reviewed evaluation. If review can introduce errors, r may exceed q. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026ag)
   CausalChat supplies a reason to study the presentation and review components together.
Its six-student study reports mean edge-editing times of 3.3 minutes with LLM text and 0.9
minutes with CausalChat Lite. The study used a fixed sequence of stages and participants
chose which edges to resolve. The paper also reports concerns about missing citations and the
reliability of scientific support. Those observations motivate a banking comparison of review
51.9. Retry and fallback costs depend on the failure mechanism                               985


burden, target errors and evidence inspection. They do not identify a transferable productivity
effect or justify multiplying 2.4 minutes by a bank salary and calling the result a saving. A
prospective comparison should control task difficulty, learning and reviewer allocation, while
preserving the time spent on consequential mistakes and unresolved cases. (Zhang, 2024)


51.9     Retry and fallback costs depend on the failure mechanism
Agent workflows often retry after malformed output, unavailable tools or a failed scientific
check. Let T be the first attempt that passes a specified check and let m be a fixed attempt
cap. The number of attempted calls is N = min(T, m), with T > m when none passes. For
integer N , N = m j=1 1{N ≥ j}, giving
               P

                                            m
                                            X
                                     EN =         Pr(T ≥ j).
                                            j=1

This identity needs no independence assumption. With an identical per-attempt cost c and
terminal fallback charge F , expected execution cost is cEN + F Pr(T > m). Attempt-specific
review and transfer costs can be included inside the corresponding indicators. Passing an
operational check is still separate from answering the causal question correctly; a protocol
that detects only malformed JSON needs an additional scientific-error term. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026ag)
  Two stipulated mechanisms have the same 20% first-attempt failure rate. In the first, failures
are independent with probability 1/5. At m = 3,

                         EN = 1 + 51 + 25

In the second, one tenth of requests have a permanent defect. Other requests have independent
transient failure probability 1/9 per attempt. For k ≥ 1, the probability that the first k
attempts all fail is
                                                    k
                                         1    9     1
                                         10 + 10    9     .
The first-attempt failure rate is again 1/5, but EN = 1 + 1/5 + 1/9 = 59/45 and the terminal
failure probability is 41/405, approximately 10.12%. At USD 2 per attempt and USD 50
for the terminal fallback, expected costs are USD 2.88 and approximately USD 7.68. Full
enumeration of permanent status and all three transient outcomes gives the same values as
the tail-sum calculation. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ag)
   A missing identification method, inconsistent units, inaccessible evidence or an ambiguous
causal target can behave like the permanent component. A new prompt does not necessarily
change the missing information. Independent retry arithmetic would substantially understate
terminal workload in that case. The proposed agent should classify the failure, retain the failed
request and route to an appropriate remedy: repair a format, select a supported method, seek
evidence or return an unresolved decision. A retry budget limits spending; it does not establish
that repeated reasoning supplies independent evidence. The classification itself should be
checked because a mistaken “transient” label can generate costly repetition.
   CausalDS reports marked differences in tool-use strategy and total tokens, alongside tool-
output-management failures and distinct content and abstention outcomes. Its reported ATE
interval coverage uses only seven eligible cases per model, or five for one model, in that
particular exam. These scoped results support retaining trajectories and component outcomes.
They do not supply the permanent-failure fraction of a banking workflow, and total tokens do
not determine dollars without dated input/output/cache prices and the relevant billing rules.

The prototype should measure the actual sequence of attempts, which input changed between
them, and the eventual fallback. No named service price or bank runtime is assumed here.
(Leban and Sun, 2026)


51.10      Causal ambiguity needs a declared decision rule
The funding example in Section 56.18 maps a supplied response set through a stated profit
function and obtains net values from minus USD 625 to plus USD 1,625. Holding the rate fixed
has zero incremental value in that example. To examine the decision rule, temporarily treat
those endpoints as a declared ambiguity set containing the true state; this is a conditional
decision construction. If the set came from a confidence procedure, its coverage uncertainty
remains an additional issue. It is not a posterior probability law over the possible profits.
  A robust net-value rule holds because the worst net value from acting is negative. A
deterministic minimax-regret rule acts. To see the difference, define regret in state θ as
                            R(a, θ) =      max         V (b, θ) − V (a, θ).
                                        b∈{hold,act}

Acting has worst regret USD 625, whereas holding has worst regret USD 1,625. Robust value
protects the attained payoff; minimax regret protects the shortfall relative to what could have
been chosen with state knowledge. Neither rule is deduced from the graph or interval alone.
They express different preferences for the same scientifically unresolved funding question.
   If randomizing the entire action were an admissible policy, choose action with probability
p. Expected regret within the adverse and favorable states is 625p and 1625(1 − p). Their
maximum is minimized at
                             1625       13              8125
                     p=              = ,       Rmax =          ≈ 451.39.
                          625 + 1625    18               18
This is a randomized decision across instances, not permission to replace the rate change by
13/18 of its size. The latter needs a response model for the new intervention. A bank may
prohibit randomized treasury actions, so the deterministic analysis can remain the relevant
one. An assistant should explain which criterion generated a recommendation and preserve
the alternatives. It should never silently convert an interval midpoint into a uniquely justified
choice. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ag; Causal banking research project, 2026i)
   Sequential servicing adds a second information requirement: the joint values of the feasible
policies. Suppose two generated worlds give net policy values (VA , VB ) = (−100, −200) and
(100, 0). Policy A exceeds B by USD 100 in both worlds. Separate coordinate projections give
VA ∈ [−100, 100] and VB ∈ [−200, 0], whose unrestricted difference spans [−300, 100]. That
box suggests a possible advantage for B by combining coordinates from incompatible worlds.
It is a conservative enlargement, but it can conceal a strict policy ranking. A useful policy
interface should preserve the joint world or region identity where available and state when
only coordinate bounds have been computed. An LLM can explain this distinction; it cannot
recover lost joint information from two displayed intervals. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ag)
   For discovery, the information purchase should concern an unresolved feature that can change
an action, such as a consequential orientation or an admissible intervention regime. Improving
unrelated edges may have no value for the specified offer. For observation construction, the
consequential distinction may instead be the origin map, inclusion design or label law. A
timestamp audit can be useful while leaving those questions untouched. The four journeys
therefore share an accounting language but require different information. Their proposed
acceptance cases keep unsupported estimators, equal-law counterexamples and unresolved
scientific premises visible. (Causal banking proposal, 2026af)
51.11. A public prototype buys an option to make a later investment                           987


51.11      A public prototype buys an option to make a later in-
           vestment
A proposal need not know bank ROI before it can justify a small prototype. It does need an
account of which later decision the prototype could change. Let G be the eventual net value
of constructing a selected capability, after all subsequent implementation and operating costs
in a declared horizon. The choice today is to build or decline. A pilot supplies a signal S,
costs K today and delays the later value by a discount factor d ∈ (0, 1]. Under an explicitly
stipulated joint probability model, the two option values are

                W0 = max{0, EG},         Wpilot = −K + d E[max{0, E(G | S)}].

The maximum inside the expectation represents the option to decline after an unfavorable
signal. It must correspond to a feasible stop decision: costs already committed before the
signal cannot be removed by a retrospective choice. Pilot cost is excluded from G because it
is subtracted separately. The law of S describes how the prototype informs the commercial
and scientific state; a benchmark score is not automatically such a signal. (Causal banking
proposal, 2026ag)
   For an exact planning example, let G be USD 100,000 or minus USD 60,000 with equal
probability. Immediate construction has expected net value USD 20,000. Stipulate a pilot
signal with sensitivity and specificity both 4/5. Positive and negative signals each occur
with probability 1/2. Conditional expected construction values are USD 68,000 and minus
USD 28,000, so the pilot policy builds only after a positive signal. Expected value before pilot
cost and delay is USD 34,000. This also follows directly from
                             14              11
                             2 5 (100,000) + 2 5 (−60,000) = 34,000,

which keeps the loss from an unfavorable state with a positive signal explicit. At K = 10,000
and d = .9, the pilot option is worth USD 20,600: only USD 600 more than immediate
construction. Without delay it is worth USD 24,000. Comparing the USD 34,000 gross value
with a zero baseline would incorrectly discard the already available USD 20,000 construction
option. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ag)
   The example gives testable planning thresholds instead of a declared ROI. At signal quality
4/5, the pilot is weakly preferred to immediate construction exactly when d ≥ 15/17. With
d = .9 and symmetric signal quality s in the regime s > 5/8, where the negative signal leads
to declining construction, the gross option value is 80,000s − 30,000. The break-even quality is

                              30,000 + (20,000 + K)/d   19
                         s≥                           =    ≈ .7917.
                                       80,000           24
At lower quality the correct action after each signal must be recalculated; the displayed branch
cannot be extrapolated through a change of optimal action. Perfect information would have
gross value USD 50,000, an incremental USD 30,000 over immediate construction before
costs and delay. No imperfect signal about this same fixed state and action set exceeds that
perfect-information value, because conditional maximization cannot outperform choosing with
the state observed. This comparison says nothing about pilots that themselves create new
feasible capabilities, which require a different model. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ag)
   For the causal proposal, the first signal should come from a bounded public or generated
prototype: can a selected adapter preserve the target; can it refuse an unidentified request; does
a proposed uncertainty method have useful width under its declared law; and how much review
and recovery does the complete workflow require? These outcomes can change a construction
988                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


decision without claiming bank validation. A later authentic experiment becomes justified
when its expected information can resolve a consequential uncertainty that the prototype
cannot. The staged decision should include delay and the ability to stop, as well as favorable
technical results. (Causal banking proposal, 2026af)


51.12      Transferring workflow value requires the deployment
           mixture
Even if a prototype measured paired workflow value exactly on its own cases, the average need
not transport to the requested bank population. Write ∆j for the incremental saving, after
errors and full costs, in stratum j, and wj for the deployment proportion. Under the strong
assumption that within-stratum values transport, deployment value is
                                                 X
                                     ∆deploy =       wj ∆j .
                                                 j

This assumption includes task difficulty, information availability, feasible actions, review and
losses within each stratum. Matching a topic name alone does not establish it. If the weights
are unknown but constrained to a set W, the corresponding value set is the range of the
displayed linear function over W. Its extrema can be computed without inventing a single
deployment average. (Causal banking proposal, 2026ag)
   Suppose the workflow saves USD 10 on a routine case and loses USD 30 on a difficult
case, with all components stipulated. If w is the difficult-case fraction, incremental value is
10 − 40w dollars per requested case. A public development collection with w = 1/5 has a
USD 2 advantage, while a deployment mix with w = 3/5 has a USD 14 disadvantage. The
threshold is w = 1/4. Knowing only that w ∈ [.1, .4] gives a value range from minus USD 6
to plus USD 6. Neither a public positive result nor uncertainty about the target mixture
justifies choosing its favorable endpoint. Selection by the assistant can change the mix again;
the routing policy and fallback outcomes must be part of the transported object. (Causal
banking proposal, 2026ag)
   This is especially relevant when business translation is the proposed benefit. A public
dataset with clean treatment and outcome names can test numerical orchestration yet supply
little information about ambiguous requests, changing population definitions or delayed records.
A difficult-case stratum should be defined by the causal task and information obstacle, not
merely by a model’s low confidence. Language assistance can suggest the strata and identify
missing fields, but their prevalence and consequences need separate evidence. Feng et al.’s
reliability study restricts its accessible-corpus analysis and notes its largely commonsense
setting; it does not provide an error law for all closed models or complex dynamic banking
problems. That limitation supports explicit transport assumptions, not an extrapolated bank
failure rate. (Feng, 2024)
   Prices also need a transport argument. A prototype’s observed analyst minutes are resource
use; converting them into savings requires a decision about reassigned capacity, wage overhead
and whether staffing expenditure changes. Compute cost can have minimum charges, cached
inputs, reserved capacity or shared infrastructure. A model with lower variable cost can require
more adjudication or a larger fixed integration. For annual requested volume n, eligible-use
fraction u, per-used-request incremental value v and additional fixed cost F , the elementary
no-discount scenario is nuv − F . Both u and v can change with expansion, and v already
includes the fallback and loss terms. A cost-per-answer claim should therefore be accompanied
by the requested denominator and resource totals. This proposal supplies the accounting and
51.13. What each banking case still needs to justify further work                            989


break-even questions; actual deployment weights, prices and accepted values are prospective
measurements. (Causal banking proposal, 2026af)


51.13      What each banking case still needs to justify further
           work
Funding has a concrete immediate prototype route: connect a selected summary estimator to
joint nuisance and dependence accounting, preserve the complete response set, and propagate it
through the stated profit map. Generated calendars and known inclusion designs can reveal an
invalid covariance or misstated household unit cheaply. Public bank observations can establish
availability and preparation burden. Neither route by itself verifies a bank’s proxy exclusion,
household truth or future margin. The economic question is whether improved information or
precision changes a treasury action enough to justify the next acquisition. An interval that
still spans consequential gains and losses is an informative inconclusive result.
   Servicing requires a policy that uses the information actually available at each action, and
an evaluation that preserves the original eligible cohort. The finite-table example supplies an
exact reference and a conservative bound that is too wide for useful selection. A first prototype
should compare a specified estimator with that reference under controlled assignment, support
and dropout. Sharper valid uncertainty is a research objective; it is not created by asking an
agent to report a narrower interval. Hidden-state and informative-observation examples with
equal observed laws require an information change or a defensible restriction. The eventual
value of resolving them depends on feasible servicing actions and rewards, including assistance
costs.
   Discovery requires a specified graph family, an honest identification state and an effect
or decision comparison after graph uncertainty. A prototype can first check endpoint and
node-order conversions against generated truth, then test a selected discovery procedure under
its own assumptions. The investment question is whether a retained ambiguity changes the
offer decision, and which additional evidence can resolve it. Agreement among packages or
among repeated language answers is not an authenticated signal of the causal state. A stronger
claim about language-assisted discovery requires a separate controlled comparison of the data,
source evidence and expert effort supplied to each alternative.
  Observation construction needs different evidence again. Valid clocks and unchanged
hashes can coexist with false labels, duplicated origins and wrong inclusion probabilities.
A public/generated prototype can test measurement correction and the transmission of its
uncertainty, including singular cases. The agent’s contribution may be to expose the missing
audit or distinguish an outcome clock from a feature clock. Authentic truth labels, ownership
and joint inclusion evidence are later inputs when the decision benefit warrants their cost. The
observation module should report which uncertainty remains instead of awarding a truthful-
population label from a successful timestamp check. (Causal banking proposal, 2026af)
   These routes have known engineering steps and genuine scientific limits. We know how
to implement a bounded adapter, preserve failed requests, compare exact references, collect
workflow costs and prepare a controlled pilot. We do not know a universal theorem for arbitrary
hidden-state decisions, unrestricted dependent learners or arbitrary temporal graph effects,
and no language model can make observationally equivalent worlds distinguishable without
additional information. We also do not yet know the empirical accuracy, calibrated risk, review
burden or accepted bank value of the proposed assistance. A coherent proposal treats each
unknown as a specific next decision: prove a restricted claim, change the information, test a
prototype or decline the unsupported use. Independent journeys can proceed under their own
990                                                        Causal analysis for a universal bank


prerequisites. Bank experiments follow demonstrated prototype merit and a useful information
question. (Causal banking proposal, 2026af)
Chapter 52

Deriving a common causal-analysis
product

The bank’s recurring difficulty is that an analysis crosses several scientific representations. A
commercial question names a feasible action and a financial consequence. Its data are event
records with changing identities and reporting delays. An economist supplies restrictions
on assignment or shocks; a learner estimates conditional distributions; a validator needs a
sampling argument; a decision maker needs the value of a feasible policy. A shared product is
useful when it preserves the meaning of the question across those transformations.
   The proposed product is a library and a standalone analytical workspace built around the
same scientific objects. Its first release should expose a bounded collection of well-defined
operations. More general discovery, inverse problems and latent control remain important
research capabilities, but their outputs must retain the assumptions and unresolved alternatives
developed in the preceding chapters. The construction below derives this boundary; it is a
specification, not a claim that the entire product already exists.


52.1     The scientific request is larger than an estimator call
Write a request as
                                   Q = (M, K, g, ν, θ, E, F),                              (52.1)
where M is a class of causal models, K the observation operator, g the intervention, ν the target
population, θ the requested functional, E the sampling experiment and F the information
available to the decision rule. For a model M ∈ M, the observed law is P = K(M ) and the
causal answer is θ(M ; g, ν). The observation operator includes selection, measurement, clocks,
aggregation and record linkage when relevant. The sampling experiment specifies independent
households, randomized branches, a dependent calendar series, or another explicit design.
   For deposit retention, the request might ask for the difference in six-month discounted net
funding contribution under two invitation rules for households eligible on a specified date.
It must distinguish invitation from receipt, and baseline eligible households from eventual
activators. If the action is instead an increase in offered interest, both customer balances and
the price paid on existing balances change. These are different interventions and financial
functionals even when the same table is used.
  The target needs a measurable definition before computation. For example, with monthly




                                              991
992                                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


contribution Rt in a declared currency and discount factor dt , use
                                                "T −1             #           "T −1             #
                                                        dt Rtg1                       dt Rtg0
                                                 X                             X
                     θ(M ; g1 , g0 , ν) = EνM                         − EνM                         .
                                                 t=0                           t=0

Here Rt includes the agreed funding, servicing, incentive and expected loss components without
counting the same balance benefit twice. An average balance effect is an input to this account,
not already its answer. Currency conversion, discounting, exposure weights and eligibility are
part of the target rather than invisible formatting options.
   Several request fields can be inferred syntactically from data, but the scientific restrictions
cannot. Software can detect a duplicate decision or a covariate first recorded after action. It
cannot infer that a pricing instrument has no direct effect or that all private underwriting
information has been measured. The workspace should let an analyst draw and explain
the model, compare plausible alternatives, and attach empirical diagnostics to particular
restrictions. A single numerical validity score would erase the distinction between those
obligations.


52.2     Identification returns a mathematical object or an explicit
         limit
Define the identified set

                         ΘQ (P ) = {θ(M ; g, ν) : M ∈ M, K(M ) = P }.

An identification routine receives the model and observation declarations; it does not receive
permission to add whichever assumptions make a preferred estimator available. A singleton
set can be represented by an observed-law functional Ψ(P ). A non-singleton set may admit
bounds, a union of functionals, or only a nonidentification witness. The useful result types are
therefore distinct.
Identified expression.
An expression for Ψ together with the assumptions and transformations that derive it. Numer-
ical evaluation may still be unsupported.
Identified set or outer bound.
A set with its model class, support, restrictions and sharpness status. A conservative outer
bound is useful, but must not be labelled sharp without a compatible-model construction.
Nonidentification witness.
Two allowed models with the same observed law and different targets, or a valid source-specific
failure certificate such as a hedge in the applicable ID model.
Unsupported query.
The registered algorithm does not handle the graph class, intervention, observation process or
requested target. This makes no claim that the target is unidentified.
Incompatible specification.
The declarations are logically inconsistent or violate a deterministic support/schema require-
ment. A statistical model-check rejection should separately carry its test and error level.
   These types follow from Chapter 1 and the ID/IDC construction of Shpitser and Pearl
(2006). Failure to find a back-door set is not a nonidentification certificate. Nor is failure
of an optimizer. For example, the front-door expression is identified under its restrictions,
but a backend implementing only covariate adjustment should return an identified expression
with no available estimator. Conversely, the two invitation models of Section 2.3 agree on
52.3. Adapters must preserve targets and statistical experiments                              993


all observed records and disagree on the population ATE. Increasing an estimator’s iteration
budget cannot supply that missing information.
   For an initial implementation, observed-law expressions can use a small typed language:
conditional probability kernels, products, integrals or finite sums, substitutions, and ratios on
declared positive support. A kernel records its random arguments, conditioning arguments,
units, dominating measure and observation regime. The type of p(y | a, x) differs from pg (y | x);
a density in currency units differs from a probability mass. Marginalization removes a random
argument; it must not accidentally integrate a fixed intervention value.
   Each allowed transformation should produce a trace. In ordinary adjustment, that trace
names the adjustedR
                     variables, explains why their predecision status and separation condition
apply, and yields p(y | a, x)p(x) dx. In recursive ID, it records ancestors, districts, extracted
kernels and support restrictions. The trace certifies the consequence of the supplied assumptions.
It cannot certify that the graph supplied by a bank economist is the true graph.


52.3      Adapters must preserve targets and statistical experi-
          ments
The target-preservation identity Ψ(P ) = ΨB (T# P ) in Section 17.1 is necessary for converting
data through T to backend B. It also constrains uncertainty. Suppose, for this paragraph, that
observations Oi are independent and identically distributed, T is fixed and applied separately
to each unit, and Z = T (O). Let Pε be a regular submodel with score S(O). Differentiating
the pushforward density gives the reduced score

                                      SZ (Z) = E[S(O) | Z].

If ϕB (Z) is a gradient for the reduced functional, then
                                d
                                   Ψ(Pε ) = E[ϕB (Z)SZ (Z)]
                                dε       0
                                           = E[ϕB (T (O))S(O)].                            (52.2)

Thus the pulled-back score is a gradient for the original target. In an unrestricted original
model it is the canonical gradient when the stated differentiability conditions hold; in a
restricted model projection onto the model’s tangent space may improve efficiency. This is
a project consequence of the pathwise argument in Chapter 3, not a theorem for arbitrary
preprocessing.
   The qualifications explain common failures. A learned encoder is random and may need
independent training and a remainder analysis. Demeaning over a panel is not a fixed
transformation of each independently sampled row. Expanding one household into transactions
changes the sampling units. Discarding a component of history may destroy target preservation.
An adapter must therefore declare both its mathematical transformation and its mapping of
sampling units, weights and information sets.
   A backend estimator should return sufficient information for the specified inference route.
For a regular scalar moment this includes unit-level scores, the Jacobian, target normalization,
fold assignments and nuisance estimates or their immutable references. For an identified set
it includes bound objectives and constraint certificates. For a weak-IV inversion it includes
the accepted set, including disconnected or unbounded components. For a likelihood model it
includes the exact factorization, numerical approximation and parameter restrictions. Forcing
all of these outputs into an estimate/standard-error pair would discard information that
changes the bank decision.
994                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The companion scientific protocol gives this separation a concrete design form. A request
binds the model, observation, target and sampling specifications by content hash. A result
separately records computational completion, identification and inferential availability. A scalar
confidence set is an ordered union of intervals, including empty, disconnected and unbounded
sets; posterior credible sets have a different type. Derivations, bounds and failure witnesses
have distinct artifact roles. The supplied schema fixtures check these representation invariants.
They do not execute an identification algorithm or establish coverage. The following versioned
extension supplies explicit vector, curve and graph-set types for the bounded constructions
developed in this monograph. A general graph probability distribution remains a different
object.


52.4      A bounded mathematical language and a concrete lower-
          ing rule
The specification must be stronger than a collection of file hashes. A variable declaration
contains its name, support, physical unit, causal role and clock. A population declaration
identifies the economic unit and the role of its weights. An observation declaration identifies the
immutable view, revision relation, availability convention and sampling frequency. The model
specifies a structural class and an assumption set. A target specifies the action, outcomes, fixed
horizons or policies, normalization and population. These declarations together determine a
statistical experiment; no single field can substitute for the others.
  For finite mechanisms an executable expression grammar is particularly transparent. A
mass kernel has ordered parent variables U , ordered child variables V , declared finite supports
and an array of shape |XU | × |XV |. Every parent slice must be nonnegative and sum to one
over the child axes. A generative product j Kj (xj | xpa(j) ) requires one mechanism per child
                                          Q

and a topological order. Marginalization sums named random axes; substitution fixes an axis
without summing it. Replacing an action mechanism by g(a | h) requires that its information
variables precede the action. This operation evaluates the supplied causal factorization; it
does not establish that an arbitrary observed kernel can be intervened upon.
   The local finite-mass interpreter implements product, marginalization and mechanism
replacement, checking support, normalization and information order. For a binary confounded
example it recovers the interventional mean 0.5 and rejects a policy using a future outcome. A
general expression language would additionally need density measures, positive-denominator
restrictions and numerical integration error. The initial lowering rules do not pretend that
this finite interpreter implements continuous ID or general latent identification. Instead they
recognize the complete constructions already derived and reject mismatched target/sampling
combinations.

   These are conditional method choices, not six interchangeable backends. The standalone

52.4.1    Results that can carry the actual uncertainty

Protocol version 0.4 supplements the historical scalar protocol. A scalar is a one-coordinate
result; vectors and response curves have named ordered axes and one physical unit per flattened
coordinate. A response curve orders outcome before horizon. Its covariance has that same
coordinate order and already includes the sample-size divisor. A confidence object carries its
method, level, coverage target and an interval union for each coordinate. For a simultaneous
rectangular set, the Cartesian product of these unions is the confidence region. Empty,
disconnected and unbounded coordinate sets remain representable; an unbounded endpoint is
a typed null, not a JSON infinity or a large arbitrary number. Pointwise coverage cannot be
relabeled simultaneous by an adapter.
   A graph result retains ordered nodes and its graph class. A DAG set stores directed binary
adjacency matrices. CPDAG/PAG endpoint matrices use zero for absence, one for a tail, two
for an arrowhead and three for a circle; the latter is permitted only for a PAG. Basic endpoint
validation is not a complete PAG-recognition algorithm. The temporal reference instead stores
lower and upper coefficient matrices with edge marks “present” or “zero or nonzero”. Its graph
class is not a posterior distribution over graphs. The effect union is explicitly an outer set,
and uncertainty about the causal-sufficiency assumption is not encoded as its confidence level.
   Computational completion, conditional identification and inference have separate status
fields. Numerical error bounds, when available, use the same output units. A null numerical
bound means no certified bound was provided; it must not be interpreted as zero error. Solver
diagnostics and all requested failed repetitions remain attached evidence. Hashes bind those
arrays and declarations to a computation, while scientific validation determines whether their
asserted premises are plausible.
996                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


52.4.2    Allowed conversions and explicit rejection cases

For a fixed known diagonal scale matrix S, the converted effect and covariance are S θb and S Vb S ′ .
Interval endpoints reverse when a scale is negative; the order of disconnected components
also reverses. A rate denominator changing from percentage points to basis points divides a
normalized response by 100. A fixed currency multiplier can be applied in the same way. A
time-varying exchange rate generally changes the reward functional and requires rebuilding it;
a monthly stock cannot be converted into daily flows by relabeling an axis.
   Population weights, inverse behavior probabilities, inverse observation probabilities and
bootstrap frequencies have different mathematical roles. The request validator rejects their
substitution. It also rejects an iid row experiment for the dependent response route, a split
inside a purportedly independent trajectory, inclusive availability when the request requires
strict predecision information, and a learned policy supplied to fixed-policy inference. A
valid clock conversion can preserve timestamp/sequence order exactly; changing that order
requires a new observation analysis. These checks enforce declared meaning, not the truth of
exchangeability or instrument exclusion.


52.5      Concrete sibling boundaries and the standalone study
Read-only inspection of the actual sibling APIs changes the integration design. FinMarketing’s
CausalData.from_record requires pretreatment features, mature outcomes, binary actions
and independent groups. Its FeatureSnapshot orders availability, cutoff and decision by
timestamp/sequence pairs. The local mapping preserves those pairs, horizon and dependence
unit. It does not coerce a dynamic curve into FinMarketing’s scalar Estimate; that requires a
richer result consumer. A causal response to a macro shock also cannot inherit its independent-
group standard error merely because the source rows are account records.
   dataml’s LineageGraph.append accepts run, dataset, partition and metadata, while its cor-
rection schema requires a resolvable assumption and a numerical confidence field. Observation
candidates therefore map to lineage metadata with their assumptions and alternatives. An
uncalibrated hint score does not populate correction confidence, and ambiguous candidates do
not generate an automatic correction. This preserves dataml’s distinction between an original
source and an assumed overlay.
   BayesFilter’s SSMStaticShape, SSMDataSignature and BayesianSSMProblem can record
dimensions, data/mask identities and parameter coordinates. For the binary controlled family,
the local mapping adds action identity, randomized-logger semantics, reward, finite state
support and the full observation order to its model manifest. A generic Bayesian SSM
descriptor alone does not supply those causal meanings or a controlled categorical filter
implementation. Its numerical target and derivative still need to refer to the same likelihood,
as required by Chapter 7.
   MacroFinance’s DirectedPairMeasurement and ObservationContract distinguish
directed quote pairs, maturity, observed rows and derived diagnostics. Its convention is
xm = −χ; reversing a pair reverses the quoted wedge sign. The local mapping preserves these
identities and requires a separate causal role for the measured variable. A triangle diagnostic
is not automatically an identified structural cycle intervention. The inspected MacroFinance
BayesFilter facade also references a different import root from the workspace checkout, so
inspection alone cannot establish runtime compatibility between them.
  The same scientific request/result files support an independent study: choose the economic
target and observation plan, inspect the identifying assumptions, select a supported regime,
52.6. A bounded catalogue of scientific operations                                        997


execute its estimator and mandatory comparison, and publish the result with its uncertainty
and source trace. Local examples exercise the mappings and numerical operations here. Sibling
checkouts remain unchanged; accepted adoption, shared release management and institutional
data access remain separate implementation work.
